text:
INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Nombre de la pt: Mateo Hernández Cruz ("Teo")
Fecha de nacimiento (DOB): 14 de julio de 2021 (14/07/2021)
Edad en la eval: 4;2
Fecha de la eval: 3 de septiembre de 2025
Fecha del informe: 10 de septiembre de 2025
Horario de la sesión: de 9:00 a.m. a 11:15 a.m.
Idiomas del hogar: español (approx 70%) e inglés (approx 30%)
Evaluadora: Laura Jiménez, MS, CCC-SLP, bilingüe esp/ing
Clínica: Carolina Pediatric Speech Therapy, PLLC, sede satélite en Garner
Correo de la clínica: intake@carolinapedsspeech.com
Médico de referencia: Dra. Angela Kim, pediatra, Wake Valley Medical Center
Coordinadora de servicios (CDSA): Marisol Reyes
Caso CDSA del condado de Wake: NC-CDSA-48217-W
Medicaid #: 9384721056M
Autorización: AUTH-2025-66841
Teléfono de contacto (madre): (919) 555-0148
Dirección del hogar: 742 Maple Ridge Lane, Raleigh, NC 27610

MOTIVO DE REFERENCIA

Pt referido por Marisol Reyes (coordinadora CDSA) y la pediatra Dra. Angela Kim luego de screening inicial el 12/05/2025, donde CG reportó retraso notable en el habla tanto en esp como en ing. Madre, Verónica Cruz Flores, refiere que pt usa "pocas palabras" y que mucha gente fuera de la familia "no le entiende nada." Vecina de la familia, Diane Walsh, fue quien recomendó buscar eval formal luego de notar que pt no respondía igual que otros niños de su edad en el parque. Pt fue inscrito en Little Learners Program (programa de intervención temprana del condado de Wake) desde 20 de mayo de 2025 recibiendo 1x/semana de servicios de desarrollo, pero no había recibido eval de habla-lenguaje formal hasta la fecha. Esta eval se realiza para determinar elegibilidad y guiar el IFSP.

ANTECEDENTES DE NACIMIENTO Y DESARROLLO

Pt nació a término, 38 semanas de gestación, parto vaginal sin complicaciones en Wake Valley Medical Center, Raleigh. Peso al nacer 3,100 gramos (6 lb 14 oz). Apgar 8/9. Sin estancia en UCIN. Hx médica incluye otitis media recurrente desde los 9 meses, tx con antibióticos en múltiples ocasiones; tubos de ventilación (miringotomía bilateral) colocados a los 18 meses por Dr. Steven Park, ORL pediátrico. Desde la colocación de tubos, CG reporta menos episodios de otitis, approx 1 por año. Audición evaluada el 20/08/2025 — resultado: audición WNL bilateral, timpanogramas tipo A. Visión no evaluada formalmente, CG no reporta preocupaciones. Desarrollo motor grueso y fino dentro de límites esperados: caminó indep a los 13 meses, agarre de pinza fino presente a los 11 meses. Hitos de lenguaje reportados por CG: primeras palabras approx 15 meses ("mamá", "papá"), pero vocabulario no aumentó mucho desde entonces — CG estima vocabulario actual de approx 40-50 palabras combinando esp e ing, muchas veces aproximaciones no inteligibles fuera del contexto familiar.

Sin dx previo de autismo ni trastorno genético. CG niega hx de convulsiones, trauma craneal, o intoxicación por plomo. Pt no toma medicamentos de rutina. Última eval pediátrica de rutina (well-child check) el 01/08/2025 — sin hallazgos nuevos, pediatra Dra. Angela Kim apoya referido a SLP y a terapia ocupacional.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

Pt es el segundo de tres hermanos. Hermana mayor, Sol Hernández Cruz, 8 años, cursa tercer grado en Lockhart Elementary School sin dificultades académicas reportadas; según CG, Sol habla esp e ing fluido y a veces funciona como "traductora" informal de su hermano menor con otros niños. Hermano menor, Diego Hernández Cruz, 10 meses, desarrollo prelingüístico típico hasta la fecha (balbuceo canónico presente).

Madre, Verónica Cruz Flores, 29 años, trabaja turno nocturno en Procesadora Avícola Carolina; habla esp como lengua primaria, ing conversacional limitado. Padre, Luis Hernández Pérez, no reside en el hogar; visitas los fines de semana, approx cada 15 días; habla esp e ing. Padres reportan separación amistosa desde enero de 2024; ambos mantienen contacto regular con pt.

Abuela materna, Rosa Flores, vive en Aldea El Rosario, cerca de La Esperanza, Honduras; la familia visita 1x/año, última visita diciembre de 2024. Pt mantiene llamadas video semanales con abuela, principalmente en esp. Tía materna, Carmen Cruz, cuida a pt y a su hermano menor 3 días/semana (lunes, miércoles, viernes) mientras madre trabaja; habla exclusivamente esp con los niños. Perrita de la familia, Luna, muy querida por pt — CG reporta que una de las primeras palabras claras de pt fue el nombre de la perra.

Exposición de lenguaje estimada por CG: esp approx 70% del tiempo (casa, con tía Carmen Cruz, llamadas con abuela), ing approx 30% (daycare, hermana mayor a veces, programas de TV). CG reporta que pt mezcla ambos idiomas frecuentemente y que esto "no le preocupa," pero sí le preocupa que no se le entienda en ninguno de los dos idiomas.

HISTORIA ESCOLAR Y SOCIAL

Pt asiste a Little Learners Daycare en Garner desde enero de 2024, de lunes a viernes approx 7:30 a.m. a 3:30 p.m.. Maestra principal: Srta. Jennifer Soto. Maestra asistente: Srta. Patricia Gómez. Ambas reportan que pt es cariñoso y sociable pero que su habla es "difícil de entender" approx 80% del tiempo para alguien fuera de la familia. Pt juega frecuentemente con su compañera Emma Castillo y su compañero Liam Thompson; CG reporta que Emma a veces "habla por él" cuando otros niños no le entienden. Srta. Jennifer Soto reporta que pt usa gestos y señalar con frecuencia para comunicarse cuando las palabras no son suficientes.

La familia recibe beneficios de WIC del condado de Wake desde el nacimiento de pt y está inscrita en servicios de Smart Start of Wake County para apoyo de alfabetización temprana. Madre fue referida recientemente al Departamento de Servicios Sociales del condado de Wake (DSS) para evaluar elegibilidad para subsidio de cuidado infantil, y a la oficina de Partnership for Children of Wake County para recursos adicionales de desarrollo infantil. CG también está considerando inscribir a Diego, el hermano menor, en Early Head Start una vez cumpla 1 año.

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

Eval realizada completamente en esp por la evaluadora bilingüe, con muestras adicionales en ing para comparar desempeño entre idiomas. No se requirió interprete. Pt participó con afecto positivo durante la mayoría de la sesión; requirió descansos cortos y mod cues para mantenerse en tarea. CG presente durante toda la sesión y proveyó info de hx. Instrumentos administrados:

- Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA) — subpruebas de Morfosintaxis y Fonología
- Preschool Language Scales-5 versión en español (PLS-5 Español) — Comprensión Auditiva y Comunicación Expresiva
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 adaptado al español (GFTA-3) — Sonidos en Palabras
- Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo (juego estructurado, approx 15 minutos)
- Observación informal de pragmática y juego simbólico

RESULTADOS — LENGUAJE RECEPTIVO Y EXPRESIVO

Prueba / Subprueba — Puntaje estándar — Percentil — Intervalo de confianza (95%)
PLS-5 Español, Comprensión Auditiva — 79 — 8 — 71–87
PLS-5 Español, Comunicación Expresiva — 74 — 4 — 66–82
BESA, Morfosintaxis — 72 — 3 — 65–79
BESA, Fonología — 68 — 2 — 61–75

Edad equivalente para Comunicación Expresiva: 2;6–3;0, por debajo de la edad cronológica de pt (4;2). En la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, pt produjo principalmente enunciados de 1-2 palabras, con MLU approx 1.8 morfemas. Ejemplos de producción: "quiero agua", "no mamá", "perro ahí". Omite consistentemente artículos y conjugaciones verbales más allá del presente simple. En ing, pt produjo únicamente palabras aisladas ("ball", "no", "mommy"), consistente con menor exposición relativa a ese idioma.

Comprensión: pt siguió instrucciones de 1 paso de forma consistente (8/10), de 2 pasos con mod cues (3 of 5), y tuvo dificultad marcada con conceptos espaciales (dentro/fuera, debajo/arriba) y cuantificadores (todos, ninguno). Identificación de vocabulario básico (partes del cuerpo, animales, colores) fue approx 70% precisa sin apoyo visual adicional.

RESULTADOS — HABLA / FONOLOGÍA

Prueba — Puntaje estándar — Percentil — Intervalo de confianza
GFTA-3 (adaptado al español), Sonidos en Palabras — 65 — 1 — 58–72

Inteligibilidad estimada por la evaluadora: approx 40% para oyentes no familiarizados, approx 75% para CG. Lista de palabras meta administrada incluyó: "casa", "pescado", "dos", "flor", "perro", y "sol", dirigidas a los fonemas /s/, grupos consonánticos con /r/, y consonantes finales en posición de coda.

Patrones de error identificados:
- Omisión de consonante final [EW] — p.ej., "do" por "dos", "flo" por "flor"
- Sustitución de /r/ por [w] en posición inicial y medial — p.ej., "pewo" por "perro"
- Simplificación de grupos consonánticos — "poblema" por "problema"
- Frontalización de /k/ a /t/ en algunas producciones — "tasa" por "casa"

Nota sobre un ítem administrado: al mostrarle la lámina correspondiente a la palabra meta "sol" (fonema /s/ en posición inicial, una de las palabras del protocolo de articulación), pt miró hacia la puerta del consultorio donde en ese momento entraba su hermana a buscarlo y dijo "Sol" señalando hacia ella, en vez de producir la palabra objetivo de la lámina. La evaluadora repitió la instrucción aclarando "dime qué ves en la foto" y redirigió la atención de pt a la lámina; en el segundo intento, pt produjo "to" (omisión de consonante inicial y final, [EW]), lo cual se registró como el intento válido para fines de puntuación. Se documenta esta observación porque la coincidencia entre la palabra meta administrada y el nombre de la hermana de pt generó confusión momentánea durante el ítem.

En la comparación entre esp e ing, los patrones de error fonológico fueron consistentes en ambos idiomas (omisión final, simplificación de grupos consonánticos), lo cual sugiere un trastorno fonológico de base más que una dificultad limitada a la adquisición de un idioma específico.

PRAGMÁTICA Y JUEGO

Pt inició interacción social apropiadamente (contacto visual, sonrisas, señalar protodeclarativo) pero dependió fuertemente de gestos para compensar lenguaje expresivo limitado. Juego simbólico presente pero con secuencias cortas (2-3 pasos); por ejemplo, pt alimentó a un muñeco y luego lo "durmió," sin elaborar más la secuencia sin mod cues de la evaluadora. Turnos conversacionales presentes pero breves; pt abandonó la tarea o cambió de tema cuando no logró ser entendido, mostrando signos leves de frustración comunicativa (vocalizaciones de queja, empujar el material lejos).

IMPRESIONES DIAGNÓSTICAS

Con base en los hallazgos de esta eval, pt presenta:

1. Trastorno mixto receptivo-expresivo del lenguaje, evidente en ambos idiomas, con mayor afectación en el dominio expresivo (ICD-10 F80.2).
2. Trastorno fonológico (ICD-10 F80.0), caracterizado por omisión de consonantes finales, simplificación de grupos consonánticos, y sustitución de /r/ por [w], afectando la inteligibilidad de forma significativa.

Los hallazgos son consistentes a través de esp e ing, por lo que no se atribuyen a adquisición bilingüe típica ni a diferencia dialectal. Pt califica para servicios continuados de intervención temprana bajo Parte C según criterios de elegibilidad de CDSA de NC. Códigos de servicio facturados: CPT 92523 (eval de lenguaje y habla) y CPT 92522 (eval de trastorno de sonidos del habla).

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Iniciar terapia de habla-lenguaje individual 2x/semana, sesiones de approx 45 minutos, en esp con generalización dirigida a ing, provista por SLP bilingüe.
2. Incorporar el enfoque Cycles para el trastorno fonológico, dado el patrón de errores identificado (omisión final, simplificación de grupos).
3. Capacitación de CG mediante el modelo Hanen ("It Takes Two to Talk") para fomentar estrategias de estimulación de lenguaje en el hogar, incluyendo a la tía Carmen Cruz como cuidadora principal 3 días/semana.
4. Considerar el enfoque PROMPT si el progreso con cueing tradicional es limitado tras 8-10 semanas de tx.
5. Añadir como Objetivo 3 del IFSP: "Pt producirá consonantes finales en palabras funcionales con min cues en 8/10 oportunidades durante actividades estructuradas, según reporte de CG y datos de sesión."
6. Mantener coordinación con Little Learners Program y con Marisol Reyes (CDSA) para alinear objetivos de IFSP entre proveedores.
7. Referido a terapia ocupacional para evaluar coordinación motora oral/alimentación; considerar co-tx con Kevin Álvarez, OT, si está disponible dentro del mismo programa.
8. Continuar seguimiento audiológico anual dado hx de otitis media recurrente; próxima cita sugerida con Dr. Steven Park.
9. Informar a Srta. Jennifer Soto y Srta. Patricia Gómez en Little Learners Daycare sobre estrategias simples de apoyo en el aula (esperar, modelar, expandir enunciados).
10. Revisión de progreso recomendada en 6 meses; próxima revisión del IFSP programada para el martes 4 de junio de 2026. Reunión de coordinación de servicios tentativa el 15/01/2026.

Esta evaluadora está disponible para discutir estos hallazgos con el equipo del IFSP y con la familia. Cualquier pregunta puede dirigirse a Laura Jiménez, Carolina Pediatric Speech Therapy, PLLC, al (919) 555-0148 o al correo intake@carolinapedsspeech.com.

Firma: Laura Jiménez, MS, CCC-SLP
Fecha: 10 de septiembre de 2025

TRIANGLE PEDIATRIC SPEECH & LANGUAGE CENTER
410 Evergreen Grove Lane, Cary, NC 27511
Phone: (919) 555-0142
Email: intake@trianglepeds-slp.com

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Child's Name: Mateo Flores
Date of Birth: April 9, 2023
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 3;2
Evaluation Dates: June 10, 2026 and June 17, 2026
Report Date: June 24, 2026
Record/Case ID: LD-30417
Medicaid ID: 982445173C
Referring Physician: Dr. Hannah Kim, Piedmont Pediatric Associates
Interpreter (Spanish): Marisol Vega
Service Coordinator: Tasha Brown, Piedmont Regional CDSA
Evaluator: Carmen Ibarra, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual-Certified

Parent/Guardian Contact Information:
Name	Relationship	Phone	Email
Lucía Flores	Mother	(919) 555-8820	lflores82@carolinamail.net
Daniel Flores	Father	(919) 555-8821	dflores.work@cbalabs.com

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a bilingual speech-language evaluation by Dr. Kim and by the service coordinator at Piedmont Regional CDSA, Tasha Brown, after his mother, Lucía Flores, and his classroom teacher, Jennifer Lopez, raised concerns about his limited expressive vocabulary and unclear speech in both Spanish and English. Mateo attends The Curious Caterpillar Early Learning Center four days a week, where Ms. Lopez reports that he frequently points or pulls adults by the hand rather than using words, and that his classmates, Emma, Noah, and Isabella, often speak for him during play. This evaluation was conducted to establish eligibility for ongoing speech-language intervention and to update Mateo's Individualized Family Service Plan ahead of the review scheduled for July 15, 2026.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía Flores and Daniel Flores, and his older sister, Sol Flores, in Morrisville, Wake County, North Carolina. The family also receives regular help from a babysitter, Hope Jenkins, who picks Mateo up from The Curious Caterpillar Early Learning Center on Fridays, and from his maternal grandmother, who visits most weekends. The family's dog, Rocky, is frequently mentioned by Mrs. Flores as a motivator for Mateo's attempts at communication; during the home interview, Mateo pointed at the back door and said "Rocky go," which his mother reported is one of his few consistent two-word combinations.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at Pinecrest Women's Hospital at 37 weeks gestation following an uncomplicated pregnancy. Birth weight was 6 lbs 4 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. He was discharged home with his mother after a two-day stay. Medical history is notable for recurrent otitis media between 8 months and 18 months of age, treated with antibiotics, with no history of tympanostomy tubes. A hearing screening completed at March 3, 2026 at Pinecrest Women's Hospital was within normal limits bilaterally. There is no history of seizures, head injury, or significant developmental regression. Mateo's pediatrician, Dr. Kim, noted gross and fine motor milestones within normal limits, with independent walking achieved at 13 months.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

The home language environment is bilingual. Lucía Flores and Daniel Flores report speaking primarily Spanish with Mateo at home, while his sister, Sol, and the babysitter, Hope Jenkins, often use English with him. Mrs. Flores works part-time at Carolina BioAssay Labs, and Mr. Flores works full-time in construction. Mateo's cousins, Camila and Marco, visit frequently from Durham and are reported to understand him better than unfamiliar listeners do, likely due to familiarity with his speech patterns. Mrs. Flores reports that Sol began combining words by 18 months and was fully intelligible to strangers by age three, which has heightened the family's concern about Mateo's slower trajectory. No other family members have a history of speech, language, or learning disorders, though Mr. Flores reports he himself was a "late talker."

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Across both evaluation sessions, Mateo was cooperative and socially engaged, making consistent eye contact and initiating joint attention with toys. He transitioned between tasks with mod cues and required min cues for turn-taking during structured play. He demonstrated a preference for gesture and vocalization over verbal language when frustrated, for example reaching toward a container and vocalizing "[EH]" rather than requesting "open" verbally. Attention and play skills, including symbolic play with a toy kitchen set, were age-appropriate.

ASSESSMENT RESULTS

The following standardized and informal measures were administered across both sessions, with items presented in both English and Spanish as appropriate, and with Marisol Vega providing interpretation support for the parent interview portions.

Test/Subtest	Standard Score	Percentile Rank	Age Equivalent	Classification
PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension	73	4th	2;6	Below Average
PLS-5 Expressive Communication	68	2nd	2;3	Below Average
PLS-5 Total Language Score	70	3rd	2;4–2;6	Below Average
GFTA-3 Standard Score	79	8th	--	Below Average
BESA Semantics-Spanish	85	16th	--	Average
BESA Semantics-English	72	3rd	--	Below Average

The 95% confidence interval for the PLS-5 Total Language Score was 65-75. On the GFTA-3, Mateo produced /k/ correctly in 8/10 trials and the Spanish tap /ɾ/ correctly in 3 of 5 trials, substituting [d] in the remaining attempts. For the target word "copa," Mateo produced "tapa," reflecting a fronting pattern consistent with a phonological process rather than a structural or motor-based disorder. Connected speech sampling, coded using SALT conventions, included several word-level errors marked [EW]. Single-word intelligibility to familiar listeners was estimated at 80%, dropping to approximately 55% for unfamiliar listeners, consistent with parent and teacher report.

Expressively, Mateo's spontaneous utterances were largely single-word with occasional two-word combinations ("Rocky go," "más agua"). He demonstrated an estimated expressive vocabulary of approximately 45 words across both languages, below the expected range for his chronological age. Receptively, he followed one-step directions reliably and some two-step directions with mod cues.

A trial of visual supports was introduced during the second session; Mateo readily used a three-picture PECS array to request a preferred toy, suggesting he may benefit from augmentative strategies as a bridge to spoken language rather than as a long-term replacement.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized assessment, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder in the context of bilingual language exposure, with an associated phonological disorder. These findings are consistent with ICD-10 codes F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) and F80.0 (phonological disorder). His difficulties are present and comparable across both Spanish and English, which, combined with his bilingual home environment and typical exposure history, supports a true language disorder rather than a difference attributable to second-language acquisition or dialectal variation. Mateo's strong social engagement, play skills, and responsiveness to visual and gestural supports are favorable prognostic indicators.

Today's evaluation session was billed under CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression).

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo qualifies for ongoing speech-language intervention and should continue to receive services under his updated IFSP, with treatment addressing IFSP Outcome 2 (functional communication across settings).
2. Individual speech-language therapy sessions, billed under CPT 92507, are recommended at the frequency outlined below.
3. Treatment should incorporate PROMPT for motor-speech planning given Mateo's inconsistent sound substitutions, and the Cycles approach to target phonological patterns in a developmentally sequenced manner.
4. Given Mateo's apraxia-like inconsistency on repeated productions, a trial of the Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol is recommended to build approximations toward functional words.
5. Mateo's family would benefit from parent coaching through a Hanen program, specifically It Takes Two to Talk, to support language facilitation strategies across both Spanish and English during daily routines.
6. PECS should be introduced as a supplemental communication support during high-frustration moments, with the explicit goal of fading as spoken language increases.
7. Continued collaboration with The Curious Caterpillar Early Learning Center staff, including Ms. Lopez, is recommended to generalize strategies to the classroom setting.
8. A re-evaluation is recommended in six months to monitor progress and adjust the treatment plan.

Recommended Service Schedule:

Parent Coaching (Hanen/It Takes Two to Talk)	1x/month	45 minutes	92507	Carmen Ibarra, CCC-SLP
IFSP Team Review	Quarterly	60 minutes	N/A	Tasha Brown, Piedmont Regional CDSA

This evaluation was conducted in collaboration with Piedmont Regional CDSA and reflects Mateo's current speech and language status as of the dates of testing. Please contact Triangle Pediatric Speech & Language Center at (919) 555-0142 with any questions regarding this report or the recommendations above. A follow-up appointment has been scheduled for July 15, 2026 at 1:30 PM to coincide with the IFSP review meeting.

speech-language evaluation report

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Hernández Rodríguez
Preferred Name: Mateo
Date of Birth: April 2, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;6
Dates of Evaluation: October 6, 2026 and October 8, 2026
Evaluator: Mariana Delgado López, M.S., CCC-SLP
Employer: Carolina Bilingual Speech and Language Services, PLLC
Referral Source: Mr. Tom, service coordinator, la Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios para Familias de Siler City (la Agencia)
Responsible CDSA: el Centro de Servicios para el Desarrollo Infantil del Piedmont Central (el CDSA)
Case Number: CDSA-44871-NC
Medicaid ID: 9284771053M
Home Address: 1409 Chatham Church Road, Siler City, Chatham County, NC 27344
Home Phone: 919-555-0173
Mother's Cell: (919) 555-2284
Father's Cell: 919.555.6627
Maternal Grandmother's Phone (Guanajuato): +52 1 473 555 0192
Clinic Email: intake@carolinabilingualslp.com

razón de la referencia / reason for referral

mateo was referred by Mr. Tom at la Agencia after his mother Lucía Hernández Pérez told the service coordinator that Mateo is hard to understand in both languages and that his teacher at Pequeños Pasos Early Learning Center had also raised concerns so the family was connected to el CDSA for a full speech and language evaluation and this report summarizes that evaluation which was completed over two sessions on October 6, 2026 and October 8, 2026 at the family's home and at the office of Carolina Bilingual Speech and Language Services, PLLC in Siler City.

the mother Lucía Hernández Pérez reported during intake que Mateo no se le entiende bien ni en español ni en inglés and said quote he talks a lot pero la gente no le entiende nada unquote and the father Jorge Hernández Morales agreed and said through the evaluator who conducted the interview bilingually that at home they mostly speak spanish but Mateo hears a lot of english too from his older sister Luz Hernández who is in second grade and corrects him constantly.

historia del nacimiento y médica / birth and medical history

Mateo was born on April 2, 2022 at Chatham Regional Medical Center in Siler City at 39 weeks gestation via vaginal delivery with no complications reported his birth weight was 7 lbs 2 oz and his apgar scores were 8 and 9 mother Lucía Hernández Pérez stated she had regular prenatal care through the health department and denied any substance use during pregnancy there was no nicu stay and the family reports normal newborn hearing screen though the paper copy was lost in a move.

medical history is reportedly unremarkable for Mateo he has had recurrent ear infections per mother about 6 episodes between 18 months and 3;0 of age treated with antibiotics he has not had tubes placed his pediatrician Dr. Patel at Siler City Pediatrics referred the family for an audiology evaluation in June 2026 and that report noted mild fluctuating conductive loss bilaterally consistent with the ear infection history a repeat screening done September 2026 showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally no current ear infection no current ear tube and family denies any seizures head injuries or hospitalizations beyond birth Mateo takes no daily medications currently his diagnosis code on the referral paperwork from el CDSA lists R47.9 speech disturbance unspecified and H90.6 mixed conductive and sensorineural hearing loss bilateral as history.

historia familiar y del lenguaje / family and language history

Mateo lives with his mother Lucía Hernández Pérez, his father Jorge Hernández Morales, his older sister Luz Hernández who is 7, and his younger brother Will Hernández who is 2 the family also receives regular help from the maternal grandmother doña Lupe who lives nearby and watches the younger kids several days a week while the parents work mother Lucía Hernández Pérez currently works at un restaurante mexicano llamado La Hacienda in Siler City usually mid-day shifts and before that she worked for about two years at the poultry plant trabajaba en la planta de pollo Case Farms on the night shift which the family says made it hard for her to be home at bedtime back then father Jorge Hernández Morales trabaja en una compañía de construcción called Triangle Framing & Construction he is often gone before the kids wake up and gets home late depending on the job site an aunt on the mother's side tía Rosa Pérez also helps with childcare on weekends she works for a cleaning company una compañía de limpieza called Sparkle Clean Commercial Services and sometimes brings Mateo along to small jobs on saturdays an uncle trabaja en una granja a few counties over, a produce farm, Rolling Hills Farm, and is only around on sundays.

language exposure at home is primarily spanish mother and father both report spanish as their first and strongest language father has limited english and mother is functionally bilingual having worked in english-speaking settings for years the children speak spanish with the parents and grandmother and a mix of spanish and english with each other sister Luz Hernández is described as very verbal in both languages and the family reports she often translates for Mateo and finishes his sentences for him which the evaluator noted may be masking some of his own language production at home mother estimates the home language mix is about 70 percent spanish and 30 percent english with english increasing since Mateo started at Pequeños Pasos Early Learning Center in January 2025.

there is a family dog named Rocky who mother says Mateo talks to constantly in both languages and the parents feel this is actually one of the few contexts where he talks the most freely no other developmental concerns were reported motor milestones were within normal limits per parent report walked at 13 months no feeding concerns currently though mother noted some early feeding difficulty as an infant that resolved by 6 months.

reportes escolares / school and daycare reports

Mateo attends Pequeños Pasos Early Learning Center four days a week his lead teacher la maestra Carmen and the assistant teacher Miss Ana were both consulted by phone for this evaluation with parental consent la maestra Carmen reported that Mateo plays well with peers including his friend Diego but gets frustrated when adults or other children do not understand him right away and sometimes gives up and points instead Miss Ana noted he follows simple directions in english reasonably well but his spontaneous speech in the classroom is mostly single words or short phrases and hard to understand even in context both teachers independently estimated his intelligibility to unfamiliar listeners at around 40 to 50 percent.

procedimientos de evaluación / assessment procedures

the following measures were administered in both english and spanish as appropriate with results interpreted considering his bilingual status and the family's primary language being spanish testing was conducted across two sessions to reduce fatigue, caregiver report measures were also gathered.

- Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) Spanish
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA)
- Oral mechanism examination
- Language sample analysis
- Parent and teacher interview
- Clinical observation of play-based interaction

resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas / standardized test results

Test / Subtest | Raw Score | Standard Score | Percentile Rank | Age Equivalent
PLS-5 Spanish Auditory Comprehension | -- | 79 | 8th | 3;1
PLS-5 Spanish Expressive Communication | -- | 73 | 4th | 2;9
PLS-5 Spanish Total Language Score | -- | 74 | 4th | 2;10
BESA Morphosyntax Index Spanish | -- | 76 | 5th | --
BESA Morphosyntax Index English | -- | 81 | 10th | --
BESA Semantics Subtest Spanish | -- | 78 | 7th | --
BESA Semantics Subtest English | -- | 85 | 16th | --
GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words | 37 | 68 | 2nd | 2;6-3;0

standard scores below 85 are considered below average confidence intervals for the PLS-5 spanish total language score fall within 69-79 at the 90 percent confidence level the BESA results show relatively stronger performance in english than spanish which per bilingual assessment guidelines is not unusual given increasing english exposure at daycare but the pattern of weaker scores across both languages especially spanish which is the dominant home language is consistent with a primary language impairment rather than typical bilingual development or second language acquisition alone.

examen oral-motor / oral mechanism exam

structures and function of the lips tongue hard and soft palate and jaw were within normal limits for speech no structural abnormalities noted no signs of dysarthria or apraxia characteristics observed diadochokinetic rate was age appropriate oral mechanism exam did not reveal a structural basis for the speech sound errors noted below.

habla y fonología / speech and phonology

on the GFTA-3 Mateo produced the following error patterns final consonant deletion occurred in about 6 of 10 opportunities for example he said quote ca unquote for cat and quote do unquote for dog he also showed fronting of velars producing /t/ for /k/ saying quote tasa unquote for casa and gliding of liquids producing [w] for /ɾ/ in spanish for example saying quote peho unquote for perro he was stimulable to /k/ in isolation with mod cues but not consistently at the word level across both languages these patterns were similar whether he was speaking spanish or english suggesting a shared underlying phonological system affected rather than two separate language-specific disorders intelligibility in connected speech to an unfamiliar listener this evaluator estimated at approximately 40 percent in context and lower out of context which is consistent with parent and teacher report.

lenguaje expresivo y receptivo / expressive and receptive language

during the language sample Mateo used mostly one to two word utterances with some three word combinations he code-switched frequently within the same utterance for example he said quote mi perro run unquote mixing spanish and english in a single phrase which is a normal feature of bilingual development and was not counted against him but his overall mean length of utterance was 1.8 morphemes which is below expectations for his age in either language he used very few grammatical markers in spanish for example frequently omitting plural -s and gender agreement and in english he omitted most verb tense markers for example saying quote he run unquote instead of he is running receptively he followed one-step directions reliably in both languages but struggled with two-step directions that included a spatial or temporal concept for example quote put the ball under the table and then close the door unquote he required repetition or simplification on 7 of 10 two-step trials.

pragmática y juego / pragmatics and play

Mateo initiated interaction readily with this evaluator and with his sister Luz Hernández during the home visit he used eye contact and gesture appropriately and showed good joint attention during shared play he became visibly frustrated twice during testing when he could not make himself understood and resorted to pulling the evaluator's sleeve and pointing rather than repeating or rephrasing his play was age appropriate he engaged in pretend play with toy animals and narrated simple actions though mostly nonverbally.

resumen de impresiones / summary of impressions

based on standardized testing parent and teacher report and clinical observation Mateo presents with a speech sound disorder and a language disorder affecting both spanish and english that is a true bilingual child with communication delays affecting both of his languages rather than a child who is simply learning two languages typically his scores fall well below average in both receptive and expressive language in spanish his dominant home language and his speech intelligibility is significantly reduced due to multiple phonological process errors present across both languages his hearing history of recurrent otitis media likely contributed to early speech and language development though his hearing is currently within normal limits per the most recent screening family and teacher support for his communication including his sister's tendency to speak for him and his enjoyment of talking to the family dog Rocky are both protective factors and areas to build on in intervention.

diagnostic impression: R47.9 speech disturbance, unspecified and F80.9 developmental disorder of speech and language, unspecified, both languages affected.

recomendaciones / recommendations

1. Mateo qualifies for ongoing speech-language intervention through el CDSA under his current ifsp recommend individual therapy twice weekly for 30 minutes per session targeting both spanish and english given his dual language exposure.
2. target final consonant deletion velar fronting and liquid gliding using a cycles approach Cycles across both languages concurrently rather than treating spanish and english as separate caseloads.
3. incorporate Hanen strategies for the family to use at home including Lucía Hernández Pérez Jorge Hernández Morales and grandmother doña Lupe since she provides significant daytime care emphasizing expansion and modeling rather than correction.
4. coordinate with Pequeños Pasos Early Learning Center staff la maestra Carmen and Miss Ana to support carryover of targets in the classroom setting and reduce reliance on peer interpretation from classmates like Diego.
5. gently discourage sister Luz Hernández from speaking for Mateo and instead coach her in simple ways to prompt him to try saying things himself first.
6. recommend a repeat audiological evaluation in 6 months given his history of recurrent otitis media to confirm hearing remains within normal limits.
7. share this report with pediatrician Dr. Patel at Siler City Pediatrics and with service coordinator Mr. Tom at la Agencia for ifsp planning purposes.
8. reassess in approximately 6 months to monitor progress in both languages and adjust goals as needed.

this evaluation and its recommendations were discussed with the family in spanish at the conclusion of the second session on October 8, 2026 mother Lucía Hernández Pérez verbalized understanding and agreement with the recommendations and signed consent for the results to be shared with el CDSA and la Agencia for ifsp purposes father Jorge Hernández Morales was not present for the results meeting due to his work schedule at Triangle Framing & Construction but was briefed by phone the same evening at approximately 6:45 pm.

please contact this evaluator with any questions at mdelgado@carolinabilingualslp.com or at the clinic number (919) 555-0148.

respectfully submitted,

Mariana Delgado López, M.S., CCC-SLP
bilingual speech-language pathologist
Carolina Bilingual Speech and Language Services, PLLC

**2. Family Concerns, Priorities, and Resources**

As stated by Lucía Rodríguez Martínez (spoken in Spanish, translated and recorded by Mariana Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP with Jennifer Álvarez present):

"My biggest worry is that Mateo doesn't talk like other kids his age. He points and he grunts, but he only has maybe ten words, and half of those only his sister Sol understands. Sol talked so much by this age, and she helps him a lot, but I don't want him to depend on her to speak for him forever. My mother, Rosario, watches him in the mornings and she worries too. We want him ready for preschool next year, and we want him to be able to tell us when something hurts, or when he's scared."

Carlos Hernández Pérez added, through Jennifer Álvarez interpreting during an evening call: "I work nights, so I don't see the therapy sessions much, but my wife tells me everything. I want to understand the home exercises so I can do them with him on weekends."

Family priorities for this review period:
1. Increase Mateo's expressive vocabulary and intelligibility so unfamiliar listeners can understand him.
2. Support the transition to a preschool classroom at Sunshine Steps Early Learning Center in fall 2027.
3. Coach both parents and Rosario Cruz Martínez in consistent strategies across home, school, and therapy settings.
4. Continue Medicaid coverage and WIC nutrition support without interruption.

**3. Daily Routines**

Weekday mornings, Mateo wakes around 6:30 AM and eats breakfast with Sol and Rosario Cruz Martínez before Lucía Rodríguez Martínez leaves for work. Rosario walks him to Sunshine Steps Early Learning Center by 8:15 AM, where his teacher, Keisha Lopez, reports he engages well with peers during free play but becomes frustrated and bites when he cannot make a request understood. Afternoons include a nap, snack, and outdoor play; Lucía Rodríguez Martínez picks him up around 4:00 PM. Evenings are family dinner together, bath, and a bedtime story that Sol "reads" to him from memory. Carlos Hernández Pérez is present for bedtime most nights before his shift.

**4. Present Levels of Development (Speech-Language)**

Evaluator: Mariana Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP

Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4th Edition	Receptive Communication	Scaled Score 6	9th percentile
Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5	Receptive Vocabulary	Standard Score 71	3rd percentile

Mateo presents with expressive language and speech sound production significantly below age expectations in both Spanish and English, with relative strength in nonverbal problem-solving per Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4th Edition Cognitive domain (Scaled Score 9, 37th percentile). His phonetic inventory is limited to bilabials and a few alveolars; he substitutes [d] for /t/ and omits final consonants (e.g., "ba" for "bath"). During the picture-naming task, Mateo produced the target word "sol" (Spanish for "sun") with moderate cues, approximating it as [so]; this was scored as an attempt, not a word match, and is unrelated to any person's name within the family. He imitated single words with min-mod cues roughly 4 of 10 trials and showed emerging two-word combinations in Spanish only ("más agua"). Suspected diagnosis under review: F80.2 (Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder). Service billed under CPT 92523.

**5. Other Agencies Involved**

The family receives nutrition support through Catawba County WIC and has an open case with Catawba County Department of Social Services for a childcare subsidy. Smart Start of Catawba County funds a portion of Mateo's tuition at Sunshine Steps Early Learning Center. Jennifer Álvarez coordinates quarterly check-ins across these agencies and Foothills CDSA.

**6. Outcomes and Strategies**

Outcome 1: Mateo will use 50 or more single words functionally across home and daycare settings within six months, as reported by Lucía Rodríguez Martínez and Keisha Lopez.
Strategies: Weekly direct therapy using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" coaching principles with Lucía Rodríguez Martínez and Rosario Cruz Martínez present; modeling expansion and self-talk during daily routines; home log of new words shared with Keisha Lopez weekly.

Outcome 2: Mateo will produce final consonants in single words with no more than moderate cues in 8 of 10 opportunities.
Strategies: PROMPT-based tactile-kinesthetic cueing during 1:1 sessions; home practice sheet reviewed with Carlos Hernández Pérez on weekends; introduce Cycles phonological approach targeting final consonant deletion as the first pattern.

Outcome 3: Mateo will use a backup visual system to reduce frustration-related biting at daycare within three months.
Strategies: Introduce core-vocabulary picture cards modeled on PECS Phase 1 for requesting; Keisha Lopez trained to prompt card use during free play; data collected daily by Sunshine Steps Early Learning Center staff and reviewed biweekly by Mariana Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP.

Outcome 4: Mateo will increase vowel accuracy and syllable shape variety to support later multisyllabic word attempts.
Strategies: Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol hierarchy for motor-planning practice, beginning with reduplicated syllables before moving to true words; coordinate with Brian Walsh, OTR/L regarding oral-motor tone findings noted during his evaluation.

The team, including Jennifer Álvarez, Mariana Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP, Dana Kim, PT, Brian Walsh, OTR/L, and both parents, agreed the outcomes above remain appropriate with the strategy additions noted. También visitan el programa de cuentos bilingües de la Biblioteca Pública del Condado de Durham los sábados, y han recibido apoyo de ropa y pañales del El Puente Comunitario, una organización sin fines de lucro local.

Rutinas diarias: Por las mañanas, Rosa lleva a Mateo al Early Head Start a las 7:30 a.m.; su niñera, Yesenia Morales Pineda, lo recoge a las 4:00 p.m. los días que Rosa trabaja hasta tarde en Empacadora Avícola del Triángulo. En casa, Mateo juega con su perrita, Luna, y con sus primos, Diego y Valeria, quienes visitan los fines de semana. A la hora del baño, a las 7:00 p.m., Jorge canta canciones con Mateo para fomentar la imitación verbal.

Resultados del IFSP y estrategias:

Resultado 1 (Comunicación funcional): En la evaluación de seguimiento con el PLS-5, Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 76 en Comunicación Expresiva (percentil 5, intervalo de confianza 70-82) y una puntuación estándar de 88 en Comprensión Auditiva (percentil 21). Su edad equivalente en lenguaje expresivo es de 18 meses. Produce de forma consistente "mamá", "más" y "no", y recientemente intentó la palabra objetivo "agua" como [ˈa.wa]. Estrategia: la familia usará el enfoque Hanen en casa, siguiendo el liderazgo de Mateo durante el juego, y la terapeuta continuará con claves de mod cues para combinaciones de dos palabras.

Resultado 2 (Articulación e inteligibilidad): Mateo omite consonantes finales y simplifica grupos consonánticos; sustituye /s/ por [t] en posición inicial, como en su producción de "sapo" dicha como [ˈta.po]. Se recomienda el enfoque PROMPT para apoyar la colocación articulatoria, con sesiones de terapia individual facturadas bajo el código 92523. En 8 de 10 ensayos durante la sesión del 2 de septiembre de 2025, Mateo imitó correctamente la vocal /a/ en palabras monosílabas con claves mínimas.

Resultado 3 (Interacción social con pares): En el Early Head Start, Mateo inició contacto visual y gestos de señalar compartida con Liam en 3 de 5 observaciones estructuradas. Se recomienda continuar el modelado de lenguaje paralelo durante el juego grupal.

Próximos pasos y fechas de servicio: La próxima sesión de terapia de habla y lenguaje está programada para el 20 de octubre de 2025 a las 10:00 a.m. en el hogar de la familia. La próxima revisión formal del IFSP está programada para el 15 de abril de 2026. La coordinadora de servicios, Ana Patricia Gómez Villalobos, realizará una visita de seguimiento el 5 de noviembre de 2025 para coordinar la transición de Mateo hacia servicios preescolares antes de su tercer cumpleaños. La familia fue informada de que puede llamar a la línea del CDSA de la Región del Triángulo al 919-555-0180 si surgen preguntas antes de la próxima visita.

Firmado: Leticia Carmona Ríos, SLP bilingüe, Terapias Bilingües del Triángulo, 6 de octubre de 2025.

text:
Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Center
Speech-Language Evaluation Report

Client: Mateo de la Cruz ("Teo")
DOB: November 14, 2022 CA: 3;10
Eval date: September 9, 2026
Medicaid #: NC8847216K
Record #: LD-33920
Referral source: Dr. Htun, pediatrician
Clinician: Jennifer Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Interpreter: Sofia Reyes (Spanish, consecutive)
Setting: clinic, w/ mom present

BACKGROUND / REFERRAL

Teo was referred by Dr. Htun 2° parent concern re: limited intelligible speech and few 2-wd combos. Pt lives w/ mother Lucía de la Cruz, father Carlos Flores-Martínez, and older sister Camila de la Cruz (age 7) at 412 Willowbrook Ln, Greensboro, NC 27406. Pt attends Little Sprouts Daycare M-F, 8am-5pm, in Ms. Patterson's rm. CG report pt prefers to play w/ classmate Ethan but gets frustrated when not understood; teacher notes similar.

Mom Lucía de la Cruz works 2 jobs: housekeeping at the Hampton Inn on Battleground Ave days, and overnight shifts at UPS several nights/wk. Dad Carlos Flores-Martínez works full time in landscaping. Family reports limited time for home practice given both parents' schedules; aunt Marta Gómez often watches pt and Camila de la Cruz in the evenings. Case referred by Denise Walker, EI service coordinator w/ Triangle CDSA, who completed intake July 22, 2026 and recommended this eval for IFSP outcome 2.

BIRTH & MEDICAL HISTORY

Per mom's report, pregnancy unremarkable, no substance use. Delivery at Piedmont Regional Hospital via vaginal delivery at 39 weeks gestation. Birth wt 7 lbs 2 oz, Apgar scores 8/9. No NICU stay. Hx of recurrent OM, 4 episodes b/w 12-24 months, tx'd w/ amoxicillin each time; ENT placed bilateral PE tubes February 5, 2026 at Piedmont Regional Hospital, per op note from Dr. Castellanos. Hearing screen post-tube placement WNL per audiology report, February 19, 2026. No hx of seizure, head injury, or hospitalization beyond above. No current meds. Vision screening WNL. No fam hx of speech/lang delay reported by mom; dad reports he himself was a "late talker" per his own mother.

FAMILY & LANGUAGE HISTORY

Home lang is Spanish-dominant; mom and dad both report speaking approx 80% Spanish / 20% English w/ pt at home. Camila de la Cruz is more English-dominant since starting school and often code-switches w/ pt, modeling both langs. Pt's maternal grandmother Rosa Hernández lives in Caserío El Carmen, Chalatenango, El Salvador, and video calls 2-3x/wk; pt reportedly "shuts down" during these calls per mom, possibly d/t limited expressive output in either lang. Family dog, Max, is a frequent play partner per mom; pt calls him "Mah" (prod. for Max).

Family contact numbers on file: home (336) 555-0148, mom's cell 336.555.0199, dad's cell (336) 555-0172, and grandmother's number in El Salvador +503 7123-4567. Family requests all appt reminders go to mom's cell only, 2° dad's shift schedule.

DEVELOPMENTAL HISTORY

Gross/fine motor milestones per mom report WNL; walked indep at 13 months. First words approx 18 months ("mamá," "agua"), but vocab growth slow since; pt currently uses approx 25-30 words/word approximations across both langs per parent report on checklist completed August 28, 2026. Few 2-wd combos noted ("más agua," "no no"). No regression reported. Pt uses gestures (pointing, pulling CG) to communicate wants; frequent tantrums when not understood, per both mom and Ms. Patterson.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Pt presented as a friendly, curious 3;10 y.o. male, easily separated from mom for structured tasks w/ Sofia Reyes interpreting prompts into Spanish as needed. Attention to task fair, required mod cues/redirection approx q3-5 min. Play skills age-appropriate; engaged in symbolic play w/ toy animals, used a few labels ("perro," "gato") spontaneously. Articulation judged significantly reduced in intelligibility (~30% intelligible to unfamiliar listener per CG report, confirmed in session). Oral mech exam WNL, no structural concerns noted; adequate labial/lingual ROM for speech.

TEST RESULTS

Standardized and informal measures administered in both Spanish and English w/ interpreter support; Spanish forms used as primary given home lang dominance.

| Measure | Date admin | Score | 95% CI | %ile |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Preschool Language Scales-5 Spanish Auditory Comprehension | September 9, 2026 | SS 68 | 62-74 | 2nd |
| PLS-5 Spanish Expressive Communication | September 9, 2026 | SS 62 | 57-67 | 1st |
| PLS-5 Spanish Total Lang Score | September 9, 2026 | SS 64 | 59-69 | 1st |
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Lang Scale (supplemental, EN) | September 9, 2026 | AE 18-20 months | -- | -- |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (EN screen) | September 10, 2026 | SS 71 | 65-77 | 3rd |
| Contextual Probes of Articulation-Phonology-Spanish | September 10, 2026 | raw 14/40 correct | -- | -- |

On the Spanish phonology probe, pt demonstrated phoneme collapses including /ɾ/ → [l] (e.g., pt said ""paɾo"" for target ""perro""), stopping of fricatives, and frequent final consonant deletion. English probe showed similar patterns: /k/ and /g/ fronted to [t]/[d] consistently, cluster reduction in all word positions. Pt imitated target word ""cup"" as ""tuh"" w/ mod cues. Pt's MLU in spontaneous Spanish sample (50 utterances, collected w/ mom in room) was 1.2 morphemes, below expected range for CA.

Oromotor/feeding screen unremarkable; no dysphagia concerns. Pragmatic skills age-appropriate for nonverbal communication (joint attention, turn-taking in play) but limited by expressive output.

IMPRESSIONS

Mateo de la Cruz presents w/ a Severe Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent w/ a primary language impairment rather than typical bilingual variation given deficits noted across both langs by informant report and direct testing. Pt also presents w/ a moderate-severe Speech Sound Disorder affecting both langs, w/ phonological process patterns (stopping, fronting, final consonant deletion, liquid simplification) beyond what would be expected for a typically developing bilingual child at this age. Hx of recurrent OM w/ PE tube placement may have contributed to early receptive lang delays, though current hearing is WNL per audiology. ICD-10: F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive lang disorder), F80.0 (phonological disorder). CPT codes for eval: 92523, 92522.

Family engagement is strong despite significant time constraints from parents' combined 3 jobs; recommend flexible scheduling and home program materials in Spanish to maximize carryover given limited CG availability for formal practice.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Individual speech-lang tx 2x/wk, 30 min sessions, targeting both Spanish and English phonology and expressive syntax; bilingual clinician or interpreter support required at all sessions.
2. Augmentative strategies (modeling expansions, parallel talk) to be coached w/ mom and aunt Marta Gómez given their primary caregiving roles; consider evening or wknd appt slots given dad's shift at UPS and mom's hours at Hampton Inn.
3. Referral to Triangle CDSA for IFSP update; recommend adding a speech-lang outcome (outcome 3) addressing functional communication across settings.
4. Continue audiology monitoring q6 months given OM hx; next screen recommended March 2027.
5. Provide family w/ bilingual home program handouts; coordinate w/ Little Sprouts Daycare and Ms. Patterson re: classroom strategies (visual supports, simplified directions, mod cues for requesting).
6. Re-eval in 6 months to monitor progress across both langs; consider Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" parent coaching model given CG time constraints, delivered in condensed format.
7. Follow-up call to confirm scheduling to be made to mom's cell 336.555.0199; written summary to be mailed to 412 Willowbrook Ln, Greensboro, NC 27406. Clinic contact: jalvarez@piedmontpeds-slp.com, front desk 336-555-0160.

Results and recommendations reviewed w/ mom and interpreter Sofia Reyes at conclusion of session; mom verbalized understanding and agreement w/ plan, voiced relief that services would be offered bilingually. Written summary to be sent to Dr. Htun's office and to Denise Walker at Triangle CDSA w/ signed consent on file.

Report completed by:
Jennifer Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Center
September 14, 2026

RAZÓN DE LA REUNIÓN / REASON FOR MEETING

Esta es la revisión anual del IFSP de Mateo, un niño de 3;6 que recibe servicios de terapia del lenguaje a través del Western Piedmont CDSA. La reunión se llevó a cabo en las oficinas del CDSA en Morganton con la participación de Rosa del Río, Esteban Flores-Jiménez, Denise Watkins y Marisol Ortega-Peña.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA / FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES

Rosa del Río shared: "Mateo quiere hablar pero le cuesta mucho que la gente lo entienda. En la casa decimos 'agua' y él dice algo como "awa". At daycare they say he gets frustrated y a veces muerde." She added, "I just want him to be able to tell us lo que necesita, you know? Point and grunt no es suficiente para él."

Esteban Flores-Jiménez agreed: "Queremos que hable los dos idiomas, español en casa and English for school later. Mi mamá, Dolores del Río, lo cuida mucho and she only speaks Spanish, so necesitamos que él pueda comunicarse con ella también."

La familia priorizó: (1) that Mateo use words instead of gestures to request items; (2) que mejore la claridad de su habla en ambos idiomas; (3) peer interaction at Honeycomb Hollow.

HISTORIA / BACKGROUND

Mateo nació el 14 de marzo de 2023 en Frye Regional Medical Center, gestational age 38 weeks, birth weight 3,200 grams, Apgar scores of 8 and 9. La familia de Rosa del Río es originaria de San Miguel Ixtahuacán, un pueblo donde todavía vive su madre, Dolores del Río, en Calle Principal #14. La abuela viaja dos veces al año para ayudar con el cuidado de Mateo y de su hermana mayor, Camila Flores-Jiménez, de 5 years old.

RUTINAS DIARIAS / DAILY ROUTINES

Mateo se despierta alrededor de las 7:00 a.m. y desayuna con su familia. Esteban Flores-Jiménez lo lleva a Honeycomb Hollow a las 8:30 a.m., donde permanece hasta las 4:00 p.m. de lunes a viernes. Su maestra, Ms. Patterson, reporta que juega bien con compañeros como Liam y Sofía Castillo, pero se frustra cuando no puede pedir turnos verbalmente.

Dolores del Río lo recoge algunas tardes y se queda con él hasta que los padres terminan de trabajar. Esteban Flores-Jiménez trabaja en Blue Ridge Furniture Company en Hickory, y Rosa del Río trabaja medio tiempo en Foothills Linen Services. By 6:30 p.m. the whole family eats dinner together, y es en ese momento cuando Mateo intenta comunicar más, mostly through gestures y algunas palabras aproximadas.

OTRAS AGENCIAS / OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

- Catawba County DSS: family receives support for housing stability.
- WIC: nutrition support, última cita 09/02/2026.
- Smart Start of Catawba County: funded Mateo's slot at Honeycomb Hollow.
- Western Piedmont CDSA: coordinates all Part C services through Denise Watkins.

NIVELES ACTUALES DE DESARROLLO / PRESENT LEVELS

Mateo fue evaluado con el Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5), edición bilingüe español-inglés, el 15 de septiembre de 2026, administrado por Marisol Ortega-Peña. Resultados: Auditory Comprehension standard score 73 (4th percentile); Expressive Communication standard score 68 (2nd percentile); Total Language Score 70, confidence interval 73-83; age equivalent 2;6–3;0.

En articulación, el GFTA-3 arrojó una puntuación estándar de 77 (6th percentile). Mateo produce /p/, /b/ y /m/ de forma consistente pero omite /k/ y /g/ en posición final. Target word "taza" se produjo como "tata"; target "casa" se produjo como "asa". Responde bien a mod cues and shows stimulability for /k/ in isolation with max cues.

En pragmática, Mateo inicia interacción con pares en 3 of 5 oportunidades observadas, principalmente mediante gestos. Combina dos palabras en 8/10 intentos cuando se le da un modelo, pero rara vez lo hace de forma espontánea.

RESULTADOS DEL IFSP / IFSP OUTCOMES

Outcome 1: Mateo usará combinaciones de dos a tres palabras en español e inglés para pedir objetos deseados y comentar durante el juego, aumentando a 8/10 oportunidades a través de rutinas diarias con minimal cues.

Strategies:
- Marisol Ortega-Peña modelará expansión de enunciados durante sesiones quincenales en el hogar.
- Rosa del Río y Esteban Flores-Jiménez usarán estrategias de Hanen ("It Takes Two to Talk") durante las comidas y el juego.
- Dolores del Río reforzará vocabulario en español durante las tardes que cuida a Mateo.
- Staff at Honeycomb Hollow, including Ms. Patterson, ofrecerán oportunidades estructuradas de turnos con Liam y Sofía Castillo.

Outcome 2: Mateo producirá /k/ y /g/ en posición final de palabra en 3 of 5 trials durante tareas estructuradas, usando el enfoque Cycles.

Strategies:
- Marisol Ortega-Peña implementará ciclos de Cycles enfocados en patrones finales de sílaba, con práctica de palabras objetivo en ambos idiomas.
- Family will practice target words during bath time and car rides, reforzando /k/ en palabras como "gato" y "lago."

Outcome 3: Mateo iniciará interacción con compañeros usando una palabra o gesto más vocalización en 4 of 5 observed opportunities at Honeycomb Hollow.

SERVICIOS / SERVICES

Speech-language therapy: 2x/semana, 30 minutos cada sesión, home-based y en Honeycomb Hollow, proporcionada por Marisol Ortega-Peña. Fecha de inicio: 10/13/2026. Autorización vigente hasta 4/6/27 bajo Western Piedmont CDSA. CPT code 92507. ICD-10 code F80.2.

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Child's Name: Maria Jose Hernandez Ortiz ("Majo")
Date of Birth: August 20, 2021
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;6
Medicaid ID: 740228913B
Case/Record ID: LD-2026-0417
Date of Evaluation: March 2, 2026
Date of Report: March 10, 2026
Evaluating Clinician: Rebecca A. Martinez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Referral Source: Dr. James Whitfield, pediatrician
School/Program: Lindale Elementary School, Briar County Schools, Pre-K classroom of Mrs. Debbie Lopez
Service Coordinator: Monica Reyes, Briar County CDSA
Prior IFSP Review: January 15, 2026

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Maria Jose Hernandez Ortiz, known to her family and teachers as Majo, was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by her pediatrician, Dr. James Whitfield, due to continued concerns about expressive language delay and reduced speech intelligibility in both English and Spanish. Majo currently attends the Pre-K classroom of Mrs. Debbie Lopez at Lindale Elementary School, part of Briar County Schools. Her mother, Lucia Ortiz Ramirez, reported that Majo's teacher, Mrs. Lopez, raised concerns at a recent conference that Majo is difficult to understand compared to same-age peers and often gestures instead of using words. This evaluation was requested to update Majo's Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) through Briar County CDSA and to determine continued eligibility for early intervention services.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Majo lives with her mother, Lucia Ortiz Ramirez, her father, Carlos Hernandez Flores, and two brothers: Jesus Hernandez Ortiz, known as "Chuy," age 8, and Jose Hernandez Ortiz, known as "Pepe," age 2. The family resides at 87 Willow Bend Court in Lindale, Briar County. Lucia Ortiz Ramirez works two jobs to support the family: a day shift as a server at the Pine Valley Diner and an overnight shift at JCI. Carlos Hernandez Flores works in roofing and is frequently away from home for several days at a time. Due to the parents' demanding work schedules, Majo's primary daytime caregiver is her grandmother, Guadalupe Ramirez, affectionately called "Lupita" by the family, who speaks primarily Spanish and cares for Majo and her brothers most weekday afternoons. A cousin, Juan Ortiz, nicknamed "Juanito," age 5, also spends several afternoons a week at the home and is described as Majo's closest playmate outside of school. The family's dog, Rocky, is reportedly a source of great enjoyment for Majo, who frequently talks to him at home.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Per maternal report, Majo was born at 37 weeks gestation following an uncomplicated pregnancy. Birth weight was 5 lbs 11 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. Lucia Ortiz Ramirez reported no complications during delivery and no NICU stay. Majo's early developmental milestones were reportedly within normal limits for gross motor skills; she walked independently at 13 months. Fine motor and self-help skills have developed age-appropriately according to Angela Brooks, OTR/L, who has provided occasional consultation through the CDSA.

Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media beginning around 18 months of age, with bilateral tympanostomy tube placement (CPT 69436) performed at November 4, 2023. Lucia Ortiz Ramirez reported that hearing has not been formally reassessed since the tubes were placed, though Majo passed a hearing screening at that time. Majo carries diagnoses of Expressive Language Disorder (ICD-10 F80.1) and history of recurrent otitis media (ICD-10 H65.0), both established during a prior developmental evaluation on June 12, 2024. No seizure history, no significant hospitalizations, and no known allergies were reported. Vision was reported as normal per a recent well-child visit with Dr. James Whitfield.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Majo is being raised in a bilingual Spanish-English home. Lucia Ortiz Ramirez reported that Spanish is the primary language spoken at home, particularly with Lupita, while English is increasingly used by Chuy and at school. Lucia Ortiz Ramirez estimated that Majo hears approximately 70% Spanish and 30% English in a typical week, with English exposure increasing since she began attending Pre-K with Mrs. Lopez in August 2025. Carlos Hernandez Flores reportedly prefers to speak Spanish with the children when he is home. Majo's cousin Juanito is also bilingual and reportedly serves as an informal language model and playmate, often translating for Majo when she struggles to be understood by English-speaking peers.

Per parent and teacher report, Majo's classmate Mateo Diaz, called "Teo" by the class, is one of her preferred playmates at Lindale Elementary School and reportedly helps her during centers time when she becomes frustrated trying to communicate. Lucia Ortiz Ramirez denied any family history of hearing loss, autism, or genetic syndromes. There is a reported family history of late talking on the maternal side; Lucia Ortiz Ramirez stated that she herself "did not talk much" until around age four.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Majo presented as a friendly, socially engaged child who separated easily from her mother for testing. She demonstrated good eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking during structured and unstructured play. She transitioned between tasks with minimal cueing and required occasional redirection to remain seated during tabletop activities. Majo used a combination of single words, gestures, and short phrases in both English and Spanish to communicate, frequently code-switching within the same utterance (for example, producing "quiero milk" when requesting a drink). Intelligibility was reduced for unfamiliar listeners, estimated at approximately 50% in connected speech, though it improved to roughly 70% when context was known. No concerns were noted regarding attention, play skills, or social reciprocity during this session.

ASSESSMENT RESULTS

Standardized and informal measures were administered in both English and Spanish, with instructions and stimuli presented bilingually as appropriate, given Rebecca A. Martinez's bilingual Spanish-English proficiency.

Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-English bilingual administration:
- Auditory Comprehension: Standard Score 76 (5th percentile), 90% confidence interval 71-81
- Expressive Communication: Standard Score 70 (2nd percentile), 90% confidence interval 65-75
- Total Language Score: Standard Score 71 (3rd percentile)
- Age Equivalent: 2;6-3;0

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3), English administration:
- Sounds-in-Words: Standard Score 73 (4th percentile)

Spanish Articulation Measures (informal, criterion-referenced):
- Stimulability for /r/ and /ɾ/: 3 of 5 trials correct with mod cues
- Production of "carro" was noted as [kajo], substituting [j] for /ɾ/
- Production of "pescado" was noted as [peˈkado], omitting medial /s/

Oral mechanism examination was within normal limits for structure and function. Diadochokinetic rates were judged age-appropriate. Majo demonstrated stimulability for final consonants in English with min cues, achieving 8/10 correct for final /k/ in single words, for example producing the target word "cake" as [keɪk] with model and imitation.

A language sample was collected in both languages during play with toy animals and a farm set. Mean length of utterance (MLU) in English morphemes was calculated at 2.1, below expected range for her age. In Spanish, MLU was calculated at 2.4 morphemes. Majo used primarily noun-verb or noun-noun combinations (for example, "perro come" and "more juice") and demonstrated limited use of grammatical morphemes such as plurals, past tense markers, and possessives in either language. SALT coding of the sample identified frequent use of [EW] codes for word-finding difficulty and several instances of [EO] for omitted obligatory morphemes.

Receptively, Majo followed two-step directions with 8/10 accuracy in Spanish and 6/10 accuracy in English. She identified basic categories, colors, and prepositions above chance level in both languages but struggled with sequencing and "wh-" questions, particularly "why" and "how" questions, answering appropriately only 2 of 10 times across both languages.

IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, informal measures, language sampling, and parent and teacher report, Majo presents with a moderate-to-severe expressive and receptive language delay affecting both English and Spanish, consistent with a bilingual presentation of Developmental Language Disorder rather than a language difference attributable solely to dual-language exposure. Her language delay is present across both languages, which supports a true disorder rather than typical second-language acquisition patterns. Majo also demonstrates a moderate speech sound disorder affecting both languages, with specific difficulty producing /ɾ/ and medial /s/ in Spanish and final consonants and multisyllabic words in English. Given her history of recurrent otitis media and tympanostomy tube placement, a hearing re-screening is also recommended to rule out any residual conductive component contributing to her speech and language profile.

Majo's social communication skills, play skills, and attention appear to be relative strengths and are not of clinical concern at this time. Her rich bilingual home environment, including frequent interaction with her grandmother Lupita, her cousin Juanito, and her classmate Teo, appears to provide strong relational and motivational support for communication, and should be leveraged as a resource in treatment planning rather than viewed as a barrier.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Majo continues to qualify for speech-language intervention services through Briar County CDSA under her existing IFSP. It is recommended that direct therapy frequency increase to two 45-minute sessions per week, to be provided bilingually given Majo's dual-language home environment.

2. Therapy should target expressive vocabulary growth, use of grammatical morphemes (plurals, past tense, possessives) in both English and Spanish, and increased MLU through structured play-based activities and modeling.

3. Speech sound intervention should target /ɾ/ and medial /s/ in Spanish and final consonants and multisyllabic word shapes in English, using a cycles-based approach (Cycles) given the number of sound classes affected.

4. A hearing re-screening or full audiological evaluation is recommended given Majo's history of recurrent otitis media and tube placement, to rule out any residual hearing component.

5. Continued coordination with Mrs. Debbie Lopez and the team at Lindale Elementary School is recommended to support classroom language use and to monitor progress toward Pre-K readiness goals.

6. Home carryover strategies will be provided in both English and Spanish for Lucia Ortiz Ramirez, Carlos Hernandez Flores, and Lupita, given their roles as Majo's primary caregivers and communication partners.

7. Re-evaluation is recommended in approximately six months, or sooner if significant progress is noted, to update Majo's IFSP goals in coordination with Monica Reyes at Briar County CDSA.

Please contact this clinician with any questions regarding this report or Majo's plan of care.

Respectfully submitted,

Rebecca A. Martinez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist

Concerns were echoed by staff at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare, where Mateo is enrolled four days a week from 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

3. BACKGROUND INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN DE ANTECEDENTES

3.1 Birth and Medical History

Mateo was born at 34 weeks gestation at Duke Regional Hospital in Durham, following a pregnancy complicated by preeclampsia. Birth weight was 4 lbs 2 oz, with Apgar scores of 6 and 8 at one and five minutes, respectively. He was admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) at Duke Regional Hospital for 19 days for respiratory support and feeding difficulties. His attending neonatologist was Dr. Patricia Nguyen, and he was followed after discharge by pediatrician Dr. Samuel Osei at Duke Children's Primary Care. Mother reports no additional hospitalizations. Mateo passed his newborn hearing screening, and a repeat audiological evaluation at 18 months was within normal limits bilaterally. He has a history of recurrent otitis media, with tympanostomy tubes placed at 22 months by Dr. Osei's referral to an ENT. No seizure history. Current diagnoses include ICD-10 R63.3 (feeding difficulties, resolved) and a standing referral for ICD-10 F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, rule out).

3.2 Developmental History

Gross and fine motor milestones were met within expected ranges, per mother's report (walked independently at 14 months). First words in Spanish ("mamá," "agua") emerged around 18 months; two-word Spanish combinations were not consistently present until approximately 30 months. English exposure began at 26 months with daycare enrollment.

3.3 Historia Familiar y Lingüística (Family and Language History)

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Peña; father, Hernán Cruz Martínez; and older sister, Camila Cruz Rodríguez (age 8), at the family's home in Durham County. Lucía works two jobs: as a CNA on the evening shift at a local nursing facility, and folding linens part-time at a laundromat on weekend mornings. Hernán works in landscaping, often leaving the home before 6:00 a.m. Mateo's maternal grandmother, Rosario Peña, lives nearby and provides childcare most afternoons, picking him up from daycare around 5:15 p.m. and staying with him until a parent returns home, sometimes as late as 10:30 p.m.

The home language is primarily Spanish; Rosario and Hernán speak almost exclusively Spanish to Mateo, while Lucía code-switches depending on context. Camila, who is more English-dominant from school, often translates for Mateo with unfamiliar adults. The family attends Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida on Holloway Street most Sundays, where Mateo participates in a children's Sunday school class conducted in Spanish. The family also regularly attends the bilingual "Cuentos y Cantos" storytime program at the Durham County Public Library, East Regional Branch on Tuesday mornings, which Lucía described as one of the few activities where she has seen Mateo attempt new English vocabulary spontaneously.

Lucía reported, "En casa habla bien, pero cuando llegamos a lugares nuevos se pone callado" ("At home he speaks well, but when we get to new places he gets quiet"). She also noted frustration: "A veces se enoja porque no lo entienden" ("Sometimes he gets angry because they don't understand him").

4. BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Testing was conducted across two sessions at the Erwin Road office. Session one ran from 9:00 a.m. to 10:15 a.m. on September 15, 2026; session two ran from 1:30 p.m. to 2:45 p.m. on September 17, 2026. Mateo separated from his mother without distress and engaged readily with play-based materials. He required frequent redirection and benefited from visual schedules and brief movement breaks between tasks. Rapport was established quickly when the evaluator used Spanish; Mateo appeared noticeably more verbal and spontaneous in Spanish-language play than in English-language tasks. Attention and behavior were judged adequate to support valid testing in both languages.

5. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND RESULTS

5.1 Standardized Testing

The following measures were administered in both English and Spanish as appropriate, with results interpreted in light of Mateo's bilingual status per current best practice for dual-language learners.

Measure | Language | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% CI
Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) – Morphosyntax Subtest | Spanish | 82 | 12th | 76-88
BESA – Semantics Subtest | Spanish | 88 | 21st | 81-95
Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5) Spanish Edition, Auditory Comprehension | Spanish | 79 | 8th | 71-87
PLS-5 Spanish Edition, Expressive Communication | Spanish | 74 | 4th | 66-82
PLS-5, Auditory Comprehension (English) | English | 68 | 2nd | 60-76
PLS-5, Expressive Communication (English) | English | 65 | 1st | 57-73
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) | English/Spanish mixed | 71 | 3rd | 64-78

5.2 Speech Sound Production

In connected speech sampled across both languages, Mateo demonstrated a moderate phonological disorder affecting intelligibility. He substituted /t/ for /k/ (e.g., producing "tasa" for the target "casa") and /d/ for /g/ (e.g., "dato" for "gato"), consistent with fronting that is typically resolved by 3;0 in monolingual Spanish-speaking children. He also exhibited final consonant deletion in English (e.g., "ca" for "cat") and cluster reduction (e.g., "top" for "stop"). Stimulability testing showed Mateo could produce /k/ and /g/ in isolation with mod cues, and in syllables with max cues. Overall intelligibility was estimated at 40% to unfamiliar listeners in connected speech, and 70% to familiar listeners (mother, grandmother).

5.3 Language

Receptively, Mateo followed two-step directions in Spanish 8 of 10 trials but only 3 of 10 trials in English. He identified 9/10 common objects by function in Spanish compared to 5/10 in English. Expressively, his Spanish mean length of utterance (MLU) was calculated at 3.2 morphemes, within the low average range for his age; his English MLU was 1.8 morphemes, below expectations even accounting for limited exposure. He used present-tense verb forms inconsistently in Spanish, omitting the required subject-verb agreement marker in "él come" produced as "él comer," and relied heavily on gesture and single-word utterances in English.

5.4 Bilingual Considerations

Error patterns were compared against typical bilingual Spanish-English development to differentiate language difference from language disorder. Mateo's difficulties — reduced MLU, limited morphosyntax, and a phonological disorder — were present across both of his languages, which supports a true language disorder rather than a difference attributable solely to dual-language exposure. His stronger performance in Spanish is consistent with Spanish being the dominant input language at home.

6. IMPRESIONES / CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized assessment, parent report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a moderate-to-severe speech sound disorder and a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with ICD-10 F80.2 and ICD-10 F80.0. Deficits are present across both languages, ruling out typical second-language acquisition as the primary explanation for his profile. His history of chronic otitis media and NICU stay are considered likely contributing risk factors, though his current hearing is within normal limits.

7. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo qualifies for ongoing speech-language intervention services. Recommend individual bilingual speech-language therapy, twice weekly, in 30-minute sessions, targeting both Spanish and English goals.
2. Continue IFSP services through CDSA; recommend adding a specific outcome addressing speech intelligibility (proposed IFSP Outcome 3) at the next review, scheduled for March 3, 2027.
3. Recommend a trial of a Cycles phonological approach targeting final consonants and velar sounds, delivered bilingually.
4. Family education regarding bilingual language stimulation strategies, including continued exposure through Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida's children's programming and the Durham County Public Library, East Regional Branch storytime, both of which appear to support spontaneous language use.
5. Coordinate with Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare staff regarding classroom strategies and consistent use of visual supports.
6. Recommend repeat audiological monitoring annually given history of recurrent otitis media, in coordination with Dr. Samuel Osei.
7. Reassess in six months to monitor progress toward outcomes.

During the daycare observation portion of intake, Mateo was noted sitting beside a classmate, A.P., during circle time, and initiated a brief exchange in Spanish that his teacher, Ms. Delgado, described as unusually spontaneous for him.

This evaluation was interpreted with the assistance of J. Ortiz, whose services were coordinated through Carolina Bilingual Speech-Language Services, PLLC.
