text:
Piedmont Region Children's Developmental Services Agency (CDSA)
NC Infant-Toddler Program — Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) Periodic Review

1. Identifying Information / Información de Identificación

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Ramírez ("Teo")
Date of Birth: April 9, 2023 (38 weeks gestation, birth weight 6 lb 2 oz, Apgar 8/9)
Current Age: 29 months
CDSA Case ID: PR-2026-00417
Medicaid ID: 800417963C
IFSP Review Date: October 6, 2026
Initial IFSP Date: February 14, 2026
Primary Language of the Home: Spanish and English (bilingual household)

Parents/Guardians:
Mother: Lucía Rodríguez, phone (336) 555-0198 (home) and 919-555-0142 (cell)
Father: Hugo Cruz, phone 336.555.0233

Siblings in the home:
Guadalupe Cruz Ramírez ("Lupita"), age 7 years
Jesús Cruz Ramírez ("Chuy"), age 11 months

Home address: 1420 Maple Hollow Drive, Burlington, Alamance County, NC 27215

2. Service Coordination / Coordinación de Servicios

Service Coordinator: David Nguyen, Piedmont Region CDSA, office phone (336) 555-7710 ext. 204
Evaluating/Treating Speech-Language Pathologist: Mariana Torres, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (español/inglés), Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners, (336) 555-9012
Physical Therapist: Sarah Williams, PT, DPT
Pediatrician: Dr. Angela Foster, Alamance Children's Health Clinic

Esta revisión fue completada en la casa de la familia con interpretación mutua, ya que la terapeuta Torres y la familia se comunican en ambos idiomas, inglés y español, según la preferencia de cada momento.

3. Reason for Review / Motivo de la Revisión

This six-month IFSP periodic review was conducted to update progress on current outcomes, confirm continued eligibility, and revise strategies based on Teo's rate of growth in expressive and receptive language. The family's last annual IFSP was completed on February 14, 2026, following the initial eligibility evaluation on January 22, 2026.

4. Family Concerns, Priorities, and Resources / Preocupaciones, Prioridades y Recursos de la Familia

Lucía Rodríguez shared the family's concerns and priorities in her own words during the home visit:

"Lo que más me preocupa es que Teo no habla como su hermana Lupita a esta edad. Ella ya decía frases completas, y él solo dice unas palabras sueltas, como 'agua' y 'más.' Yo trabajo dos trabajos, uno en el restaurante y otro de limpieza en el RDU por las noches, y a veces me preocupa que no paso suficiente tiempo con él para ayudarlo."

Lucía went on to describe her work schedule: she works daytime shifts at El Rinconcito restaurant and overnight cleaning shifts at RDU (Raleigh-Durham International Airport), often returning home after midnight. Hugo Cruz, the father, works in residential construction with variable hours and is sometimes away for several days at a time on out-of-town jobs.

Lucía added: "Mi mamá, Rosa Ramírez, viene de México a veces para ayudarnos, pero ahora está allá. Hablamos por teléfono casi todos los días al +52 55 1234 5678. Ella me dice que Teo se parece mucho a su tío a esa edad, que tampoco hablaba mucho y después habló bien."

Family priorities identified for this review period:
1. Increase Teo's functional vocabulary in both English and Spanish so he can request wants and needs without frustration.
2. Support Lupita and Chuy in using simple strategies at home to encourage Teo's talking during play.
3. Help the family access reliable childcare given the parents' overlapping work schedules.
4. Continue bilingual service delivery, as the family wants Teo to keep both languages.

Lucía stated: "No quiero que pierda el español, pero tampoco quiero que se quede atrás en inglés para cuando entre a la escuela."

5. Daily Routines and Natural Environments / Rutinas Diarias y Ambientes Naturales

Teo spends most weekdays with his maternal grandmother, Rosa Ramírez, when she is in the United States, and otherwise with a family friend who provides informal childcare, Yesenia Morales, at her home two streets over. Yesenia also cares for her own toddler and occasionally Teo's cousin José Hernández ("Pepe"), age 4 years, after preschool.

On weekdays when Lucía works the lunch shift, Teo wakes around 7:00 a.m., eats breakfast with Lupita before she leaves for school, and is dropped at Yesenia's house by 8:30 a.m. Hugo picks him up around 5:30 p.m. when his work schedule allows; otherwise Yesenia keeps Teo until Lucía finishes her restaurant shift around 6:00 p.m. and comes to collect him before her overnight cleaning shift begins at 11:00 p.m.

The family's dog, Rocky, is a favorite play partner; Teo often points to Rocky and says "perro" or attempts "[dɔ]" for "dog." Bath time, mealtimes, and the nightly routine with Lupita reading picture books are identified as natural, language-rich opportunities. Lupita reports that Teo likes to imitate her saying "no no no" and claps when she sings to him.

Teo attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center on Chapel Hill Road in Burlington two mornings per week while his grandmother is out of the country. His classroom teacher there, Ms. Keisha Lopez, reports that he plays well alongside peers but rarely initiates verbal exchanges. A classmate, Juan Pablo Torres ("Juanito"), is described as Teo's closest friend in the classroom; the two frequently push toy trucks together.

6. Other Agencies and Community Resources / Otras Agencias y Recursos Comunitarios

The family currently receives services and support from the following agencies:

- Alamance County Department of Social Services (DSS): The family receives SNAP benefits; a caseworker, Monica Reyes, is assigned to the household.
- Alamance County WIC Program: Teo and Chuy are both enrolled; the family's WIC appointments are coordinated through the office on South Mebane Street.
- Partnership for Children of Alamance County (the local Smart Start partner agency): referred the family for a childcare subsidy application given Lucía's and Hugo's combined work schedules.
- Alamance-Caswell Early Head Start: the family is on the waiting list for Chuy; staff there, Denise Carter, has offered to help coordinate transportation once a slot opens.

Lucía noted that the WIC nutritionist recommended continuing to offer Teo a variety of textures at mealtimes to support both feeding and speech-motor development, which the family has incorporated.

7. Present Levels of Development / Niveles Actuales de Desarrollo

Communication: On re-administration of the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) on September 29, 2026, Teo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 76 (5th percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 71 (3rd percentile), both within the range reflecting significant delay, though improved from initial scores of 68 and 62 respectively at the January 22, 2026 evaluation. His expressive vocabulary has grown from approximately 8 words to approximately 35 words across both languages, including code-switched approximations such as "agua," "más," "up," and "bye-bye." He combines two words inconsistently (e.g., "más agua," "no no") but does not yet produce consistent two-word combinations across contexts.

Phonetic inventory in both languages includes /m/, /p/, /b/, /n/, and /a/, with inconsistent production of /t/ and /d/. When asked to imitate "perro," Teo produced "[pɛo]," omitting the medial /r/ and final /o distortion, consistent with expected developmental error patterns at his age in Spanish. Stimulability for /t/ was noted with moderate cues during the session.

Motor/Physical: Sarah Williams, PT, reports age-appropriate gross motor skills; Teo is walking, running, and climbing stairs with alternating feet, and does not require ongoing physical therapy services at this time.

Social-Emotional: Teo demonstrates joint attention with familiar adults and siblings, engages in reciprocal play with Juanito and Lupita, and shows mild frustration behaviors (throwing toys, brief crying) when unable to make his wants known, consistent with expressive language delay rather than a primary behavioral concern.

8. IFSP Outcomes and Strategies / Resultados y Estrategias del IFSP

Outcome 1: Teo will use 2-word combinations to request desired items and activities during daily routines in at least 4 of 5 opportunities, in English or Spanish, as observed by caregivers.
Strategies: Caregivers will model two-word phrases during snack, bath, and play ("más leche," "more juice") using expectant waiting and a brief pause before providing the item. Rosa Ramírez and Yesenia Morales will be coached by Mariana Torres on using this strategy consistently across both caregiving settings. Progress will be reviewed at each visit using caregiver report and direct observation.

Outcome 2: Teo will imitate and spontaneously produce the sounds /t/ and /d/ in single words with no more than min cues, across 3 consecutive sessions.
Strategies: Direct elicitation using preferred words containing target sounds (e.g., "toma," "dame," "tú"); Torres will provide the family a short list of target words in both languages to practice during car rides and mealtimes.

Outcome 3: Lupita and Chuy's caregivers will report using at least 2 new language-facilitation strategies (expectant waiting, imitation and expansion) during home routines, as reported at the next review.
Strategies: Torres will model strategies during coaching visits with Lupita present, since she is a highly motivated language model for Teo and enjoys participating in sessions.

Outcome 4: The family will identify and access a consistent, Early Head Start–eligible childcare option by the next IFSP review, reducing reliance on informal arrangements.
Strategies: David Nguyen will continue to coordinate with Denise Carter at Alamance-Caswell Early Head Start and with the Partnership for Children of Alamance County regarding subsidy status; the service coordinator will follow up by phone within 30 days.

9. Service Delivery / Prestación de Servicios

Speech-language therapy: 60 minutes weekly, home-based (at 1420 Maple Hollow Drive) and at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center on alternating weeks, provided by Mariana Torres, bilingual service delivery per family preference, beginning October 13, 2026.
Physical therapy: Discontinued this review period per PT recommendation; Sarah Williams will remain available for consultation if concerns arise.
Service coordination: Monthly contact by phone or home visit, David Nguyen, Piedmont Region CDSA.

Hugo Cruz confirmed he would try to be present for at least one session per month: "Yo quiero estar ahí cuando pueda, aunque mi horario es difícil. Los sábados en la mañana casi siempre estoy libre."

10. Transition Planning / Planificación de Transición

As Teo is 29 months old, the team briefly discussed transition planning ahead of his third birthday, including eligibility evaluation for Alamance-Burlington School System Preschool Services and continued coordination with DSS and WIC for family support services. A formal transition conference will be scheduled for February 2027.

11. Review Summary and Next Steps

The team, including Lucía Rodríguez, Hugo Cruz (by phone during part of the visit), David Nguyen, and Mariana Torres, agreed that outcomes 1 through 4 above represent updated priorities reflecting Teo's progress and the family's current circumstances. The next periodic review is scheduled for April 6, 2027, with the annual IFSP due no later than February 14, 2027.

Signatures:

Lucía Rodríguez, Parent

_______________________________ Date: October 6, 2026
David Nguyen, Service Coordinator, Piedmont Region CDSA

text:
Estimada familia Lucía Rodríguez y Carlos Hernández:

Les escribo este resumen de la revisión del Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP) de su hijo Mateo Hernández Cruz. Fue un placer reunirnos el martes pasado para hablar sobre su progreso y los próximos pasos. Quiero agradecerles por su paciencia conmigo mientras aprendo más sobre las rutinas de su hogar y las metas que tienen para Mateo. Espero que esta carta les sirva como referencia fácil de leer, además del documento oficial del IFSP que recibirán por correo de nuestra oficina.

Me llamo Ana Martínez, soy la patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe que trabaja con Mateo a través del programa Little Learners Program. También participó en la reunión nuestra coordinadora de servicios, Maritza Gómez, de la oficina del CDSA del Triángulo, y contamos con la ayuda de nuestra intérprete, Rosa Valdez, para asegurar que toda la información fuera clara en ambos idiomas durante la reunión.

**Información de la familia**

Mateo nació el 26 de marzo de 2023, con un peso de 3,200 gramos y una edad gestacional de 39 semanas. Su puntuación de Apgar fue de 8 y 9 al minuto uno y cinco respectivamente. Actualmente tiene 3;6 años de edad. Vive con su mamá, Lucía Rodríguez; su papá, Carlos Hernández; su hermana mayor, Sofía Hernández, de 5 años; y frecuentemente pasa las tardes con su abuela materna, Rosa Cruz, quien lo cuida mientras sus padres trabajan. La familia vive en Calle Roble 482, Durham, condado de Durham, Carolina del Norte, 27705. Pueden comunicarse con la familia al (919) 555-0148 o por correo electrónico a lucia.rodriguez82@gmail.com.

El número de Medicaid de Mateo es 987654321B y su número de expediente en el programa es TIP-2024-00567.

Carlos trabaja en Construcciones Bravo y Lucía trabaja medio tiempo en Supermercado Compare. Ambos hacen un gran esfuerzo para asistir a las citas y practicar las estrategias en casa, incluso cuando los horarios de trabajo son difíciles de coordinar.

**Coordinadora de servicios y oficina del CDSA**

Nuestra coordinadora de servicios, Maritza Gómez, continúa apoyando a la familia desde la oficina del CDSA del Triángulo. Ella puede contactarse al (919) 555-0193 si tienen preguntas sobre elegibilidad, servicios o la próxima revisión del IFSP. Maritza ha sido fundamental para coordinar las evaluaciones, solicitar la autorización de servicios y asegurar que la familia reciba apoyo en su idioma preferido.

**Inquietudes y prioridades de la familia, en sus propias palabras**

Durante la reunión, Lucía compartió: "Lo que más nos preocupa es que Mateo todavía no combina palabras como su hermana lo hacía a esta edad. Queremos que pueda decirnos lo que necesita sin frustrarse tanto." Carlos añadió: "También queremos que se lleve bien con los otros niños en la guardería y que aprenda a esperar su turno. Y nos preocupa un poco qué va a pasar cuando cumpla tres años y tenga que dejar el programa."

Las prioridades principales de la familia son:
1. Que Mateo use más palabras y frases cortas para pedir cosas.
2. Que disminuyan las rabietas cuando no se le entiende.
3. Que participe más en el círculo de canciones en la guardería.
4. Que la familia aprenda estrategias para usar durante la cena y el baño.
5. Entender mejor el proceso de transición hacia los servicios preescolares del distrito escolar.

**Rutinas diarias**

Mateo se despierta alrededor de las 7:00 a.m. y desayuna con su hermana Sofía antes de que su mamá lo lleve a Little Learners Daycare a las 8:30 a.m.. Su maestra en la guardería, la Srta. Pamela Ortiz, reporta que Mateo disfruta las actividades sensoriales pero se frustra durante el círculo de canciones porque no puede seguir las instrucciones verbales tan rápido como sus compañeros. Su compañera de clase, Emily, a menudo intenta jugar con él, y Mateo responde mejor cuando ella usa gestos simples en lugar de solo palabras.

Por las tardes, su abuela Rosa lo recoge a las 4:30 p.m. y juegan en el patio con el perro de la familia, Rocky, quien es una gran motivación para que Mateo use palabras como "perro" y "pelota". La cena familiar es alrededor de las 6:00 p.m., y el baño y la rutina de dormir comienzan cerca de las 7:30 p.m.. Los fines de semana, la familia suele visitar el parque cerca de su casa, lo cual ofrece otra buena oportunidad para practicar lenguaje en un ambiente motivador.

**Otras agencias involucradas**

Además del CDSA del Triángulo, la familia ha recibido apoyo de varias agencias comunitarias:

- DSS (el Departamento de Servicios Sociales del condado) ayudó a la familia a solicitar asistencia con el cuidado infantil.
- WIC continúa proporcionando apoyo nutricional para Mateo y su hermana.
- El programa Smart Start conectó a la familia con recursos de crianza y clases de desarrollo infantil en español.
- Mateo fue referido anteriormente a Early Head Start, pero la familia decidió continuar con Little Learners Daycare por ahora debido a la cercanía con el trabajo de Lucía.

**Evaluación y diagnóstico**

En la evaluación más reciente, administrada con la ayuda de nuestra intérprete Rosa Valdez, Mateo obtuvo en el PLS-5 una puntuación estándar de 73 (intervalo de confianza 68-78) en el subtest de Comprensión Auditiva, y una puntuación estándar de 65 en el subtest de Comunicación Expresiva, ubicándolo en el percentil 4. Su edad equivalente en lenguaje expresivo fue de 2;0. En el GFTA-3 obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 78, con una edad equivalente de 2;6-3;0.

Con base en estos resultados, el diagnóstico actual es trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo y expresivo, código F80.2. Los servicios de terapia del habla y lenguaje continuarán con dos sesiones semanales de 30 minutos cada una, facturadas bajo el código 92507 para terapia individual de lenguaje, y periódicamente usamos el código 92523 para evaluaciones combinadas de habla y lenguaje.

**Resultados (outcomes) y estrategias**

Outcome 1: Mateo combinará dos palabras para pedir objetos o acciones deseadas en al menos 8/10 oportunidades durante las rutinas de juego y comida.
Estrategias: Usaremos el enfoque de It Takes Two to Talk para enseñar a la familia a esperar y narrar durante el juego, junto con el modelo Hanen de "seguir el interés del niño". También incorporaremos PROMPT para apoyar la producción motora de palabras como "más" y "quiero".

Outcome 2: Mateo reducirá las conductas de frustración (llanto, tirarse al piso) durante las rutinas estructuradas, usando un sistema de comunicación alternativa.
Estrategias: Introduciremos tarjetas de PECS en casa y en la guardería para que Mateo pueda señalar lo que necesita antes de frustrarse. La Srta. Ortiz ya practicó esto durante el círculo de canciones con buenos resultados iniciales.

Outcome 3: Mateo imitará sonidos y sílabas objetivo con mod cues en al menos 80% de los ensayos durante actividades estructuradas.
Estrategias: Trabajaremos los sonidos /p/, /b/ y /m/ usando el enfoque de Cycles para fonología, con énfasis en palabras funcionales como "bebé" y "papá". También usaremos actividades del método Kaufman para facilitar la producción de secuencias motoras del habla.

Outcome 4: La familia reportará que usa estrategias de comunicación durante las rutinas del hogar (cena, baño, juego) para apoyar el lenguaje de Mateo.
Estrategias: Continuaremos las sesiones de entrenamiento para padres basadas en Hanen, con práctica específica en el uso de preguntas abiertas y pausas de espera. Carlos y Lucía ya reportan éxito usando "espera y observa" durante la cena, y Mateo respondió diciendo "más agua" la semana pasada, lo cual fue un gran avance.

**Otros proveedores involucrados**

El equipo de Mateo también incluye a su terapeuta ocupacional, Kevin Park, quien trabaja en la integración sensorial y las transiciones entre actividades; su fisioterapeuta, Diane Foster, quien monitorea su desarrollo motor grueso y la planificación motriz; y su pediatra, el Dr. Samuel Lee, quien supervisa su salud general y confirmó que no hay preocupaciones auditivas después de la prueba de audición más reciente. Todos nos reunimos trimestralmente para coordinar cuidado y compartir estrategias comunes entre disciplinas.

**Planificación de la transición**

Dado que Mateo cumplirá tres años el próximo 26 de marzo de 2027, comenzaremos a hablar sobre la transición hacia los servicios preescolares del distrito escolar aproximadamente seis meses antes de esa fecha. Maritza Gómez coordinará una reunión de planificación de transición con la familia y, si la familia lo desea, con representantes del distrito escolar. Esta planificación no cambia los servicios actuales; solo nos ayuda a prepararnos con tiempo.

**Fechas de servicio**

El IFSP inicial se firmó el 12 de abril de 2026, y esta revisión se llevó a cabo el 8 de octubre de 2026. Las sesiones de terapia de lenguaje continuarán los martes y jueves a las 10:00 a.m. en el centro de Little Learners Program, con una sesión mensual adicional en el hogar para apoyar la generalización de estrategias. La próxima revisión del IFSP está programada para el 8 de abril de 2027.

**Cierre**

Gracias, Carlos y Lucía, por su dedicación y amor hacia Mateo. Estamos muy contentos con el progreso que ha logrado, especialmente con el aumento de palabras nuevas en las últimas semanas. Es un placer trabajar con una familia tan comprometida, y sabemos que el camino hacia una mejor comunicación requiere paciencia de todos, incluyendo de Mateo mismo. Si tienen alguna pregunta antes de la próxima revisión, no duden en comunicarse conmigo o con Maritza Gómez en la oficina del CDSA del Triángulo.

Con cariño y respeto,

Ana Martínez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Little Learners Program
(919) 555-0177

RAZÓN DE LA REMISIÓN

Lucía Vega-Hernández y Miguel del Río solicitaron esta evaluación por preocupación con el desarrollo del habla y del lenguaje de su hijo Chuy. Según la madre, Chuy "habla muy poquito" en comparación con otros niños de su edad y usa principalmente gestos y sonidos aislados para comunicarse. La familia fue referida originalmente por Dr. Roberto Nguyen después de la revisión de los 18 meses y de nuevo en la revisión de los 30 meses, cuando el pediatra notó que el vocabulario expresivo del niño era muy limitado para su edad. La familia también fue conectada con el CDSA del Piamonte a través del Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Alamance (DSS), donde la coordinadora Yesenia Ortiz completó la referencia inicial.

[ ] Preocupación de la familia  [X] Referido por pediatra  [X] Referido por CDSA  [ ] Autorreferido

HISTORIA DEL DESARROLLO Y ANTECEDENTES MÉDICOS

Chuy nació a las 38 semanas de gestación mediante parto vaginal, sin complicaciones reportadas. Peso al nacer: 6 libras, 11 onzas. Puntuación de Apgar: 8 al minuto y 9 a los cinco minutos. La madre reporta un embarazo sin incidentes, aunque menciona que tuvo presión arterial ligeramente elevada en el tercer trimestre, controlada sin medicamento. No hubo estancia en la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales.

El niño tuvo una infección de oído (otitis media) recurrente entre los 8 y 20 meses de edad, con un total de 5 episodios documentados. Se le colocaron tubos de ventilación (miringotomía bilateral) a los 22 meses, realizada por el Dr. Samuel Okafor, otorrinolaringólogo pediátrico. Desde entonces, la madre reporta mejoría notable en la atención del niño a los sonidos, aunque el lenguaje expresivo no mejoró de forma proporcional. No hay historial de convulsiones, hospitalizaciones mayores, ni cirugías adicionales. La audición fue evaluada formalmente el 3 de septiembre de 2026 en el programa de audiología pediátrica, con resultados dentro de límites normales bilateralmente.

Historia médica relevante:
[ ] Prematuridad  [X] Otitis media recurrente  [ ] Convulsiones  [X] Tubos de ventilación
[ ] Problemas cardíacos  [ ] Problemas visuales  [ ] Retraso motor grueso  [X] Ninguna otra condición conocida

Diagnósticos previos: Ninguno formal de lenguaje hasta la fecha. El pediatra documentó "retraso en el desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo, sin especificar" (ICD-10 F80.9) en la nota de la revisión de los 30 meses.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DEL LENGUAJE

La familia de Chuy es de origen mexicano y lleva aproximadamente nueve años viviendo en Alamance County. En el hogar se habla principalmente español; el inglés se usa cuando llegan visitas de habla inglesa o cuando los padres hablan con los proveedores médicos. Lucía Vega-Hernández reporta que ella misma aprendió inglés como segundo idioma en la escuela secundaria y se siente más cómoda hablando español con sus hijos. Miguel del Río trabaja en el turno de noche en Carolina Comfort Furniture, una fábrica de muebles en Burlington, por lo que pasa menos tiempo con los niños durante el día.

Chuy tiene dos hermanos. Su hermana mayor, Guadalupe del Río Vega, a quien todos llaman "Lupita", tiene 7 años y según la madre tuvo un desarrollo del lenguaje típico, sin preocupaciones. Su hermano menor, Juan Pablo del Río Vega, apodado "Juanito", tiene 18 meses y todavía es muy pequeño para comparar. La madre no reporta antecedentes familiares de trastornos del habla, lenguaje o aprendizaje en la familia extendida, aunque menciona que un primo del lado paterno, de apellido Martínez-Oliveira, recibió terapia del habla de niño por razones que la familia no recuerda con claridad.

La abuela materna, Rosa Hernández, cuida a Chuy y a sus hermanos dos o tres días por semana mientras los padres trabajan. Según la madre, la abuela Rosa Hernández le habla a Chuy exclusivamente en español y es muy cariñosa, pero tiende a "adivinar" lo que el niño quiere antes de que él tenga que pedirlo con palabras. Una tía paterna, Carmen del Río, ayuda ocasionalmente con traducciones cuando la familia tiene citas médicas en inglés, aunque no estuvo presente en esta evaluación.

Chuy asiste tres días por semana al programa preescolar "El Nido de Mariposas", ubicado en Burlington, donde su maestra principal es Araceli Soto. Según la maestra Soto, en el salón Chuy juega cerca de otros niños pero rara vez inicia interacción verbal. Dos compañeros de clase que se mencionan con frecuencia son "Pepe" y "Teo", con quienes Chuy comparte juegos de bloques, aunque la comunicación entre ellos es mayormente no verbal. La familia también recibe apoyo del Partnership for Children de Alamance County y ha utilizado los servicios de WIC del Condado de Alamance desde que nació Juanito.

La familia tiene un perro llamado Rocky, al que Chuy quiere mucho. Durante la sesión de observación en el hogar, al intentar nombrar al perro, Chuy produjo "Wawi" en lugar de "Rocky", sustituyendo el sonido /r/ por /w/ y simplificando la estructura silábica.

Exposición al lenguaje:
Porcentaje de tiempo en español: 80%  Porcentaje de tiempo en inglés: 20%
[X] Español como primer idioma  [ ] Inglés como primer idioma  [X] Expuesto a ambos desde el nacimiento

OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES

Durante ambas sesiones, Chuy se mostró activo y curioso, explorando los juguetes disponibles sin dificultad motora aparente. Mantuvo contacto visual de forma consistente con la evaluadora, Mónica Fernández Castillo, y con su madre. El niño demostró buena atención conjunta cuando se le presentaron libros con imágenes, señalando objetos cuando se le preguntó "¿dónde está...?" en español. Sin embargo, su respuesta verbal fue mínima; en la mayoría de los intercambios comunicativos usó gestos (señalar, jalar la mano del adulto, negar con la cabeza) en lugar de palabras.

Se observaron aproximadamente 15 palabras funcionales distintas durante las dos sesiones combinadas, entre ellas aproximaciones de "mamá", "papá", "agua" (producida como [aɣa]), y "más". El niño no combinó palabras en frases de dos elementos durante ninguna de las observaciones directas, aunque la madre reporta haber escuchado "más agua" en casa de forma ocasional.

Nivel de interacción social:
[X] Busca atención conjunta  [X] Contacto visual apropiado  [ ] Juego simbólico limitado
[X] Usa gestos comunicativos  [ ] Ecolalia  [ ] Conductas repetitivas

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

Se administraron las siguientes pruebas estandarizadas, con instrucciones en español, complementadas con observación informal en inglés y español:

- Preschool Language Scale-5 Spanish Edition (PLS-5 Spanish)
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), adaptado con transcripción fonética en español
- Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (secciones de interacción y gestos)
- Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, analizada con códigos tipo [EW] y [EU] para enunciados ininteligibles
- Entrevista estructurada a los padres

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS

Tabla de puntuaciones:

Prueba / Subprueba                         Puntuación estándar    Percentil       Edad equivalente
PLS-5 Spanish — Comprensión Auditiva      68              2do percentil   18-20 meses
PLS-5 Spanish — Comunicación Expresiva    62              1er percentil   15-17 meses
PLS-5 Spanish — Índice de Lenguaje Total  63              1er percentil   N/A
GFTA-3 — Sonidos en palabras              71              3er percentil   N/A

Intervalo de confianza del Índice de Lenguaje Total (95%): 58-68

El niño obtuvo puntuaciones consistentemente por debajo del rango promedio en comprensión y expresión del lenguaje. En la subprueba de Comunicación Expresiva del PLS-5 Spanish, Chuy nombró correctamente 3 de 10 objetos presentados y no logró combinar dos palabras cuando se le solicitó describir una imagen de acción. En la subprueba de Comprensión Auditiva, siguió instrucciones de un paso con 8/10 de precisión, pero tuvo dificultad marcada con instrucciones de dos pasos, logrando solo 2 de 8 correctamente.

En el análisis de habla espontánea, se identificaron los siguientes patrones fonológicos: sustitución de /r/ por [w] (ejemplo: "Wawi" por "Rocky"), omisión de consonantes finales (ejemplo: "pa" por "pan"), y reducción de grupos consonánticos (ejemplo: "tes" por "tres"). La inteligibilidad general se estimó en 40% para oyentes familiares y menor para oyentes no familiares.

En la Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, las áreas de interacción-apego y gestos cayeron dentro del rango esperado para la edad, mientras que las áreas de lenguaje expresivo y vocabulario cayeron notablemente por debajo, consistentes con los hallazgos del PLS-5 Spanish.

Cuestionario de los padres sobre bilingüismo:
[X] El niño entiende mejor en español que en inglés
[ ] El niño entiende mejor en inglés que en español
[X] Los padres desean que el niño mantenga el español como idioma principal
[X] Preocupación de que el retraso ocurra en ambos idiomas, no solo por bilingüismo

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Con base en los resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas, la observación clínica, y el reporte de los padres, Chuy presenta un retraso significativo en el desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo y receptivo en español, su idioma dominante, con hallazgos fonológicos consistentes con un trastorno del habla también presente. Dado que el niño muestra dificultades en ambos dominios del lenguaje en su idioma primario (y no solo diferencias esperadas por adquisición bilingüe), los hallazgos son consistentes con un Trastorno del Desarrollo del Lenguaje de tipo mixto (receptivo-expresivo), junto con un trastorno fonológico concurrente.

Códigos diagnósticos sugeridos:
ICD-10 F80.2 — Trastorno del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo
ICD-10 F80.1 — Trastorno del lenguaje expresivo
CPT 92523 — Evaluación de habla y producción de sonidos con evaluación de comprensión y expresión del lenguaje

El patrón de otitis media recurrente en la primera infancia puede haber contribuido al retraso, aunque no explica por sí solo la magnitud del déficit observado actualmente. Se recomienda monitoreo continuo de audición, aunque los resultados más recientes del 3 de septiembre de 2026 fueron normales.

Áreas de fortaleza: atención conjunta, contacto visual, uso de gestos comunicativos, comprensión de vocabulario cotidiano concreto, e interacción social apropiada para la edad con adultos familiares.

Áreas de necesidad: vocabulario expresivo, combinación de palabras en frases, seguimiento de instrucciones de múltiples pasos, inteligibilidad del habla, y producción de sonidos específicos (/r/, consonantes finales, grupos consonánticos).

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda que Chuy reciba terapia de habla y lenguaje individual, con frecuencia sugerida de 2 veces por semana, sesiones de 30 minutos cada una, enfocadas en el desarrollo del vocabulario expresivo y la combinación de palabras.

2. Se recomienda el uso del enfoque Hanen para entrenar a los padres y a la abuela materna en estrategias de estimulación del lenguaje durante actividades cotidianas, dado que la mayor parte del tiempo del niño transcurre con cuidadores familiares que hablan español.

3. Dada la presencia de errores fonológicos múltiples, se recomienda incorporar un abordaje basado en Cycles para el tratamiento de los patrones fonológicos identificados, con atención particular a la sustitución de /r/ y la omisión de consonantes finales.

4. Se recomienda continuar la asistencia de Chuy al programa preescolar "El Nido de Mariposas", y se sugiere coordinación entre esta evaluadora y la maestra Araceli Soto para reforzar estrategias de lenguaje dentro del aula.

5. Se recomienda que la familia continúe trabajando con la coordinadora de servicios Yesenia Ortiz del CDSA del Piamonte para la actualización del Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP), incluyendo la revisión del Resultado 2 relacionado con comunicación funcional.

6. Se sugiere reevaluación de audiología en 6 meses dado el historial de otitis media recurrente, en coordinación con el Dr. Samuel Okafor.

7. Se recomienda reevaluación formal del habla y lenguaje en aproximadamente 6 meses para medir el progreso y ajustar el plan de tratamiento según sea necesario.

Plan de seguimiento:
[X] Terapia individual recomendada  [X] Entrenamiento a padres recomendado  [ ] Grupo de lenguaje recomendado
[X] Reevaluación en 6 meses  [X] Coordinación con CDSA  [ ] Alta de servicios

Esta evaluación y sus recomendaciones fueron discutidas verbalmente con Lucía Vega-Hernández y Miguel del Río al finalizar la sesión del 8 de octubre de 2026. Ambos padres expresaron acuerdo con el plan propuesto y desean iniciar servicios lo antes posible.

Piedmont Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC

Hola Lucía,

Le escribo para compartir la nota de la sesión de hoy con Mateo. Trabajamos de las 3:30 p.m. a las 4:15 p.m. en el centro de Carolina Pediatric Therapy Group, PLLC, en 4210 Avondale Drive, Durham, NC 27705.

S: Mateo llegó contento, acompañado por su tía Rosa, porque usted estaba trabajando su turno en UPS. Mencionó que también trabaja los fines de semana limpiando casas para ganar un poco más, y que la vecina, Carmen, a veces lo recoge cuando ninguna de las dos puede llegar a tiempo.

O: Usamos el CELF-5 (subprueba de Formulación de Oraciones) y obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 78, en el rango 73-83, percentil 7. En el PLS-5, el área de Comprensión Auditiva mostró una edad equivalente de 2;6–3;0, comparado con su edad cronológica de 4;2. Produjo /k/ inicial con mod cues en 6 de 10 ensayos (6/10), por ejemplo dijo "tasa" por "taza". Trabajamos también el fonema /ɾ/ con apoyo de PROMPT. Durante el juego en grupo, imitó a su compañera Emma al pedir turnos usando tarjetas de PECS, con éxito en 8 de 10 intentos.

A: Mateo sigue elegible bajo el diagnóstico de retraso del habla (ICD-10 F80.1). Su hermanita Sol estuvo presente parte de la sesión porque la guardería Little Sprouts Daycare cerró temprano hoy.

P: Continuar sesiones semanales. Avisé a la coordinadora de servicios, Marta Jiménez, de CDSA del Triángulo, sobre el progreso para la revisión del IFSP del 15 de noviembre de 2026. La próxima sesión será el 16 de octubre de 2026 a las 3:30 p.m..

Recomendaciones para casa: practicar de 5 a 10 minutos diarios nombrando objetos con /k/ al inicio, como "casa" y "copa", usando las tarjetas de PECS que le di. Si su tía Rosa puede ayudar los días que usted trabaja, sería ideal.

Cualquier pregunta, puede llamarme al (919) 555-0148 o escribir a ana.torres@cptgtherapy.com.

Nota de sesión diaria – terapia del habla y lenguaje

Fecha: 14 de octubre de 2025. Hora de la sesión: 3:30 p.m. a 4:15 p.m.. Lugar: domicilio de la familia en Calle Maple 215, Durham, Carolina del Norte.

Hoy se llevó a cabo una sesión de 45 minutos con Mateo Fernández (4;2). Estuvo presente su mamá, Lucía Fernández, quien participó activamente y respondió preguntas sobre el progreso del niño en casa. También asistió la intérprete certificada Carmen Ruiz, quien tradujo entre inglés y español durante toda la visita, ya que la madre prefiere recibir información clínica en español aunque entiende algo de inglés. La hermana mayor de Mateo, Luz, de ocho años, estuvo presente parte de la sesión y ayudó a mantener la atención del niño con juegos breves de turnos.

Lucía comentó que la familia asiste con regularidad al programa bilingüe de cuentos infantiles de la Biblioteca Pública del Condado de Durham, los sábados por la mañana, donde Mateo interactúa con otros niños, incluyendo a su amigo Diego, y practica vocabulario nuevo en un ambiente social relajado. También mencionó que el Programa de Intervención Temprana para Niños con Discapacidades del Desarrollo del Condado de Durham (PINDD) aprobó recientemente una evaluación adicional de terapia ocupacional. La coordinadora de servicios de PINDD, Ana Beltrán, llamará la próxima semana para programar esa cita.

Según Lucía, Mateo ha comenzado a combinar dos palabras en casa, como "quiero agua" y "más galleta", aunque todavía omite el sonido final en palabras como "pan", que produce como "pa". Su pediatra, el Dr. Javier Soto, recomendó continuar la terapia dos veces por semana. Durante la sesión se trabajó la producción del fonema /p/ en posición final usando el enfoque PROMPT. Mateo logró producir "sopa" correctamente en 7 de 10 ensayos con claves mínimas. En la prueba PLS-5, administrada el mes pasado, obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 82 en Comunicación Expresiva (percentil 12), dentro del rango 78-88.

Mateo también recibe fisioterapia con David Chen y terapia ocupacional con Sarah Kim en el mismo centro comunitario. Lucía agregó que la familia asiste cada domingo a la Iglesia San Juan Bautista, donde el párroco conoce bien la situación del niño y ha ofrecido ayuda con transporte a las citas médicas.

Plan: se continuará el enfoque PROMPT para sonidos finales y se incorporará el programa Hanen para estimular el lenguaje expresivo en el hogar. Se pidió a la familia practicar la lista de palabras objetivo cinco minutos diarios. La próxima sesión está programada para el 21 de octubre de 2025 a las 3:30 p.m.

Contacto de la familia: (919) 555-0148. Número de Medicaid del niño: 987654321A. Número de caso de PINDD: PIN-20394.

Nota escrita por Marisol Herrera, CCC-SLP bilingüe, Carolina Pediatric Speech Partners.

NORTH CAROLINA INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM
IFSP SIX-MONTH REVIEW — SPEECH-LANGUAGE SECTION

Child: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Fuentes ("Teo")
DOB: 04/18/2024  Age at review: 26 months
Medicaid ID: 928471620B
Child ID #: NCITP-55821
CDSA: Foothills CDSA, Catawba County
Service Coordinator: Jennifer Brooks, (828) 555-0143
Prior IFSP: March 10, 2026  Review Date: September 22, 2026
Author: Maria Elena Gutierrez-Smith, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual SLP, Piedmont Bilingual Speech & Language Partners
Interpreter: Carmen Ríos, Spanish/English, contracted via Foothills CDSA

S:
Visit at family home, 482 Willow Bend Lane, Hickory. Present: mother Lucía Fuentes, father Alejandro Cruz (joined by phone, lunch break), Teo, sister Sol (4;1), grandmother Paz Fuentes, family dog Rocky.

Background: Teo was referred to Foothills CDSA at 18 months by pediatrician Dr. Angela Kim for absent words. Initial eval February 2, 2026 by Maria Elena Gutierrez-Smith, M.S., CCC-SLP, confirmed eligibility; first IFSP written March 10, 2026. Family history significant: father Alejandro Cruz reports he himself did not speak in short phrases until 3 years; no other developmental concerns reported in extended family.

Via interpreter Carmen Ríos, Lucía reports: "Teo habla más pero no le entiendo casi nada. Dice como cuatro palabras que yo reconozco." (He talks more, but I understand almost nothing. He says about four words I recognize.) Primary concern unchanged from initial IFSP: expressive language delay, limited single-word vocabulary, poor intelligibility even to familiar listeners. Lucía states Teo points and grunts for wants, pulls her hand toward the fridge, and uses two consistent approximations: "mamá" and "guau" for dog. No single words reported spontaneous beyond these.

Family priorities restated: (1) Teo communicate wants without tantrums; (2) family understand him in Spanish and English at home; (3) Teo ready for preschool transition near 36 months.

Daily routine per Lucía: wakes 6:30 AM, breakfast with grandmother Paz Fuentes while parents work. Alejandro works swing shift, trabaja en la planta de pollo Eastbrook Poultry Plant (works at the Eastbrook poultry plant), leaves 5:00 AM. Lucía works mornings, limpia oficinas en el Sparkle Clean Services (cleans offices at Sparkle Clean Services, a cleaning service), returns home by 1:00 PM. Extended family previously worked construction and restaurant jobs before relocating: paternal uncle still works for a construction company, Hermanos Torres Construcción Torres Brothers, and a cousin works at a restaurant, el Restaurante El Fogón, per parent report, not directly relevant to this child's routine but noted for family context.

Teo attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center three mornings weekly; classmate Noah is his closest peer per teacher report; lead teacher Keisha Mooreland notes Teo prefers solitary play, limited vocalization in classroom, improved turn-taking since last review.

Family is enrolled with Catawba County WIC for nutrition support; Lucía mentioned a recent Catawba County DSS home visit unrelated to this case (housing voucher renewal). Grandmother Paz Fuentes was referred to Smart Start of Catawba County for a grandparent support group; has not yet enrolled. Family was given information on Catawba County Early Head Start as a possible fall placement; currently waitlisted.

Pediatric follow-up: Lucía reports last well visit with Dr. Angela Kim at Catawba Valley Medical Center on August 14, 2026; hearing screen pass bilaterally, referral to audiology for comprehensive eval still pending due to scheduling.

No new illness, no ear infections since last review. Sleep and feeding within normal limits per parent report. Teo shares a room with Sol; no behavioral concerns at night.

O:
PLS-5 Spanish and English bilingual administration (combined form per examiner judgment, dominant-language scoring):
Auditory Comprehension standard score 76 (5th percentile); Expressive Communication standard score 68 (2nd percentile); Total Language Score 70, confidence interval 64-76.

Expressive sample: MLU 1.1 morphemes, consistent with emerging single-word stage. Syllable shape inventory: CV present consistently; CVC emerging only with cueing; no CVCV reduplicated or diversified forms observed spontaneously.

Single-word inventory elicited via toy play and snack routine, Spanish-dominant home environment, English modeled by examiner for comparison:
Target "sol" (sun), modeled with picture card: child productions [so] (final consonant deletion, mod cues) and [tol] (stopping of /s/, min cues) across trials; no spontaneous production without cue.
Target "pan": [pa] x3, min cues.
Target "agua": approximated [awa], max cues first trial, mod cues second. Imitated on repeat: 3/5 trials with max cues.
Target "perro" (dog): card pushed away, not attempted this session.
Target "ball": [ba], spontaneous, no cue — the only fully spontaneous production observed this session.
Child referred to dog as "Rocky" using approximation [waka] when shown family photo; parent confirmed this is the consistent home production.

Consonant inventory estimated from spontaneous and elicited sample: /m, p, b, w/ present; /s, t, d, k, g/ inconsistent, cue-dependent; /l, r, ɾ/ absent. Phonetic inventory consistent with significant expressive phonology delay for 26 months.

Oral-motor exam: structures within normal limits, no dysphagia signs, adequate jaw/lip/tongue range for age during snack trial (crackers, puree).

Joint attention and gesture use: moderate, inconsistent. Teo used pointing 4/6 opportunities, pulled examiner's hand 2/6, no conventional gestures (wave, nod) observed this session.

Play skills informally screened within functional play; symbolic play emerging (fed doll, pushed car with sound effect "brrm").

A:
Mateo Alejandro Cruz Fuentes continues to present with severe expressive language delay and moderate receptive delay, consistent with mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, ICD-10 F80.2. Expressive phonology significantly delayed relative to 26-month expectations; stimulable for several target sounds with cueing, suggesting favorable prognosis with structured intervention. Bilingual exposure (Spanish-dominant home, English at daycare) is not the primary driver of delay; deficits present across both languages per parent and teacher report, consistent with a true language disorder rather than a typical bilingual acquisition pattern.

Risk factors for a persistent disorder include a reported paternal history of late talking and an inconsistent phonetic inventory beyond the typical variability window for bilingual learners. Protective factors include strong family engagement, consistent routine-based practice opportunities (grandmother Paz Fuentes home on weekdays), and stimulability across multiple target sounds with cueing.

Family's stated priorities remain appropriate and achievable within the IFSP framework. Continued eligibility for NC Infant-Toddler Program speech-language services confirmed under the established diagnosed condition category.

Social-communication concerns (limited gesture range, solitary play preference at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center) noted; recommend continued monitoring, no referral for additional evaluation at this time given emerging symbolic play and responsiveness to joint-attention routines during session.

Outstanding referral: audiology eval via Dr. Angela Kim's office remains open; service coordinator Jennifer Brooks to follow up on the scheduling barrier, since both parents' work schedules at Eastbrook Poultry Plant and Sparkle Clean Services limit daytime appointment availability.

P:
Outcome 1 (carried forward, revised): Teo will produce 10 functional single words (combined Spanish/English lexicon) across home and daycare settings with no more than mod cues, by next review. Strategy: shared book reading nightly (grandmother Paz Fuentes identified as primary implementer during daytime hours); target word list co-created with family including "sol," "pan," "agua," "perro," "mamá," "papá"; SLP to model simplified cueing hierarchy (min to max) for family and daycare staff (teacher Keisha Mooreland) via joint coaching session. Home practice log to be reviewed at each session for carryover.

Outcome 2 (new): Teo will use 3 consistent gestures (point, wave, nod/shake head) to communicate across 4/5 opportunities by next review. Strategy: PECS-informed visual choice board for home and daycare; family trained on gesture modeling during daily routines (breakfast, bath, play with Sol).

Outcome 3 (new, family priority re: preschool readiness): Family will identify and tour 2 preschool options, including continued Catawba County Early Head Start waitlist status, by next review, supported by service coordinator Jennifer Brooks.

Services continued: Speech-language therapy, CPT 92507, individual, 60 minutes weekly, home-based, bilingual delivery (Spanish/English), provider Maria Elena Gutierrez-Smith, M.S., CCC-SLP, Piedmont Bilingual Speech & Language Partners. Effective dates September 22, 2026 through March 22, 2027.

Developmental/service coordination: ongoing, Jennifer Brooks, Foothills CDSA, monthly contact minimum.

Audiology referral: open, pending scheduling; service coordinator to contact family by October 1, 2026 to assist with appointment logistics, possibly coordinating around Alejandro Cruz's shift schedule at Eastbrook Poultry Plant.

Next IFSP review scheduled March 10, 2027, six-month interval per NC Infant-Toddler Program policy. Annual eligibility redetermination due April 18, 2027 (child's third-birthday transition planning to begin no later than January 18, 2027 per Part C timeline).

Family contact information on file; interpreter services to be requested for all future contacts per family preference (Spanish primary, limited English comprehension for clinical/legal content). Clinician contact: Maria Elena Gutierrez-Smith, mgutierrez-smith@piedmontbilingualslp.com, (828) 555-0199.

Note: target word "sol" was selected deliberately for its high-frequency, early-developing phonetic structure (CVC, stimulable vowel/final consonant). Clinician is aware this is also sister Sol's name and confirmed with the family that this creates no confusion during home practice; family reports they already distinguish "el sol" (the sun) from calling sister Sol by context and will continue to do so during practice sessions.

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT / INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Niño/Child: Mateo Alejandro Fernández Rodríguez ("Teo")
Fecha de nacimiento/DOB: 3 de marzo de 2023 (03/03/2023)
Edad al momento de la evaluación/Age at Evaluation: 3;3
Sexo/Sex: Masculino/Male
Fecha de evaluación/Date of Evaluation: el martes 4 de junio de 2026 and 12 de marzo de 2026
Expediente/Case ID: CDSA-DUR-2026-00589
Medicaid ID: NC4487213J
Dirección/Address: 214 Juniper Hollow Lane, Durham, NC 27703 (Durham County)
Teléfono de contacto/Contact Phone: (919) 555-0148
Correo electrónico/Email: lucia.rodriguez84@example.com
Madre/Mother: Lucía Rodríguez Martínez
Padre/Father: Diego Fernández Castillo
Coordinadora de Servicios/Service Coordinator: Ana Gómez, Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios para la Niñez Temprana "Raíces y Alas" (Raíces y Alas)
Oficina del CDSA/CDSA Office: Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Durham (CDSA de Durham)
Médico que refiere/Referring Physician: Dr. Henry Osei, Pediatría General
Evaluadora/Evaluator: Rebecca A. Hutchins, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Spanish-English Speech-Language Pathologist, Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC

MOTIVO DE REFERENCIA / REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a bilingual speech-language evaluation by Dr. Henry Osei following concerns raised at his 36-month well-child visit regarding limited expressive vocabulary and reduced speech intelligibility in both English and Spanish. His mother, Lucía, reports, "A veces ni yo le entiendo lo que quiere decir, y se frustra mucho" (sometimes even I don't understand what he wants to say, and he gets very frustrated). The family was connected to CDSA de Durham through Raíces y Alas, and the service coordinator, Ana Gómez, completed the intake on 28 de enero de 2026. This evaluation was conducted to determine eligibility for early intervention services under the IFSP and to establish baseline functioning for goal development.

HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA / BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestational age via scheduled cesarean section due to breech presentation. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz (3,040 grams). Apgar scores were 8 at 1 minute and 9 at 5 minutes. Per maternal report, there were no complications during the NICU stay, as Mateo was not admitted to the NICU. He was discharged home on 6 de marzo de 2023.

Developmental milestones were reportedly within normal limits for gross motor skills; he walked independently at 13 months. However, Lucía and Diego both noted that his first words emerged later than expected, around 22 months, and that his vocabulary growth has remained slow relative to his older sister, Camila, who is now 6 years old and attends elementary school.

Medical history is notable for recurrent otitis media, with five documented episodes between March 2024 and December 2025. Mateo underwent bilateral myringotomy with tube placement on 9/15/2025, performed by Dr. Osei's referral to an ENT specialist. Hearing was screened post-tympanostomy and passed bilaterally at 20 dB HL across frequencies, per audiological report dated 10/02/2025. No history of seizures, head trauma, or significant illness was reported. Current ICD-10 diagnostic impression under consideration includes F80.1 (expressive language disorder) and R62.0 (delayed milestones), pending final determination.

Lucía reports that the family's pediatric visits have been consistent, and that Mateo is up to date on immunizations. She also shared that Mateo's abuela, Rosa Martínez, who helps with childcare three days a week while Lucía works, has mentioned similar early language delays in Diego as a child, though no formal diagnosis or services were pursued at that time ("mi esposo también habló tarde, pero nadie hizo nada").

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DEL LENGUAJE / FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo lives at home with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Martínez; his father, Diego Fernández Castillo; his older sister, Camila; and the family dog, Rocky. Lucía works as a medical assistant at Duke Regional Medical Center, and Diego is employed as a site supervisor with Bright Horizons Construction. The family's primary language at home is Spanish, though English is increasingly used, particularly by Camila, who is now fluent in both languages following her enrollment at Hope Valley Elementary School.

According to parent report on a bilingual language history questionnaire, Mateo hears approximately 70% Spanish and 30% English input across his week. His maternal grandmother, Rosa Martínez, speaks exclusively Spanish with him during the three days she provides care. At his daycare, Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pequeños Pasos, his primary teacher, Ms. Carmen Lopez, reports that classroom instruction occurs mostly in English, with some Spanish support provided by an assistant, Ms. Nguyen.

Lucía described Mateo's current expressive output as consisting mostly of single words and some two-word combinations, such as "más agua" and "no quiero." She estimates his expressive vocabulary at approximately 50-75 words combined across both languages, which is significantly below expectations for his age. Comprehension in both languages appears stronger than expression; Lucía reports he follows simple one-step directions in Spanish reliably and is beginning to respond to familiar English phrases such as "come here" and "sit down."

Ms. Lopez shared via a classroom observation note that Mateo often becomes frustrated during group activities and resorts to pulling peers' sleeves or pointing rather than using words, particularly with his classmate Jonas, with whom he frequently plays during free time. She noted, "He wants to tell Jonas something and just can't get it out, so he gets upset."

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN / ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

This evaluation was conducted across two sessions to minimize fatigue and allow for both English and Spanish administration of standardized measures. The first session took place on 12 de marzo de 2026 from 9:15 a.m. to 10:45 a.m. at the CDSA de Durham office located at 1105 Corporate Way, Durham, NC 27703. The second session occurred on el martes 4 de junio de 2026 from 1:30 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. at the family's home. Ana Gómez was present for portions of both sessions in her role as service coordinator.

Procedures administered included:
- Case history interview and bilingual language use questionnaire (parent report)
- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish/English bilingual edition - Auditory Comprehension and Expressive Communication subtests, administered in both languages
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories (CDI), Words and Sentences form, Spanish version, completed by Lucía
- Informal oral mechanism examination
- Language sample analysis, coded using SALT conventions
- Clinical observation of play-based interaction and parent-child communication

OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES / BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo separated easily from Lucía during the clinic-based session and engaged readily with toys presented. He demonstrated functional play skills, including appropriate use of a toy kitchen set and simple pretend sequences (feeding a doll, stirring a pot). Attention to task was adequate for structured activities lasting 8-10 minutes before requiring a break or change in materials.

Socially, Mateo was affectionate and sought proximity to Lucía throughout testing, frequently looking to her for reassurance. He smiled and made eye contact appropriately. When unable to produce a desired word, he was observed to vocalize loudly, point insistently, or physically lead the examiner by the hand to desired items. No repetitive or restricted behaviors were observed. Oral motor structures appeared grossly within normal limits for symmetry, range of motion, and strength during non-speech tasks (blowing bubbles, imitating tongue protrusion).

RESULTADOS / TEST RESULTS

Standardized and informal measures yielded the following results. Confidence intervals and age-equivalent ranges reflect 95% confidence levels per test manual norms.

| Test/Subtest | Language | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% CI | Age Equivalent | Date Administered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | English | 73 | 4th | 68–78 | 2;6–2;9 | 03/12/2026 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication | English | 70 | 2nd | 65–75 | 2;3–2;6 | 03/12/2026 |
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | Spanish | 82 | 12th | 76–88 | 2;9–3;0 | 06/04/2026 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication | Spanish | 79 | 8th | 73–85 | 2;6–2;9 | 06/04/2026 |
| GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words | English | 81 | 10th | 75–87 | 2;9–3;3 | 03/12/2026 |
| CDI Words Produced (Spanish, parent report) | Spanish | n/a | 9th | 5th–15th | 2;0–2;6 | 06/04/2026 |

Composite bilingual functioning, calculated using the conceptual scoring method that credits a concept if produced in either language, yielded an Auditory Comprehension conceptual score corresponding to the 18th percentile and an Expressive Communication conceptual score at the 11th percentile, both of which remain below the 16th percentile cutoff typically used to indicate risk for language impairment in this clinic's bilingual protocol for the expressive domain, though receptive composite scoring approached the typical range.

On the GFTA-3, Mateo demonstrated the following error patterns in English single-word productions: final consonant deletion (e.g., target "dog" produced as [dɑ]), cluster reduction (target "spoon" produced as [pun]), and gliding of liquids (target "red" produced as [wɛd]). In Spanish, informal phonological analysis of a 20-word probe list revealed similar patterns: the target word "pelota" was produced as "[peota]," with deletion of the medial /l/, and "carro" was produced as "[kajo]," substituting [j] for the Spanish tap /ɾ/. These error patterns are consistent across both languages and are not attributable to typical second-language phonological transfer alone, given the degree of inconsistency and the presence of patterns atypical for either monolingual Spanish or English development at this age.

Language sample analysis, coded using SALT conventions, included utterances such as "[EW] mas" (more, with an early word code) and "quiero [EW] 'pelota'" during the home-based play session. Mean length of utterance in morphemes (MLU-m) was calculated at 1.4 across the combined 50-utterance sample, which falls well below the expected MLU-m of 2.5–3.0 for a typically developing child at 3;3.

During a structured naming task, Mateo correctly labeled 8 of 20 familiar objects presented in English (40%) and 13 of 20 in Spanish (65%), suggesting stronger single-word retrieval in his home language. He required moderate cues (mod cues) to imitate two-word phrases and maximum cues (max cues), including full verbal and gestural modeling, to attempt three-word combinations. With minimal cues (min cues), he successfully imitated the target phrase "quiero más," producing "[kjejo ma]."

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS / CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized assessment results, parent report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a Developmental Language Disorder affecting both receptive and expressive domains, with expressive language more significantly impacted, present across both of his languages, Spanish and English. His scores fall below the eligible range on standardized bilingual measures in at least one domain, and his performance is consistent with a true language disorder rather than typical bilingual language development, given that deficits are observed across both languages rather than confined to the language of lesser exposure.

Concurrently, Mateo demonstrates a moderate speech sound disorder characterized by phonological error patterns that cross both languages, including final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, gliding, and liquid distortion. Given his documented history of recurrent otitis media with effusion and subsequent tympanostomy tube placement, a component of his speech-language delay may be attributable to fluctuating conductive hearing loss during a critical period of early phonological and lexical development; however, the persistence of errors following resolution of middle ear pathology (confirmed by passing audiological screening on 10/02/2025) suggests that hearing history alone does not fully account for his current profile.

Mateo's pragmatic communication skills, including joint attention, social reciprocity, and functional play, appear to be developing appropriately relative to his language level, and no concerns regarding autism spectrum features were identified during this evaluation. His frustration behaviors (pulling, pointing, vocalizing) appear secondary to limited expressive language rather than indicative of a primary behavioral or social-communication disorder.

RECOMENDACIONES / RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo meets eligibility criteria for early intervention services under Part C through CDSA de Durham, based on standardized scores falling more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean in the expressive language domain across both languages.

2. It is recommended that Mateo receive individual speech-language therapy services a minimum of two times per week for 45-minute sessions, delivered bilingually to support development in both Spanish and English, consistent with current best-practice guidance for bilingual language learners with a true language disorder.

3. Therapy should incorporate a combination of naturalistic, parent-coaching approaches, including principles from the Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" program, alongside more structured motor-based approaches such as PROMPT to address the speech sound errors noted above. A Cycles phonological approach is also recommended to target the cluster reduction and final consonant deletion patterns identified in both languages.

4. Lucía and Diego should be included as active participants in therapy sessions and coached in strategies to expand Mateo's utterances at home, with specific emphasis on modeling two- and three-word combinations in Spanish, the family's primary language.

5. Continued monitoring of hearing status is recommended given the history of recurrent otitis media; a repeat audiological evaluation is suggested within 6 months if further ear infections occur.

6. Coordination with Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pequeños Pasos staff, including Ms. Lopez, is recommended to ensure consistent use of simplified language models and visual supports across environments.

7. These findings and recommendations should be incorporated into Mateo's Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) at the upcoming review meeting. Proposed outcomes include Outcome 1: Mateo will use two-to-three-word combinations to request desired items and actions across settings; and Outcome 2: Mateo will produce target sounds in word-initial position with 80% accuracy with no more than min cues across both languages.

8. A follow-up IFSP review meeting should be scheduled within 90 days of service initiation to monitor progress toward these outcomes.

This evaluation was billed under CPT code 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression) with modifier -22 applied to reflect the extended bilingual administration time required across two sessions.

Lucía and Diego were present for feedback at the conclusion of the second session and expressed agreement with the findings and recommendations. Lucía stated, "Gracias por explicarlo todo, ahora entendemos mejor por qué se frustra tanto." Ana Gómez will coordinate scheduling of the IFSP review meeting and connect the family with service providers within the Raíces y Alas network.

SUNRISE PEDIATRIC THERAPY CLINIC (EMPLOYER)
Sunrise Pediatric Therapy Clinic
214 Birchwood Lane, Suite 3, Maple Grove, NC 27591
Phone: 919-555-0148 | Fax: 919-555-0149

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Flores Nuñez ("Teo")
Date of Birth: February 14, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Evaluation Dates: April 9, 2026 and April 16, 2026
Report Date: April 22, 2026
Record Number: SP-20394
Medicaid ID: 503218764A
County of Residence: Piedmont County

Parents/Guardians: Lucía Rodríguez Flores (mother), Carlos Flores Medina (father)
Home Address: 214 Birchwood Lane, Maple Grove, NC 27591
Home Phone: 919-555-0172
Mother's Email: lucia.rflores88@mailbasket.com

Referring Pediatrician: Dr. Angela Stewart, Carolina Pines Medical Center Pediatrics
Evaluating Clinician: Jennifer Marsh, M.S., CCC-SLP
Spanish Language Interpreter: Patricia Núñez, Certified Medical Interpreter
Service Coordinator: Brenda Hall, Piedmont County Children's Developmental Services Agency

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo ("Teo") is a 4;2-year-old bilingual (Spanish/English) boy referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Angela Stewart following a well-child visit in which his parents, Lucía Rodríguez Flores and Carlos Flores Medina, raised concerns about unclear speech, limited expressive vocabulary in both languages, and difficulty being understood by unfamiliar listeners, including his teachers at Little Sprouts Daycare. This evaluation was completed with the assistance of interpreter Patricia Núñez to support full participation of both parents, whose primary language is Spanish. Teo is currently enrolled in the Infant-Toddler Program through Piedmont County Children's Developmental Services Agency and receives occupational therapy services; this evaluation was requested to determine eligibility for speech-language services under his Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP), with a review scheduled for May 1, 2026.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Teo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Carolina Pines Medical Center via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Birth weight was 6 lbs 9 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. Lucía Rodríguez Flores reported an uneventful pregnancy with routine prenatal care. Teo experienced three episodes of otitis media between 8 months and 18 months of age, treated with antibiotics; a pressure-equalizing tube placement was recommended by his pediatrician but was not ultimately pursued after a follow-up hearing screening at 22 months returned within normal limits. He has no history of seizures, significant illness, or hospitalization beyond birth. Gross and fine motor milestones were reported as age-appropriate, though occupational therapy was initiated at 30 months to address mild fine motor delays and sensory sensitivities, provided by Megan Price, OTR/L. A physical therapy consultation with David Chen, PT, DPT, at 3 years of age ruled out any gross motor concerns, and Teo was discharged from physical therapy services after two sessions.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Teo lives at home with his parents, Lucía Rodríguez Flores and Carlos Flores Medina, and his older sister, Valentina Flores, age 7. The family reports that Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home, with English introduced through Little Sprouts Daycare and extended family interactions. Lucía Rodríguez Flores works part-time at Carver Textile Mills, and Carlos Flores Medina works full-time as a delivery driver. The family's regular childcare support includes Rosa Guzmán, a family friend who provides after-school babysitting several days per week, and frequent visits from Teo's cousins, Diego Ramírez and Sofía Ramírez, who live nearby and speak primarily Spanish. Lucía Rodríguez Flores reported that Teo is very attached to the family dog, Rocky, and frequently narrates the dog's activities during play.

Developmental language milestones were reported as mildly delayed: first words around 16 months, two-word combinations around 28 months. Both parents denied any family history of speech, language, or learning disorders, though Carlos Flores Medina noted that he himself was a "late talker" as a child. Lucía Rodríguez Flores reported that unfamiliar adults and even some family members, including Rosa Guzmán, frequently ask Teo to repeat himself. At Little Sprouts Daycare, his primary teacher, Ms. Hannah Lopez, and the assistant teacher, Mr. Dawson, both report that Teo is social and well-liked by peers but is sometimes left out of pretend play with classmates Ethan and Ava because they struggle to understand his requests.

During the session, Teo pointed to a photograph of his dog and said, "Rocky run," reducing the final consonants in both words, consistent with phonological process patterns noted below.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

The following standardized and informal measures were administered across two sessions, in both English and Spanish as appropriate, with interpretation support from Patricia Núñez:

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English and Spanish editions
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF-P3)
- Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Phonology subtest
- Oral-motor examination
- Language sample analysis (spontaneous speech, both languages)
- Parent interview and classroom observation at Little Sprouts Daycare

TEST RESULTS

Test/Subtest	Standard Score	Percentile	Confidence Interval	Date Administered
PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension	76	5th	70-82	April 9, 2026
PLS-5 Expressive Communication	71	3rd	65-77	April 9, 2026
PLS-5 Total Language Score	72	3rd	67-77	April 9, 2026
CELF-P3 Core Language Score	74	4th	69-79	April 16, 2026
GFTA-3 Standard Score	68	2nd	62-74	April 16, 2026
BESA Phonology Score	70	2nd	63-77	April 16, 2026

Age equivalent scores on the PLS-5 placed Teo's receptive language skills at approximately 2;6–3;0 and expressive language skills at approximately 2;3–2;9, representing a significant delay relative to his chronological age of 4;2.

ARTICULATION AND PHONOLOGY

Oral-motor examination revealed adequate structure and function of the oral mechanism, with mild reduced diadochokinetic rate noted. Connected speech intelligibility was estimated at approximately 40% for unfamiliar listeners and 65% for familiar listeners, including his parents and teachers.

Phonological process analysis identified consistent patterns of final consonant deletion (e.g., "ca" for target "cat"), cluster reduction (e.g., "poon" for target "spoon"), and fronting of velar sounds (e.g., substitution of /t/ for /k/, as in "tootie" for target "cookie"). Gliding of liquids was also noted, with [w] substituted for /ɾ/ in Spanish productions, such as "cawo" for target "carro." These patterns were consistent across both English and Spanish samples, supporting a diagnosis of a primary speech sound disorder rather than a feature of typical bilingual phonological development.

During structured probes, Teo produced target words with 8/10 accuracy (80%) when given moderate cueing (mod cues) for single syllable CV and CVC words, but accuracy dropped to 3 of 10 (30%) for multisyllabic words without support. With maximal cueing (max cues), accuracy on multisyllabic targets improved to 7/10 (70%).

LANGUAGE SAMPLE

A 50-utterance spontaneous language sample was collected in both English and Spanish during structured play. Mean length of utterance was 2.8 morphemes in English and 3.1 morphemes in Spanish, both below expected ranges for his age. Teo relied heavily on gesture and single-word utterances to communicate needs, and was coded using SALT conventions where overgeneralized word forms were marked [EW]. He demonstrated emerging use of early semantic relations (agent + action, e.g., "Teo go") but limited use of grammatical morphemes, including plural -s, past tense -ed, and copula "is/está."

IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Teo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder and a moderate speech sound disorder affecting intelligibility in both English and Spanish. His difficulties are consistent across both languages, confirming a primary disorder rather than second-language acquisition variability. This is consistent with a diagnosis of F80.2 (Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder). His reduced intelligibility, phonological process patterns, and delayed grammatical development are significantly impacting his functional communication at home, at Little Sprouts Daycare, and in social interactions with peers such as Ethan and Ava.

Teo qualifies for speech-language services under North Carolina's Infant-Toddler Program eligibility criteria based on a delay of 25% or greater in two developmental domains. His current OT services with Megan Price should continue concurrently, as sensory and fine motor factors may be contributing to feeding and oral-motor coordination patterns relevant to speech production.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Teo is recommended for individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, targeting phonological awareness, articulation accuracy, and expressive/receptive language in both English and Spanish, using a bilingual service delivery model.

2. Recommended therapy approaches include Cycles phonological approach for the targeted phonological processes, and principles from Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" to support caregiver-implemented language strategies at home. A trial of PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing may also be considered given the oral-motor component of his presentation.

3. Billing for individual treatment sessions should use CPT code 92507 (treatment of speech, language, voice, communication, and/or auditory processing disorder, individual). Sessions incorporating evaluation of swallowing or oral-motor function may additionally use CPT code 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression).

4. Continued coordination with Megan Price (occupational therapy), Dr. Angela Stewart (pediatrician), and service coordinator Brenda Hall is recommended to support an integrated IFSP, with the next formal review scheduled for May 1, 2026.

5. Parent coaching sessions with Lucía Rodríguez Flores and Carlos Flores Medina are recommended monthly to reinforce home carryover strategies, with interpreter Patricia Núñez present as needed.

6. A hearing re-screening is recommended given his history of recurrent otitis media, to rule out any fluctuating conductive component contributing to his language delay.

PROPOSED SESSION SCHEDULE

Day	Start Time	End Time	Location
Monday	9:30 AM	10:15 AM	Sunrise Pediatric Therapy Clinic, Room 2
Wednesday	2:00 PM	2:45 PM	Little Sprouts Daycare, Maple Grove
Friday	9:30 AM	10:15 AM	Sunrise Pediatric Therapy Clinic, Room 2

CARE TEAM CONTACTS

Name	Role	Phone	Email
Jennifer Marsh, M.S., CCC-SLP	Speech-Language Pathologist	919-555-0148	jmarsh@sunrisepedtherapy.com
Megan Price, OTR/L	Occupational Therapist	919-555-0163	mprice@sunrisepedtherapy.com
David Chen, PT, DPT	Physical Therapist	919-555-0190	dchen@carolinapinespt.com
Dr. Angela Stewart	Pediatrician	919-555-0211	astewart@carolinapinesmc.com
Brenda Hall	Service Coordinator	919-555-0237	bhall@piedmontcdsa.gov
Patricia Núñez	Interpreter	919-555-0254	pnunez@interpretlink.com

TRANSITION AND SCHOOL PLANNING

As Teo approaches kindergarten eligibility, the family has indicated interest in enrolling him at Maple Grove Elementary School for the 2027–2028 school year. It is recommended that a transition meeting be held approximately six months prior to his anticipated start date, including Lucía Rodríguez Flores, Carlos Flores Medina, Brenda Hall, and school-based speech-language staff, to ensure continuity of services and appropriate evaluation for school-based eligibility under IDEA criteria. Given his sister Valentina Flores's positive experience at the same school, the family is hopeful that a similar support structure can be established for Teo.

SUMMARY

Mateo Alejandro Flores Nuñez presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder and moderate speech sound disorder impacting intelligibility and functional communication across English and Spanish. Services are recommended twice weekly at 92507/92523 billing codes, with continued interdisciplinary coordination among Jennifer Marsh, Megan Price, David Chen, Dr. Angela Stewart, and Piedmont County Children's Developmental Services Agency. Caregiver involvement, including with Lucía Rodríguez Flores, Carlos Flores Medina, and extended support from Rosa Guzmán, will be essential to generalization of skills across home, daycare, and community settings.

Report prepared by:
Jennifer Marsh, M.S., CCC-SLP
Sunrise Pediatric Therapy Clinic
