Phonemic inventory limited; stimulable for /t/ and /d/ with mod cues; consistently produces "mo" for "more" and "ba" for "bottle."
Oral-motor screening noted reduced lateral tongue movement and gagging on textured solids, consistent with earlier parent report.

IFSP OUTCOMES

Outcome 1: Majo will use 2-word combinations to request and comment during daily routines, so her family and caregivers can understand her without guessing.
Strategies: Parents will implement Hanen It Takes Two to Talk strategies (OWL: Observe, Wait, Listen) during mealtime and bath. Ana Beltrán will coach Lucía Hernández Ramos and Luz Ramos in bilingual expansion techniques during home visits, since Luz Ramos is the primary midday caregiver. Direct therapy will incorporate PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing to support jaw and lip placement for early consonant-vowel combinations.
Criteria: 4 of 5 observed opportunities per session with no more than mod cues.
Start Date: October 20, 2026          Projected Review: April 20, 2027

Outcome 2: Majo will reduce frustration-related behaviors (throwing, hitting) during communication breakdowns by using a functional communication alternative.
Strategies: Introduce a core-vocabulary PECS board with 12 symbols covering preferred foods, activities, and people, including photos of Sol and Luz Ramos. Majo's phonological system will also be addressed through a Cycles approach, targeting final consonant deletion and stopping of fricatives in alternating two-week cycles. Family will be given a simplified home card deck in Spanish to reinforce PECS use with extended family at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida nursery staff.
Criteria: Decrease in reported tantrum frequency from daily to 3 of 7 days per week, per parent log.
Start Date: October 20, 2026          Projected Review: April 20, 2027

Outcome 3: Majo will improve speech sound accuracy and oral-motor planning to support intelligibility, given suspected features of childhood apraxia of speech.
Strategies: Trial of the Kaufman Speech to Praxis Kit, beginning with level 1 single-syllable targets, paired with high-frequency drill in both English and Spanish target words. Ana Beltrán will monitor for carryover of "up," "hi," and "bye" across settings, including reports from Luz Ramos and Óscar Flores Castillo.
Criteria: 8/10 accuracy on trained targets across two consecutive sessions.
Start Date: November 3, 2026          Projected Review: April 20, 2027

Outcome 4: Majo will tolerate and chew a wider variety of textured table foods during family meals.
Strategies: Oral-motor desensitization activities embedded into daily mealtime; coordination with Caldwell County WIC nutritionist for food texture progression guidance; family to track tolerated textures in a shared log reviewed at each visit.
Criteria: Tolerates 3 of 5 presented textured foods without gagging, across two consecutive weeks.
Start Date: November 3, 2026          Projected Review: April 20, 2027

text:
+ Nombre: Mateo Fernández Rodríguez
+ Apodo: Mateín
+ Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de marzo de 2024
+ EC: 1;6
+ Número de expediente: RM-2024-0317B
+ Número de Medicaid: MD4471982K
+ Contexto: Revisión semestral del Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP), realizada el martes 4 de junio de 2025 en el hogar de la familia, ubicado en 214 Calle Olmo, Rivermont, Condado de Rivermont, y en el salón de terapia de Little Learners Program. Participaron la madre, Lucía Rodríguez; el padre, Carlos Fernández; la coordinadora de servicios, Mónica Reyes, del CDSA de Rivermont; y la patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe, Laura Jiménez, M.S., CCC-SLP, de Carolina Pediatric Therapy Group.

Resumen:

Mateo es un niño de 1;6 que reside con su madre, Lucía Rodríguez; su padre, Carlos Fernández; y su hermana mayor, Sol, de 4 años, en Rivermont, Condado de Rivermont. La familia es de origen mexicano y el español es el idioma principal del hogar; Lucía indica que entiende algo de inglés pero prefiere recibir todos los servicios en español, y Carlos prefiere lo mismo. Mateo fue referido al Programa de Carolina del Norte para Bebés y Niños Pequeños (NC Infant-Toddler Program) el 10 de septiembre de 2024 por su pediatra, el Dr. Esteban Vargas, debido a preocupaciones sobre el desarrollo del lenguaje, la alimentación y un posible retraso motor leve. Esta visita documenta la segunda revisión del IFSP desde la calificación inicial y resume el progreso, las preocupaciones actuales de la familia y los resultados actualizados.

**Historia de nacimiento y médica**

Mateo nació el 14 de marzo de 2024 (14-03-2024) en el Hospital Memorial de Rivermont, con una edad gestacional de 34 semanas y un peso al nacer de 1,980 gramos. Los puntajes de Apgar fueron de 6 al minuto y 8 a los cinco minutos. El embarazo estuvo marcado por preeclampsia materna, lo cual motivó el parto prematuro por cesárea de emergencia. Mateo pasó 18 días en la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos Neonatales (NICU) del Hospital Memorial de Rivermont bajo el cuidado de la neonatóloga, la Dra. Patricia Núñez, por dificultad respiratoria transitoria e ictericia neonatal que requirió fototerapia. Durante su estancia en la NICU recibió alimentación por sonda nasogástrica debido a succión-deglución-respiración descoordinada, patrón común en bebés prematuros. Fue dado de alta el 1 de abril de 2024 (04/01/2024) con seguimiento ambulatorio a cargo del Dr. Esteban Vargas, pediatra de cabecera en Rivermont, y con referido a audiología de seguimiento, la cual resultó normal en ambos oídos según timpanometría y otoemisiones acústicas realizadas el 2 de mayo de 2024.

No se reportan otras hospitalizaciones importantes, aunque Mateo fue visto en la sala de emergencias el 12/22/2024 por una infección de oído (otitis media aguda, código H66.90), tratada con antibióticos orales sin complicaciones. Tiene además antecedentes de reflujo gastroesofágico (código K21.9), actualmente manejado con modificación de dieta, espesante en los líquidos y posición vertical después de las comidas, según indicación del Dr. Esteban Vargas. Lucía reporta que un primo paterno tuvo "un retraso para hablar" en la niñez que se resolvió sin intervención, pero no se identifican otros antecedentes familiares de trastornos del habla, lenguaje o audición de importancia.

**Coordinación de servicios y agencia designada**

El caso de Mateo es coordinado por Mónica Reyes, coordinadora de servicios del CDSA de Rivermont (Centro de Desarrollo Infantil y Familiar), ubicado en 820 Avenida del Parque, Rivermont. Se le puede contactar al (336) 555-0148 o por correo electrónico a mreyes@cdsarivermont.org. La evaluación multidisciplinaria inicial que calificó a Mateo para el Programa de Bebés y Niños Pequeños se realizó el 3 de octubre de 2024, y el IFSP inicial se firmó el 17 de octubre de 2024 (2024-10-17). La primera revisión de seis meses ocurrió el 5 de diciembre de 2024; esta visita del 4 de junio de 2025 corresponde a la segunda revisión programada, conforme al calendario establecido por el CDSA de Rivermont.

**Preocupaciones y prioridades de la familia**

Durante la entrevista familiar, Lucía expresó lo siguiente, en sus propias palabras: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Mateo todavía no dice ninguna palabra clara. Mi sobrina a esta edad ya decía 'mamá' y 'agua', y él solo hace sonidos." Carlos añadió: "También nos preocupa cómo come. Se atraganta con ciertas texturas y a veces tarda una hora en terminar de comer. Nos da miedo que se vaya a ahogar." Lucía también comentó sobre la interacción social de su hijo: "En la guardería dicen que juega solo casi todo el tiempo. Queremos que juegue con los demás niños."

La familia identificó las siguientes prioridades para esta revisión:

1. Que Mateo aprenda a usar palabras o señas para pedir cosas que quiere, como comida, agua o un juguete.
2. Que mejore la tolerancia a texturas variadas durante las comidas, para reducir el riesgo de arcadas y acortar el tiempo de las comidas.
3. Que la familia reciba estrategias en español que puedan usar en casa, y que el personal de Little Learners Daycare pueda reforzar las mismas estrategias durante el día.
4. Que Mateo participe más con otros niños durante el juego en la guardería.

Lucía también mencionó: "Yo quiero que cuando Mateo empiece a hablar, hable los dos idiomas, español e inglés, como su hermana Sol." La familia fue tranquilizada de que el desarrollo bilingüe no causa ni empeora los retrasos del lenguaje, y que el equipo fomentará activamente el uso continuo del español en el hogar mientras se introduce el inglés de manera gradual en la guardería.

**Rutinas diarias**

Mateo asiste a Little Learners Daycare de lunes a viernes, de 7:30 a.m. a 5:00 p.m., mientras Lucía trabaja como auxiliar administrativa en Piedmont Furniture Supply y Carlos trabaja en construcción con un contratista local. Su maestra en la sala de bebés es la Sra. Ivonne Castillo, quien reporta que Mateo disfruta de la hora de música y de los juegos con pelotas, pero se frustra fácilmente cuando otro niño, Derek, le quita un juguete, y responde llorando o empujando en lugar de usar palabras o gestos. La Sra. Castillo también observó que Mateo prefiere jugar cerca de los adultos más que con sus compañeros, Derek y Sofía, durante el tiempo de juego libre.

En casa, la rutina matutina incluye el desayuno a las 6:45 a.m., seguido de que Carlos lo lleve a la guardería antes de ir al trabajo. Por las tardes, Lucía lo recoge alrededor de las 5:15 p.m. y la familia cena junta a las 6:30 p.m.. La hora de dormir es hacia las 8:00 p.m., con una rutina consistente de baño, lectura de cuentos y canciones de cuna en español. Los fines de semana, la familia frecuentemente visita a la abuela materna, Dolores Rodríguez, quien vive a pocas cuadras y a veces cuida a Mateo y a Sol cuando los padres trabajan horas extra. Dolores habla con Mateo principalmente en español y, según reporta Lucía, ya ha comenzado a reforzar el uso de gestos para pedir cosas, siguiendo las sugerencias de la terapia anterior.

Durante las comidas, Mateo muestra una marcada preferencia por alimentos suaves y en puré; se atraganta con alimentos de textura mixta, como la sopa con trozos de verdura, y rechaza por completo los alimentos crujientes, como las galletas saladas. La familia ha estado trabajando en casa con las estrategias de posicionamiento y presentación gradual de alimentos recomendadas en la visita anterior, con mejoría parcial mencionada por ambos padres.

**Otras agencias y servicios comunitarios**

Además de los servicios del Programa de Bebés y Niños Pequeños, la familia recibe apoyo de varias agencias comunitarias en el Condado de Rivermont:

- El Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Rivermont (DSS) ayuda a la familia con un subsidio de cuidado infantil y con el proceso de renovación de Medicaid, gestionado por la trabajadora social Teresa Ocampo.
- El programa WIC del Condado de Rivermont provee fórmula especializada y consejería nutricional; la familia asiste a citas mensuales con la nutricionista, Beatriz Salinas, quien también ha dado recomendaciones sobre texturas apropiadas para la edad de Mateo.
- Smart Start del Condado de Rivermont financia parcialmente la matrícula de Mateo en Little Learners Daycare a través de una subvención de calidad de cuidado infantil, lo cual ha permitido que la familia mantenga el cupo a pesar de ingresos limitados.
- La familia también fue referida a Early Head Start para el próximo ciclo escolar, con la posibilidad de que Mateo reciba servicios combinados de educación temprana e intervención.

Lucía expresó gratitud por el apoyo de estas agencias, pero mencionó que a veces es difícil coordinar las citas: "Siento que tengo cuatro trabajos diferentes nada más llenando papeles y yendo de una oficina a otra." La coordinadora de servicios, Mónica Reyes, ofreció ayudar a sincronizar las fechas de las próximas citas con DSS y WIC para reducir la carga administrativa de la familia.

**Evaluación actual y progreso**

En esta revisión se administró la Escala Rossetti de Lenguaje Infantil (Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale), obteniendo Mateo un desempeño correspondiente a una edad equivalente de 9-11 meses en el área de lenguaje expresivo y 12-14 meses en el área de lenguaje receptivo, en comparación con su edad cronológica de 1;6. Se observó que usa 3 gestos consistentes (señalar, levantar los brazos, negar con la cabeza) y produce aproximadamente 5 vocalizaciones consonante-vocal, incluyendo algo similar a "mamá" dirigido inconsistentemente hacia Lucía. En una muestra de juego de 15 minutos, produjo 2 de 10 intentos de imitación verbal exitosos, y en una tarea estructurada logró 70% de respuestas correctas a instrucciones simples de un paso (por ejemplo, "dame" y "ven"). También se observó un repertorio de fonemas limitado a /m/, /p/ y /a/, sin producción consistente de /t/ o /k/ en ninguna posición.

Durante la evaluación de alimentación, realizada conjuntamente con terapia ocupacional, se observó un patrón de masticación inmaduro y una respuesta de arcada con texturas mixtas; no se observaron signos manifiestos de aspiración, aunque, por protocolo estándar del programa, la familia fue referida a una evaluación formal de deglución con un terapeuta ocupacional especializado en alimentación pediátrica.

Comparado con la evaluación inicial del 3 de octubre de 2024, en la que Mateo obtuvo una edad equivalente de 6-8 meses en lenguaje expresivo, se observa un progreso de aproximadamente dos a tres meses de desarrollo en ocho meses de intervención, lo cual indica una tasa de progreso más lenta que la esperada para la edad y apoya la continuación de servicios intensivos de habla y lenguaje, así como la adición de terapia de alimentación.

**Resultados del IFSP (outcomes) y estrategias**

Resultado 1: Mateo usará al menos 10 señas o gestos funcionales de manera consistente para pedir objetos, comida o actividades preferidas, en al menos 8 de 10 oportunidades observadas, para la próxima revisión.
Estrategias: Implementar comunicación aumentativa basada en gestos siguiendo el enfoque de Hanen ("It Takes Two to Talk"), con modelado de señas simples durante las rutinas de comida y juego. La familia continuará además con el programa PROMPT para apoyar la producción motriz del habla, introducido en la sesión del 15 de mayo de 2025, con énfasis en las aproximaciones a "mamá" y "más".

Resultado 2: Mateo tolerará al menos 5 texturas de alimentos variadas (incluyendo purés espesos, alimentos machacados y pequeños trozos suaves) sin arcadas, en 4 de 5 comidas observadas.
Estrategias: La terapeuta ocupacional y la patóloga del habla y lenguaje colaborarán en sesiones conjuntas de alimentación una vez por semana en Little Learners Program, usando un protocolo de desensibilización oral y progresión gradual de texturas, con seguimiento semanal del peso en coordinación con el Dr. Esteban Vargas.

Resultado 3: La familia reportará el uso de al menos 3 estrategias de lenguaje (expansión, pausa expectante y narración paralela) durante las rutinas diarias, según lo registrado en un diario familiar semanal.
Estrategias: Sesiones de capacitación familiar en español, coordinadas por Laura Jiménez, con material visual y práctica en vivo durante las comidas y el juego. Se reforzará también con el personal de Little Learners Daycare, quienes recibirán una breve orientación sobre las estrategias usadas en terapia, con el permiso firmado por la familia para compartir información.

Resultado 4: Mateo iniciará interacción con al menos un compañero durante el juego estructurado en la guardería, en al menos 3 ocasiones por semana, según observación de la maestra.
Estrategias: La maestra, Sra. Ivonne Castillo, implementará actividades de juego paralelo guiado entre Mateo y sus compañeros, Derek y Sofía, con apoyo visual, modelado de turnos y reforzamiento positivo inmediato.

**Frecuencia y ubicación de los servicios**

Mateo continuará recibiendo terapia de habla y lenguaje dos veces por semana, en sesiones de 45 minutos, en Little Learners Program, bajo la autorización AUTH-33920R. La terapia ocupacional para alimentación se agregará una vez por semana, también de 45 minutos, iniciando el 9 de junio de 2025 (09/06/2025). Los servicios continuarán facturándose bajo los códigos 92507 y 92526, con el modificador GN para servicios de habla y lenguaje, y bajo el código 97165 para la evaluación inicial de terapia ocupacional.

**Plan de transición**

La próxima revisión del IFSP está programada para el 3 de diciembre de 2025, y la evaluación anual completa se realizará antes del 17/10/2025. Se recomienda que la familia continúe el contacto regular con la coordinadora de servicios, Mónica Reyes, para iniciar la planificación de la transición a servicios preescolares cuando Mateo cumpla 3 años. Dicho proceso debe comenzar formalmente al menos noventa días antes de su cumpleaños número 3, de acuerdo con las políticas de transición del NC Infant-Toddler Program, e incluirá una evaluación de elegibilidad para servicios de educación especial preescolar a través del sistema escolar local.

**Firma**

Documento preparado por Laura Jiménez, M.S., CCC-SLP, patóloga bilingüe del habla y lenguaje, Carolina Pediatric Therapy Group, el 4 de junio de 2025. Revisado y aprobado por la coordinadora de servicios, Mónica Reyes, CDSA de Rivermont. Copia proporcionada a la familia y al pediatra de referencia, Dr. Esteban Vargas.

text:
INDIVIDUALIZED FAMILY SERVICE PLAN (IFSP) — ANNUAL REVIEW
North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program

Child: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Hernandez ("Teo")
Date of Birth: April 9, 2024
Medicaid ID: 8827451903B
IFSP Case ID: ITP-40217
CDSA Office: CDSA of Mecklenburg County
Review Date: October 6, 2026
Previous IFSP Date: October 2, 2025

Family Address: 4418 Tuckaseegee Road, Charlotte, Mecklenburg County, 28208
Home Phone: (704) 555-0198
Parent Email: lucia.rodriguez0409@gmail.com

Family Members:
Mother: Lucia Rodriguez
Father: Jorge Cruz
Brother: Jesus Cruz Jr., known to the family as "Chuy," age 6
Maternal grandmother: Maria Guadalupe Hernandez, called "Lupita" by Teo's cousins and known to the family as doña Lupe

Service Coordinator: Mr. Tom (Thomas Whitfield), CDSA of Mecklenburg County
Phone: (704) 555-0142

Report prepared by: Ana Beatriz Solorzano, MS, CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist, Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners

Background

Teo was born at 32 weeks gestation (birth weight 3 lb 9 oz, Apgar 6/9) and spent 19 days in the NICU at Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital, Myers Park Campus. He was later seen for recurrent otitis media at Novant Health Pediatric ENT & Audiology, Ballantyne Campus, where tympanostomy tubes were placed at 14 months. His pediatrician, Dr. Amit Patel of Mint Hill Pediatric Clinic, referred the family to the CDSA of Mecklenburg County after a well-child visit flagged delayed expressive language. Early intervention eligibility was confirmed, and a first IFSP was written when Teo was 16 months old.

At intake, the family was also connected with Centro de Desarrollo Infantil y Servicios para la Familia Hispana (CDISFH), a community-based agency serving Spanish-speaking families in Mecklenburg County. CDISFH continues to provide parent support groups and has helped the family apply for WIC and for respite childcare through Smart Start of Mecklenburg County. Lucia Rodriguez reports that CDISFH staff were the first to explain, in Spanish, what an IFSP is and what services the family could expect.

Teo has an ICD-10 diagnosis of F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) and attends speech-language therapy twice weekly, billed under CPT 92507 (individual treatment) and CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production and language). His most recent PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension standard score was 78 (7th percentile); Expressive Communication standard score was 73 (4th percentile), both within the 73-83 range expected given his history of chronic ear infections.

Family Concerns and Priorities

During the review meeting on October 6, 2026 at 9:30 a.m., Lucia Rodriguez shared, through interpreter Marisol Garcia, that her top priority is for Teo to be understood by his daycare teacher, la maestra Carmen, and by his classmates without his older brother Chuy having to translate for him. She said, "Quiero que Teo pueda pedir lo que necesita sin frustrarse" (I want Teo to be able to ask for what he needs without getting frustrated). Jorge Cruz added that he wants Teo to be ready for kindergarten registration next year and worries about his son being teased by a neighbor boy, Juanito, who sometimes mimics Teo's speech at the playground.

The family also asked that services continue to be delivered bilingually, noting that doña Lupe primarily speaks Spanish and provides childcare three afternoons a week while Lucia Rodriguez works at Compass Group Foodservice and Jorge Cruz works evening shifts in environmental services at Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center. Both parents stated they want written materials and home practice sheets in English and Spanish.

Daily Routines

Teo wakes around 7:00 a.m. and eats breakfast with his brother Chuy before daycare drop-off at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare on West Boulevard. Afternoons are spent with doña Lupe or with the family babysitter, Miss Ana, who picks him up most Tuesdays and Thursdays and stays until 5:30 p.m.. Evenings include dinner as a family, bath time, and a bedtime routine with picture books that Lucia Rodriguez reads in both English and Spanish. The family dog, Canela, often sits with Teo during story time, which Lucia Rodriguez reports helps him stay calm and attentive. On weekends the family often visits relatives, where Teo plays with his cousin, nicknamed "Pepe."

Other Agencies and Services

In addition to CDISFH and Smart Start of Mecklenburg County, the family receives nutrition support through WIC and has an open case with Mecklenburg County Department of Social Services for housing assistance. Teo's audiology follow-up remains with Novant Health Pediatric ENT & Audiology, Ballantyne Campus, with the next hearing recheck scheduled for January 14, 2027.

Present Levels of Development

Cognitive: Age-appropriate per the Bayley-4, age equivalent 24 months at chronological age 2;6.

Communication: Teo uses single words and some two-word combinations. During the evaluation session he produced "wawa" for water and "baba" for bottle; the target production "more please" was modeled with moderate cues and he imitated it correctly 8/10 trials (80% accuracy). He uses /m/, /b/, /p/ consistently but omits /k/ and /g/ in final position, producing "duh" for "duck."

Social-emotional: Teo enjoys parallel play with his cousin Jose Luis Martinez, nicknamed "Pepe," during weekend family gatherings, but becomes frustrated when peers at daycare, including Juanito, do not understand his requests.

Adaptive/Motor: Within normal limits; no concerns reported by la maestra Carmen or by the family.

Outcomes and Strategies

Outcome 1: Teo will use three- to four-word phrases to request items and comment during play, increasing from his current 2;6 expressive age equivalent toward an age equivalent of 3;0, measured by PLS-5 rescore.
Strategy: Continue twice-weekly individual therapy (CPT 92507) using the Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" approach; caregiver coaching for Lucia Rodriguez, Jorge Cruz, and doña Lupe on expansion and modeling during daily routines.

Outcome 2: Teo will produce final consonants /k/ and /g/ in single words with 80% accuracy across three consecutive sessions.
Strategy: Cycles phonological approach targeting final velars; home practice list sent in both English and Spanish for use by doña Lupe and Miss Ana.

Outcome 3: Teo will be understood by unfamiliar listeners, including classmates at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare, 3 of 5 opportunities during structured activities.
Strategy: Classroom consultation with la maestra Carmen; visual supports and a core vocabulary board introduced at daycare and reinforced at home.

Service Delivery

text:
Nombre del niño: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Fernández ("Teo")    Fecha de nacimiento: 15 de enero de 2024    Edad actual: 2;3

Expediente CDSA: PT-440219    Número de Medicaid: 920481773N    Idioma del hogar: español e inglés

Dirección: 2318 Calle Primrose, Charlotte, Condado de Mecklenburg, NC 28205    Teléfono de contacto: (704) 555-0192

Madre: Lucía Fernández Ramos    Padre: Carlos Cruz Delgado    Hermana: Sol Cruz Fernández, 3 años

Cuidadora habitual: abuela materna Rosa Delgado    Vecina que ayuda con transporte: Carmen Ríos

Coordinadora de servicios: Ana María Torres, CDSA del Piedmont, oficina de Charlotte    Correo de la coordinadora: anamaria.torres@cdsapiedmont.org    Sitio web de la agencia: www.cdsapiedmont.org

Terapeuta del habla y lenguaje: Gabriela Núñez, MS, CCC-SLP, bilingüe español-inglés    Agencia proveedora: Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Services, PLLC    Correo de la terapeuta: gabriela.nunez@piedmontpeds-slp.com

Fecha de este IFSP de revisión: 3 de octubre de 2026    Fecha del IFSP inicial: 12 de abril de 2026    Fecha de la próxima revisión: 2 de abril de 2027

ANTECEDENTES DE NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICOS

Teo nació a las 34 semanas de gestación, con un peso al nacer de 2,150 gramos, en Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center – Campus Dilworth. Pasó 18 días en la UCIN por dificultad respiratoria y succión débil. Su puntaje de Apgar fue de 6 al minuto y 8 a los cinco minutos. Después del alta, su pediatra, el Dr. Michael Chen, de Novant Health Pediatrics – Campus SouthPark, refirió a la familia al CDSA del Piedmont por preocupaciones de alimentación y retraso de lenguaje observado en la visita de los 9 meses. A los 14 meses, la otorrinolaringóloga, la Dra. Patricia Owens, de Novant Health Ear, Nose & Throat – Campus Ballantyne, diagnosticó otitis media recurrente y colocó tubos de ventilación bilaterales. La audióloga del mismo centro, la Dra. Susan Keller, confirmó audición dentro de límites normales en ambos oídos después de la cirugía, con timpanogramas tipo A bilaterales. El diagnóstico médico actual que consta en el expediente es ICD-10 F80.1 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo).

EVALUACIONES

En la evaluación inicial, Teo fue evaluado con el Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, que arrojó una puntuación equivalente de edad de 11-13 meses en el área receptiva y 9-11 meses en el área expresiva, cuando su edad cronológica era de 1;9. En la revisión actual, el mismo instrumento mostró una edad equivalente de 18-20 meses receptivo y 15-17 meses expresivo, con una edad cronológica de 2;3, lo cual refleja progreso pero continúa un retraso significativo. Se administró también el Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3, con una puntuación estándar de 73 (intervalo de confianza 68-78) y un percentil de 4. Las Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4 se administraron en el área cognitiva y motora, con puntuaciones compuestas de 92 en cognición y 88 en motor grueso, dentro de límites esperados. El Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 no pudo completarse de manera estandarizada por la edad del niño, pero se usaron ítems de muestra que sugieren vocabulario receptivo limitado para su edad.

Durante la observación de juego, Teo produjo once palabras funcionales de manera consistente, entre ellas "mamá", "papá", "agua" (producida como ["ahua"]), y "más". Al pedirle que nombrara una tarjeta de dibujo del sol, dijo ["tol"], sustituyendo el fonema /s/ por /t/ en posición inicial. Esto es consistente con el patrón fonológico de frontalización observado en toda la muestra de habla.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA, EN SUS PROPIAS PALABRAS

La Sra. Fernández Ramos compartió: "Lo que más nos preocupa es que Teo no nos dice lo que quiere, y se frustra mucho, grita y a veces se tira al piso. En la guardería dicen que se pone así con los otros niños también. Queremos que pueda pedir las cosas con palabras antes de que empiece la escuela."

El Sr. Cruz Delgado agregó: "Para mí es importante que entienda las instrucciones simples en la casa, como 'recoge los juguetes' o 'ven aquí', porque ahora tenemos que mostrarle todo con gestos o repetirlo muchas veces. Y también quisiera que hablara más con su hermana Sol, porque ella quiere jugar con él y él no le responde."

La abuela Rosa Delgado, quien cuida a Teo tres días a la semana mientras Lucía trabaja, dijo: "Yo paso más tiempo con él que nadie y veo que entiende más de lo que habla. Cuando le hablo en español me mira, pero cuando viene la gente que habla solo inglés en la guardería, se queda callado. Quiero que los dos idiomas se trabajen juntos, no uno después del otro."

Las prioridades familiares acordadas para esta revisión son: (1) que Teo use al menos 50 palabras diferentes de manera espontánea en ambos idiomas combinados; (2) que siga instrucciones de un solo paso sin apoyo visual el 8/10 de las veces; y (3) que disminuyan los episodios de frustración conductual relacionados con la comunicación, según el registro de la guardería.

RUTINAS DIARIAS

Los días de semana, Teo se despierta alrededor de las 6:30 a.m. y desayuna con su familia antes de que la Sra. Fernández Ramos lo lleve a Little Learners Daycare a las 7:45 a.m.. Su maestra principal es la Srta. Jennifer Álvarez, quien reporta que Teo disfruta las actividades sensoriales y de bloques, pero se frustra durante el círculo de canciones porque no puede seguir las palabras. Su compañero de clase favorito es Ethan Brooks, con quien comparte juguetes de carritos, aunque la interacción verbal entre ellos es mínima. Teo permanece en la guardería hasta las 4:00 p.m., cuando lo recoge la abuela Rosa Delgado o la vecina Carmen Ríos, según el horario de trabajo de los padres.

Dos tardes por semana, después de la guardería, Teo asiste al Little Learners Program, un grupo de intervención temprana centrado en lenguaje y juego social, donde también participa Teo con otros niños de edad similar bajo la supervisión de personal de intervención temprana. La cena familiar es a las 6:00 p.m., y es un momento que los padres identifican como clave para practicar vocabulario de comida y rutina de mesa. El baño es a las 7:30 p.m., seguido de la lectura de cuentos en español e inglés antes de dormir a las 8:30 p.m.. Los fines de semana, la familia visita con frecuencia a los abuelos paternos y asiste a misa los domingos, donde Teo interactúa con otros niños de la congregación.

El padre, Carlos Cruz Delgado, trabaja en Charlotte Pipe and Foundry en turnos rotativos, y la madre, Lucía Fernández Ramos, trabaja medio tiempo en el departamento de panadería de Harris Teeter, cerca de su casa. El perro de la familia, Rocky, suele estar presente durante el juego en el patio, y los padres notan que Teo dice el nombre del perro con más claridad que otras palabras, posiblemente por la repetición frecuente.

OTRAS AGENCIAS Y APOYOS

La familia recibe apoyo nutricional del programa WIC del Condado de Mecklenburg y participa en actividades de alfabetización temprana a través de Smart Start de Mecklenburg. En el pasado, la familia tuvo contacto breve con el Departamento de Servicios Sociales de Mecklenburg (DSS) por una evaluación de vivienda que ya se cerró sin seguimiento adicional. No hay otras agencias activas en este momento aparte del CDSA del Piedmont y los servicios médicos ya mencionados.

RESULTADOS (OUTCOMES) Y ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1: Teo se comunicará sus necesidades y deseos usando palabras o frases cortas en lugar de conductas de frustración, en el hogar y en Little Learners Daycare, medido por el registro diario de la maestra y el reporte de los padres durante tres semanas consecutivas.
Estrategias: modelar lenguaje expandido durante rutinas de alta motivación (comida, juego con Rocky); usar el método de tiempo de espera y la técnica de "modelo más expansión"; coordinar con la Srta. Álvarez para usar las mismas tres frases clave en inglés y español durante la transición de actividades.

Resultado 2: Teo seguirá instrucciones familiares de un solo paso sin apoyo gestual el 8 de 10 intentos en al menos dos entornos (hogar y guardería), según datos recolectados por los cuidadores.
Estrategias: practicar instrucciones funcionales durante la rutina de recoger juguetes y de vestirse; usar apoyo visual decreciente; capacitar a la abuela Rosa Delgado y a la Srta. Álvarez en el uso de instrucciones cortas y consistentes en ambos idiomas.

Resultado 3: Teo producirá el fonema /s/ en posición inicial de palabra con precisión en al menos 3 de 5 ensayos durante actividades estructuradas de juego, generalizando desde la palabra meta "sol" hacia otras palabras con el mismo sonido.
Estrategias: usar claves táctiles y modelo auditivo con mod cues (claves moderadas); practicar la palabra meta "sol" durante canciones y juego sensorial con tarjetas ilustradas; reforzar en casa relacionando el sonido con actividades cotidianas, evitando confundir la práctica fonológica con el nombre de su hermana Sol, a quien Teo nombra por separado durante el juego familiar.

Resultado 4: Teo aumentará su vocabulario expresivo combinado (español e inglés) a al menos 50 palabras diferentes, documentado mediante registro de palabras de los padres y la terapeuta durante un período de seis semanas.
Estrategias: usar el enfoque de lenguaje natural dentro de rutinas diarias; incorporar libros bilingües durante la lectura nocturna; coordinar con el programa Little Learners Program para reforzar las mismas palabras meta usadas en terapia individual.

SERVICIOS Y FECHAS

Terapia de habla y lenguaje individual: dos sesiones de 45 minutos por semana, en el hogar, código CPT 92523, con autorización vigente desde 15 de abril de 2026 hasta 14 de abril de 2027.    Proveedora: Gabriela Núñez, Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Services, PLLC.

Intervención temprana en grupo, Little Learners Program: dos sesiones de 60 minutos por semana, iniciadas el 3 de mayo de 2026, continúan hasta la próxima revisión.

Seguimiento audiológico: cita de control programada para el 20 de enero de 2027 en Novant Health Ear, Nose & Throat – Campus Ballantyne con la Dra. Susan Keller.

Visita de coordinación de servicios: realizada el 28 de septiembre de 2026 por la coordinadora Ana María Torres; próxima visita de coordinación programada para el 28 de diciembre de 2026.

Esta revisión del IFSP fue completada el 3 de octubre de 2026 con la participación de la Sra. Lucía Fernández Ramos, el Sr. Carlos Cruz Delgado, la coordinadora Ana María Torres y la terapeuta Gabriela Núñez. La familia expresó satisfacción con el progreso de Teo y solicitó continuar con el mismo plan de servicios hasta la próxima revisión programada.

Firma de la terapeuta: Gabriela Núñez, MS, CCC-SLP    Fecha de firma: 3 de octubre de 2026

INFORME DE EVALUACION DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE / SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Client / Nino: Mateo Reyes-Vargas
Date of Birth: April 14, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Evaluation Dates: September 18, 2026 and September 25, 2026
Report Date: October 2, 2026
Record ID: LD-2026-00483
Medicaid ID: NC9284671B
Referral Source: Dr. Anna Whitfield, Foothills Pediatric Care
Referring Agency: Catawba Valley CDSA
Service Coordinator: Brenda Alvarez
Interpreter Present: Rosa Fernandez, Spanish-English medical interpreter
Evaluating Clinician: Maria Hayes, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist
Parents/Guardians: Lucia del Rio (mother), Diego Reyes-Vargas (father)
Home Address: 218 Birchwood Trail, Claremont, Catawba County, NC 28610
Home Phone: (828) 555-0219
Primary Home Language(s): Spanish and English

I. MOTIVO DE LA REMISION / REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by Dr. Whitfield following a well-child visit on August 11, 2026, at which parent concerns regarding limited intelligibility and reduced sentence length were documented. Mateo has an open case with Catawba Valley CDSA under his original Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP), initiated at age 2;6, and is due for his annual review on November 3, 2026. His mother, Lucia del Rio, reported in the initial phone screening, "no le entiendo casi nada cuando habla rapido, y en la escuela dicen que se frustra porque no lo entienden." His father, Diego Reyes-Vargas, added during the intake call that Mateo "gets mad and just points instead of talking when his sister or his cousins don't get what he's saying."

This evaluation was requested to update standardized testing for IFSP eligibility redetermination, to characterize speech sound production and expressive/receptive language skills in both languages, and to generate updated goals and recommendations for continued early intervention services.

II. ANTECEDENTES / BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucia del Rio; his father, Diego Reyes-Vargas; his older sister, Camila Reyes-Vargas, age 7; and the family dog, Rocky, a terrier mix. His paternal grandmother, Rosario del Rio, lives nearby and provides childcare three afternoons per week while both parents work. Lucia del Rio is employed at Catawba Valley Furniture Outlet and Diego Reyes-Vargas works second shift at a regional distribution facility. Mateo attends Tumbleweed Treehouse Preschool four days a week, where his lead teacher is Ms. Patterson and his classroom assistant is Mr. Osei. He has two close friends in his class, Ethan and Sofia, whom his parents say he talks about frequently at home. A neighbor, Mr. Thompson, occasionally watches Mateo and his sister in the evenings when both parents work late.

Mateo was initially referred to early intervention at 24 months of age due to limited expressive vocabulary and was evaluated at that time using the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, which yielded age-equivalent scores ranging from 15-18 months across the Language Comprehension and Language Expression subscales, at a chronological age of 2;0. He began receiving early intervention speech therapy at that time through Catawba Valley CDSA, with services delivered in the home and later transitioned to Tumbleweed Treehouse Preschool once he was enrolled.

III. HISTORIA MEDICA Y DE NACIMIENTO / BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Carolina Piedmont Regional Medical Center via spontaneous vaginal delivery. Birth weight was recorded as 6 lbs 11 oz and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. Lucia del Rio reported no complications during pregnancy, although she noted mild gestational hypertension managed with monitoring in the third trimester. Mateo remained in the hospital for routine observation and was discharged on April 16, 2022.

Developmental milestones were reported as generally within normal limits for gross and fine motor domains; Mateo walked independently around 13 months. Parents reported a history of recurrent otitis media between 18 and 30 months of age, with placement of bilateral pressure equalization tubes on January 9, 2024 by an ENT at Foothills Pediatric Care. Hearing was most recently screened on March 4, 2026 and passed bilaterally. No history of seizure disorder, significant head injury, or genetic syndrome was reported. Mateo's vision has not been formally screened but parents report no concerns. Current diagnoses on his pediatric chart include history of recurrent otitis media, resolved, and developmental speech and language delay, previously coded F80.9 prior to this evaluation.

IV. HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE / FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

The home language environment is predominantly Spanish, with increasing English exposure since Mateo began attending Tumbleweed Treehouse Preschool at age 3. Lucia del Rio reported, "en casa hablamos puro espanol, pero el ya me contesta mas en ingles, sobre todo cuando esta jugando con Rocky o con su hermana." Rosario del Rio, the paternal grandmother, speaks almost exclusively Spanish with Mateo during her afternoons of care and reports that he understands her well but increasingly responds with a mix of both languages, a pattern consistent with typical bilingual development.

Diego Reyes-Vargas estimated that Mateo's current language exposure is approximately 60 percent Spanish and 40 percent English, though this ratio has shifted toward English since preschool enrollment. Camila Reyes-Vargas is reported to be fully bilingual and often serves as an informal language model and interpreter for her younger brother at home and in community settings, which Lucia del Rio expressed some concern about: "no quiero que ella tenga que traducir todo por el, pero a veces es la unica que le entiende."

There is no reported family history of speech, language, or learning disorders on either side of the family. Diego Reyes-Vargas reported that he himself was "a late talker" as a child but had no formal intervention. Both parents are highly motivated and consistently attend scheduled therapy and evaluation appointments.

V. PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACION Y OBSERVACIONES / ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

This evaluation was conducted across two sessions at the offices of Piedmont Pediatric Speech and Language Associates. Session one, conducted in English with interpreter support, took place from 9:00 AM to 10:30 AM on September 18, 2026. Session two, conducted primarily in Spanish, took place from 2:00 PM to 3:15 PM on September 25, 2026. Lucia del Rio was present for both sessions, and the interpreter, Rosa Fernandez, assisted with instructions and clarification of responses during the Spanish-language portion.

Mateo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with toys and testing materials. He demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks of approximately 10 to 15 minutes before requiring a brief movement break. Rapport was established quickly using a stuffed dog that Mateo spontaneously named "Rocky, como mi perro," referencing his own pet at home. Behavior and cooperation were judged to be representative of his typical functioning, per parent report. No significant behavioral concerns were noted during testing, though mild frustration was observed when Mateo was not understood on the first attempt, consistent with parent report of frustration at home and at Tumbleweed Treehouse Preschool.

VI. RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS / TEST RESULTS

The following standardized assessments were administered. English norms were used for the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) and Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition (PPVT-5), while the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) was administered using the Spanish-English Bilingual Edition protocol, incorporating responses from both languages per test guidelines. The Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4) Cognitive Scale was administered to screen nonverbal cognitive functioning given Mateo's significant expressive delay.

Test Name | Standard Score | Percentile Rank | Age Equivalent
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) | 76 | 5th | 2;9
Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 (PPVT-5) | 88 | 21st | 3;4
PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | 82 | 12th | 3;1
PLS-5 Expressive Communication | 74 | 4th | 2;11
PLS-5 Total Language Score | 76 | 5th | --
Bayley-4 Cognitive Composite | 91 | 27th | --

Confidence intervals for the PLS-5 Total Language Score fell within 71-81 at the 95 percent confidence level. On the GFTA-3, Mateo's raw error pattern was most consistent with simplification of consonant clusters and final consonant deletion, discussed further below.

Mateo's overall performance places his receptive and expressive language skills within the below average to significantly below average range relative to same-age monolingual English peers, with relatively stronger performance on auditory comprehension than expressive tasks. Given his bilingual status, these scores were interpreted in conjunction with parent-reported language use in both Spanish and English rather than as a sole indicator of disorder, consistent with best practice for dual-language learners.

VII. PRODUCCION DE SONIDOS DEL HABLA / SPEECH SOUND PRODUCTION

Connected speech samples were obtained in both English and Spanish during structured play and conversation. In English, Mateo's intelligibility was judged to be approximately 60 percent to unfamiliar listeners in context and improved to roughly 80 percent to familiar listeners such as his parents and the examiner by the end of the session. In Spanish, intelligibility was estimated at 70 percent to unfamiliar listeners and approximately 85 percent to familiar listeners.

Phonological error patterns observed included consistent final consonant deletion (for example, "ca" for "cat" and "pe" for "perro", deleting the final /r/), cluster reduction (for example, "paw" for "spoon" and "mesa" produced as "mea"), and fronting of velar sounds, with /k/ frequently produced as [t] and /g/ produced as [d]. During a structured articulation probe targeting word-initial /k/, Mateo produced the target sound correctly in 8/10 trials with mod cues, an accuracy rate of approximately 80%. On a separate probe targeting final consonants in English, accuracy was 3/10, or 30%, even with max cues.

During play with the stuffed dog, Mateo was heard to say "Rocky go fast" while running a toy across the table, producing the target as approximately "Wocky go fah" with gliding of /r/ and final consonant deletion. Later in the session, when shown a family photograph, he pointed and said "Camila no quiere," demonstrating appropriate use of a two-word combination with age-appropriate negation structure despite reduced intelligibility of the proper name itself.

Oral mechanism examination revealed structures within normal limits for strength, symmetry, and range of motion. No signs of dysarthria or significant oral-motor weakness were observed. Diadochokinetic rates for repeated syllable sequences were judged to be mildly slow but within functional limits for a child of his age. No concerns regarding voice quality, resonance, or fluency were noted; speech rate and rhythm were judged to be within normal limits in both languages, with no evidence of stuttering-like behaviors.

VIII. ANALISIS DE MUESTRA DE LENGUAJE / LANGUAGE SAMPLE ANALYSIS

A 100-utterance connected speech sample was collected and transcribed, combining both English and Spanish utterances consistent with Mateo's natural code-switching patterns. Mean length of utterance in morphemes (MLU-m) was calculated at 2.8, which falls below the expected range of 3.5-4.5 morphemes for a child of his chronological age. Mateo primarily used two- and three-word combinations such as "mas agua", "Rocky come", and "no quiero eso", with limited use of grammatical morphemes including plural -s, third person singular -s, and regular past tense -ed in English, and limited use of verb conjugation beyond present tense forms in Spanish.

Code-switching was frequent and appeared to follow typical patterns for a young bilingual child rather than confusion between the two language systems; for example, Mateo was observed to say "quiero jugar with Rocky," appropriately embedding an English prepositional phrase within a Spanish-dominant utterance, labeled under the SALT transcription convention as [EW] for English word insertion. This pattern of intra-sentential code-switching is considered developmentally appropriate and was not counted as an error in scoring.

Comprehension of basic following directions was assessed informally. Mateo followed one-step directions with 90% accuracy and two-step directions with 60% accuracy, or 6 of 10 trials correct, in both English and Spanish. He demonstrated understanding of basic spatial concepts (in, on, under) with 8/10 accuracy but showed inconsistent comprehension of temporal concepts (before, after) at 40% accuracy.

IX. PRAGMATICA Y COMUNICACION SOCIAL / PRAGMATICS AND SOCIAL COMMUNICATION

Mateo demonstrated age-appropriate joint attention, eye contact, and turn-taking during structured and unstructured play. He initiated communication frequently using gesture combined with single words or short phrases, and he responded appropriately to greetings and simple social routines in both languages. Parents report that at Tumbleweed Treehouse Preschool, Mateo plays well with Ethan and Sofia but becomes withdrawn in larger group activities when he struggles to be understood. Ms. Patterson reported via parent communication that Mateo has begun using more gestures in place of verbal attempts over the past month, which the team views as a possible compensatory strategy warranting monitoring.

X. IMPRESIONES / IMPRESSIONS

Mateo presents with a moderate expressive language delay and mild to moderate receptive language delay across both Spanish and English, consistent with a diagnosis of a primary language disorder rather than typical second-language acquisition, given that delays are present across both of his languages relative to bilingual developmental expectations. His speech sound production is characterized by multiple phonological processes including final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and velar fronting, which are contributing significantly to reduced intelligibility across both languages and across listener familiarity. His receptive language skills, while also below age expectations, are relatively stronger than his expressive skills, a pattern consistent with his history and with typical early intervention trajectories.

Mateo's nonverbal cognitive skills, as estimated by the Bayley-4 Cognitive Composite, fall within the average range, supporting that his language and speech sound difficulties are not attributable to global developmental delay. His bilingual language environment is considered a strength to be supported rather than a cause of his delays, and services should continue to be delivered using a bilingual approach consistent with current best practice guidelines for dual-language learners.

XI. DIAGNOSTICO / DIAGNOSIS

Based on standardized testing, language sample analysis, parent report, and clinical observation, the following diagnoses are supported:

Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, ICD-10 F80.2
Speech sound disorder (phonological), associated with the above

XII. RECOMENDACIONES / RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo continues to meet eligibility criteria for early intervention services through Catawba Valley CDSA and should continue to receive individual speech-language therapy at a frequency of two 30-minute sessions per week, billed under CPT code 92507, delivered in both Spanish and English consistent with his home language environment.

2. It is recommended that Mateo receive a follow-up comprehensive speech-language re-evaluation (CPT 92523) in approximately 6 months to monitor progress and update IFSP goals, or sooner if significant changes in function are observed.

3. Therapy should target reduction of phonological error patterns, specifically final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and velar fronting, using a cycles-based approach (Cycles) to address multiple error patterns efficiently across both languages.

4. Expressive language goals should target increased mean length of utterance, use of grammatical morphemes in both Spanish and English, and expansion of vocabulary, with consideration of a Hanen-based coaching approach to support Lucia del Rio and Diego Reyes-Vargas in facilitating language development during daily routines at home.

5. Given reports of increased gesture use and occasional frustration-related withdrawal, the team recommends continued monitoring for the emergence of compensatory nonverbal strategies and consideration of a brief trial of core vocabulary visual supports, informed by PECS principles, if verbal frustration continues to increase at Tumbleweed Treehouse Preschool.

6. Continued coordination with Ms. Patterson and Mr. Osei at Tumbleweed Treehouse Preschool is recommended to support classroom communication strategies and to monitor peer interactions with Ethan and Sofia.

7. A referral to audiology for a repeat comprehensive hearing evaluation is not currently indicated given a recent passed screening on March 4, 2026, but should be reconsidered if recurrent otitis media symptoms return, given Mateo's prior history of tube placement.

8. The family is encouraged to continue providing rich language exposure in Spanish at home, including continued involvement of Rosario del Rio, and to view Mateo's bilingualism as an asset to be supported rather than reduced.

9. The team will reconvene with Brenda Alvarez at Catawba Valley CDSA to update the IFSP prior to the scheduled annual review on November 3, 2026.

XIII. RESUMEN DE CODIGOS DE SERVICIO / SERVICE CODE SUMMARY

Evaluation services rendered during this assessment period are billed under CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression). Ongoing individual treatment sessions will be billed under CPT 92507. Diagnosis coding reflects ICD-10 F80.2, mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, with speech sound disorder as a co-occurring condition.

This report was prepared by Maria Hayes, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist, Piedmont Pediatric Speech and Language Associates, with interpretation services provided by Rosa Fernandez. Questions regarding this report may be directed to (828) 555-0147 or mhayes@piedmontpedspeech.com.

North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program
Individualized Family Service Plan — Periodic Review

CDSA Office: Triangle Regional CDSA, 3500 Westgate Drive, Raleigh, 27617
County of Residence: Wake County
Review Date: October 9, 2026
Initial IFSP Date: February 14, 2025
Most Recent Annual Review: February 20, 2026
Child's Record ID: NC-2025-004471
Medicaid ID: 990112233A

Child: Mateo Hernandez
Date of Birth: June 2, 2024
Chronological Age at Review: 2;4
Gestational Age at Birth: 37 weeks
Birth Weight: 5 lb 14 oz
Apgar Scores: 8 and 9
Primary Diagnosis: F80.1 (Expressive Language Disorder), F80.0 (Phonological Disorder)

Mother: Lucia Hernandez
Father: Ruben Hernandez
Home Address: 118 Sweetgum Court, Garner, 27529
Home Phone: 919-555-0142
Mother's Cell: 919-555-0187
Family Email: hernandezfamily24@notarealmail.com

Service Coordinator: Angela Byrd, Triangle Regional CDSA, office line 919-555-0310
Evaluating and Treating Speech-Language Pathologist: Daniela Ruiz, M.S., CCC-SLP, Little Steps Therapy Services

Reason for Review

This periodic review updates Mateo's Individualized Family Service Plan after his six-month re-evaluation. The team, including Lucia Hernandez, Ruben Hernandez, service coordinator Angela Byrd, and speech-language pathologist Daniela Ruiz, met at the family's home on October 9, 2026 to review progress on current outcomes and set new ones. Daniela Ruiz conducted the meeting in both English and Spanish, since the family prefers to talk about Mateo's needs in Spanish.

Family Concerns, Priorities, and Resources

Lucia Hernandez shared, in Spanish, "El esta aprendiendo a pedir mas cosas, pero todavia se frustra mucho cuando no lo entendemos." Daniela Ruiz translated this for the written plan as: Mateo is learning to ask for more things, but he still gets very frustrated when the family does not understand him. Ruben Hernandez added that his top priority is for Mateo to tell his older sister Sol what he wants instead of hitting her when he is upset. He said, "Quiero que el pueda decirle a su hermana lo que necesita, sin pegarle."

Lucia Hernandez also said she worries about Mateo's speech sounds, since his grandmother sometimes cannot understand him at all, even when he is trying hard. The family's grandmother, Rosa Martinez, lives with the family and watches Mateo and his baby brother, Diego Hernandez, on the days when neither parent is home. Rosa Martinez told the team, through Daniela Ruiz's interpretation, that she is proud of how much Mateo has grown but gets tired keeping up with him and the baby at the same time.

The family named several resources they rely on: Rosa Martinez's help with childcare, a reliable car, and a close relationship with Mateo's pediatrician, Dr. Sandra Kim, at WakeMed Children's. The family also noted that their dog, Oso, is Mateo's favorite playmate at home and that Mateo often says the dog's name clearly before he will attempt most other words.

Daily Routines

Mateo wakes most days around 6:30 AM. Lucia Hernandez works nights as a certified nursing assistant at Pinewood Manor Nursing Home, with a shift from 11:00 PM to 7:00 AM, so on weekday mornings Ruben Hernandez gets Mateo and Sol Hernandez ready while Lucia Hernandez is still finishing her shift. Ruben Hernandez works days as a framing crew lead for Carver Brothers Construction and drops Mateo at daycare on his way to job sites.

Mateo attends Buttercup Meadow Early Learning on weekdays from about 7:15 AM to 4:30 PM. His lead teacher in the toddler room, Ms. Keisha Owens, reports that Mateo is affectionate with staff and peers but gets overwhelmed in loud group transitions, such as moving from the playground to lunch. Ms. Keisha Owens noted that a classmate, Amara, has started imitating Mateo's gestures back to him, which seems to help him calm down faster than redirection from an adult alone.

Rosa Martinez picks Mateo up most afternoons around 4:30 PM and brings him home, where he plays with Oso and waits for his sister. Sol Hernandez, age 6, is a kindergartener in Wake County Public School System at Lakeside Elementary, in Mrs. Alvarez's classroom. Sol Hernandez rides the bus home and arrives around 3:45 PM, after which she and Mateo usually have about an hour of unstructured play before dinner. The family eats dinner together most nights around 6:00 PM, and Lucia Hernandez leaves for work shortly before 10:30 PM once Ruben Hernandez is home to take over bedtime with Mateo, Sol Hernandez, and baby Diego Hernandez.

Present Levels of Development

Daniela Ruiz re-administered the Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) in English and Spanish on September 22, 2026. On the Auditory Comprehension subtest, Mateo earned a standard score of 76 (5th percentile), with an age equivalent of 18-20 months. On Expressive Communication, he earned a standard score of 71 (3rd percentile), age equivalent 16-18 months. These scores represent modest gains from his annual evaluation, where his standard scores were 68 and 65 respectively.

Articulation and phonology screening showed consistent use of /b/, /m/, /d/, and emerging /t/, with frequent final consonant deletion and stopping of fricatives. Mateo produced "ba" for ball with min cues, and attempted the target word "sol" for the initial /s/ cluster, producing "tol" with mod cues and "sol" with max cues on 2 of 10 trials. Daniela Ruiz noted that the family chose this target word on purpose, since it carries meaning for Mateo as his sister's name, which seemed to increase his motivation during drill trials.

Pragmatically, Mateo used joint attention and protodeclarative pointing consistently, and combined gesture with vocalization in 8 of 10 observed opportunities. He has approximately 15 functional words across both languages and is not yet combining words.

Other Agencies Involved

The family receives nutrition support through Wake County WIC and has an open file with Smart Start of Wake County for a childcare subsidy that helps cover tuition at Buttercup Meadow Early Learning. Mateo's pediatrician, Dr. Sandra Kim at WakeMed Children's, continues routine well-child visits and referred the family for an audiology recheck, which came back within normal limits on August 11, 2026. The family has no open case with Wake County Department of Social Services at this time. Angela Byrd will continue to coordinate across these agencies and will follow up with Smart Start of Wake County about subsidy renewal before the next review.

Outcomes and Strategies

Outcome 1: Mateo will use two-word combinations to request and comment during daily routines at home and at Buttercup Meadow Early Learning.
Strategies: Daniela Ruiz will coach Lucia Hernandez and Ruben Hernandez using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies, including following Mateo's lead, expanding his single words into two-word models, and building in pause time during snack and bath routines. Ms. Keisha Owens will use the same expansion strategy during daycare mealtimes and will track frequency weekly.

Outcome 2: Mateo will produce initial /s/ and final consonants in single words with mod cues in structured play, including his target word "sol".
Strategies: Daniela Ruiz will use a PROMPT-informed tactile cueing approach during twice-weekly sessions, moving from max cues toward min cues as accuracy improves. The family will practice five minutes nightly using a short list of meaningful words, including "sol", "papa", and "agua".

Outcome 3: Mateo will use a gesture or word instead of hitting when frustrated with his sister or peers, in 4 of 5 observed conflicts.
Strategies: Ruben Hernandez and Lucia Hernandez will model the sign for "more" and "help" at home, and Ms. Keisha Owens will prompt Mateo with the same signs during conflicts with Amara and other classmates. Sol Hernandez will be coached by her parents to pause and offer Mateo a choice of two toys rather than removing an item outright, which the family reports already reduces some conflicts at home.

Services and Dates

Speech-Language Therapy: direct, in-home, two 45-minute sessions weekly, provided by Daniela Ruiz of Little Steps Therapy Services, beginning October 20, 2026 and continuing through the next annual review.
Service Coordination: monthly contact and quarterly home visits from Angela Byrd, Triangle Regional CDSA.
Developmental Therapy Consultation: one 30-minute visit to Buttercup Meadow Early Learning monthly, to support Ms. Keisha Owens with classroom strategies, beginning November 3, 2026.
Next Periodic Review: April 9, 2027.
Next Annual Review: February 20, 2027.

RESULTADOS DEL IFSP CON ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1: Mateo usará palabras y gestos combinados para solicitar objetos y acciones en el hogar y en la guardería.
Estado actual: en la evaluación con el PLS-5, obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 72 en Comunicación Expresiva (percentil 3), con una edad equivalente de 14 meses. En Comunicación Receptiva obtuvo 81 (percentil 10).
Estrategias: uso de PECS en el hogar y la guardería; modelado de lenguaje aumentado siguiendo el enfoque Hanen; la familia practicará la frase modelo "más, por favor" durante las comidas.
Progreso: Mateo combina gesto más palabra en 6/10 oportunidades observadas, un aumento desde 2/10 en abril. Produjo de forma espontánea "mamá" y "agua" durante la sesión.

Resultado 2: Mateo participará en juego paralelo y luego interactivo con otros niños durante al menos 5 minutos continuos.
Estrategias: sesiones conjuntas con un compañero de la guardería; uso de PROMPT para apoyar la articulación durante el juego compartido; se trabajará el turno con las frases "mi turno" y "tu turno."
Progreso: con mod cues, Mateo mantuvo juego paralelo con una compañera de clase durante 4 minutos la semana pasada, según reportó la maestra Ms. Álvarez.

Resultado 3: Mateo producirá los sonidos /m/, /p/ y /b/ de forma inteligible en palabras de una sílaba.
Estrategias: enfoque Cycles dirigido a procesos fonológicos; práctica de palabras meta como "pan" y "bebé."
Progreso: produjo [p] con min cues en 8/10 ensayos; aún omite la sílaba final en palabras como "más," producido como "má."
