INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y DEL LENGUAJE

**Nombre del niño:** Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez ("Teo")
**Fecha de nacimiento:** 14 de agosto de 2022
**Edad cronológica en la evaluación:** 4;2
**Sexo:** Masculino
**Idiomas del hogar:** español e inglés
**Número de expediente:** 45218
**Número de Medicaid:** NC4487213B
**Dirección:** 1420 Redbud Lane, Durham, NC 27703
**Teléfono de contacto:** (919) 555-0273
**Padre:** Hugo Flores Martínez
**Madre:** Lucía Rodríguez Pérez
**Guardería:** Centro de Cuidado Infantil Sunny Days
**Médico de cabecera:** Dr. Samuel Winters
**Fuente de referencia:** Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Durham
**Fecha(s) de evaluación:** 9 de septiembre de 2026 y 11 de septiembre de 2026, a las 9:30 a.m.
**Fecha del informe:** 25 de septiembre de 2026
**Evaluadora:** Patricia Nguyen-García, MS, CCC-SLP, patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe (español-inglés), Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Center, PLLC

---

**1. Identificación y motivo de la referencia**

Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez, conocido en casa como "Teo", es un niño de 4;2 que fue referido para una evaluación integral del habla y del lenguaje por el Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Durham, a solicitud de su madre, Lucía Rodríguez Pérez, y con el apoyo de la trabajadora social asignada a la familia. La preocupación principal es que Teo presenta un habla difícil de entender tanto en español como en inglés, un vocabulario limitado para su edad en ambos idiomas, y dificultad para seguir instrucciones de dos y tres pasos en el salón de clase. La madre reporta que, en el hogar, Mateo usa principalmente español, mientras que en la guardería recibe instrucción casi completamente en inglés.

La familia fue contactada inicialmente a través del programa WIC del Condado de Durham, donde la nutricionista notó que Teo hablaba considerablemente menos que otros niños de su edad durante una consulta de rutina en marzo de 2026. La nutricionista remitió a la familia al Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Durham, que a su vez coordinó esta evaluación con nuestra clínica. Previamente, la familia había tenido contacto con la Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Piedmont (CDSA) cuando Mateo tenía 26 meses, pero el caso se cerró sin servicios porque, en ese momento, su desempeño estuvo dentro de límites normales en la evaluación de detección.

**2. Antecedentes prenatales, perinatales y médicos**

Según refiere Lucía, el embarazo de Mateo fue de término completo, sin complicaciones significativas, aunque ella reporta haber tenido presión arterial elevada durante el tercer trimestre, controlada sin medicación. Mateo nació por parto vaginal el 14 de agosto de 2022 en un hospital de la zona, con un peso al nacer de 3,400 gramos y una puntuación de Apgar de 8 al minuto y 9 a los cinco minutos. La edad gestacional fue de 39 semanas. No se reportan complicaciones neonatales, estancia en la unidad de cuidados intensivos, ni necesidad de intubación.

El desarrollo motor grueso de Teo se describe como típico: se sentó solo alrededor de los 6 meses y caminó de forma independiente cerca de los 13 meses. Sin embargo, Lucía y Hugo coinciden en que el desarrollo del lenguaje fue más lento: las primeras palabras aparecieron después de los 18 meses, y las combinaciones de dos palabras no surgieron de forma consistente hasta cerca de los 3 años.

Historial médico: Mateo ha tenido cuatro episodios de otitis media aguda documentados entre enero de 2024 y julio de 2025, tratados con antibióticos. El Dr. Winters colocó tubos de ventilación (timpanostomía bilateral) el 14 de agosto de 2025, procedimiento CPT 69436, tras documentar derrame en ambos oídos (diagnóstico H65.93) en visitas repetidas. Desde la colocación de los tubos, la madre reporta menos episodios de infección, aunque persisten las dificultades de habla y lenguaje. No hay antecedentes de convulsiones, hospitalizaciones prolongadas, ni diagnósticos genéticos conocidos. La visión fue evaluada como normal en el examen pediátrico más reciente, con fecha 3 de junio de 2026.

**3. Historia familiar y de idiomas en el hogar**

Mateo vive con sus padres, Hugo Flores Martínez y Lucía Rodríguez Pérez, y con su hermanita menor, Sol Flores Rodríguez, de 2 años. La abuela materna, a quien la familia llama doña Lupe, cuida a Sol y a Teo dos días por semana mientras los padres trabajan, y habla exclusivamente español con los niños.

El padre, Hugo, trabaja en la Carolina Pride Processing Plant, una planta de procesamiento de carne ubicada en las afueras de Durham, donde tiene turnos rotativos que a veces incluyen el turno nocturno. En conversaciones previas con la trabajadora social, la familia también se refirió al mismo lugar de trabajo como la planta procesadora Carolina Pride, usando el orden de palabras típico del español. La madre, Lucía, trabaja de lunes a viernes para la Bright Homes Cleaning Service, una empresa que limpia oficinas y consultorios médicos en varias partes de la ciudad; ella misma la describe en casa como la empresa de limpieza Bright Homes. Debido a los horarios de ambos padres, Mateo pasa aproximadamente 35 horas semanales en la guardería y el resto del tiempo con su familia extendida.

En el hogar se habla español de manera predominante. Lucía estima que la exposición de Mateo al español es de aproximadamente 70% y al inglés de 30%, principalmente a través de la televisión, canciones infantiles y la guardería. Ningún miembro de la familia inmediata reporta antecedentes de trastornos del habla, lenguaje o aprendizaje, aunque la madre menciona que un primo materno, Will, recibió terapia del habla cuando era pequeño por razones que ella no recuerda con claridad.

La familia ha recibido apoyo de Durham's Partnership for Children a través de un programa de alfabetización familiar, y en el pasado se inscribieron en Early Head Start cuando Mateo tenía apenas 14 meses, aunque dejaron el programa después de seis meses por un cambio de domicilio dentro del Condado de Durham.

**4. Historia educativa y observaciones de la guardería**

Mateo asiste al Centro de Cuidado Infantil Sunny Days desde los 20 meses. Actualmente está en el salón de niños de cuatro años, conocido dentro del centro como el salón de la Srta. López. La maestra asistente de ese salón, la maestra Carmen, completó un cuestionario de desarrollo antes de esta evaluación y reportó que Mateo participa en actividades grupales, pero con frecuencia se frustra cuando otros niños no entienden lo que dice. También señaló que Teo prefiere jugar con un compañero en particular, Diego, con quien se comunica principalmente a través de gestos y juego físico en lugar de palabras.

Según la maestra Carmen, Mateo sigue instrucciones de un paso de manera consistente, pero necesita repetición y apoyo visual para instrucciones de dos pasos. En el área de preacademia, reconoce algunos colores y números hasta el 5 en español, pero muestra menos consistencia en inglés. La Srta. López reportó, en una nota breve adjunta al cuestionario, que durante el círculo de canciones Mateo con frecuencia solo hace gestos con las manos en lugar de cantar, lo cual atribuye a la dificultad articulatoria más que a falta de interés.

**5. Procedimientos de evaluación**

Esta evaluación se llevó a cabo en dos sesiones, en las instalaciones del Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Center, PLLC, con la participación activa de Lucía en ambas sesiones. Se utilizaron los siguientes instrumentos estandarizados y procedimientos informales:

- Entrevista con los padres y revisión de antecedentes del desarrollo.
- Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA), subpruebas de Morfosintaxis y Fonología, administradas en ambos idiomas.
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), subprueba de Conceptos y Siguiendo Instrucciones, administrada en inglés.
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation 3 (GFTA-3), administrada en inglés, con análisis comparativo de errores en español.
- Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo en español (50 enunciados) durante juego libre con bloques y figuras de animales.
- Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo en inglés (40 enunciados) durante juego con la madre y la evaluadora.
- Observación informal de alimentación y motricidad oral.
- Evaluación dinámica (prueba-enseñanza-reprueba) para distinguir diferencia de adquisición bilingüe de un posible trastorno.

La evaluadora, Patricia Nguyen-García, es hablante nativa de español y administró todas las partes en ambos idiomas sin necesidad de intérprete. Lucía estuvo presente durante toda la evaluación y sirvió como informante sobre el uso del lenguaje de Mateo en el hogar.

**6. Resultados**

**6.1 Comprensión y expresión del lenguaje**

En el BESA, subprueba de Morfosintaxis en español, Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 76 (percentil 5), ubicándose por debajo del rango promedio en comparación con otros niños bilingües de su edad. En la subprueba de Morfosintaxis en inglés, obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 71 (percentil 3). Estos resultados en ambos idiomas, sin un patrón de fortaleza relativa en ninguno de los dos, sugieren una dificultad subyacente que no se explica únicamente por la exposición bilingüe.

En el CELF Preschool-3, subprueba de Conceptos y Siguiendo Instrucciones, Mateo obtuvo una puntuación escalada de 5 (percentil 5), con un intervalo de confianza del 95% de 73-83 para el índice compuesto correspondiente. Siguió correctamente instrucciones de un paso en 9 de 10 ensayos, pero solo 3 de 10 en instrucciones de dos pasos con elementos espaciales (por ejemplo, "pon el carro debajo de la silla").

En la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo en español, la longitud media de enunciado fue de 3.1 morfemas, por debajo de lo esperado para su edad. Se observaron omisiones frecuentes de artículos y errores en la concordancia de género, por ejemplo, produciendo "el pelota" en lugar de "la pelota" y "un casa" en lugar de "una casa". En inglés, la longitud media de enunciado fue de 2.6 morfemas, con omisión frecuente de la cópula ("he happy" en lugar de "he is happy") y de marcadores de tiempo pasado.

**6.2 Habla y fonología**

En el GFTA-3, Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 68 (percentil 2), con una edad equivalente de 2;9–3;0. Su inteligibilidad fue evaluada como aproximadamente 50% para oyentes familiares y 30% para oyentes no familiares en conversación espontánea. Los procesos fonológicos observados en ambos idiomas incluyeron:

- Reducción de grupos consonánticos: "pato" por "plato", "toche" por "broche".
- Frontalización de velares: produjo [t] en lugar de /k/ en palabras como "taza" por "casa".
- Simplificación de líquidas: sustituyó [w] por /ɾ/ en palabras como "guapo" en lugar de "guapo" con la /r/ correcta, y omitió la /l/ final en "sa" por "sal".
- En inglés, sustituyó [w] por /r/ de forma consistente, produciendo "wabbit" por "rabbit".

Con claves de cuing mínimo (modelo auditivo), Mateo logró producir correctamente el sonido /k/ en posición inicial en 7 de 10 ensayos, lo cual sugiere buena capacidad de imitación y estimulabilidad. Con claves de cuing moderado (modelo más indicaciones táctiles), logró la secuencia consonántica /pl/ en 4 de 10 ensayos.

**6.3 Motricidad oral y alimentación**

La evaluación informal de la motricidad oral no reveló debilidad estructural evidente. Se observó ligera dificultad para elevar la punta de la lengua de forma aislada y para realizar movimientos alternantes rápidos de la lengua, aunque sin indicios de apraxia significativa. La madre no reporta dificultades de alimentación actuales, aunque menciona que Mateo fue "comelón lento" durante la introducción de alimentos sólidos.

**Tabla de resultados**

| Prueba / Subprueba | Idioma | Puntuación estándar / escalada | Percentil |
|---|---|---|---|
| BESA – Morfosintaxis | Español | 76 | 5 |
| BESA – Morfosintaxis | Inglés | 71 | 3 |
| BESA – Fonología | Español | 74 | 4 |
| CELF Preschool-3 – Conceptos y Siguiendo Instrucciones | Inglés | 5 (escalada) | 5 |
| GFTA-3 | Inglés | 68 | 2 |

**7. Impresiones clínicas**

Con base en los resultados estandarizados, la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, la evaluación dinámica y la información proporcionada por los padres y el personal del Centro de Cuidado Infantil Sunny Days, Mateo presenta un trastorno del lenguaje que afecta tanto el español como el inglés, además de un trastorno fonológico. El hecho de que Teo muestre dificultades similares en ambos idiomas, sin una fortaleza relativa en el idioma de mayor exposición, apoya la impresión de un trastorno primario del lenguaje (diagnóstico F80.9) más que una diferencia esperada de adquisición bilingüe. El procedimiento de evaluación dinámica confirmó esta impresión: con enseñanza breve de estructuras morfosintácticas específicas, Mateo mostró una generalización limitada, lo cual es consistente con un trastorno del lenguaje más que con una brecha de exposición lingüística que se resolvería con más tiempo.

El perfil fonológico, caracterizado por reducción de grupos consonánticos, frontalización de velares y simplificación de líquidas en ambos idiomas, es consistente con un trastorno fonológico (diagnóstico F80.0) de gravedad moderada a severa. La inteligibilidad reducida (aproximadamente 30% con oyentes no familiares) representa una limitación funcional significativa para la participación social y educativa de Mateo, particularmente en el entorno de la guardería, donde depende de comunicarse con compañeros como Diego y con las maestras Carmen y López.

Es importante señalar que las dificultades de Mateo no parecen explicarse por los antecedentes de otitis media, dado que su perfil de errores persiste de forma similar después de la resolución del derrame del oído medio tras la colocación de los tubos de ventilación. Tampoco se identificaron indicadores de un trastorno motor del habla de tipo apráxico, aunque se recomienda seguimiento si la respuesta al tratamiento es más lenta de lo esperado.

**8. Recomendaciones**

1. Se recomienda que Mateo reciba terapia del habla y lenguaje de forma individual, dos veces por semana, con sesiones de 30 minutos, utilizando un enfoque bilingüe que incorpore tanto español como inglés, dado que ambos idiomas están afectados.
2. Se recomienda el uso de un enfoque de intervención basado en el enfoque Hanen para apoyar las estrategias de los padres en el hogar, con énfasis en la expansión del enunciado y el modelado en ambos idiomas.
3. Para el componente fonológico, se recomienda un enfoque de Cycles dirigido a los procesos fonológicos identificados (reducción de grupos consonánticos, frontalización de velares, simplificación de líquidas), con sesiones estructuradas en ambos idiomas cuando sea posible.
4. Se recomienda coordinación con el Centro de Cuidado Infantil Sunny Days, incluyendo a la maestra Carmen y a la Srta. López, para reforzar estrategias de comunicación dentro del salón, incluyendo el uso de apoyos visuales para instrucciones de dos pasos.
5. Se recomienda que la familia continúe el seguimiento con el Dr. Winters para monitorear la salud del oído medio, dado el historial de otitis media recurrente.
6. Dado que la familia ya no califica para servicios de intervención temprana de la Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Piedmont (CDSA) por la edad de Mateo, se recomienda la referencia al programa de educación especial preescolar del distrito escolar correspondiente para una posible evaluación de elegibilidad bajo la categoría de trastorno del habla y lenguaje.
7. Se recomienda que la coordinadora de casos de la familia, con el apoyo del coordinador de servicios, Mr. Tom, en la Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Durham, ayude a la familia a completar el proceso de referencia escolar dentro de los próximos 30 días.
8. Se recomienda reevaluación en 6 meses para monitorear el progreso y ajustar las metas de tratamiento según corresponda.
9. Se sugiere que la familia considere continuar su participación en los programas de apoyo de Durham's Partnership for Children, que ofrecen recursos de alfabetización familiar bilingüe que podrían complementar la terapia directa.

**Metas sugeridas para el plan de tratamiento (si se inicia IFSP o IEP):**

- Meta 1: Mateo producirá enunciados de al menos cuatro palabras con concordancia de género correcta en el 80% de las oportunidades durante actividades estructuradas, en español, con claves mínimas.
- Meta 2: Mateo producirá el sonido /k/ en posición inicial de palabra con 80% de precisión en conversación espontánea, en ambos idiomas, con claves moderadas o menos.
- Meta 3: Mateo seguirá instrucciones de dos pasos con elementos espaciales en el 80% de las oportunidades en el salón de clase, con apoyo visual.

**9. Resumen**

Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez, de 4;2, presenta un trastorno del lenguaje que afecta tanto el español como el inglés, junto con un trastorno fonológico de gravedad moderada a severa, con inteligibilidad reducida que limita su participación en el hogar y en el Centro de Cuidado Infantil Sunny Days. Se recomienda terapia bilingüe individual, coordinación estrecha con la familia, incluyendo a Hugo, Lucía y doña Lupe, y con el personal educativo, así como referencia oportuna a servicios de educación especial preescolar. Agradecemos a la familia Flores Rodríguez su participación activa y su disposición para colaborar con todas las partes involucradas en el cuidado de Teo.

Quedo disponible para cualquier pregunta adicional sobre este informe.

Respetuosamente,

Patóloga del Habla y Lenguaje Bilingüe

Plan de Servicio Familiar Individualizado (PSFI) — Six-Month IFSP Review

**Child's Legal Name:** Mateo Alejandro Vásquez-Ortiz (called "Teo" at home)
**Date of Birth:** April 9, 2024
**IFSP Review Date:** October 2, 2026
**Previous IFSP Date:** March 18, 2026
**Record Number:** IT-204871
**Medicaid ID:** 881204673B
**Home Address:** 142 Sycamore Hollow Lane, Haverford, NC 28677, Ashcombe County
**Home Phone:** (828) 555-0147  **Mother's Mobile:** (828) 555-0183
**Parent Email:** lucia.rodriguezdelacruz@gmail.com

**Mother:** Lucía Rodríguez de la Cruz
**Father:** Carlos Vásquez
**Sibling:** hermana mayor Camila, 3 years old
**Family Caregiver:** abuela materna Rosa de la Cruz, currently residing in Aldea El Progreso, Quetzaltenango, Guatemala, who visits for several weeks each year
**Family Caregiver:** niñera Teresa Nguyen, who cares for Teo two afternoons a week

**Service Coordinator:** Jennifer Hall, Foothills CDSA, 920 Westbrook Avenue, Suite 200, Haverford, NC 28677; office phone (828) 555-2200

**Report Prepared By:** Isabel Martín-Suárez, MS, CCC-SLP, bilingual (English/Spanish) speech-language pathologist, Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC
**Clinician Email:** isabel.martinsuarez@carolinabilingualtherapy.com  **Clinician Phone:** (704) 555-9021

---

**Preocupaciones, Prioridades y Recursos de la Familia / Family Concerns, Priorities, and Resources**

During the home visit on September 20, 2026, su mamá Lucía Rodríguez de la Cruz shared, in her own words: "Queremos que Teo pueda decirnos lo que necesita, that he can tell us sin frustrarse tanto. En la casa hablamos español, pero en el daycare todo es inglés, and we worry he's getting confused, que no va a hablar ninguno de los dos idiomas bien."

Carlos Vásquez added, through the same conversation, "I just want him to be able to play with his cousins at Navidad and have them understand him. Ahorita nadie le entiende, ni nosotros a veces."

The family's priorities, as stated during the review, are:

1. Que Teo aumente su vocabulario funcional en español e inglés para que la familia pueda comunicarse con él sin tanta frustración.
2. That Teo's speech become clearer so that his hermana Camila and extended family, including Rosa de la Cruz when she visits from Guatemala, can understand him.
3. Coaching for both parents and for la niñera Teresa Nguyen on consistent strategies across home and daycare.

The family identified the following resources and supports: Lucía Rodríguez de la Cruz's extended maternal family in Aldea El Progreso, Quetzaltenango; involvement with their church community in Haverford; and stable employment for Carlos Vásquez at Ridgeline Furniture Manufacturing.

---

**Background and Medical History**

Teo was born at 35 weeks gestational age at Catawba Valley Health System – Pinecrest Campus on April 9, 2024, birth weight 4 lbs 9 oz, with Apgar scores of 6 and 8 at 1 and 5 minutes. He spent 11 days in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit for respiratory support and feeding stabilization before discharge.

He has a history of recurrent otitis media and was referred to Blue Ridge Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology – Haverford Office, where pressure-equalization tubes were placed in June 2025. A follow-up audiogram on August 14, 2026 showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally. His pediatrician, Dr. Grace Odom at Catawba Valley Health System – Pinecrest Pediatric Clinic, has monitored growth and development since birth and supports continued speech-language services.

Lucía Rodríguez de la Cruz reported that Teo said his first words, "mamá" and "agua," around 18 months, but that his vocabulary growth has been slow since. ICD-10 diagnostic code F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) applies based on current evaluation.

---

**Niveles Actuales de Desarrollo / Present Levels of Development**

The Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5, Spanish-English bilingual edition) was administered on September 20, 2026 by Isabel Martín-Suárez, MS, CCC-SLP, using best-performance scoring across both languages.

| Subtest | Standard Score (95% CI) | Percentile | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auditory Comprehension | 73–83 | 4th | 1;9–2;0 |
| Expressive Communication | 70–80 | 2nd | 1;6–1;9 |
| Total Language Score | 68–78 | 2nd | 1;7–1;10 |

At his chronological age of 2;5, Teo produces an estimated 35 single words and 0 two-word combinations across both languages combined. Spontaneous speech samples showed frequent final-consonant deletion and stopping of fricatives. He produced "agua" as [ˈawa] and "perro" as [ˈpejo], and in English, "water" was produced as [ˈwawa]. Target consonants /s/, /r/, and the trilled /ɾ/ were absent in spontaneous speech; with moderate cues, he approximated the target word "pan" as [pan] in 3 of 5 trials. On a 20-item single-word articulation probe administered in both languages, he scored 8/10 in Spanish and 6/10 in English for stimulability of final consonants with minimal cues.

Teo uses pointing and some conventional gestures to request preferred items but does not yet combine gesture with vocalization consistently. He engages in brief turn-taking during peekaboo and ball-rolling play but shows limited joint attention during book-sharing, per both clinical observation and caregiver report.

---

**Rutinas Diarias y Ambientes Naturales / Daily Routines and Natural Environments**

**Mornings at home:** Teo wakes around 6:30 a.m. and eats breakfast with Lucía Rodríguez de la Cruz and Camila before daycare drop-off. Lucía Rodríguez de la Cruz described this routine: "Él señala el refrigerador y yo le pregunto, '¿qué quieres?,' pero casi nunca me contesta con palabras, just points and grunts."

**Daycare:** Teo attends Sunshine Beginnings Daycare in Haverford from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. His lead teacher, Ms. Donna Pruitt, reports that he participates in circle time but rarely imitates songs or words and tends to play alongside, rather than with, classmates such as Avery and Jamal.

**Afternoons/Evenings:** Two afternoons a week, la niñera Teresa Nguyen picks up Teo and Camila and supervises snack and outdoor play until Carlos Vásquez arrives home around 5:45 p.m. Dinner and bath are the most communication-rich routines, according to the family; bedtime includes a shared Spanish-language picture book, "Buenas noches, Luna" (a title, not a client identifier).

**Family visits:** When Rosa de la Cruz visits from Aldea El Progreso, Quetzaltenango, she reports difficulty understanding Teo's speech and relies heavily on Lucía Rodríguez de la Cruz to interpret his requests.

---

**Otras Agencias Involucradas / Other Agencies Involved**

The family currently receives services and supports through the following agencies in addition to Foothills CDSA:

- Haverford WIC Office — nutrition supports for Teo and Camila
- Ashcombe County Department of Social Services — Medicaid case management
- Smart Start of Ashcombe County — childcare subsidy supporting enrollment at Sunshine Beginnings Daycare
- Blue Ridge Ear, Nose & Throat and Audiology – Haverford Office — ongoing hearing monitoring

---

**Resultados / Outcomes**

**Outcome 1:** Teo will use words and gestures together to request and comment during daily play and mealtime routines, in Spanish and/or English.

*Strategies:* Isabel Martín-Suárez will coach Lucía Rodríguez de la Cruz and Carlos Vásquez using Hanen It Takes Two to Talk strategies, including OWL (Observe, Wait, Listen), during home visits and via a brief video-review model. Daycare staff will be coached to use the same wait-time strategies during snack and center time.

*Criteria/Procedures/Timelines:* Teo will use 10 different word approximations paired with gesture across 3 of 5 observed opportunities, measured through clinician observation and caregiver log, by April 2027.

**Outcome 2:** Teo will increase speech sound intelligibility in both languages for familiar listeners.

*Strategies:* Cycles phonological approach targeting final consonant deletion and stopping of fricatives, alternating target patterns across Spanish and English words each session. PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing will support jaw and lip placement for bilabial and alveolar targets.

*Criteria/Procedures/Timelines:* Teo will produce targeted final consonants in words with min-mod cues in 8/10 trials across two consecutive sessions, by April 2027.

**Outcome 3:** Teo will use a functional communication system to reduce frustration during transitions at home and daycare.

*Strategies:* Introduce PECS (Picture Exchange Communication System) for choice-making during transitions, with picture symbols labeled in both Spanish and English. If verbal approximations increase, incorporate the Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol word-approximation hierarchy to shape closer productions of core vocabulary.

*Criteria/Procedures/Timelines:* Teo will initiate a picture exchange or word approximation during 4 of 5 transition routines, measured via daycare and home data sheets, by April 2027.

---

**Servicios / Services**

| Service | Frequency/Intensity | Location | Provider/Agency | Dates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Speech-Language Therapy | 2x/week, 45 minutes | Home and Sunshine Beginnings Daycare | Isabel Martín-Suárez, Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC | October 15, 2026–April 15, 2027 |
| Service Coordination | Monthly | Home/phone | Jennifer Hall, Foothills CDSA | October 15, 2026–April 15, 2027 |

Billing codes associated with this evaluation and ongoing treatment include CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression) and CPT 92507 (individual speech-language treatment).

---

**Consentimiento y Firmas / Consent and Signatures**

The team, including Lucía Rodríguez de la Cruz, Carlos Vásquez, Jennifer Hall, and Isabel Martín-Suárez, met on October 2, 2026 to review progress and update outcomes. The family consented to continued services as outlined above.

Mateo Alejandro Fernández Rodríguez — Speech-Language Evaluation Report

**1. IDENTIFYING INFORMATION**

Client: Mateo Alejandro Fernández Rodríguez ("Mateo")
Date of Birth: April 19, 2023
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 2;7
Evaluation Date: November 3, 2025
Report Date: November 10, 2025
Primary Language(s): Spanish (home), English (preschool)
Medicaid ID: 803417562B
Case/Referral ID: WCDSA-2025-11284
Referral Source: Wake County CDSA, Service Coordinator Monica Alvarez
Evaluating Clinician: Jennifer Lin, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Clinic: Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Partners, PLLC
Clinic Address: 118 Kildaire Court, Suite 204, Cary, NC 27518
Clinic Phone: (919) 555-0148
Clinician Email: jlin@carolinabilingualslp.com
Interpreter present: Mr. Tom Reyes (certified medical interpreter, Spanish/English)

**2. REASON FOR REFERRAL**

Mateo was referred to Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Partners, PLLC by Wake County CDSA following a Child Find screening on October 6, 2025 that flagged delayed expressive language in both Spanish and English. His mother, Lucía Rodríguez, reports that Mateo uses fewer than 20 single words and does not yet combine words into phrases. His father, Carlos Fernández, reports similar concerns and notes that Mateo's older sister, Valentina Fernández Rodríguez, was speaking in full sentences by 2;0. The family requests evaluation in Spanish and English to determine eligibility for early intervention services and to guide a home program.

**3. BACKGROUND INFORMATION**

**3.1 Family Constellation**

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez; his father, Carlos Fernández; and his sister, Valentina Fernández Rodríguez, age 7, at 142 Willow Bend Lane, Apex, NC 27502, in Wake County. His maternal grandmother, referred to in the home as "doña Lupe," lives with the family three days a week and provides primary daytime care when Lucía Rodríguez is at work. The family also has a pet dog named Rocky, whom Mateo enjoys chasing in the backyard.

Lucía Rodríguez is originally from the village of El Rosario, in the department of Olancho, Honduras, and moved to the United States in 2016. She works as a loan processor at Blue Ridge Financial Group in Raleigh. Carlos Fernández was born in Siguatepeque, Honduras, and works in logistics locally. Both parents report that extended family, including an aunt who still lives near El Rosario, call frequently by video and speak Spanish with Mateo during those calls.

**3.2 Birth and Medical History**

Mateo was born at 39 weeks gestation via uncomplicated vaginal delivery at Piedmont Women's Hospital in Raleigh on April 19, 2023. Birth weight was 7 lbs 2 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. There were no complications during pregnancy or delivery, and Mateo did not require NICU care.

Medical history is largely unremarkable. Mateo passed his newborn hearing screening bilaterally and has had no further audiological concerns reported by the family, although a diagnostic audiological evaluation is recommended below given the speech-language profile. He has had no history of chronic ear infections, tympanostomy tubes, or hospitalizations. His pediatrician, Dr. Amrita Patel of Apex Pediatric Associates, last evaluated him for a well-child visit on September 15, 2025, with no concerns noted outside of the speech-language referral. Developmental milestones for gross and fine motor skills were reported as age-appropriate by parent report; Mateo walked independently at 13 months.

**3.3 Family and Language History**

The home language environment is predominantly Spanish. Lucía Rodríguez and Carlos Fernández both report speaking Spanish approximately 80% of the time at home, with English used primarily when Valentina Fernández Rodríguez is present, as she attends an English-medium elementary school. Doña Lupe speaks exclusively Spanish with Mateo.

Mateo attends The Caterpillar's Corner Early Learning Cottage, a small bilingual preschool program located at 905 Beaver Creek Commons, Apex, NC 27502, four mornings per week. His lead teacher, referred to by the family as "la maestra Carmen," reports that Mateo primarily uses gestures and a small number of English words to communicate with peers, including his classmate Sofia, with whom he plays most often during free time. The assistant teacher, "Miss Ana," corroborated these observations and noted that Mateo becomes frustrated when peers do not understand his requests.

There is no reported family history of speech, language, or hearing disorders on either side of the family. No other children in the household have required early intervention services.

**4. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES**

The following procedures were completed across two sessions, on October 27, 2025 and November 3, 2025, at the clinic location listed above. Testing was conducted in both English and Spanish, with items administered in the child's stronger language where appropriate and interpreter support from Mr. Tom Reyes for parent interview portions.

- Parent interview and case history review
- Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (Spanish and English forms)
- Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4), Language subtests
- Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition (PPVT-5), English administration
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3), Spanish-adapted protocol
- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-English bilingual edition
- Oral-motor examination
- Clinical observation of play-based communication across two settings

**5. BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS**

Mateo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with toys and the clinician across both sessions. He demonstrated functional play skills, including pretend feeding of a stuffed animal and stacking blocks to build a tower of 6 blocks. Joint attention and eye contact were age-appropriate. Mateo used pointing and reaching consistently to request desired items and demonstrated protodeclarative pointing to share interest in objects, such as pointing to an airplane toy while vocalizing.

Expressively, Mateo produced a small number of single words in both languages, including "mamá," "agua" (produced as "awa"), "more," and "up." He combined two words on only one observed occasion, saying "más awa" when requesting more water. Oral-motor structures were within normal limits for symmetry, strength, and range of motion. No signs of dysarthria or apraxia of speech were observed, although continued monitoring for motor speech involvement is recommended given the limited consonant inventory.

**6. TEST RESULTS**

| Measure | Domain | Standard Score | Percentile | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale | Receptive Language | 78 | 7th | 18-20 months |
| Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale | Expressive Language | 70 | 2nd | 14-16 months |
| Bayley-4 | Language Composite | 76 | 5th | 19 months |
| PPVT-5 | Receptive Vocabulary (English) | 82 | 12th | 22 months |
| GFTA-3 (Spanish-adapted) | Articulation | 73 | 4th | — |
| PLS-5 | Auditory Comprehension | 75 | 5th | 20 months |
| PLS-5 | Expressive Communication | 68 | 2nd | 16 months |

Confidence intervals for the PLS-5 composite scores fell in the range of 65-79 at the 90% confidence level. Mateo's expressive vocabulary, measured through parent report checklist and direct elicitation, totaled approximately 18 words across both languages, falling well below the expected range of 50 or more words for his chronological age. His consonant inventory included /m/, /p/, /b/, and /w/, with notable absence of /t/, /d/, /k/, and /g/ in spontaneous speech. He demonstrated final consonant deletion in all attempted productions, for example producing "pato" as "pa."

**7. CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS**

Mateo presents with a significant expressive and receptive language delay across both Spanish and English, consistent with a diagnosis of Language Disorder affecting both of his languages, rather than a difference attributable solely to bilingual exposure. His performance on the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, Bayley-4, and PLS-5 converge to indicate expressive language functioning at approximately the 14-16 month level against a chronological age of 2;7, representing a delay of roughly 12-14 months. Receptive language, while also delayed, is relatively stronger than expressive language, a pattern consistent with an expressive-predominant language disorder.

Articulation and phonology are also significantly delayed, with a restricted consonant inventory and consistent final consonant deletion that further limits intelligibility. Given the combination of limited expressive vocabulary, limited phonemic inventory, and parent report of frustration during communication breakdowns, Mateo meets criteria for early intervention eligibility under both language delay and speech sound disorder categories per North Carolina's Infant-Toddler Program guidelines.

No concerns regarding oral-motor structure, hearing acuity (pending formal audiological evaluation), or social-pragmatic skills were identified at this time. Mateo's play skills, joint attention, and nonverbal communication are age-appropriate strengths that will support intervention.

**8. RECOMMENDATIONS**

1. Mateo qualifies for an Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) through Wake County CDSA. An IFSP meeting should be scheduled within 45 days of this evaluation per federal timelines.
2. Initiate speech-language therapy twice weekly, targeting expressive vocabulary growth, two-word combinations, and expansion of the consonant inventory, with sessions delivered in Spanish, English, or both per family preference.
3. Refer for a diagnostic audiological evaluation to rule out subtle hearing loss contributing to the language delay, despite normal newborn screening results.
4. Provide the family with a home language stimulation program emphasizing shared book reading and parallel talk in Spanish, the family's dominant language, to support first-language development alongside English exposure at The Caterpillar's Corner Early Learning Cottage.
5. Coordinate with la maestra Carmen and Miss Ana at the preschool to implement classroom-based communication supports, including visual choice boards, during peer interactions with children such as Sofia.
6. Re-evaluate in six months to monitor progress and adjust the IFSP outcomes as needed.
7. Continue to monitor oral-motor and feeding skills informally at future sessions given the limited consonant inventory, with referral to a motor speech specialist if minimal progress is observed after three months of therapy.

**9. PROPOSED SESSION SCHEDULE**

The following schedule was proposed and agreed upon with the family, effective November 17, 2025:

| Day | Start Time | End Time | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 9:00 AM | 9:45 AM | Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Partners, PLLC, 118 Kildaire Court, Suite 204, Cary, NC 27518 |
| Wednesday | 2:30 PM | 3:15 PM | The Caterpillar's Corner Early Learning Cottage, 905 Beaver Creek Commons, Apex, NC 27502 |
| Every other Friday | 10:15 AM | 11:00 AM | Home visit, 142 Willow Bend Lane, Apex, NC 27502 |

Transportation and scheduling were confirmed by phone with Lucía Rodríguez at (919) 555-0177 on November 5, 2025. The family indicated that doña Lupe would be present for the home visits given her daytime caregiving role, and that Carlos Fernández would attend the Monday clinic sessions when his work schedule allows.

**10. SUMMARY**

Mateo Alejandro Fernández Rodríguez, a 2;7-year-old bilingual Spanish-English speaking child, presents with a significant language disorder affecting both expressive and receptive domains across both languages, alongside a co-occurring speech sound disorder characterized by a restricted consonant inventory and final consonant deletion. Testing across the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, Bayley-4, PPVT-5, GFTA-3, and PLS-5 converged to support this diagnosis. He qualifies for early intervention services through Wake County CDSA and is recommended for twice-weekly bilingual speech-language therapy, audiological referral, and coordinated home and preschool programming. Strengths in play, joint attention, and nonverbal communication provide a solid foundation for intervention.

This evaluation was completed by Jennifer Lin, M.S., CCC-SLP, of Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Partners, PLLC, with interpreter support from Mr. Tom Reyes. Questions regarding this report may be directed to jlin@carolinabilingualslp.com or (919) 555-0148.

Electronically signed: Jennifer Lin, M.S., CCC-SLP
Date: November 10, 2025

S:
Mamá Lucía Ortiz and stepfather Ramón Castillo present for visit start; bio father Héctor Reyes joined by phone at 9:30 AM. Abuela Rosa (maternal grandmother, primary daytime caregiver) also present w/ family dog "Toby" underfoot throughout.

Mamá, via interpreter Soto: "Teo dice más palabras pero todavía mezcla español e inglés, y a veces solo gruñe cuando quiere algo." SC Hollis documented translation. Priority restated: more words at home in both languages, fewer tantrums when not understood.

Work/schedule update, impacting session timing and carryover: mamá Lucía works mornings at Tienda La Esperanza (corner grocery) and 2x/wk evenings cleaning at Servicio de Limpieza Estrella Dorada, shift 5:00 PM–9:00 PM; per mom in English, "I'm at the Star Dorada Cleaning Service most Tuesdays and Thursdays." Bio father Héctor works 2nd shift at Planta Procesadora de Pollo Monte Verde, 2:00 PM–10:00 PM, and picks up weekend hours with Díaz Construction Co.; mamá noted, "Héctor trabaja en la Planta Procesadora de Pollo Monte Verde y los sábados con Construcciones Díaz." Stepfather Ramón works line cook at Restaurante El Sazón, 11:00 AM–7:00 PM, and seasonally helps at Granja Hermanos Pérez during harvest; mamá: "Ramón trabaja en el Restaurante El Sazón, y en la Granja Hermanos Pérez cuando hay cosecha." Per mom, in English order, stepfather works at the El Sazón Restaurant and, during harvest, the Pérez Brothers Farm.

Pickup varies 4:30 PM–6:00 PM depending who is off shift. Dinner approx 6:30 PM, bath 7:30 PM, bedtime routine w/ books 8:00 PM, asleep by 8:30 PM. Weekends split between home and occasional visits to bio father Héctor's apartment.

Older sister Camila Reyes Ortiz (age 6, 1st grade, Oakdale Elementary) models language for Teo and often translates/speaks for him; team discussed reducing sibling-translating role, coaching family to pause and let Teo attempt communication first per Hanen "it's your turn" strategy. Neighbor Walt Pruitt occasionally watches Camila after school when all three adults' shifts overlap; not involved in Teo's care.

Other agencies/supports: family enrolled in Catawba County WIC; applied for childcare subsidy through Catawba County DSS; SC Hollis referred family to Catawba County Smart Start home-visiting program given varied parent shifts and request for literacy support in both languages. Family also previously connected w/ Catawba County Early Head Start waitlist (pending slot).

Birth/med hx reconfirmed: born March 14, 2024 at Foothills Regional Medical Center, GA 36 wks, birth weight 5 lb 4 oz, Apgar 8/9. No hospitalizations since. Hearing screen WFL at birth; no current ENT concerns per mom.

O:
Teo engaged readily in reciprocal play w/ Alston using bubbles, shape sorter, and cause-effect toys; joint attention adequate, eye contact consistent, affect bright. Brief session format 9:15 AM–10:00 AM (45 min total; 9:15–9:30 play-based language sampling, 9:30–9:50 direct coaching w/ family, 9:50–10:00 wrap-up/planning).

PLS-5 Spanish-English Bilingual Edition administered September 22, 2026: Auditory Comprehension SS 78 (8th %ile), Expressive Communication SS 73 (4th %ile), Total Language Score 74 (4th %ile), 95% CI 68-80. Age-equivalent range 18-21 months expressive. Compare prior admin April 10, 2026: Total Language Score then 65.

Expressive language sample today: approx 35 distinct single words across both languages, 2 spontaneous two-word combinations noted — "mas agua" and "up please." Vocalized frustration grunts x6 across session when a request wasn't understood by Abuela Rosa; each resolved w/ mod cues plus modeling and a visual choice board. Imitated CV combos w/ /p/, /m/, /b/ onsets; [w] substitution for /w/ stable across trials. Attempted target "pelota" produced as [peˈota] (glide/liquid substitution, medium intelligibility in context).

Receptive: followed 2-step directions in Spanish 3/5 trials, in English 2/5 trials. Pointed to 9/10 familiar objects named in Spanish, 7/10 in English. No oral-motor structural concerns noted on brief screen; feeding/swallowing WFL per mom report, no coughing/choking reported.

Social: brief protest behavior (dropping to floor, pushing toy away) x2 when daycare transition mentioned; redirected w/ min cues within 30 sec. No concerns re: motor skills; walking, running, climbing age-appropriate per observation and mom report.

A:
Teo continues to present w/ expressive and receptive language delay in the context of bilingual development, consistent w/ ICD-10 F80.9. CPT 92523 billed this visit, modifier GN. Current PLS-5 Total Language Score 74 (CI 68-80) reflects measurable gain from April 10, 2026 baseline score of 65; vocabulary has roughly doubled and first spontaneous two-word combinations are emerging, consistent with family's reported progress.

Frustration behaviors (grunting, brief protest/tantrum) correlate directly w/ unmet communicative attempts across caregivers and settings; behaviors are responsive to mod-to-min cues and visual supports, a favorable prognostic sign.

IFSP Outcome #1 (written April 14, 2026): "Teo will use 2-word combinations to request and comment across settings w/ min-mod cues." Progress: emerging — 2 spontaneous combos today, up from 0 at prior review. Outcome continues, not yet met.

IFSP Outcome #2: "Family will report decreased frustration behaviors at home and at daycare." Per mom report and phone contact w/ Little Sprouts Daycare staff (October 2, 2026), tantrum frequency decreased from daily to approx 3x/week. Outcome partially met; continue.

Family priorities confirmed and reordered: (1) more words at home in both languages; (2) continued reduction in frustration/tantrum behaviors; (3) consistent bilingual strategy carryover between home, Abuela Rosa, and Little Sprouts Daycare; (4) connection to Catawba County Smart Start home visitor re: literacy supports given parents' rotating shifts across Tienda La Esperanza, Planta Procesadora de Pollo Monte Verde, and Restaurante El Sazón.

3. Strategies for all caregivers: Hanen "it's your turn," expansion and extension of child utterances, consistent use of a visual choice board at transition points, reduced sibling-translating role for Camila, wait-time coaching for Abuela Rosa.
4. SC Hollis to coordinate consult w/ daycare lead teacher Keisha Lamb at Little Sprouts Daycare re: strategy carryover and classroom peer interactions (peers Jaylen and Sofía noted as frequent playmates per teacher report).
5. SC Hollis to follow up on Catawba County Smart Start referral status and Catawba County DSS subsidy application by October 23, 2026.

Author: Jennifer Osei, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingüe, Carolina Bilingual Therapy Associates

S: Visita en el hogar con Lucía Rodríguez (mamá) y abuela Rosa Cruz presentes; papá Carlos Fernández se unió por teléfono desde su turno en Food Lion Distribution Center. Mamá reports Mateo ("Teo") is "más cariñoso pero todavía no habla como su hermana a esta edad," comparing him to Camila Fernández Cruz, who was "hablando oraciones completas" by 18 months.

Preocupaciones de la familia (en sus propias palabras): mamá dice, "No entiende cuando le hablo en español o en inglés, se frustra y me jala la mano." Abuela Rosa Cruz, who cares for Mateo weekday mornings while mamá works, adds, "Se enoja y tira las cosas cuando no lo entendemos." Papá, by phone, reports Mateo "repite sonidos pero no palabras claras" en casa por las tardes.

Prioridades de la familia: 1) Mateo use words instead of tantrums to request wants; 2) family understand his attempts in both Spanish and English; 3) support transition into the toddler classroom at daycare.

Rutinas diarias: Wakes ~7:00 a.m.; breakfast with abuela Rosa Cruz; Mateo attends the Early Head Start toddler classroom housed at Forest Pines Elementary, a Wake County Public School System collaborative site, 8:30 a.m.–3:00 p.m. Mon–Fri; teacher Keisha Lopez reports he "points and grunts to get toys from Liam" rather than using words. Evenings: bath, cena en familia, bedtime routine with abuela Rosa Cruz cantándole canciones.

Otras agencias involucradas: family enrolled in WIC; coordinadora Ana María Torres also referred the family to the Early Head Start home-visiting component for reinforcement between SLP visits; previously connected to Durham County DSS for childcare subsidy.

Family dog Luna is "su compañera favorita"; mamá reports he says "uh uh" when he wants to go outside with Luna — not yet a true word attempt.

Developmental/medical history per parent report and chart review: Mateo born at 32 weeks gestation at Duke Regional Hospital on 14 de enero de 2023 (discharge summary dated 01/14/2023), birth weight 3 lb 14 oz, Apgar scores 6 and 8; 21-day NICU stay at Duke Regional Hospital under neonatologist Dr. Fatima Ahmed. Pediatrician Dr. Rajesh Patel referred for CDSA eval at 12 months adjusted age due to absence of words. No history of ear infections per mamá; passed newborn hearing screen.

O: Direct assessment conducted el martes 4 de junio de 2024 por Jennifer Osei, SLP, with interpreter Marta Delgado present for portions in Spanish; reassessment observation today, 3 de marzo de 2025, during home visit, 10:00 a.m.–11:15 a.m.

Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5) bilingual Spanish-English administration: Auditory Comprehension standard score 68 (2nd percentile); Expressive Communication standard score 62 (1st percentile); Total Language Score 63, confidence interval 58-68. Age equivalents 11-13 months expressive, 14-16 months receptive.

Spontaneous sound inventory: produces /m/, /b/, /p/, /a/, vocal play approximating [w]; no consonant-vowel-consonant combinations observed. Imitated "mamá" as [ma], omitting final syllable. Did not imitate "agua" with mod cues; produced "más" as [ma] with max cues on 2 of 5 trials.

Receptive probes (bilingual, alternating per family use): followed one-step directions without gesture 3 of 10 (30%); with gesture cue, 8/10 (80%). Pointed to body parts on request (nariz/nose, ojos/eyes) 4 of 8. Joint attention present but brief; initiated bids by pulling adult's hand rather than pointing or vocalizing on 7 of 10 opportunities.

Play/pragmatics: functional play with cars and blocks; no symbolic play observed; limited turn-taking in routine games — participated 2 of 5 rounds.

Oral-motor exam: structures within normal limits; adequate strength/ROM for age; no feeding concerns per mamá.

Hearing: passed newborn screen; no formal audiological eval since; referral recommended given severity of delay.

PT collateral report from Sarah Kim, PT: gross motor skills age-appropriate, ambulating independently since 14 months; fine motor mildly delayed, working on pincer grasp.

Classroom observation (reported by Ms. Lopez): Mateo uses 2-3 gestures functionally (reaching, pushing away); no spoken words noted across 3 months of classroom data; frustration tantrums 3-4x/day when wants are not understood by peers including Liam.

Billing this visit: 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression); 92507 (individual treatment of speech, language disorder) for the parent-coaching portion, modifier GN.

A: Mateo presents with severe mixed receptive-expressive language delay in both Spanish and English, consistent with ICD-10 F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder), in the context of prematurity (32 weeks gestation) and a NICU course at Duke Regional Hospital. Scores remain in the severe range across standardized (PLS-5) and informal bilingual probes; receptive gains noted with visual/gesture support (80% vs 30% without), suggesting stimulability for structured cueing. No emerging word approximations beyond [ma] for "mamá"; vocabulary and MLU remain pre-linguistic. M-CHAT screening administered this visit negative; social reciprocity and joint attention intact, reducing concern for a co-occurring autism spectrum presentation at this time.

Family concerns are consistent with and corroborated by direct assessment, parent report, and classroom data from Ms. Lopez's room. Mateo continues to meet NC eligibility criteria for Infant-Toddler Program services based on a 50% delay in the communication domain. Prognosis guarded-to-fair with intensive, consistent bilingual intervention and caregiver coaching; risk factors include limited symbolic play, infrequent intentional communication attempts, and a classroom communication barrier with peers.

Recommend continued SLP services at current intensity, caregiver-implemented strategies at home and at Forest Pines Elementary, audiology referral to rule out a mild hearing loss contributing to the delay, and coordination with Ms. Lopez's classroom for low-tech AAC supports pending further progress.

P: IFSP outcomes reviewed and revised, effective 3 de marzo de 2025 through 03/03/2026:

Outcome 1: Mateo will use 10 functional single words or approximations (Spanish and/or English) to request wants across home and classroom settings, from baseline 0 to 8/10 opportunities with mod cues, by next review. Strategy: family and Ms. Lopez model target words during routines (snack, outside time); SLP to coach using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies in Spanish and English during biweekly sessions; introduce a core board as backup.

Outcome 2: Family (mamá, papá, abuela Rosa Cruz) will report increased understanding of Mateo's communication attempts, rated via caregiver checklist, from "rarely understands" to "usually understands" (3 of 4 routines) by next review. Strategy: SLP to provide bilingual caregiver coaching handouts; coordinadora Ana María Torres to connect family with the Early Head Start home visitor for reinforcement between SLP visits.

Outcome 3: Mateo will participate in 3 of 5 turn-taking routines with peers (including Liam) in the classroom without tantrum, up from 2 of 5, by next review. Strategy: classroom staff to use visual supports and wait time; SLP consult visit to the Forest Pines Elementary classroom scheduled for 14 de abril de 2025.

Services continued: speech-language therapy, individual, home and daycare settings, billed 92507; annual reassessment billed 92523. PT consult continued per Sarah Kim. Service coordination monthly contact by Ana María Torres, CSFT, phone (919) 555-0148, email atorres@csftriangulo.org.

Audiology referral placed to rule out contributing hearing loss; results due to CDSA Centro-Oriente by 04/01/2025.

Next IFSP review: el martes 2 de septiembre de 2025, or sooner if eligibility or services change. Family consents to continued services and to share records with Wake County Public School System for future Part C-to-B transition planning. Transition conference tentatively marzo de 2026, as Mateo approaches 3 years of age.

Reviewed and signed: Jennifer Osei, M.S., CCC-SLP; Ana María Torres, Service Coordinator; Lucía Rodríguez; Carlos Fernández (verbal consent via phone, documented 3/3/2025).

text:
+ Name: Mateo Alejandro Reyes Castillo
+ CA: 4;2
+ Context: Comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation, clinic-based, with interpreter support
+ Examiner: Dana Whitfield, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
+ Interpreter: Rosa Elena Fuentes, Spanish Medical Interpreter
+ Date of Evaluation: 3 de marzo de 2025
+ Date of Report: March 10, 2025
+ Date of Birth: 01/05/2021
+ Referral Source: Dr. Priya Kapoor, Pediatrician, Cape Fear Pediatric Associates
+ Record #: LD-48291-R
+ Medicaid ID: 920483715K

SUMMARY

Mateo is a 4;2-year-old bilingual (Spanish/English) boy who was referred by his pediatrician, Dr. Priya Kapoor, due to concerns regarding limited intelligibility, reduced expressive vocabulary in both languages, and difficulty following multi-step directions at his preschool. Mateo attends Little Sprouts Garden Cottage in Fayetteville, North Carolina, five days per week. This evaluation was requested by his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Flores, and his father, Andrés Reyes Morales, to determine eligibility for speech-language services and to guide an Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) through Cumberland County CDSA. The evaluation was conducted with the assistance of a certified Spanish interpreter, Rosa Elena Fuentes, and incorporated both formal standardized testing and informal observation across both of Mateo's languages.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía and Andrés, his older sister Camila Reyes Flores (age 7), and his maternal grandmother, Delfina Flores Núñez, who provides after-school childcare for Camila and occasional evening care for Mateo. The family resides at 118 Sombrilla Lane, Fayetteville, North Carolina 28303. Lucía works at una fábrica de empaques, Carolina Packaging Plant, on the second shift, while Andrés trabaja en una empresa de construcción, Triad Builders Construction Company, as a framing crew lead. Mateo's paternal aunt, Marisol Reyes Castillo, occasionally babysits on weekends and reports that Mateo "se frustra mucho cuando no lo entienden."

Mateo's birth history is notable for a full-term pregnancy with delivery at 39 weeks gestational age via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Birth weight was 7 lbs 4 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. Lucía reported no complications during pregnancy, labor, or delivery, and no NICU stay was required. Mateo met early gross motor milestones within expected ranges (sitting at 6 months, walking independently at 13 months), though fine motor and speech-language milestones were reported as delayed.

Medical history includes recurrent otitis media between the ages of 18 months and 3 years, with bilateral myringotomy tubes placed on el martes 4 de junio de 2024 by Dr. Hector Alvarado, ENT, at Sandhills ENT and Audiology. Post-tube placement, Lucía reports some improvement in attention to sound but continued concerns regarding speech clarity. Mateo passed his most recent audiological screening on 06/18/2024, with results within normal limits bilaterally. No seizure history, no significant head trauma, and no hospitalizations beyond tube placement were reported. Family medical history is unremarkable for genetic syndromes; however, Andrés reports that he himself "no hablaba bien hasta los cinco años" and received speech therapy briefly as a child in Mexico, though no records are available.

Mateo has a family dog named Nube, a white terrier mix, whom he reportedly enjoys "hablando con" in short phrases, per parent report. Lucía shared that Mateo once said "Nube come" when the dog was eating, demonstrating an early subject-verb combination in Spanish.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo was born in the United States; both parents emigrated from Michoacán, Mexico prior to his birth. Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home by all family members, including Delfina and visiting relatives. Andrés reports moderate proficiency in English, used primarily at work, while Lucía reports more limited English proficiency, relying on Spanish for all home communication. Camila, who attends Hope Mills Elementary School, is described as fluently bilingual and often serves as an informal interpreter for Mateo with English-speaking peers and staff. Lucía reported that Mateo was exposed to English starting at approximately 2;6 when he began attending Little Sprouts Garden Cottage, though exposure before that was exclusively Spanish.

Per parental report using a developmental checklist completed with interpreter support, Mateo's first words emerged around 18 months in Spanish ("mamá," "agua," "perro"), which was noted as somewhat later than his sister's first words. Two-word combinations emerged closer to 3;0. Parents report that unfamiliar listeners, including extended family and daycare staff, frequently have difficulty understanding Mateo, estimating intelligibility to familiar listeners (parents) at approximately 70% and to unfamiliar listeners at 30-40%.

Mateo's preschool teacher, Ms. Brenda Hollis, at Little Sprouts Garden Cottage, reports that Mateo is social and enjoys parallel play with peers, including his classmate Jaxon Whitfield and a close friend, Soleil Nguyen, but that he frequently resorts to gesture or pulling peers by the hand rather than using verbal requests. Ms. Hollis also noted that during a classroom activity on el 14 de febrero de 2025, Mateo became visibly frustrated when peers could not understand his request for a toy, resulting in a brief tantrum. The classroom assistant, Ms. J. Alvarez, has also observed similar episodes and has begun using visual supports during transitions.

Mateo currently receives occupational therapy through Cumberland County CDSA with Kristen Oyelaran, OTR/L, addressing mild fine motor delays, and has recently been referred for physical therapy evaluation with Marcus Deluca, PT, due to reported low muscle tone noted during a well-child visit. Service coordination is provided by Ana Beltrán at Cumberland County CDSA, who coordinated today's evaluation and arranged interpreter services.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND RESULTS

Standardized and informal assessment was conducted across two sessions: an initial session on 3 de marzo de 2025 (90 minutes) and a follow-up session on March 5, 2025 (45 minutes) to complete Spanish-language subtests with interpreter support. Both parents were present for portions of each session. The following tools were administered:

Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) – English and Spanish editions, administered in a counterbalanced order across sessions to reduce fatigue and language-mixing effects.

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) – administered in English with supplemental Spanish phoneme inventory analysis.

Bilingual Spanish-English Assessment (BESA) – Morphosyntax and Phonology subtests.

Clinical observation of play-based language sampling in both languages, with Rosa Elena Fuentes providing real-time interpretation and cultural consultation.

Standardized Test Results

| Test / Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile Rank | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension (English) | 76 | 5th | 2;9 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication (English) | 71 | 3rd | 2;6 |
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension (Spanish) | 82 | 12th | 3;2 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication (Spanish) | 79 | 8th | 3;0 |
| GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words (English) | 68 | 2nd | 2;11 |
| BESA Morphosyntax | 73-83 | 9th | N/A |
| BESA Phonology | 78 | 7th | N/A |

Composite scores across both languages place Mateo's overall receptive and expressive language skills in the moderately delayed range relative to same-age bilingual peers. Confidence intervals of 90% were applied across all standardized measures, yielding a confidence interval of 68-80 for the English Expressive Communication score and 74-88 for the Spanish Auditory Comprehension score.

Articulation and Phonology

Conversational speech samples in both languages revealed a moderate phonological disorder characterized by final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and gliding of liquids. In English, Mateo produced "wabbit" for the target word "rabbit," substituting [w] for /r/. He also produced "poo" for "spoon," demonstrating cluster reduction and final consonant deletion. In Spanish, Mateo demonstrated age-appropriate use of the trilled /r/ in words such as "perro," though he substituted /ɾ/ with [l] in "flor," producing "flol." Of note, several English phonological patterns observed (gliding, cluster reduction) are consistent with typical cross-linguistic transfer patterns in Spanish-English bilingual development and were weighted accordingly rather than scored as purely disordered.

Intelligibility in connected speech was estimated at 60% to familiar listeners and 30% to unfamiliar listeners across both languages, consistent with parent report. Mateo demonstrated a phonetic inventory inclusive of /p, b, m, n, t, d, k, g, f, s, j/ across both languages, with notable absence of /r/, /ɾ/ (except in select words), /ʃ/, and consonant clusters.

Language Sampling and Pragmatics

During a 20-minute play-based language sample conducted at 10:15 AM on March 3, 2025, Mateo produced primarily 2-3 word utterances in both languages, with mean length of utterance (MLU) calculated at 2.1 morphemes in English and 2.4 morphemes in Spanish. He demonstrated emerging use of plurals ("dos perros") and possessives ("mi carro") in Spanish, but inconsistent use of these morphological markers in English. Mateo engaged in turn-taking and joint attention appropriately, initiated requests using gesture paired with single words, and demonstrated functional play skills consistent with his chronological age, including pretend play sequences (feeding a doll, "driving" a toy truck while saying "vroom vroom").

Mateo showed good eye contact, responded to his name consistently, and demonstrated appropriate joint attention and social referencing with both the examiner and interpreter. No concerns regarding autism spectrum features were noted during today's observation; however, given the complexity of differentiating language difference from language disorder in bilingual contexts, ongoing monitoring is recommended.

Oral-Motor and Feeding

Oral-motor examination revealed structures and function within normal limits. Lucía reported no feeding concerns, noting that Mateo eats a wide variety of textures without difficulty. No signs of dysarthria or apraxia of speech were observed; however, the clinician notes mild inconsistency in sound sequencing during multisyllabic word attempts (e.g., "pasghetti" for "spaghetti"), which will be monitored as therapy progresses to rule out a motor planning component.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a moderate expressive and receptive language delay affecting both Spanish and English, alongside a moderate phonological disorder characterized by cluster reduction, final consonant deletion, and gliding. Importantly, because Mateo demonstrates delays across both of his languages relative to bilingual normative data, his profile is consistent with a true language disorder rather than a language difference attributable solely to bilingual exposure or second-language acquisition. His stronger performance in Spanish relative to English is consistent with his primary language exposure at home and should be considered when interpreting overall severity.

Mateo's reduced intelligibility across both languages is contributing to communicative frustration, as evidenced by behavioral episodes reported by both parents and his teacher, Ms. Hollis. His pragmatic and play skills remain a relative strength and support a positive prognosis for intervention. Given his history of recurrent otitis media, continued coordination with audiology and his ENT, Dr. Alvarado, is recommended to monitor hearing status, as fluctuating conductive hearing loss may have contributed to and may continue to impact speech sound development.

Mateo meets eligibility criteria for speech-language intervention services under Cumberland County CDSA guidelines based on standard scores more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean in both receptive and expressive domains across both languages.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo is recommended for bilingual speech-language therapy services, ideally with a Spanish-English bilingual provider or with consistent interpreter support, at a frequency of two 30-minute sessions per week, focusing on expressive language, phonological patterns, and functional communication strategies.

2. Therapy should incorporate a combined approach drawing on Cycles phonological intervention for targeted sound patterns and Hanen-based strategies (e.g., "OWL": Observe, Wait, Listen) to support caregiver-implemented language facilitation during daily routines.

3. Continued coordination with occupational therapy (Kristen Oyelaran, OTR/L) and the pending physical therapy evaluation (Marcus Deluca, PT) is recommended to ensure an integrated IFSP addressing motor and communication goals concurrently.

4. The family is encouraged to continue providing rich language exposure in Spanish at home, as home language maintenance supports, rather than hinders, overall language development. Simplified, repeated models of target words in both languages, with min to mod cues, are recommended during daily routines such as mealtimes and play with Nube.

5. Referral to audiology for a follow-up hearing screening is recommended given the history of recurrent otitis media, to be coordinated through Dr. Priya Kapoor's office or directly with Sandhills ENT and Audiology.

6. Classroom-based support at Little Sprouts Garden Cottage is recommended, including visual supports for transitions (already initiated by Ms. J. Alvarez) and structured opportunities for Mateo to practice requesting with peers such as Jaxon Whitfield and Soleil Nguyen in low-pressure contexts.

7. An IFSP meeting is recommended to formalize goals, with a tentative review date set for el 2 de junio de 2025. Service coordinator Ana Beltrán will follow up to schedule this meeting and will coordinate interpreter services for all future appointments.

8. Re-evaluation of standardized language scores is recommended in approximately 6 months to monitor progress and adjust the treatment plan as needed, with particular attention to whether the gap between Spanish and English performance narrows or persists.

This evaluation and these recommendations were reviewed with Lucía Rodríguez Flores and Andrés Reyes Morales with the assistance of interpreter Rosa Elena Fuentes at the conclusion of testing on March 5, 2025. Both parents verbally agreed with the findings and recommendations and expressed eagerness to begin services as soon as possible. Written consent for services will be obtained by Ana Beltrán prior to the IFSP meeting.

Please contact the undersigned with any questions regarding this evaluation.

Respectfully submitted,

Dana Whitfield, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Sandhills Pediatric Speech & Language Services
2240 Raeford Road, Suite 110, Fayetteville, North Carolina 28305
Phone: (910) 555-2847
Email: d.whitfield@sandhillspeds-slp.com

NC INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM — INDIVIDUALIZED FAMILY SERVICE PLAN (IFSP) REVIEW

Child's Name: Mateo Andrés Flores  Date of Birth: April 9, 2024  Record ID: IT-48217
Medicaid ID: 920483715C  County of Residence: Catawba County
Initial IFSP Date: July 15, 2025  Review Date: January 12, 2026  Review Type: Six-Month Review
CDSA Office: Catawba Valley CDSA  Service Coordinator: David Alvarez
Family Address: 118 Willowbrook Lane, Hickory, NC 28601  Home Phone: (828) 555-0147
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Flores (madre)   Parent/Guardian: Carlos Flores (padre)
Sibling(s) in Home: Sol Flores, age 6, enrolled at Riverbend Elementary

Participants Present: Lucía Flores, Carlos Flores, David Alvarez (service coordinator), Jennifer Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP, and Sarah Kim, OTR/L, who co-leads the family's developmental therapy sessions.

Background: Mateo was referred to Catawba Valley CDSA after his 18-month well-child visit, where his pediatrician, Dr. Angela Whitfield of Foothills Pediatrics, noted significantly delayed expressive language compared to peers. He has been enrolled in Part C services since the initial IFSP meeting on July 15, 2025.

Family Concerns and Priorities (en las palabras de la familia):

During the review, Lucía Flores shared, switching between Spanish and English as she often does, "Estoy preocupada porque Mateo todavía no dice muchas palabras. He is almost two and solo dice como diez palabras, y a veces nadie lo entiende, ni siquiera yo." She explained that at Little Learners Daycare, his teacher, Ms. Patricia Gómez, has told her Mateo gets frustrated when he cannot make himself understood by the other children, and recently he has started pushing a classmate, Dylan Harmon, when he wants a toy that Dylan is holding.

Carlos Flores said his biggest priority is "que mi hijo pueda hablar con su hermana. Sol lo cuida mucho y yo quiero que puedan jugar juntos sin que él se frustre." He also explained that he is rarely home in the evenings because he works two jobs — full time in the warehouse at Harris Teeter distribution, and most weekends driving a delivery route for UPS — so the evening and bedtime routines usually fall to Lucía Flores and to the children's grandmother, Rosa Cruz, who watches Mateo on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons while Lucía Flores works her shift at a local bakery.

The family's priorities, in the order they stated them, are: (1) grow Mateo's spoken vocabulary so familiar listeners can understand him most of the time; (2) reduce frustration-related aggression at daycare; and (3) help Sol and Mateo play together con menos conflicto, since right now Sol often ends up doing everything for him instead of waiting for him to try.

Daily Routines and Natural Environments:

Mateo attends Little Learners Daycare Monday through Friday, 7:30 AM to 5:00 PM, in the toddler room with Ms. Patricia Gómez and assistant teacher Ms. Brianna Souza. Mealtimes at home are a shared family routine: Mateo sits with Sol and asks for more food mostly by pointing or pulling on his mother's sleeve rather than using words. Bath time and bedtime are led by Lucía Flores, who reports Mateo babbles happily in the bath but rarely imitates actual words during that routine. On Tuesdays and Thursdays, Rosa Cruz picks him up from daycare and takes him to her apartment, where he plays in the back patio and chases her neighbor's dog along the fence line.

Other Agencies Involved:

The family also receives nutrition support through Catawba County WIC and has an open referral with Catawba County Smart Start for a Spanish-language parenting support group starting in the spring. David Alvarez is coordinating between these agencies and the CDSA to avoid duplicate paperwork for the family.

Evaluation Summary (for this review):

Jennifer Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP, completed an updated assessment on January 5, 2026. Tools administered included the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition, and the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition. A brief receptive screening used items from the Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test.

On the Rossetti, Mateo's overall communication age equivalent fell at 11-13 months, with expressive skills notably behind receptive skills. On the Bayley, his Language Composite standard score was 78 (7th percentile), 90% CI 73-83, at a chronological age of 21 months. On the Goldman-Fristoe, connected-speech intelligibility was estimated at 40% to unfamiliar listeners and 65% to familiar listeners.

Diagnosis: Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, ICD-10 F80.2. This visit was billed under CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression).

Target Word Note:

During play-based sampling, Jennifer Reyes used a toy sun puzzle to elicit single words. Mateo produced the target word "sol" as "[o]," omitting the initial /s/, with 2 of 10 trials approximated under moderate cues. Note for the team: this vocabulary target happens to be identical to his sister's name. Lucía Flores reports Mateo already says "Sol" fairly clearly when calling for his sister, producing it closer to target as "[to]" than he did the unrelated sun-puzzle item. Data for the puzzle target and data for the name are being tracked separately so progress on one is not mistaken for progress on the other.

IFSP Outcomes and Strategies:

Outcome 1: Mateo will use 50 different spoken words independently across home and Little Learners Daycare settings within six months, as reported by Lucía Flores and Ms. Patricia Gómez.
Strategies: caregiver coaching in both English and Spanish on expectant pauses and modeling two-word utterances; a core vocabulary board kept at home and at daycare; Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies reviewed with Lucía Flores and Carlos Flores during the last two home visits.
Progress since the initial IFSP: Mateo has grown from an estimated 8-word vocabulary to a 22-word vocabulary, with 8/10 target words produced spontaneously during the home visit on December 18, 2025.

Outcome 2: Mateo will request a desired item using a word, sign, or picture instead of pushing, in 80% of observed opportunities at Little Learners Daycare.
Strategies: visual request cards at the toddler-room door and snack table; consistent staff response, with Ms. Patricia Gómez trained in a least-to-most prompting hierarchy; coordination with Little Learners Program, the twice-weekly toddler social-communication group that Mateo attends as a related service, so cueing is consistent across settings. The team confirmed at this review that Little Learners Daycare and Little Learners Program are separate organizations despite the similar names, so attendance and billing records are not mixed up between them.
Progress: at the most recent classroom observation, Mateo used a request card in 6 of 10 opportunities, up from 1 of 10 at the initial IFSP.

Outcome 3: Mateo and Sol will engage in a shared turn-taking play routine for at least five minutes daily, per parent report.
Strategies: Carlos Flores and Lucía Flores coached on sibling-mediated play using a preferred stacking-blocks toy; Sol given a simple bilingual script, "mi turno / tu turno," to model turn-taking for her brother.
Progress: the family reports this routine now happens most evenings when Carlos Flores is not working his UPS route late into the evening.
