text:
CONFIDENTIAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Client: María José del Río-Castillo ("Majo")
DOB: April 3, 2022  CA at eval: 4;2
Eval Dates: June 9, 2026 (9:15 AM–10:45 AM), June 11, 2026 (1:30 PM–2:40 PM)
Report Date: June 20, 2026
Referral Source: Dr. Anjali Patel, pediatrician
Primary Languages: Spanish (home-dominant), English (daycare)
School District: Wake County Public School System; projected K site Pinecrest Elementary School
Daycare: Little Learners Daycare, 4s classroom (Ms. Lopez's room)
Parents: Lucía del Río (mother), Javier Castillo-Reyes (father)
Address: 4817 Juniper Hollow Ln, Raleigh, Wake County, NC 27610
Phone: (919) 555-0142 (mother, cell)
Email: lucia.delrio82@fastmail.com
Medicaid ID: 8827461905K
Clinic Record #: TBS-22041
Evaluator: Marisol Fernández, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (Eng/Span)
Clinic: Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC

S:

Eval requested by Ms. Lopez and parents Lucía del Río/Javier Castillo-Reyes 2/2 c/o unintelligible speech, short utterances, frustration w/ peers Sofía and Diego at Little Learners Daycare. Ms. Lopez reports Majo points/gestures more than classmates, repeats self 2-3x before giving up. Parents report similar pattern at home in Spanish; Majo understood by family but strangers often ask "Majo to repeat."

Birth hx: born 35 weeks gestation via C-section 2/2 maternal preeclampsia at Carolina Pines Women's Hospital. Birth weight 5 lb 2 oz. Apgar 7 and 9 at 1 and 5 min. NICU stay x10 days, no vent, PO feeds established prior to d/c. No seizures, no genetic workup done, no syndromic features noted. Hearing screen at birth: pass bilaterally. Repeat audiogram at 26 months (per Wake County CDSA protocol): WNL both ears.

Med hx: hx of recurrent otitis media, 4 episodes btwn 8 and 20 months, tx w/ abx, no tubes placed, resolved by 24 months. No current ENT concerns. PCP Dr. Anjali Patel reports growth WNL, no vision concerns, no feeding concerns beyond toddlerhood picky eating. No current meds. No hospitalizations since NICU d/c. Family hx neg for ASD, ID, or hereditary hearing loss; mother reports her own brother (child's uncle, Tomás del Río) was a "late talker" who caught up by age 5, no formal dx.

Family/language hx: household is Spanish-dominant; Lucía del Río and Javier Castillo-Reyes both speak Spanish as L1, English as L2 (both conversational). Mother works FT at Blue Ridge Financial Group; father works as an electrician, irregular hrs. Older sister Camila del Río-Castillo, age 7, TD, attends Pinecrest Elementary School, 2nd grade, teacher Ms. Alvarez-Ruiz. Camila reportedly code-switches easily and serves as informal interpreter for Majo at times, which parents worry may reduce Majo's own verbal output. Maternal grandmother Rosa Vega provides care 3x/wk after daycare pickup, speaks only Spanish w/ Majo. Paternal grandparents live out of state, visit 2x/yr. Family dog Luna is frequently referenced by Majo in play. No other pets. Home language input estimated 80% Spanish / 20% English per parent report; daycare input estimated 90% English.

EI hx: referred to Wake County CDSA at 18 months (~October 2023) for late talking, <10 words at 18 months. IFSP written November 2, 2023; enrolled in Little Learners Program (center-based EI, 2x/wk, 45-min sessions) from January 15, 2024 through August 2025. PT Mark Sullivan addressed mild gross motor delay (resolved by 30 months). Service coordinator Angela Brooks oversaw transition planning; IFSP Outcome #2 (expressive vocab) and Outcome #3 (intelligibility) both reviewed at exit eval, age 3;0, April 2025. SLP at that time (Grace Nwosu, CCC-SLP) recommended continued monitoring given bilingual status, did not recommend ongoing EI services at exit given expressive vocab growth. Parents report concern re: regression/plateau since exit, prompting current referral.

Last formal SLP eval: August 14, 2025, age 3;4, administered by Grace Nwosu at Little Learners Program. PLS-5 Spanish-English scores at that time: Auditory Comprehension SS 85 (16th %ile), Expressive Communication SS 76 (5th %ile). No articulation measure administered at that time 2/2 limited single-word inventory.

Current parent concerns, verbatim (translated from Spanish by evaluator, bilingual, no interpreter needed): "No le entendemos a veces, y en la guardería tampoco la entienden" ("We don't understand her sometimes, and at daycare they don't understand her either"). Mother denies regression, reports steady but slow gains. No concerns re: social reciprocity, eye contact, or play skills; Majo reportedly initiates play readily w/ Sofía and Diego, shares toys, shows affect-appropriate responses.

O:

Behavioral observations: Majo presented well-groomed, cooperative, separated from mother w/o distress. Attention to task fair, required frequent redirection/breaks (~10-12 min per task block). Rapport established quickly; responded to both English and Spanish input, code-switched spontaneously mid-session. Articulation judged moderately reduced intelligibility in connected speech, ~60% intelligible to unfamiliar listener in context, ~40% out of context, per examiner judgment and parent corroboration. Oral mech exam: structure/function WNL, no dysarthric or apraxic features noted, DDK rates age-appropriate, no drooling, adequate velopharyngeal closure noted on /pa-ta-ka/ sequences.

Standardized testing administered in both English and Spanish per bilingual protocol (dominant-language-first, then cross-linguistic probes):

Test/Subtest                                   SS    %ile   Age Equiv   95% CI
PLS-5 Spanish-English Bilingual Edition
  Auditory Comprehension               82   12th  3;6-3;9   76-88
  Expressive Communication             79   8th   3;3-3;6   73-85
  Total Language Score                 78   7th   3;4       72-84
Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA)
  Morphosyntax (Spanish)               85   16th  --         --
  Morphosyntax (English)               80   9th   --         --
  Semantics (bilingual composite)       88   21st  --         --
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)
  Sounds-in-Words                      73   4th   --         67-79
Khan-Lewis Phonological Analysis-3 (KLPA-3)
  Percentage Consonants Correct                 76%  --     --         --

Phonological process analysis (English + Spanish combined sample): final consonant deletion present 8/10 opportunities; cluster reduction 7/10; stopping of fricatives 6/8; gliding of liquids 5/10. Sound inventory: stimulable for /s/ in isolation w/ mod cues, not yet stimulable for /ɾ/ (Spanish tap) even w/ max cues. Target word "sol" produced as "tol"; target "carro" produced as "cao", omitting /ɾ/; English target "cat" produced "tat", substituting /t/ for /k/; English target "spoon" produced "poon" (cluster reduction). These patterns occurred consistently across both languages, supporting a true phonological disorder rather than typical bilingual cross-linguistic transfer, per BESA bilingual-specific scoring guidance.

Language sample (15-min play-based, English + Spanish mixed): MLU in morphemes 3.1 (English), 3.4 (Spanish); below expectations for CA in both languages. Sample transcript excerpt (SALT-coded): "Majo want more juice [EW]"; "yo quiero Luna correr" (I want Luna to run), produced with mod cues from grandmother prompt during home sample collected by Rosa Vega per evaluator instruction and reviewed by evaluator. Grammatical morphemes emerging inconsistently: plural -s present 3 of 5 obligatory contexts; past tense -ed/regular Spanish preterite present 2 of 6 contexts; copula "is/está" present 4 of 7 contexts. Pragmatic skills age-appropriate: initiated topics, used eye contact, repaired breakdowns w/ min cues when given processing time.

Hearing/voice/fluency screen: pure tone screen WNL bilaterally at 20 dB, 1000/2000/4000 Hz; voice quality WNL, no hoarseness/breathiness; fluency WNL, no dysfluencies >3% of words, no secondary behaviors noted.

A:

Majo presents c/w a combined phonological disorder and expressive language delay affecting both Spanish and English, not attributable solely to bilingual language acquisition or reduced input, given cross-linguistic consistency of phonological error patterns and scores falling >1 SD below mean in both languages on bilingually-normed measures (BESA, PLS-5 Spanish-English). Receptive language mildly reduced relative to peers but stronger than expressive skills, suggesting expressive-dominant profile. History of recurrent OM, EI enrollment (Little Learners Program), and resolved GM delay are consistent w/ a multifactorial developmental language picture rather than hearing loss (current audiogram WNL) or ASD (social/pragmatic skills intact per observation and parent report).

Dx impressions:
- Phonological disorder, moderate severity (F80.0)
- Expressive language disorder, mild-moderate, with receptive involvement (F80.1)
- Bilingual status (Spanish/English) considered and ruled out as sole explanation per bilingual-normed testing protocol

Eval billed under CPT 92523 (eval of speech sound production w/ eval of language comprehension and expression), modifier GN applied per clinic policy.

Prognosis good w/ consistent, intensive, bilingual-informed intervention given Majo's strong pragmatic skills, stimulability for several target sounds, intact hearing, and engaged family support system (mother Lucía del Río, father Javier Castillo-Reyes, grandmother Rosa Vega all report willingness to carry over strategies).

P:

1. Recommend direct SLP tx 2x/wk, 30-min sessions, individual, targeting phonology and expressive syntax in both Spanish and English (bilingual service delivery, not English-only, per evaluator's clinical judgment and current research consensus on bilingual language disorder tx).
2. Phonological approach: Cycles Approach targeting final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and stopping, cycling across English/Spanish targets q6wk.
3. Language approach: PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing to support motor planning for /ɾ/ and consonant clusters; concurrent use of Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" parent-coaching model to train Lucía del Río and Javier Castillo-Reyes in responsive input strategies at home, in Spanish.
4. Recommend referral to Wake County Public School System for Child Find eval to determine eligibility for speech-language services under IDEA prior to K entry at Pinecrest Elementary School; copy of this report to be released w/ parent consent to district eval team and to incoming K teacher if assigned prior to start of year.
5. Continue current placement at Little Learners Daycare; recommend Ms. Lopez implement visual supports and allow processing time (~5-10 sec) before prompting repetition, to reduce frustration behaviors noted during unstructured play.
6. Re-screen hearing in 6 mo given hx of recurrent OM; f/u w/ Dr. Anjali Patel if further OM episodes occur.
7. Family carryover: grandmother Rosa Vega and sister Camila del Río-Castillo encouraged to continue rich Spanish-language input; discouraged from interpreting/speaking for Majo when she attempts independent communication, to support her own verbal output.
8. Re-eval recommended in 6 months (December 2026) to monitor progress and reassess need for continued EI-style supports vs transition fully to school-based services.
9. Report and release of information form sent to Lucía del Río via email (lucia.delrio82@fastmail.com) for signature prior to distribution to Wake County Public School System and Little Learners Daycare.
10. Clinic contact for scheduling and questions: (919) 555-0198, front desk, Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC.

Report prepared and signed:
Marisol Fernández, M.S., CCC-SLP
NC License #SLP-019284
Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
June 20, 2026

Información de la familia:
Mateo vive con sus padres, Lucía Rodríguez y Carlos Hernández, y con su hermana mayor, Camila Hernández Rodríguez, de 6 años, en Graham, Condado de Alamance. La familia también cuenta con el apoyo de la abuela materna, Rosa Pérez, quien cuida a los niños algunas tardes cuando los padres trabajan. Lucía Rodríguez trabaja en Panadería El Sol en turnos de la mañana, y Carlos Hernández trabaja en Construcciones Ramírez. El número de teléfono principal de la familia es (336) 555-0148 y el correo electrónico de contacto es lucia.rodriguez84@example.com. El número de Medicaid de Mateo es 402785193R y su número de identificación del CDSA es CDSA-18204.

En el hogar se habla español de manera exclusiva. Carlos Hernández explicó: "Queremos que Mateo aprenda inglés en la escuela más adelante, pero ahora en la casa solo hablamos español porque así nos entendemos mejor todos." El equipo confirmó que la evaluación y la intervención continuarán en español, con introducción gradual de vocabulario en inglés una vez que la base en español sea más sólida.

Mateo asiste a Little Learners Daycare de lunes a viernes, de 7:45 a.m. a 5:00 p.m., en el salón de la maestra Diana Pérez. La maestra asistente, Yesenia Gómez, también apoya a Mateo durante las actividades de grupo. En la guardería, Mateo interactúa principalmente con dos compañeritos, Aiden y Sofía, con quienes comparte la mesa de bloques.

Historia del desarrollo: Mateo nació con una edad gestacional de 37 semanas y un peso al nacer de 2,890 gramos, con un Apgar de 8 al minuto y 9 a los cinco minutos. No tiene diagnósticos médicos activos además del retraso en el habla y el lenguaje. Tuvo tres episodios de otitis media entre los 8 meses y los 14 meses, tratados con antibióticos por su pediatra. Una prueba de audición realizada el 2024-06-05 mostró resultados dentro de límites normales en ambos oídos.

Preocupaciones y prioridades de la familia:
Lucía Rodríguez compartió lo siguiente en sus propias palabras: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Mateo no habla casi nada en la guardería, pero en la casa sí nos dice algunas palabras. La maestra Diana me dice que él se queda callado y señala lo que quiere en vez de pedirlo con palabras." Agregó: "Queremos que pueda decirle a su hermana Camila lo que quiere cuando juegan, porque ahora ella adivina todo por él y eso no lo ayuda a hablar más."

Carlos Hernández dijo: "Para mí la prioridad es que aprenda a pedir las cosas en la mesa, porque todavía nos jala la ropa en vez de decir 'más' o 'agua'. También quiero que pueda jugar con los otros niños del parque sin frustrarse tanto."

La familia priorizó tres áreas para esta revisión: (1) aumentar las palabras funcionales que Mateo usa en la guardería y en la casa; (2) mejorar la inteligibilidad del habla para que las personas fuera de la familia lo entiendan; y (3) reducir la frustración relacionada con la comunicación durante las rutinas de comida y de juego.

Rutinas diarias:
La familia describió un día típico. Mateo se despierta alrededor de las 6:30 a.m. y desayuna con la familia a las 7:00 a.m., antes de salir hacia Little Learners Daycare. Durante el almuerzo, a las 11:30 a.m., el personal reporta que Mateo come bien pero rara vez pide más comida verbalmente. La siesta en la guardería ocurre de la 1:00 p.m. a las 2:30 p.m.. En la casa, la cena familiar es a las 6:15 p.m., seguida del tiempo de juego con su hermana Camila y el baño a las 7:30 p.m.. La rutina de la hora de dormir incluye un cuento y termina alrededor de las 8:15 p.m.

Durante la observación de juego en esta visita, a las 10:00 a.m., Mateo jugó con el perro de la familia y dijo "Rocky va" al verlo correr hacia la puerta, acercándose al objetivo "el perro se va". Esta producción fue codificada como [EW] en la transcripción de la muestra de lenguaje debido a la omisión del sustantivo. Más tarde, al escuchar a su hermana llamarlo desde la otra habitación, Mateo imitó su nombre y produjo "Cami 'ta" en vez de "ella está aquí". También señaló una foto familiar y dijo "Rocky uf uf", aproximando el sonido del perro en vez del nombre completo Rocky.

Durante la visita, Gabriela Soto también revisó un video breve grabado por la maestra Diana Pérez el 28 de febrero de 2025 durante el tiempo de círculo a las 9:00 a.m.. En el video, Mateo observó a su compañero Aiden cantar una canción y sonrió, pero no produjo palabras reconocibles, solo vocalizaciones. Cuando su compañera Sofía le ofreció un bloque, Mateo lo tomó sin establecer contacto visual ni usar un gesto de agradecimiento.

Otras agencias:
La familia recibe apoyo nutricional del programa WIC del Condado de Alamance desde el nacimiento de Mateo. También participan en actividades de Smart Start de Alamance-Caswell, incluyendo un grupo de juego bilingüe los sábados. La coordinadora de servicios, Ana Martínez, confirmó que no hay una referencia activa al DSS del Condado de Alamance en este momento, pero que la familia conoce el proceso de referencia si llegara a necesitarlo.

Resultados de evaluaciones estandarizadas:
El 20 de febrero de 2025, Gabriela Soto administró la Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale. Mateo obtuvo una edad equivalente de 14-16 meses en el dominio de Pragmática, y una edad equivalente de 16-18 meses en el dominio de Gesto, ambas por debajo de su edad cronológica de 2;4. En el dominio de Interacción-Apego obtuvo una edad equivalente de 22-24 meses, dentro de límites esperados.

En la misma sesión se administró la Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3). Mateo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 73, ubicándolo en el percentil 4, con un intervalo de confianza de 68-78. Mostró procesos fonológicos de reducción de grupos consonánticos y omisión de consonantes finales, por ejemplo "apo" por "zapato" y "pelo" por "perro". Produjo los fonemas /m/, /p/ y /a/ de manera consistente, pero sustituyó /k/ por [t] y omitió /s/ final en la mayoría de las palabras.

El equipo de terapia ocupacional administró las Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4) el 21 de febrero de 2025. Mateo obtuvo una puntuación compuesta cognitiva de 85 (percentil 16), una puntuación compuesta de lenguaje de 78 (percentil 7), y una puntuación compuesta motora de 92 (percentil 30).

También se administraron las Peabody Developmental Motor Scales, Second Edition (PDMS-2) el mismo día, con una puntuación compuesta de motor fino de 88 y una edad equivalente de 26 meses.

El equipo interdisciplinario concluyó que los resultados de la Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale y de la Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 son consistentes con un retraso significativo en el lenguaje expresivo y en el desarrollo fonológico, mientras que los resultados de las Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition y de las Peabody Developmental Motor Scales, Second Edition indican un desarrollo cognitivo y motor dentro de límites esperados o levemente por debajo del promedio. Estos hallazgos respaldan la continuación de los servicios de patología del habla y lenguaje, con un aumento sugerido en la intensidad de las estrategias de modelado del lenguaje.

Resultados del IFSP:

Resultado 1: Mateo usará al menos 20 palabras funcionales de manera espontánea en la guardería y en la casa para pedir objetos, comida y actividades preferidas.
Progreso: la familia y el personal de Little Learners Daycare reportan que Mateo actualmente usa aproximadamente 12 palabras de forma consistente, un aumento desde las 5 palabras documentadas en el IFSP inicial. Progreso parcial.
Estrategias: se recomienda el uso de modelado de lenguaje aumentado durante las comidas, con pistas de nivel moderado para palabras funcionales como "más", "agua" y "abre". Gabriela Soto continuará usando estrategias del enfoque Hanen durante las sesiones de terapia, y capacitará a la maestra Diana Pérez en el uso de "tiempo de espera" durante la merienda.

Resultado 2: la inteligibilidad del habla de Mateo mejorará de aproximadamente 30% con oyentes desconocidos a al menos 60% en contextos conocidos.
Progreso: en la sesión actual, la inteligibilidad se estimó en 35-40% con oyentes familiares y menor con oyentes desconocidos. Progreso mínimo.
Estrategias: se iniciará un enfoque de Cycles dirigido a los procesos de reducción de grupos consonánticos y omisión de consonante final, con sesiones semanales de 30 minutos. También se recomienda el uso de pistas de nivel máximo con modelado táctil-cinestésico del enfoque PROMPT para los sonidos /k/ y /s/.

Resultado 3: Mateo reducirá los episodios de frustración relacionados con la comunicación durante las comidas y el juego, usando gestos o palabras en vez de llanto o agresión en al menos 7 de 10 oportunidades observadas.
Progreso: la familia reporta una reducción de los episodios de llanto de aproximadamente 8 veces al día a 3 veces al día. Progreso significativo.
Estrategias: se continuará con el sistema de comunicación por intercambio de imágenes (PECS) iniciado el mes pasado, con tarjetas para "más", "ayuda" y "terminado". La familia usará las mismas tarjetas en casa durante las comidas y el baño.

Planificación de la transición: dado que Mateo cumplirá 3 años el 15 de julio de 2025, el equipo revisó el proceso de transición hacia los servicios del sistema escolar público. Ana Martínez explicó que la reunión de transición se realizará aproximadamente 90 días antes del tercer cumpleaños, con la participación del Programa de Preescolar del Sistema Escolar del Condado de Alamance. La familia recibirá información escrita sobre este proceso antes del 15 de mayo de 2025.

Fechas de servicio:
La evaluación inicial se completó el 14/08/2024 y el IFSP inicial se firmó el 28 de agosto de 2024. Los servicios de patología del habla y lenguaje comenzaron el 09/09/2024, con sesiones semanales de 45 minutos los martes a las 10:15 a.m., actualmente conducidas por Gabriela Soto del Little Learners Program. El diagnóstico de referencia para estos servicios es F80.2 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo), facturado bajo el código 92523 con el modificador GN. La terapia ocupacional comenzó el 16 de septiembre de 2024, con sesiones quincenales los jueves a las 2:00 p.m., conducidas por Marisol Vega.

Esta revisión del IFSP se realizó el 3 de marzo de 2025. La próxima revisión semestral está programada para el martes 2 de septiembre de 2025, y la evaluación anual completa está programada para 08/28/2025. La coordinadora de servicios, Ana Martínez, contactará a la familia antes del 15 de agosto de 2025 para confirmar la cita.

La familia firmó el consentimiento para continuar los servicios actuales sin cambios en la frecuencia. Lucía Rodríguez solicitó que se considere añadir una evaluación de alimentación si la inteligibilidad no mejora para la próxima revisión, dado que también ha notado dificultad con ciertas texturas de comida. Gabriela Soto acordó discutir esta solicitud con el equipo médico de Mateo, incluyendo a su pediatra, el Dr. Esteban Molina, en el Hospital Pediátrico Cone Health, antes de la próxima cita programada para el 10 de abril de 2025 a las 3:30 p.m.

Este documento fue completado por Gabriela Soto, CCC-SLP bilingüe, del Little Learners Program, y revisado por la coordinadora de servicios Ana Martínez del CDSA del Piedmont Central. Firmado electrónicamente el 3 de marzo de 2025.

text:
CENTRO DE LENGUAJE Y HABLA DE LAS COLINAS
PEDIATRIC SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

CHILD: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Hernández ("Mateo")
DATE OF BIRTH: April 9, 2022
AGE AT EVALUATION: 4;2
EVALUATION DATE: June 16, 2026
REPORT DATE: June 23, 2026
EXAMINER: Lucía M. Fonseca-Ríos, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
EMPLOYER: Centro de Lenguaje y Habla de las Colinas
INTERPRETER: Yesenia Ortiz (Spanish/English, certified medical interpreter)
REFERRAL SOURCE: Piedmont CDSA office, Karen Whitfield, Service Coordinator
MEDICAID ID: 784512093B
RECORD ID: LC-2026-0447

1. IDENTIFYING INFORMATION AND BACKGROUND

Mateo is a 4;2-year-old bilingual (Spanish-English) boy who was seen for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation at Centro de Lenguaje y Habla de las Colinas on June 16, 2026, at the request of his Piedmont CDSA service coordinator, Karen Whitfield, and with the consent of his parents, Rosa Idalia Hernández Molina and Alejandro Cruz Pineda. The family resides at 412 Winding Brook Lane, Lot 9, Siler City, NC 27344, Chatham County. Mateo attends Early Head Start three mornings a week and receives home-visiting support through Smart Start of Chatham County.

La evaluación se llevó a cabo en español e inglés, con el apoyo de la intérprete certificada Yesenia Ortiz. Mother reports, "Mateo entiende casi todo, pero no habla mucho con las personas que no conoce." Father added in English, "He talks more at home than anywhere else."

2. REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred due to parent and teacher concerns regarding limited expressive vocabulary, unintelligible speech, and difficulty combining words into sentences. His teacher at Early Head Start, Ms. Dana Alvarez, reports that Mateo rarely initiates communication with peers and often points or pulls adults by the hand instead of using words. His Smart Start home visitor, Brianna Coles, noted similar concerns during a home visit on May 4, 2026.

3. BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 35 weeks gestational age at Chatham Regional Birthing Center in Siler City, NC, delivered by Dr. Samuel Keene. Birth weight was 4 lbs 11 oz (2,126 grams). Apgar scores were 6 and 8 at one and five minutes. Due to respiratory distress, Mateo spent 11 days in the Chatham Regional Birthing Center NICU under the care of Dr. Priya Nandakumar, neonatologist, and was discharged home on April 20, 2022.

Mother reports a history of recurrent otitis media, with 4 documented episodes between 8 months and 26 months. Mateo had bilateral myringotomy tubes placed at UNC Children's Hospital in Chapel Hill on January 14, 2024 by Dr. Michael Tran, ENT. Hearing was last screened on March 2, 2026 and passed bilaterally (within normal limits, 20 dB HL or better across frequencies).

No history of seizures, significant illness, or hospitalization aside from the above. Vision screening within normal limits per pediatrician Dr. Felicia Okonkwo at her well-child visit on February 18, 2026.

4. FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo lives with his mother, Rosa Idalia Hernández Molina; his father, Alejandro Cruz Pineda; his older sister, Daniela (7 years); and his maternal grandmother, Juana Molina de Hernández, who helps with childcare while both parents work. Family moved to Siler City in 2019 from El Progreso, Yoro, Honduras, a small village where extended family still lives, including a paternal uncle, Mario Cruz Pineda.

Both parents work outside the home. Mother is employed at the fábrica de pollo Mountaire Farms (poultry processing plant), and father works at la compañía de construcción Triad Builders LLC. Grandmother previously worked at una empresa de limpieza, CleanPro Services, but now provides childcare full time. An older cousin occasionally babysits, Esperanza Pineda, who reports Mateo "mezcla mucho el español y el inglés cuando juega."

Language exposure in the home is estimated at approximately 80% Spanish and 20% English. Primary caregivers (mother and grandmother) speak predominantly Spanish; father and sister Daniela code-switch frequently. Mother reports Mateo's first words emerged around 18 months ("agua," "mamá," "más") and were slow to combine into phrases. She states, "A los dos años casi no hablaba, solo señalaba." Father added, "By two, his cousins his age were already putting sentences together and he wasn't."

Family history is positive for a maternal uncle, Oscar Molina, who reportedly had a "speech delay" as a child and received services in Honduras informally through a church program; no formal diagnosis is documented.

5. PRIOR SERVICES AND AGENCY INVOLVEMENT

Mateo was referred to Piedmont CDSA in September 2025 following a developmental screening conducted at a WIC appointment, where staff raised concerns about expressive language delay. An initial CDSA evaluation on October 2, 2025 resulted in eligibility for an Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP), with service coordination provided by Karen Whitfield. Mateo's current IFSP outcome 2 addresses expressive communication; outcome 3 addresses social engagement with peers.

The family also receives case management support through DSS (Chatham County Department of Social Services) related to a SNAP/food assistance case, and Mateo's sister Daniela attends an after-school tutoring program coordinated through Smart Start. Family has not previously received direct speech-language therapy; this evaluation was requested to determine eligibility for ongoing bilingual speech-language services under the IFSP.

6. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

The following standardized and informal measures were administered across two sessions (June 16, 2026 and June 18, 2026) in both English and Spanish, with interpretation support from Yesenia Ortiz:

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-English Bilingual Edition
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), selected subtests, administered in English only for cross-linguistic comparison
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Spanish articulation screening using the Contextual Probes of Articulation Competence-Spanish (CPAC-S)
- Bilingual Language Sample Analysis using SALT conventions
- Parent interview and the MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories (CDI), Spanish-English version
- Oral-motor and feeding screening
- Clinical observation during structured and unstructured play

7. TEST RESULTS

7.1 Receptive and Expressive Language — PLS-5 Bilingual

Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile | Confidence Interval
Auditory Comprehension | 68 | 2nd | 61-75
Expressive Communication | 62 | 1st | 55-69
Total Language Score | 63 | 1st | 58-68

Mateo's performance on the PLS-5 Bilingual Edition, which credits responses in either language, placed him in the Severe range for both receptive and expressive domains, well below the average range (85-115) expected for same-age peers.

7.2 English-Only Comparison — CELF Preschool-3 Selected Subtests

Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile
Sentence Structure | 58 | 0.3rd
Word Structure | 61 | 1st
Expressive Vocabulary | 55 | 0.2nd

Given that English-only administration disadvantages a child whose primary language exposure is Spanish, these scores should be interpreted with caution and are reported for comparison purposes only, not as a measure of overall language ability.

7.3 Articulation

On the GFTA-3 (English), Mateo achieved a standard score of 71 (3rd percentile), with error patterns including final consonant deletion, fronting of velars (/k/ and /g/ produced as [t] and [d]), and gliding of liquids (/r/ and /l/ produced as [w]). On the CPAC-S (Spanish), similar patterns emerged, including simplification of the trilled /r/ to [d] and frequent cluster reduction (e.g., "[pato]" for "plato").

Target word "carro" was produced as "[kaːo]" with moderate cues; target word "cat" was produced by Mateo as "tat." Speech intelligibility was rated as poor to familiar listeners (approximately 40% intelligible in connected speech) and very poor to unfamiliar listeners.

7.4 Language Sample Analysis

A 50-utterance bilingual language sample was collected during structured play with blocks and a toy farm set. Mean length of utterance (MLU) in morphemes was 1.8 across both languages combined, significantly below the expected range of 3.0-4.0 for his age. Mateo used primarily single words and occasional two-word combinations ("más agua," "no quiero," "want ball"). Code-switching within single utterances was noted (e.g., "quiero more"), consistent with typical bilingual development and not considered evidence of disorder in itself.

SALT coding identified frequent use of nonverbal communication, including pointing [NV] and eye gaze shifts, used in [EW] (end of word/utterance abandonment) patterns when Mateo appeared to lose a word mid-attempt.

7.5 Vocabulary and Developmental Checklist

On the CDI (Spanish-English version), mother reported Mateo uses approximately 85 words total across both languages, well below the expected range of 300-600 words for his age. Combined vocabulary (concepts understood in either language, counted once) was estimated at 140 words.

7.6 Oral-Motor and Feeding

Oral-motor structures were within normal limits for strength, range of motion, and symmetry. No feeding concerns were reported by parents; Mateo eats a wide variety of textures without difficulty.

7.7 Behavioral Observations

Mateo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily in play. He demonstrated joint attention and turn-taking during simple games but showed frustration (crying, pulling at his own hair) when unable to communicate a need, particularly during the block-building activity when he could not request "more blocks" and instead grabbed the examiner's hand repeatedly. Eye contact and social smiling were appropriate. No concerns regarding play skills, symbolic play, or social reciprocity were noted beyond those attributable to the language delay itself.

8. CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, parent report, language sampling, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a Developmental Language Disorder affecting both Spanish and English, with associated Speech Sound Disorder characterized by multiple phonological process errors (final consonant deletion, velar fronting, liquid gliding, cluster reduction) present across both languages. Because deficits are present in both of Mateo's languages relative to same-age bilingual peers, and given a positive family history, these findings are consistent with a primary language disorder rather than a difference attributable solely to bilingual language acquisition or reduced exposure.

Relevant ICD-10 codes: F80.2 (Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder), F80.0 (Phonological Disorder/Speech Sound Disorder), H65.9 (history of otitis media, resolved). Relevant CPT codes for this evaluation: 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression), 92521 (evaluation of speech fluency, not billed), modifier -59 applied where applicable per payer guidelines.

9. RECOMMENDATIONS

9.1 Mateo is recommended for ongoing bilingual speech-language therapy, individual sessions, 2 times per week, 45 minutes per session, with services delivered in both Spanish and English per family preference and IFSP team decision.

9.2 Therapy should incorporate a combination of evidence-based approaches, including:
- Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies for caregiver coaching, to support mother Rosa Idalia Hernández Molina and grandmother Juana Molina de Hernández in using facilitative language techniques at home in Spanish
- PROMPT (Prompts for Restructuring Oral Muscular Phonetic Targets) to address motor-based speech sound errors across both languages
- Cycles phonological approach targeting the identified error patterns (final consonant deletion, velar fronting, gliding, cluster reduction) in a bilingual cycling format alternating Spanish and English targets
- Visual supports modeled on PECS principles to reduce communicative frustration, particularly during transitions and requesting routines at Early Head Start
- Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol techniques as a supplemental approach for shaping approximations toward target words

9.3 Continued IFSP services through Piedmont CDSA are recommended, with Karen Whitfield to update outcomes 2 and 3 to reflect current goals in both expressive language and articulation. Review meeting recommended within 6 months, by December 16, 2026.

9.4 Hearing should be re-screened annually given history of chronic otitis media, through pediatrician Dr. Felicia Okonkwo or audiology referral as needed.

9.5 Caregiver coaching sessions are recommended for mother, father, and grandmother, delivered primarily in Spanish, to build consistency between home and therapy environments. Given parents' work schedules at Mountaire Farms and Triad Builders LLC, evening or weekend coaching sessions should be offered when possible.

9.6 Continued enrollment at Early Head Start is recommended, with consultation between this clinician and classroom teacher Ms. Dana Alvarez to align visual supports and vocabulary targets between the classroom and therapy settings.

9.7 Referral to WIC nutrition staff is not indicated at this time, as no feeding concerns were identified; this referral may be revisited if concerns emerge.

9.8 Family was provided with bilingual home practice materials and a list of community resources, including the Piedmont CDSA office main line and Smart Start of Chatham County contact information.

10. SUMMARY

Mateo Alejandro Cruz Hernández is a 4;2-year-old bilingual Spanish-English-speaking boy who presents with a moderate-to-severe Developmental Language Disorder and co-occurring Speech Sound Disorder affecting both of his languages. Birth history is notable for prematurity, NICU stay, and chronic otitis media with resolved hearing concerns. Family history includes a maternal uncle with a reported speech delay. Mateo qualifies for continued early intervention services and is recommended for intensive bilingual speech-language therapy combining PROMPT, Cycles, Hanen-based caregiver coaching, visual supports informed by PECS, and Kaufman protocol techniques, delivered in coordination with Piedmont CDSA, Early Head Start, and the family.

Thank you for the opportunity to evaluate Mateo. Please contact this examiner with any questions.

Respectfully submitted,

Lucía M. Fonseca-Ríos, M.S., CCC-SLP

IFSP ANNUAL REVIEW
North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program

Family/Child Name: Mateo Antonio Hernandez Cruz ("Teo")
Date of Birth: May 14, 2024
Record/Case Number: AL-2024-30871
Medicaid ID: 914772038K
CDSA Office: Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Piedmont (CDSA Piedmont), Burlington
Review Date: October 3, 2026
Initial IFSP Date: June 20, 2025

FAMILY INFORMATION

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucia Rodriguez Flores, his father, Hector Hernandez Morales, and his older sister, Camila Hernandez Cruz, at 1402 Overlook Drive, Mebane, NC 27302. The family's home phone is (336) 555-0147 and Lucia's cell is (336) 555-0298. The family's preferred language is Spanish, and Lucia reads some English but prefers Spanish for detailed medical and developmental discussions. Hector works day shifts in landscaping and speaks limited English. Lucia works nights at the Perdue Farms processing plant in Burlington, usually 11:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m., Sunday through Thursday. During Lucia's night shifts, Mateo's grandmother, Rosa Flores, stays at the home and manages the morning routine until Hector leaves for work.

Lucia's family is originally from the village of El Rosario, department of Santa Barbara, Honduras, where her mother, Rosa Flores, lived until 2021 before coming to live near the family. Hector's family is from Comitancillo, department of San Marcos, Guatemala. Mateo was born at Piedmont Regional Medical Center in Burlington.

This review meeting was held with Spanish interpretation provided by Maria Elena Vasquez, contract interpreter through CDSA Piedmont. All discussion below reflects the family's input as interpreted and confirmed with Lucia and Hector in the room.

SERVICE COORDINATION

Service Coordinator: Erika Sanchez, Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Piedmont (CDSA Piedmont), office located at 319 Graham Street, Burlington. Erika Sanchez can be reached at (336) 555-0412 or erika.sanchez@cdsapiedmont.org. Erika Sanchez has coordinated this case since the initial referral and attends all visits with the family, often bringing Maria Elena Vasquez to interpret when the primary SLP's Spanish is not sufficient for complex topics.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES

Lucia shared, in her own words through the interpreter: "Queremos que Teo hable mas, que la gente lo entienda cuando pide algo. En la casa decimos cosas y el se frustra porque no puede decir lo que quiere." Maria Elena Vasquez interpreted this as: "We want Teo to talk more, so people understand him when he asks for something. At home we say things, and he gets frustrated because he can't say what he wants."

Hector added: "A veces grita en vez de hablar, y yo no sé si es porque no entiende o porque no puede decir las palabras." Interpreted: "Sometimes he screams instead of talking, and I don't know if it's because he doesn't understand or because he can't say the words."

Lucia also raised a concern about Mateo's daycare transition: "En la guarderia dicen que el se aisla cuando los otros niños juegan. Queremos que juegue mas con los demas." (At daycare they say he isolates himself when the other kids play. We want him to play more with the others.)

The family's priorities for this review period are: (1) increase Mateo's expressive vocabulary and intelligibility so familiar listeners and new listeners can understand him; (2) support turn-taking and play skills with peers at daycare; (3) continue bilingual language exposure at home in Spanish while building English exposure through daycare and the library program; and (4) help Camila understand how to support her brother's communication without speaking for him.

DAILY ROUTINES

Mateo wakes around 6:30 a.m. and eats breakfast with Rosa Flores and Camila before Hector drops both children at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center on his way to work, usually by 7:45 a.m.. At daycare, Mateo's lead teacher is Jessica Byrd, who reports that Mateo enjoys sensory bins and building blocks but tends to play near, rather than with, classmates such as Diego during free play.

Hector or Rosa Flores picks the children up around 5:00 p.m.. Dinner is a shared family routine around 6:30 p.m., where Lucia tries to engage Mateo in naming foods and requesting more. Lucia leaves for her shift around 10:15 p.m., after bath and bedtime routines with Mateo and Camila, which include a shared picture book read aloud in Spanish.

On Saturday mornings, the family attends a bilingual story time program at Mebane Public Library, where Mateo has started to recognize a peer named Sofia from the group and will sometimes hand her a book. The family also receives support from El Centro Latino de Alamance, a nonprofit that has helped Lucia with English classes and connected the family to community resources, including WIC.

OTHER AGENCIES AND PROVIDERS INVOLVED

Mateo's pediatrician is Dr. Susan Patel at Mebane Pediatrics, who manages his well-child visits and referred the family to CDSA Piedmont after a missed-milestone screening at the 18-month visit. Mateo receives occupational therapy from Rachel Kim, OTR/L, focused on sensory regulation and fine motor skills, and physical therapy consultation from Brian Thompson, PT, DPT, who monitors gross motor milestones but has not recommended ongoing PT services at this time. The family also receives WIC nutrition support and has applied for Smart Start childcare subsidy assistance through CDSA Piedmont's referral list.

The primary speech-language pathologist for this IFSP is Ashley Caldwell, MS, CCC-SLP, bilingual provider employed by Piedmont Pediatric Speech and Language Services, PLLC. Ashley Caldwell has provided home-based speech-language services since July 8, 2025.

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT

Evaluation was completed on September 22, 2026 by Ashley Caldwell, MS, CCC-SLP, with interpretation support from Maria Elena Vasquez. Mateo's chronological age at evaluation was 2;4.

Receptive language was assessed using the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-English bilingual administration. Mateo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 79 (8th percentile), within the below average range, with an age equivalent of 19-21 months. Expressive Communication standard score was 71 (3rd percentile), age equivalent 16-18 months. The 90% confidence interval for the Total Language Score was 68-78.

Articulation and phonology were screened informally given Mateo's limited expressive output. Mateo produced primarily single words and a few two-word combinations in Spanish, with occasional English words learned at daycare ("more," "dog"). Observed sound errors included final consonant deletion, as in "pan" produced as "pa," and gliding of liquids, as in "rojo" produced as "wojo" (/ɾ/ realized as [w]). Stimulability testing showed Mateo could approximate target words with moderate cues, achieving correct productions 3 of 5 trials for word-final consonants with modeling and tactile cueing.

Play-based observation showed functional and some symbolic play (feeding a doll, pushing a car while vocalizing "vrum"), but limited joint attention bids and inconsistent response to name, correct 6 of 10 trials. Social communication checklist, completed by Lucia and Jessica Byrd separately, flagged concerns in peer engagement and frustration tolerance consistent with expressive language delay rather than a primary social communication disorder, per team consensus discussion.

Oral mechanism exam was within normal limits for structure and movement. Hearing screening passed bilaterally on August 14, 2026. Birth history reviewed: 38-week gestation, birth weight 6 lbs 11 oz, Apgar scores 8 and 9, no NICU stay, no significant medical history since birth.

Diagnostic impression: Expressive Language Disorder, bilingual (Spanish-English), with mild receptive involvement. ICD-10 code F80.1; CPT codes used for evaluation were 92523 and 96110.

IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Mateo will increase his expressive vocabulary to request wants and needs using two- to three-word combinations in Spanish, understood by familiar and unfamiliar listeners 8 of 10 opportunities across two consecutive sessions.
Strategies: Use of Hanen-based strategies (OWL: Observe, Wait, Listen) during family routines; modeling expansion of single words to two-word phrases during meals and play; family coached to narrate daily routines in Spanish using simple, repeated phrases. Ashley Caldwell will coach Lucia and Rosa Flores directly during home visits, since they are present for the most routines.

Outcome 2: Mateo will improve speech sound production of final consonants and the /ɾ/ sound in single words, achieving 70% accuracy in structured play-based trials.
Strategies: Cycles approach targeting final consonant deletion; use of tactile and visual cueing with moderate to minimal cues faded over sessions; home practice list of target words sent weekly in Spanish for family drill during bath and car routines.

Outcome 3: Mateo will initiate and respond to joint attention bids with at least one peer during structured play at daycare, 4 of 5 observed opportunities, to support the family's priority of increased peer engagement.
Strategies: Collaboration with Jessica Byrd to structure small-group play with Diego using shared toys; visual supports for turn-taking; Rachel Kim, OTR/L to co-treat on select visits to address sensory regulation that may be limiting peer approach behaviors.

Outcome 4: Camila and the family will use at least three coached strategies (wait time, modeling, avoiding speaking for Mateo) during shared play and mealtime routines, as reported by Lucia and observed during one home visit per month.
Strategies: Direct coaching with Camila present during at least one session per month; printed strategy cards in Spanish for the refrigerator; Erika Sanchez to check in on family comfort with strategies during service coordination contacts.

SERVICE DELIVERY

Speech-language therapy: one 50-minute home-based session weekly, provided by Ashley Caldwell, MS, CCC-SLP, in the family's home at 1402 Overlook Drive, Mebane. Sessions are conducted primarily in Spanish, with interpretation by Maria Elena Vasquez available by request for complex strategy discussions. Service begin date: July 8, 2025; current authorization period: July 8, 2026 through July 7, 2027.

Occupational therapy: one 45-minute session every two weeks, provided by Rachel Kim, OTR/L, in-home, continuing from prior IFSP period, begin date September 2, 2025.

Physical therapy: consultation only, quarterly check-ins by Brian Thompson, PT, DPT; next consult scheduled January 12, 2027.

Service coordination: monthly contact and quarterly home visits by Erika Sanchez, CDSA Piedmont, continuing through the IFSP period.

TRANSITION PLANNING

Because Mateo will turn three on May 14, 2027, the team discussed transition planning. Erika Sanchez will initiate a referral to the local school district's preschool exceptional children's program no later than February 14, 2027, ninety days before Mateo's third birthday, per state timeline requirements. Lucia and Hector were given written information in Spanish about transition rights and timelines and expressed that they would like Maria Elena Vasquez or another Spanish interpreter present for the transition conference.

FAMILY SIGNATURE AND CONSENT

The family participated fully in this review meeting on October 3, 2026 and agreed with the outcomes, strategies, and service delivery described above. Lucia Rodriguez Flores and Hector Hernandez Morales signed consent for continued services as outlined.

text:
Patient Name: Mateo Alejandro Flores  Date of Birth: January 14, 2022  Chronological Age: 3;9
Evaluation Dates: September 15, 2025, September 22, 2025  Report Date: September 29, 2025
Medicaid ID: 912847563A  Case/Record Number: LD-20394
Primary Home Language: Spanish  Secondary Language: English  Interpreter Needed: No (clinician bilingual)
Referring Provider: Dr. Kevin Patel  Service Coordinator: Maria Santos, Piedmont CDSA
Evaluating Clinician: Jennifer M. Hawthorne, M.S., CCC-SLP  Employer: Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Partners, PLLC
Clinic Address: 4521 Battleground Avenue, Suite 210, Greensboro, NC 27410  Clinic Phone: (336) 555-0148
Clinician Email: jhawthorne@carolinapedspeech.com  County: Guilford County

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Kevin Patel, his pediatrician, following concerns raised at his three-year well-child visit about delayed expressive language and unclear speech. Maria Santos, the service coordinator at Piedmont CDSA, contacted this clinician's office to request the evaluation as part of an open referral for early intervention services. Mateo's mother, Lucía Rodríguez Flores, reported that she and Mateo's father, Jorge Flores Medina, have been worried since his second birthday that he was not combining words the way his older sister did at the same age. Staff at Little Learners Daycare, where Mateo attends five days a week, echoed these concerns in a written note sent home with him in May 2025.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Mateo Alejandro Flores is a 3;9-year-old boy who lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Flores; his father, Jorge Flores Medina; his older sister, Camila Flores (age 6); and his younger brother, Diego Flores (age 1), in Greensboro. His maternal grandmother, Rosa Medina, lives nearby and provides after-daycare childcare three afternoons a week while Lucía works. The family also has a dog named Max, whom Mateo reportedly talks to often, according to his mother.

Mateo has attended Little Learners Daycare since August 2023, currently in the three-year-old classroom with lead teacher Ms. Angela Lopez. Ms. Lopez reports that Mateo is social and affectionate with peers but is often difficult to understand, and that he sometimes becomes frustrated and gives up trying to communicate a need. He has one particular classroom friend, Liam, with whom he plays most days, and Ms. Lopez notes that Liam often "translates" Mateo's requests to other adults in the room.

The family receives case management through Piedmont CDSA and has an open Individualized Family Service Plan, with Maria Santos serving as service coordinator. Lucía Rodríguez Flores also reported that the family receives nutrition support through WIC and that Diego was recently enrolled in a playgroup through Triad Early Head Start. The family was connected to Guilford County Smart Start last year for a kindergarten-readiness screening for Camila, and Lucía mentioned that the family has an open file with Guilford County Department of Social Services related to a prior housing-assistance application, which she said is unrelated to today's evaluation but wanted documented for continuity of records.

In addition to his time at Little Learners Daycare, Mateo has been attending a weekly caregiver-and-child communication group called Little Learners Program, which meets at a community center near the family's home and is facilitated by a graduate speech-language pathology student under supervision. Lucía Rodríguez Flores reported that she was initially confused when she received paperwork from both Little Learners Daycare and the Little Learners Program in the same week, since the names are so similar, and asked that this evaluator clarify in writing which program is being referenced in any recommendations.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 39 weeks gestation at Cone Health Women's Hospital in Greensboro via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Birth weight was 7 lbs 2 oz and Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. Lucía Rodríguez Flores reported no complications during pregnancy, labor, or delivery, and no NICU stay was required. Mateo met early gross motor milestones within typical limits, per parent report: he sat independently at 6 months and walked at 13 months.

Medical history is notable for recurrent otitis media, with Mateo experiencing approximately six documented ear infections between 18 months and 30 months of age. He underwent bilateral myringotomy with tube placement on March 10, 2024, performed by his ENT. Since that time, Lucía reports fewer infections, though Mateo had one episode of fluid behind the right tube noted at a follow-up visit on January 22, 2025. A pediatric audiological evaluation completed on February 3, 2025 indicated hearing within normal limits bilaterally at that time. Mateo has no diagnosed vision concerns, no history of seizure activity, and no significant hospitalizations beyond the tube placement. He is not currently on any daily medications. Dr. Kevin Patel's referral note listed a working diagnosis of F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder), pending this evaluation's findings.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

The home language environment is bilingual. Lucía Rodríguez Flores reported that Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home, used by her, Jorge Flores Medina, and Rosa Medina with the children approximately 80% of the time, with English used the remaining 20%, largely by Camila Flores, who is in first grade and increasingly prefers English at home. Mateo hears both languages daily and is exposed to English primarily at Little Learners Daycare and through Camila.

Lucía Rodríguez Flores reported that Mateo's early language milestones were delayed in both languages. He said his first words, "mamá" and "agua," around 18 months, which is later than his sister, who was reportedly combining two words by 16 months. By his second birthday, Mateo had an estimated vocabulary of fewer than 20 words across both languages combined, per parent report using a modified vocabulary checklist. He began combining two words inconsistently around 30 months. There is a reported family history of late talking: Jorge Flores Medina stated that he himself did not begin speaking in sentences until close to age four, and that his younger brother, Mateo's uncle, Andrés Flores Medina, received speech therapy as a child in Mexico.

No other developmental concerns were reported. Mateo plays appropriately with toys, engages in simple pretend play, makes eye contact, and shows typical social reciprocity with family members and peers such as Liam. Lucía denied any regression in skills, repetitive behaviors, or sensory concerns.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

This evaluation was conducted across two sessions at the office of Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Partners, PLLC in Greensboro. Session one, on September 15, 2025, was conducted primarily in Spanish with transition to English during structured subtests, consistent with Mateo's dominant home language; session two, on September 22, 2025, focused on English-language measures and speech sound sampling. Lucía Rodríguez Flores was present for both sessions and provided case history information and informal observations. This evaluator, Jennifer M. Hawthorne, M.S., CCC-SLP, is bilingual in English and Spanish and administered all formal and informal measures directly without need for an interpreter.

Procedures included standardized norm-referenced testing, dynamic assessment, language sampling in both languages, an oral-motor examination, a hearing screening pass/fail check (deferred to recent audiological results given tube history), and parent interview using a structured bilingual developmental questionnaire. Mateo was cooperative throughout both sessions, though he required frequent breaks and preferred tasks be framed as games. Behavioral observations were considered consistent with a valid estimate of current functioning, though scores in the lower range should be interpreted with some caution given his limited exposure to structured testing formats prior to this evaluation.

STANDARDIZED TEST RESULTS

Test / Subtest                                  Date          Standard Score   Percentile Rank   95% CI
Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5)
  Auditory Comprehension                09/15/2025   73              4th            68-78
  Expressive Communication               09/15/2025   70              2nd            65-75
  Total Language Score                   09/15/2025   69              2nd            64-74

Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), Spanish-language administration
  Sentence Structure                     09/15/2025   71              3rd            65-77
  Word Structure                         09/15/2025   68              2nd            61-75
  Expressive Vocabulary                  09/15/2025   74              4th            68-80

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)
  Sounds-in-Words                        09/22/2025   65              1st            58-72

Receptive-Expressive Emergent Language Test-4 (REEL-4)
  Receptive Language Age Equivalent       09/22/2025   26 months      —                 24-30 months
  Expressive Language Age Equivalent      09/22/2025   22 months      —                 19-25 months

Note: Mateo's chronological age at time of testing was 3;9. The CELF Preschool-3 was administered in Spanish given reported home language dominance; the PLS-5 and GFTA-3 were administered in English with Spanish supports provided as needed for task comprehension, per standardized bilingual administration guidelines.

LANGUAGE SAMPLE AND SPEECH SOUND ANALYSIS

A 100-utterance connected speech sample was collected across both languages during play-based interaction. In Spanish, Mateo's mean length of utterance was 2.1 morphemes, below expectations for his age. He produced mostly two-word combinations such as "más agua" and "no quiero," with limited use of grammatical morphemes such as plural markers and verb conjugations. In English, his MLU was 1.6 morphemes, with single-word and occasional two-word utterances such as "more juice" and "go bye-bye."

Articulation testing and conversational sampling identified a moderate-to-severe speech sound disorder affecting intelligibility in both languages. Mateo demonstrated gliding of liquids, producing /w/ for /ɾ/ in Spanish (e.g., "pewo" for "perro") and /w/ for /r/ in English. He also demonstrated final consonant deletion and stopping of fricatives, producing [t] for /s/ in word-initial position (e.g., "topa" for "sopa"). Overall intelligibility to unfamiliar listeners was estimated at approximately 40% in connected speech, improving to roughly 65% with known context. On a single-word naming task, Mateo correctly produced target consonants in 8/10 trials for early-developing sounds but only 3/10 trials for later-developing sounds such as /r/ and consonant clusters, an accuracy rate of approximately 80% and 30% respectively.

Dynamic assessment, in which this clinician modeled target structures and provided mod cues (moderate verbal and visual cueing), indicated that Mateo was responsive to instruction: with mod cues, he correctly imitated subject-verb-object word order in 7 of 10 trials, up from 2 of 10 trials without support. This pattern of improved performance with cueing and modeling is a favorable prognostic indicator and is inconsistent with a primary diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder or global developmental delay in isolation.

ORAL-MOTOR AND FEEDING OBSERVATIONS

Oral-motor examination revealed structures within normal limits for strength, symmetry, and range of motion of the lips, tongue, and jaw. Diadochokinetic rates were judged age-appropriate informally. No overt dysarthric or apraxic features were observed, though inconsistent sound substitutions across repeated productions of the same word (e.g., "perro" produced as "pewo," "peo," and "pedo" across three trials) raise a mild concern for a motor planning component that should be monitored over time. No feeding or swallowing concerns were reported by Lucía Rodríguez Flores, and Mateo eats a full range of textures without difficulty.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, language sampling, dynamic assessment, and parent report, Mateo Alejandro Flores presents with a moderate-to-severe mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with F80.2, along with a moderate-to-severe speech sound disorder affecting intelligibility in both languages. These findings are not attributable solely to typical second-language acquisition or bilingual development, as Mateo demonstrates delays relative to same-age peers in his dominant home language, Spanish, as well as in English. His pattern of stimulability and positive response to cueing during dynamic assessment suggests good candidacy for intervention and a reasonably favorable prognosis with consistent services.

The combination of expressive and receptive deficits, reduced intelligibility, and history of recurrent otitis media with tube placement is consistent with a multifactorial presentation in which early and recurrent conductive hearing loss likely contributed to, though does not fully account for, his current language and speech profile. Continued audiological monitoring is recommended given his history.

Mateo does not currently present with features suggestive of autism spectrum disorder; his social engagement, joint attention, pretend play, and response to intervention during dynamic assessment were all age-appropriate or favorable. No further autism-specific evaluation is recommended at this time, though the team should remain alert to any emerging concerns.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo qualifies for ongoing speech-language intervention based on standardized scores falling more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean across multiple measures in both languages. It is recommended that his IFSP team, including Maria Santos at Piedmont CDSA, update his Individualized Family Service Plan to reflect these findings and establish new outcomes targeting expressive syntax, vocabulary growth, and speech sound production.

2. Individual speech-language therapy is recommended twice weekly for 30-minute sessions, billed under CPT 92507 (individual treatment of speech, language, voice, communication, and/or auditory processing disorder), delivered bilingually when possible. An initial speech-language evaluation re-check using standardized measures (billed under CPT 92523, evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression) is recommended in approximately 6 months to monitor progress and adjust goals.

3. Therapy should emphasize a combination of approaches given Mateo's profile and favorable response to modeling: a Cycles approach is recommended to target his phonological error patterns (gliding, stopping, final consonant deletion) in both languages, and a Hanen-based caregiver coaching component is recommended to support Lucía Rodríguez Flores and Jorge Flores Medina in using language-facilitation strategies at home in Spanish. PROMPT techniques may be considered as a supplemental approach if inconsistent speech sound errors persist, given the mild motor planning concern noted above.

4. This clinician recommends that the family continue participation in the Little Learners Program caregiver-and-child communication group as a supplement to, not a replacement for, individual therapy. Given the naming overlap with Little Learners Daycare, it is recommended that the service coordinator clearly label each program by its full name in all IFSP documentation and correspondence to avoid confusion for the family and for billing purposes.

5. Continued close coordination with Ms. Angela Lopez at Little Learners Daycare is recommended, including a brief classroom consultation to share communication strategies and target vocabulary so that staff can reinforce therapy goals throughout the school day. Encouraging continued peer interaction with Liam and other classmates is also recommended, as Mateo shows strong motivation to communicate in socially meaningful contexts.

6. A referral back to Dr. Kevin Patel is recommended for continued monitoring of middle ear status given the history of recurrent otitis media, with a repeat audiological evaluation recommended in 6 months or sooner if new signs of hearing difficulty are observed. Results of any future audiological testing should be shared with this clinician and with Piedmont CDSA to inform ongoing service planning.

7. Given the family's connections with WIC, Guilford County Smart Start, and Triad Early Head Start, this clinician recommends that Maria Santos help coordinate information-sharing across agencies as appropriate, with family consent, to ensure consistent support as Diego Flores grows and as Mateo transitions toward preschool services.

8. Reassessment of Mateo's progress is recommended at approximately 6-month intervals, or sooner if the IFSP team determines a change in service intensity is warranted. This clinician is available for ongoing consultation and can be reached at the contact information listed above.

This evaluation and these recommendations are based on Mateo's presentation and performance on September 15, 2025 and September 22, 2025, and on reported history. Should concerns change or new information become available, the family and IFSP team are encouraged to contact this office.
