text:
PIEDMONT BILINGUAL SPEECH THERAPY, PLLC
482 Tate Boulevard SE, Suite 210, Hickory, NC 28602
Phone: (828) 555-0142 | Fax: (828) 555-0143 | intake@piedmontbilingualslp.com

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT / INFORME DE EVALUACION DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Flores Jimenez ("Teo")
Date of Birth: April 9, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 3;7
Evaluation Dates: November 12, 2025 and November 14, 2025
Report Date: November 20, 2025
Parents/Guardians: Lucia Jimenez Flores (mother), Carlos Flores (father)
Home Address: 1917 Startown Road, Newton, NC 28658
Referral Source: Catawba County Partnership for Children
Medicaid ID: 845213769B
Record Number: CDSA-30221
Home Language(s): Spanish and English
Evaluating Clinician: Maria Elena Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Spanish-English Certificate of Clinical Competence
Employer: Piedmont Bilingual Speech Therapy, PLLC
Interpreter: Rosa Elena Vega, Qualified Spanish Medical Interpreter
Service Coordinator: Denise Hall, Catawba County CDSA

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo (called "Teo" at home) was referred for a bilingual speech-language evaluation by his service coordinator, Denise Hall of the Catawba County CDSA, following a concern raised at his 3-year developmental screening. His mother, Lucia, reported that Teo "no habla tanto como su hermana a esta edad" ("does not talk as much as his sister did at this age"). The family was also referred by staff at Catawba County Early Head Start, where Teo attends a morning classroom three days a week. His teacher there, Miss Ana, noted that Teo "gets frustrated when the other kids don't understand him" and that he often points or pulls peers by the hand instead of using words.

This evaluation was conducted to determine Mateo's current speech and language skills in both Spanish and English, to rule out a primary language impairment versus a difference related to bilingual language acquisition, and to make recommendations for services.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION / HISTORIA DEL DESARROLLO

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucia Jimenez Flores and Carlos Flores, and his older sister, Sol, age 7, who attends second grade at Oakwood Elementary School. Lucia reported, "Teo y Sol se llevan muy bien, pero ella siempre habla por el" (they get along very well, but she always talks for him). The family also receives frequent childcare help from Teo's paternal grandmother, whom the family calls doña Lupe. According to Carlos, "doña Lupe cuida a los ninos cuando salimos a trabajar, y ella le habla solo en espanol" (she only speaks to him in Spanish). The household also includes a family dog named Max, whom Teo reportedly calls by pointing and saying "ah ah" rather than the dog's name.

The family attends Iglesia Bautista Nueva Esperanza in Newton, NC, where Teo participates in a Sunday children's program alongside other bilingual toddlers. Lucia stated that the volunteer who runs that program, known to the family as la maestra Carmen, has also commented that Teo "se queda calladito" (stays very quiet) during group singing time compared to other children his age.

Developmental milestones were reported by parent interview, supplemented by a review of records from Catawba County Early Head Start and the family's pediatric clinic. Mateo sat independently around 7 months, walked independently at 14 months, and fed himself with a spoon by 18 months. Fine and gross motor milestones were otherwise reported as within normal limits, and Teo has no history of physical or occupational therapy referral.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA MEDICA Y DEL NACIMIENTO

Lucia reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with routine prenatal care beginning in the first trimester. Mateo was born at 39 weeks gestation via vaginal delivery at Catawba Valley Regional Medical Center in Hickory, NC. Birth weight was 7 lbs 4 oz, and Apgar scores were reported as 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. There were no complications during delivery, and Teo was discharged home with his mother at 2 days of life.

Mateo's pediatrician, Dr. Rebecca Anh Nguyen of Foothills Pediatric Associates, has followed him since birth. Records reviewed with parental consent indicate a history of recurrent otitis media, with 4 documented episodes between 12 and 24 months of age, treated with oral antibiotics. Teo passed a newborn hearing screening and passed a repeat audiological evaluation at March 3, 2025, administered by audiologist Grace Olumide, with results within normal limits bilaterally (otoacoustic emissions and tympanometry, type A bilaterally). No surgical history, no seizure history, and no significant illnesses or hospitalizations were reported beyond the ear infections noted above. Teo is not currently taking any prescription medication. Vision was reported as unremarkable by parent report, with no referral to ophthalmology to date.

Family medical history is significant for a maternal cousin with a diagnosed speech sound disorder who received services through the local public school system, and a paternal uncle who Carlos described as "tardo mucho en hablar pero despues hablo bien" (was very late to talk but eventually talked fine). No family history of autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability, or genetic syndromes was reported.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE IDIOMAS

Lucia was born in Mexico and moved to North Carolina as a teenager; she is a native Spanish speaker and reports conversational English proficiency. Carlos was born in Catawba County to Spanish-speaking parents and is fully bilingual, using Spanish at home and English at his workplace, Catawba Valley Furniture Manufacturing, where he works a rotating shift. Lucia works part time cleaning offices for Carolina Clean Commercial Services in the evenings while Carlos is home with the children.

Per parent report using a structured language background interview, Mateo's primary input language from birth to approximately 30 months was Spanish, spoken by Lucia, doña Lupe, and extended family during frequent visits. English exposure increased notably when Teo began attending Catawba County Early Head Start at 30 months of age, where instruction is primarily in English with some Spanish-speaking classroom aides. Current estimated language exposure is approximately 60% Spanish and 40% English, occurring in overlapping daily contexts rather than strictly separated by person or setting.

Lucia described Sol's own early language development as rapid in both languages, noting "ella aprendio los dos idiomas sin ningun problema" (she learned both languages with no problem at all), which has heightened the family's concern about Teo's comparatively slower progress. The family also mentioned a weekly bilingual story-time program at the Catawba County Library branch in Newton, which Lucia attends with Teo most Tuesdays at 10:30 a.m.; she reported that the librarian who leads the program, Miss Teresa, has also observed that Teo "prefers to point and grab books rather than ask for them by name."

Lucia reported that Teo's current expressive vocabulary includes approximately 50 words combined across both languages, with more words understood than produced. She estimated that strangers and extended family members who do not know Teo well understand "como la mitad de lo que dice" (about half of what he says), while immediate family understand him more consistently due to familiarity with his speech patterns and gestures.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo presented as a friendly, engaged toddler who separated easily from his mother for testing with the interpreter, Rosa Elena Vega, present throughout. He demonstrated appropriate eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking during play-based activities. Teo used a combination of single words, gestures, and vocal approximations to communicate, and he readily imitated modeled words when prompted with moderate verbal cues (mod cues). He showed clear frustration behaviors, including pulling this examiner's hand toward desired items and vocalizing loudly, when his single-word attempts were not immediately understood.

Teo transitioned between Spanish and English materials without apparent confusion, responding appropriately to simple directions given in either language (for example, "toca la pelota" and "touch the ball"). Attention span was adequate for the duration of both testing sessions, each lasting approximately 45 minutes, with one short break at 9:40 a.m. during the first session.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

The following formal and informal measures were administered in both Spanish and English, with the interpreter present for all Spanish-language administration and parent-report components:

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition, Spanish (PLS-5 Spanish) — Auditory Comprehension and Expressive Communication subtests
- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English form — Auditory Comprehension and Expressive Communication subtests
- Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) — Morphosyntax and Semantics subtests
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) — Sounds-in-Words subtest, English
- Spanish Articulation Screening (informal, criterion-referenced)
- Parent interview and developmental questionnaire (Spanish and English versions)
- Language sample analysis, approximately 100 utterances, mixed Spanish and English
- Oral mechanism examination
- Hearing screening (pure-tone, bilaterally within normal limits)

TEST RESULTS

Standardized Test Scores:

Test / Subtest | Raw Score | Standard Score | Percentile Rank | Age Equivalent
PLS-5 Spanish Auditory Comprehension | 28 | 79 | 8th | 2;6-2;9
PLS-5 Spanish Expressive Communication | 19 | 73 | 4th | 2;0-2;3
PLS-5 English Auditory Comprehension | 31 | 82 | 12th | 2;9-3;0
PLS-5 English Expressive Communication | 21 | 75 | 5th | 2;3-2;6
BESA Morphosyntax | 14 | 72 | 3rd | n/a
BESA Semantics | 17 | 81 | 10th | n/a
GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words | 22 | 85 | 16th | n/a

Composite language scores in both Spanish and English fell within the below average to moderately delayed range when considered separately. However, conceptual scoring, which credits Teo for a concept demonstrated in either language, yielded a combined receptive vocabulary estimate in the 35th percentile, and a combined expressive vocabulary estimate in the 22nd percentile, both closer to age expectations. This pattern is consistent with typical bilingual first-language acquisition, in which skills distributed across two languages may appear artificially low when each language is scored in isolation.

SPEECH SOUND PRODUCTION

On the GFTA-3, Teo demonstrated the following error patterns in English single-word productions: final consonant deletion (for example, "ca" for "cat," target /kaet/), fronting of velars (he produced "tat" for "cat," substituting [t] for /k/), and stopping of fricatives (he produced "pish" as "pit," substituting [t] for /s/). On the informal Spanish screening, similar patterns were noted, including simplification of consonant clusters (he produced "pato" for "plato," omitting the liquid) and occasional substitution of [d] for the tapped /ɾ/ in words such as "pero," which he produced as "pedo" (phonetically [ˈpe.do]).

Intelligibility was judged to be approximately 50% to unfamiliar listeners and 70-80% to familiar listeners, consistent with parent report. These error patterns occur in both Spanish and English and are not attributable to normal cross-linguistic transfer alone, suggesting a speech sound disorder affecting both languages rather than a difference related solely to bilingualism.

LANGUAGE SAMPLE

A language sample was collected across both testing sessions during play with toy animals, a farm set, and a simple picture book, with the interpreter transcribing Spanish utterances in real time. Teo produced predominantly single words and some two-word combinations, with occasional three-word utterances. Examples of coded utterances included:

"mas agua" [MLU: 2.0] (more water)
"Max no" (telling the family dog no)
"quiero eso" [EW] (I want that — coded as an exact word-level match)
"up momma" (requesting to be picked up)
"no no no" [SR] (self-repetition code)

Mean length of utterance (MLU) across the combined sample was calculated at 1.8 morphemes, which falls below expectations for his chronological age of 3;7 even when combining both languages, and below the expected range of 2;6-3;2 typically associated with that MLU level. Teo demonstrated limited use of grammatical morphemes in both languages, including minimal use of plural markers, verb tense markers, and possessive forms, which is notable beyond what would be expected from typical bilingual development alone.

ORAL MECHANISM EXAMINATION

Oral structures were within normal limits for symmetry, strength, and range of motion. No signs of oral-motor dysfunction, tongue tie, or craniofacial abnormality were observed. Diadochokinetic rates were not formally assessed given Teo's age but informal sequential motor tasks (patty cake sequences) were completed without difficulty, suggesting adequate oral-motor planning for gross tasks.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS / IMPRESIONES CLINICAS

Based on standardized testing, parent interview, language sampling, and clinical observation, Mateo Alejandro Flores Jimenez presents with a mixed expressive-receptive language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, co-occurring with a speech sound disorder affecting both languages. ICD-10 diagnostic code F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder) and F80.0 (phonological disorder) are applied. Billing for the combined evaluation session is coded under CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression).

The pattern of delay present in both of Teo's languages, rather than isolated to one, supports a diagnosis of true language and speech disorder rather than a language difference attributable solely to simultaneous bilingual acquisition or reduced input in either single language. The combination of conceptually scored vocabulary estimates closer to age level, alongside cross-linguistic expressive and phonological weaknesses, indicates that while bilingualism is not the cause of Teo's difficulties, intervention must address both of his languages to be effective and ecologically appropriate for his home environment.

Teo's strengths include strong social engagement, intact play skills, good comprehension of simple directions in both languages, and a highly supportive family who provides rich language input through extended family, church community, and library programming. Risk factors include recurrent early otitis media, which may have contributed to inconsistent auditory input during a key developmental window, and reduced intelligibility, which appears to be contributing to frustration and some reduction in initiating communication with unfamiliar listeners, including peers at his Early Head Start classroom.

RECOMMENDATIONS / RECOMENDACIONES

1. Mateo qualifies for ongoing speech-language intervention services and should be referred for an Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) meeting through Catawba County CDSA to establish formal goals and service frequency, given his current enrollment in Part C early intervention eligibility pathways.

2. Recommend direct bilingual speech-language therapy, Spanish and English, 2 times weekly, 30 minutes per session, targeting IFSP Outcome 1 (expressive vocabulary and word combinations) and IFSP Outcome 2 (speech sound accuracy for final consonants and velar sounds) in both languages.

3. Therapy approach recommendations include a developmentally based, naturalistic framework incorporating Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies for caregiver coaching, with cueing hierarchies moving from maximal to minimal cues as skills emerge, and a cycles approach (Cycles phonological approach) for addressing final consonant deletion and velar fronting across both languages.

4. Recommend that Lucia and Carlos, along with doña Lupe when she is providing care, be coached directly in home strategies to support bilingual language development, including expansion of Teo's utterances in whichever language he initiates, rather than correcting or switching languages mid-utterance.

5. Recommend that Teo's teacher, Miss Ana, at Catawba County Early Head Start, receive a brief classroom communication strategy handout (bilingual version) to support peer interaction and reduce frustration-related behaviors during group activities.

6. Recommend continued participation in community language-rich activities already in place, including the Catawba County Library bilingual story time and Sunday children's program at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Esperanza, as these provide valuable, low-cost language exposure in both languages and should be maintained alongside formal therapy rather than discontinued.

7. Recommend re-screening of hearing given history of recurrent otitis media; if any additional episodes occur, refer promptly to audiology and consider ENT referral through Dr. Rebecca Anh Nguyen at Foothills Pediatric Associates to monitor for any recurrence affecting auditory access to language.

8. Recommend re-evaluation in 6 months to monitor progress in both languages and adjust the IFSP as needed, with particular attention to morphosyntax development and intelligibility gains.

9. Provide family with a bilingual home practice handout and a list of community resources, including information on Catawba County WIC nutrition services (already utilized by the family) and the Catawba County DSS family support line, in case additional concrete support needs arise during this period of increased appointments.

This evaluation and these recommendations were discussed with Lucia Jimenez Flores and Carlos Flores in Spanish, with interpretation support from Rosa Elena Vega, at the conclusion of testing on November 14, 2025. The family verbalized understanding of the results and expressed agreement with the recommendation to pursue IFSP services. Lucia stated, "queremos que Teo hable como su hermana, pero entendemos que cada nino es diferente" (we want Teo to talk like his sister, but we understand every child is different), reflecting realistic expectations and strong family engagement in the recommended plan.

Please contact this clinician with any questions regarding this report or the recommendations contained within.

Respectfully submitted,

Maria Elena Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Spanish-English Certificate of Clinical Competence

Family Information

Mateo Alejandro Vásquez, known to his family as "Teo," is a 2;7-year-old boy who lives with his parents, Lucía Rodríguez and Diego Vásquez, and his older sister, Camila Vásquez (age 6), at 214 Persimmon Ridge Lane, Fayetteville. The family also receives frequent support from Teo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Fernández, who lives nearby and keeps him two afternoons a week, and from his cousins, Sofía Fernández and Andrés Fernández, who visit most weekends. A family friend, Brenda Howell, babysits on Tuesday evenings when both parents work late. The family's dog, Rocky, is Teo's constant companion and frequently named in his early words.

Lucía Rodríguez reports that Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home, with English used increasingly by Camila Vásquez since she started kindergarten. Diego Vásquez works rotating shifts at Palmetto Tire Manufacturing, and Lucía Rodríguez works part-time cleaning houses in the mornings. Both parents are actively involved in Teo's care and attended this review in person, with Diego Vásquez joining by phone for the last twenty minutes.

Service Coordination

Monica Fields has served as Teo's service coordinator through Sandhills Regional CDSA since the initial IFSP meeting on June 2, 2025. Monica Fields coordinated today's review, which was held at the family's home with Jennifer M. Alvarez, Lucía Rodríguez, and Diego Vásquez present. Monica Fields confirmed that the family's Medicaid coverage remains active under Medicaid ID 784512093A and that no change in eligibility is anticipated before the next scheduled review.

Family Concerns, Priorities, and Resources

When asked what worries her most, Lucía Rodríguez said, "Me preocupa que no hable todavía como su hermana a esta edad" ("I worry that he doesn't talk yet like his sister did at this age"). She added, in English, "At daycare they say he gets frustrated and bites when the other kids don't understand him." Diego Vásquez agreed, saying, "I just want him to be able to tell us what he wants instead of screaming."

The family's priorities for the coming six months are: (1) that Teo use more words at home and at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center so he is less frustrated; (2) that he follow simple directions in both Spanish and English; and (3) that the family learn strategies to use during mealtime and bath time, which Lucía Rodríguez described as "our hardest parts of the day."

Lucía Rodríguez identified several family strengths and resources, including her mother Rosa Fernández's daily help, a stable home, and a close relationship with Teo's pediatrician, Dr. Sarah Kim. The family asked for written strategies in Spanish they could post on the refrigerator, and for sessions to continue in both languages, "porque en la casa hablamos los dos" (because at home we speak both).

Daily Routines

Teo wakes around 6:30 AM and eats breakfast with Camila Vásquez before she leaves for school. Lucía Rodríguez or Rosa Fernández drops him at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center by 8:15 AM, where he is in the toddler room with his teacher, Keisha Lopez, and assistant teacher Danielle Price. His classroom peers include Liam Chen, Ava Thompson, and Noah Patel, with whom he plays well during outdoor time but struggles during circle time and snack, when he wants help communicating.

Lucía Rodríguez picks Teo up around 4:45 PM on most days; on Tuesdays, Brenda Howell picks him up and stays until 7:00 PM. Dinner is the family's main shared meal, usually around 6:00 PM, and is the time Lucía Rodríguez finds hardest because Teo points and grunts rather than naming foods he wants. Bath time, around 7:30 PM, involves Teo, Camila Vásquez, and often Rocky waiting outside the bathroom door, which Teo finds motivating. Bedtime routines include a shared book in Spanish, read by Diego Vásquez when he is home from his shift.

Other Agencies Involved

In addition to Sandhills Regional CDSA, the family receives nutrition support through Cumberland County WIC and has applied for a childcare subsidy through Cumberland County Department of Social Services. Lucía Rodríguez also attends a weekly parenting group through Smart Start of Cumberland County, where she first learned about bilingual language strategies. Dr. Sarah Kim continues to monitor Teo's growth and hearing status and referred the family back to Sandhills Regional CDSA in July 2026 after a failed hearing screen, which was later cleared by audiology.

Present Levels of Development

Teo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Cumberland Memorial Hospital, with a birth weight of 6 lbs 10 oz and Apgar scores of 8 and 9. Early history is otherwise unremarkable aside from recurrent ear infections treated medically.

Jennifer M. Alvarez completed a comprehensive speech-language reassessment using the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Language and Communication subtests, administered jointly with the CDSA developmental specialist), the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition, and the Peabody Developmental Motor Scales, Second Edition (fine motor, for oral-motor correlation). Results are summarized below.

Test / Subtest | Date Administered | Standard Score | 95% CI | Percentile / AE
Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale – Receptive | August 18, 2026 | AE 18-21 months | — | below 10th
Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale – Expressive | August 18, 2026 | AE 14-16 months | — | below 1st
Bayley-4 Receptive Communication | August 20, 2026 | 76 | 70-82 | 5th
Bayley-4 Expressive Communication | August 20, 2026 | 70 | 64-76 | 2nd
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3, Sounds-in-Words | August 21, 2026 | 65 | 58-72 | 1st
Peabody Developmental Motor Scales-2, Fine Motor | August 22, 2026 | 88 | 80-96 | 21st

Teo's receptive vocabulary and ability to follow two-step directions remain significantly delayed, consistent with F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder). Articulation testing showed consistent final consonant deletion and cluster reduction; stimulable sounds included /k/, /g/, and /s/ with mod cues. During structured play, Teo produced "nana" for "agua" and attempted "Woki" for "Rocky," demonstrating word-initial /r/ produced as /w/. Oral-motor examination was within normal limits; fine motor skills on the Peabody Developmental Motor Scales, Second Edition were age-appropriate, supporting adequate oral-motor foundations for articulation gains.

Session Schedule

Teo receives speech-language intervention twice weekly through Sandhills Regional CDSA, provided by Jennifer M. Alvarez of Carolina Bilingual Pediatric Therapy, PLLC. The current schedule is:

Day | Start | Stop | Location
Monday | 9:00 AM | 9:45 AM | Teo's home, 214 Persimmon Ridge Lane, Fayetteville, NC
Thursday | 1:30 PM | 2:15 PM | Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, 118 Rosewood Avenue, Fayetteville, NC 28301

A monthly coaching session with Lucía Rodríguez and, when his shift allows, Diego Vásquez, is scheduled for the first Monday of each month from 5:30 PM to 6:15 PM at the home address above.

IFSP Outcomes and Strategies

Outcome 1: Teo will use words or approximations to request desired objects and activities across settings.
Criteria: Teo will spontaneously request using a word or word approximation in 8 of 10 opportunities across two consecutive sessions, with no more than mod cues.
Strategies: Jennifer M. Alvarez will coach the family in Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies, including following Teo's lead, commenting instead of questioning, and expectant pausing during snack and bath time. Keisha Lopez has agreed to use the same strategies during snack at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center.

Outcome 2: Teo will follow one-step directions paired with a gesture in familiar routines.
Criteria: Teo will follow a one-step direction with a gesture cue in 4 of 5 trials across three sessions.
Strategies: Visual supports and consistent gesture pairing will be used at home and at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center; Jennifer M. Alvarez will provide bilingual picture cards for "more," "all done," and "help."

Outcome 3: Teo will reduce frustration-related biting and screaming by using an alternative communication strategy.
Criteria: Caregiver report of a decrease in biting incidents to fewer than 1 per week within 90 days.
Strategies: Introduction of a modified PECS exchange system for high-frustration routines (transitions, mealtime), with PROMPT-informed tactile cueing to support jaw and lip movement during imitation tasks. Brenda Howell and Rosa Fernández will receive a short written guide, in Spanish and English, on honoring the exchange system consistently.

Outcome 4: Teo will produce age-appropriate consonant sounds in single words with increasing intelligibility.
Criteria: Teo will produce final consonants in 70% of attempted words during structured play across two sessions.
Strategies: A modified Cycles approach will target final consonant deletion and cluster reduction, beginning with /k/ and /t/ in final position. Home practice will use bath time and books, pairing target words with Rocky's name and family members' names, which Teo is highly motivated to imitate.

Each outcome will be reviewed informally at every session and formally at the next scheduled IFSP review.

Service Delivery and Review Dates

Teo's initial IFSP was developed on June 2, 2025, with a six-month review completed on December 9, 2025 and a second review on April 6, 2026. Today's annual review, conducted on October 6, 2026, was attended by Lucía Rodríguez, Diego Vásquez (by phone), Monica Fields, and Jennifer M. Alvarez. The next IFSP review is scheduled for April 6, 2027, with an annual comprehensive reassessment due by June 2, 2027.

Today's direct service was billed under CPT 92523 (speech/language evaluation) and CPT 92507 (individual treatment), with diagnosis codes F80.2 and R62.0 (delayed milestones) on file with Sandhills Regional CDSA. Session notes and coaching logs are maintained by Jennifer M. Alvarez at Carolina Bilingual Pediatric Therapy, PLLC and shared with Monica Fields prior to each review. Questions about scheduling or billing may be directed to Jennifer M. Alvarez at (910) 555-0177 or jalvarez@carolinabilingualpt.com.

Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP) — Revisión Semestral

El 14 de octubre de 2026, el equipo del Programa para Infantes y Niños Pequeños de Carolina del Norte se reunió para la revisión semestral del IFSP de Mateo Alejandro Vásquez Ponce, nacido el 2 de enero de 2024, número de expediente 774512639 y número de Medicaid 509284671B. La reunión se realizó en la oficina de la Agencia de Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Wake, ubicada en 4820 Industrial Drive, Raleigh, 27609. La coordinadora de servicios, Mr. Tom Bellamy, facilitó la reunión junto con la madre, Lucía Fernanda Ramírez, y el padre, Diego Ramírez, quienes residen con Mateo en 118 Willow Oak Lane, Garner, en el condado de Wake.

Mateo vive con sus padres, su hermana mayor Camila Ramírez, y el perro de la familia, Rocky. La niñera, a quien todos llaman doña Lupe, cuida a Mateo los días que no asiste a la guardería. Su prima, Valentina Ponce, vive cerca y lo visita casi todos los fines de semana. Mateo asiste al Centro de Cuidado Infantil Little Sprouts, donde su maestra principal es Miss Ana y la auxiliar del salón es la maestra Carmen.

La madre expresó sus preocupaciones en sus propias palabras: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Mateo se frustra mucho cuando no lo entendemos, y a veces grita o muerde." También dijo: "Quiero que pueda jugar con sus primos y decir lo que necesita sin que yo tenga que adivinar todo el tiempo." El padre añadió: "En la guardería dicen que se queda callado con los otros niños, pero en casa habla bastante, aunque no le entendemos casi nada." La familia priorizó que Mateo aumente su vocabulario funcional, que use frases cortas para pedir ayuda, y que mejore su interacción con sus compañeros de clase.

El historial del desarrollo de Mateo incluye un nacimiento a las 37 semanas de gestación, con Apgar de 8 y 9, y peso al nacer de 2,750 gramos. Fue evaluado por retraso en el habla y el lenguaje a la edad de 26 meses. En la evaluación con el PLS-5, obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 68 en Comunicación Auditiva y 71 en Comunicación Expresiva, ambas en el rango de 73-83, percentil 2. Su edad equivalente de lenguaje expresivo fue de 2;6–3;0. Actualmente tiene la edad de 2;10 según el expediente más reciente.

Durante la observación diaria, Mateo produjo aproximadamente 15 palabras funcionales, incluyendo "más", "agua" y "no". Sustituye consistentemente /k/ por [t], y omite los sonidos finales en palabras como "sol" producido como "so". Con mod cues, imitó la palabra meta "pan" en 8/10 ensayos. También logró producir "[EW]" según los códigos SALT registrados en la muestra de habla espontánea. Su rutina diaria incluye desayunar con su familia, ir a la guardería de 8:00 a.m. a 3:00 p.m., jugar con Rocky en el patio, y bañarse antes de dormir alrededor de las 7:30 p.m..

En la guardería, Miss Ana reportó que Mateo observa a sus compañeros Emma y Noah durante el juego grupal, pero rara vez inicia interacción verbal. la maestra Carmen comentó: "Cuando quiere un juguete, generalmente señala o empuja, en vez de pedirlo con palabras." La familia también recibe apoyo nutricional a través de WIC y participa en actividades de Smart Start del condado los sábados.

El equipo estableció tres resultados (outcomes) para este periodo. El Resultado 1 busca que Mateo use dos a tres palabras combinadas para pedir objetos o acciones, utilizando estrategias del enfoque Hanen y el programa It Takes Two to Talk para guiar a los padres en el modelaje del lenguaje durante las rutinas diarias. El Resultado 2 se enfoca en la producción de sonidos finales y consonantes iniciales usando el enfoque de Cycles para errores fonológicos, con énfasis en los fonemas /k/ y /t/, apoyado también con técnicas de PROMPT para guía táctil-cinestésica de la mandíbula y los labios. El Resultado 3 busca aumentar la comunicación funcional con compañeros usando apoyos visuales inspirados en PECS, y la familia solicitó explorar también el método Kaufman si el progreso con imitación de palabras es lento.

Las sesiones de terapia del habla y lenguaje son proporcionadas por Sofía Elena Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP, patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe empleada por Bright Start Therapy Services, PLLC. Su número de contacto es 919-555-0147 y su correo electrónico es scastillo@brightstarttherapy.com. Las sesiones se realizan según el siguiente horario:

| Día | Hora de inicio | Hora de fin | Lugar |
|-----|-----------------|--------------|-------|
| Lunes | 9:00 a.m. | 9:45 a.m. | Centro de Cuidado Infantil Little Sprouts |
| Miércoles | 10:30 a.m. | 11:15 a.m. | Hogar de la familia, 118 Willow Oak Lane |
| Viernes | 2:00 p.m. | 2:45 p.m. | Centro de Cuidado Infantil Little Sprouts |

Además de la terapia del habla, Mateo recibe terapia ocupacional con Hannah Doyle, OTR/L, los martes de 1:00 p.m. a 1:30 p.m. en el hogar, enfocada en integración sensorial. Su pediatra, Dra. Patricia Núñez, de la clínica WakeMed Pediatric Associates, refirió a la familia originalmente para esta evaluación. Durante las sesiones bilingües, se utiliza tanto español como inglés según la preferencia de la familia, y en ocasiones participa la intérprete Marisol Treviño cuando se requieren explicaciones adicionales en inglés para el padre.

El próximo IFSP se revisará en seis meses, antes del 14 de abril de 2027, o antes si la familia o el equipo lo solicitan. La familia firmó su consentimiento para continuar los servicios según lo descrito. La coordinadora Mr. Tom Bellamy enviará copias del documento firmado a la familia dentro de los próximos diez días hábiles, y el expediente completo permanecerá en los archivos de la Agencia de Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Wake y de Bright Start Therapy Services, PLLC.

PATIENT NAME: Mateo Fernández Ruiz
PREFERRED NAME: Teo
DATE OF BIRTH: August 14, 2021
AGE AT EVALUATION: 4;2
GENDER: Male
PRIMARY LANGUAGE(S): Spanish and English (bilingual, Spanish-dominant home)
MEDICAID ID: NC4487213056B
INSURANCE MEMBER ID: BCBS-NC-991827364
NC ITP CHILD ID: ITP-2021-048823
RECORD / AUTHORIZATION NUMBER: AUTH-2026-0073154
DATE OF EVALUATION: September 9, 2026
EVALUATION LOCATION: Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners, PLLC, 4420 Capewood Drive, Suite 210, Raleigh, NC 27609
SESSION TIMES: 9:15 a.m. to 11:40 a.m., with a snack break from 10:30 a.m. to 10:45 a.m.
REFERRING PROVIDER: Dr. Anil Patel, WakeMed Pediatric Primary Care
SERVICE COORDINATOR: Monica Reyes, Wake County CDSA
INTERPRETER: Beatriz Nuñez (Spanish/English, certified medical interpreter)
EVALUATING CLINICIAN: Jennifer Hayes, M.S., CCC-SLP
PARENT/GUARDIAN: Lucía Rodríguez (mother), Carlos Fernández (father)
HOME ADDRESS: 118 Birchfield Lane, Garner, NC 27529
HOME PHONE: (919) 555-0142
PARENT EMAIL: lucia.rodriguez84@gmail.com
DAYCARE/PRESCHOOL: Little Sprouts Early Learning Center
NEXT IFSP REVIEW DATE: December 2, 2026

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by Dr. Anil Patel at WakeMed Pediatric Primary Care following parent and daycare concerns about limited intelligibility, reduced expressive vocabulary in both Spanish and English, and difficulty following multi-step directions. Mateo's mother, Lucía Rodríguez, reports that she and Mateo's teacher at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, Ms. Amanda Lopez, independently raised concerns during the August 2026 parent conference. Mateo was previously seen for a developmental screening through Wake County CDSA on April 18, 2026, which resulted in referral for this evaluation. The family's authorization for today's visit, number AUTH-2026-0073154, was confirmed with Wake County CDSA service coordinator Monica Reyes prior to scheduling.

BACKGROUND AND HISTORY

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez; his father, Carlos Fernández; and his older brother, Sol, age 6, in Garner, NC. Lucía reports that Mateo's grandmother, Ofelia Ruiz, provides after-school and weekend childcare and speaks exclusively Spanish with both boys. The family also relies occasionally on a neighbor, Dora Campos, to watch Mateo when both parents work late shifts. Lucía is employed at the Food Lion distribution center in Garner, and Carlos works at Perdue Farms in Clayton, NC. The family attends Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida in Garner most Sundays, where Mateo participates in a bilingual children's class led by Pastor Hernán Vidal; Lucía reports Mateo enjoys singing there but rarely speaks to the other children. The family also regularly attends the free bilingual story-time program at the Garner branch of the Wake County Public Library, and has received diaper and formula support in the past through the Southeast Raleigh Family Resource Center, a nonprofit that Lucía learned about through her cousin.

Family history is notable for Carlos's report that he himself was a "late talker" and did not combine words until around 3;0, per his mother's recollection; he reports no formal speech therapy at the time. There is no other reported family history of speech, language, or hearing disorders. Mateo's brother, Sol, has no history of speech or language concerns and is described as verbally advanced for his age.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 38 weeks 4 days gestation via uncomplicated vaginal delivery at WakeMed Raleigh Campus. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. Lucía reports no complications during pregnancy or delivery and no NICU stay. Mateo passed his newborn hearing screening bilaterally and has had no documented ear infections requiring tubes, though he had one episode of acute otitis media at 18 months treated with oral antibiotics. His most recent audiological screening, completed July 22, 2026 at WakeMed Pediatric Primary Care, showed pass results bilaterally with normal tympanograms. There is no history of seizures, significant head injury, or hospitalization beyond the single ear infection noted above. Mateo is not currently on any medication. His pediatrician, Dr. Anil Patel, has not identified any syndromic features or dysmorphology, and genetics referral has not been pursued at this time. Gross and fine motor milestones were reportedly within normal limits: Mateo walked independently at 13 months and fed himself with a spoon by 18 months.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

The home language environment is primarily Spanish. Lucía reports she and Carlos speak Spanish with each other and with Mateo and Sol approximately 90 percent of the time at home, with occasional English mixed in, particularly when discussing school-related topics. Ofelia Ruiz, the children's grandmother, speaks only Spanish with the boys. Mateo has been enrolled at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center since he was 2;0, where instruction is delivered primarily in English by Ms. Amanda Lopez and assistant teacher Mr. Devon Pruitt. Lucía estimates Mateo's current language exposure at roughly 65 percent Spanish and 35 percent English across settings. According to parent report using a bilingual developmental checklist, Mateo's first words emerged around 16 months in Spanish ("agua," "mamá"), and he began combining two words around 28 months. Lucía denies any period of language loss or regression.

At daycare, Ms. Lopez reports that Mateo is social with peers but often uses gestures or single words rather than full sentences. His closest classmates, Jaxon and Amara, reportedly understand him better than unfamiliar adults do, often "translating" his requests to staff. Mateo has a pet dog at home named Luna, whom he reportedly talks to frequently and whose name he can say clearly, which the family notes as evidence that motivation, rather than motor ability alone, affects his output in some contexts.

DEVELOPMENTAL AND EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

Mateo has never received prior speech-language therapy. He was evaluated by Wake County CDSA on April 18, 2026 for a general developmental screening, which flagged possible delays in expressive communication and recommended this full evaluation. Mateo has not had an occupational or physical therapy evaluation. He is not currently enrolled in any IFSP-funded services. Lucía reports that Mateo attends daycare five days a week from approximately 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and that evenings and weekends are spent largely with family, including frequent visits to Ofelia Ruiz's home.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo presented as a friendly, engaged child who separated easily from his mother for the evaluation session, which ran from 9:15 a.m. to 11:40 a.m. with a snack break from 10:30 a.m. to 10:45 a.m.. Rapport was established quickly using toys and picture books. Mateo demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks of 10-15 minutes and needed brief redirection twice during the session, both times responding well to verbal redirection alone. Eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking during play were judged appropriate for age. Mateo used a combination of gestures, single words, and occasional two- to three-word phrases in both Spanish and English to communicate throughout the session. Oral-motor structures were observed to be within normal limits for symmetry, strength, and range of motion; no signs of dysarthria or apraxia were noted on informal oral-motor exam. Beatriz Nuñez provided interpretation for portions of the session conducted in Spanish and assisted with Spanish-language test administration and scoring verification.

ASSESSMENT RESULTS

Standardized and criterion-referenced measures were administered in both English and Spanish where appropriate, given Mateo's bilingual status. All scores below reflect dates of administration, standard scores or equivalent metrics, percentile ranks, and 95% confidence intervals where applicable.

Test / Measure | Date Administered | Score | Percentile | 95% CI
Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) — Auditory Comprehension | September 9, 2026 | 73 | 4th | 68-79
PLS-5 — Expressive Communication | September 9, 2026 | 68 | 2nd | 62-74
PLS-5 — Total Language Score | September 9, 2026 | 69 | 2nd | 64-74
Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3, Spanish (CELF Preschool-3 Spanish) — Core Language Score | September 9, 2026 | 71 | 3rd | 65-77
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) — Sounds-in-Words | September 9, 2026 | 78 | 7th | 72-84
Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) — Morphosyntax Scale, Spanish | September 9, 2026 | 82 | 12th | 75-89
Receptive-Expressive Emergent Language Test, Third Edition (REEL-3) — parent report form | September 2, 2026 | Age Equivalent 2;6-3;0 | — | —
Nonword Repetition Task | September 9, 2026 | 9/16 correct | — | —
Oral Mechanism Examination | September 9, 2026 | Within normal limits | — | —

Spontaneous speech sample and language sample analysis: A 100-utterance conversational sample was collected across both languages during structured and unstructured play. Mean length of utterance in morphemes (MLUm) in English was calculated at 2.1, and in Spanish at 2.4, both of which fall notably below expectations for Mateo's chronological age of 4;2. SALT coding of the sample included multiple instances of omitted grammatical morphemes, coded as [EW] for word omissions and [EO] for morpheme omissions, consistent across both languages, which supports a primary language impairment rather than a language-difference pattern attributable solely to second-language acquisition.

Articulation and phonology: Mateo demonstrated reduced intelligibility, estimated at approximately 60 percent in context for unfamiliar listeners and 80 percent for familiar listeners. Error patterns included final consonant deletion (e.g., "ca" for "cat"), cluster reduction (e.g., "poon" for "spoon"), and substitution of /k/ and /g/ with /t/ and /d/ respectively, noted in both English and Spanish productions (e.g., Spanish "tasa" for "casa"). These error patterns were judged developmentally appropriate in type but delayed in persistence for his age, and were consistent across both languages, again supporting a true articulation/phonological delay rather than a language-specific artifact. Stimulability testing showed Mateo could produce /k/ and /g/ in isolation with moderate cues, and in the initial position of words with maximal cues, suggesting a favorable prognosis for progress with intervention.

Receptive and expressive language: Mateo's receptive vocabulary and ability to follow multi-step directions fell within the below-average to significantly-below-average range in both languages, with somewhat stronger performance in Spanish, consistent with home language dominance. Expressively, Mateo relied heavily on single-word utterances and gestures, with limited use of grammatical morphemes such as plurals, verb tense markers, and pronouns in either language. During a narrative retell task using a wordless picture book, Mateo was able to sequence 3 of 6 key story events with moderate prompting, below age expectations.

Pragmatic/social communication: Mateo demonstrated age-appropriate eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking in play-based interactions, and initiated communication with both the clinician and interpreter without excessive prompting. No concerns regarding social communication, restricted interests, or atypical social reciprocity were noted during today's session; however, given the degree of expressive language delay, pragmatic skills should continue to be monitored as language skills develop.

IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and behavioral observation, Mateo presents with a moderate-to-severe expressive language delay and a mild-to-moderate receptive language delay affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with a primary language impairment rather than a language difference secondary to bilingual exposure alone. This impression is supported by the consistency of delay patterns across both of Mateo's languages, as recommended practice for bilingual assessment, and by the relative strengths noted in his home-dominant language (Spanish) compared to the less-exposed language (English), which argues against a language-difference-only explanation. Mateo additionally presents with a mild speech sound disorder characterized by reduced intelligibility and persistent developmental error patterns beyond expected age of resolution, again consistent across both languages. No concerns regarding hearing, oral-motor structure and function, or social communication were identified at this time, though continued monitoring of pragmatic skills is recommended as expressive language improves. Relevant diagnostic coding for today's visit includes ICD-10 F80.1 (Expressive language disorder), ICD-10 F80.2 (Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder), and ICD-10 F80.0 (Phonological disorder), with CPT 92523 billed for today's combined speech and language evaluation.

Mateo is eligible for early intervention services under North Carolina's Infant-Toddler Program criteria based on the degree of delay documented across multiple standardized measures in both languages, and qualifies for ongoing speech-language therapy services.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo should receive direct speech-language therapy services at a frequency of twice weekly, 30-minute individual sessions, targeting both expressive and receptive language goals as well as articulation/phonological goals, delivered bilingually or with ongoing interpreter support to honor the family's home language.

2. Therapy should incorporate a combination of Hanen-based parent coaching strategies and structured language stimulation approaches to support carryover in the home environment, where Spanish is the dominant language. Cycles approach phonological intervention is recommended to target the persistent error patterns noted above, beginning with /k/ and /g/ in word-initial position given Mateo's demonstrated stimulability with moderate cues.

3. Lucía Rodríguez and Carlos Fernández are encouraged to continue rich language exposure in Spanish at home, as supporting the home language supports overall language development and does not interfere with English acquisition. Continued participation in bilingual community activities, such as the story-time program at the Wake County Public Library and the children's class at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida, is encouraged and may be incorporated into home practice recommendations.

4. Coordination with Little Sprouts Early Learning Center staff, including Ms. Amanda Lopez, is recommended to ensure consistent strategies are used across home and daycare settings, including visual supports and simplified, repeated language models.

5. Referral for a follow-up developmental screening is not indicated at this time given the absence of concerns in motor, social, or adaptive domains; however, if pragmatic or social communication concerns emerge as expressive language improves, re-referral for a broader developmental evaluation should be considered.

6. An IFSP meeting should be scheduled with Wake County CDSA service coordinator Monica Reyes to formalize goals and service frequency. A follow-up IFSP review is scheduled for December 2, 2026 to assess progress toward initial goals, including Outcome 1 (expressive language) and Outcome 2 (speech sound production).

7. Continued monitoring of hearing status is recommended given the history of one prior ear infection; routine audiological screening should be repeated if any new concerns regarding attention, behavior, or speech clarity arise.

8. The family should be connected, if interested, with additional bilingual family support resources through the Southeast Raleigh Family Resource Center, which may offer parent training groups conducted in Spanish.

This evaluation and these recommendations were reviewed with Lucía Rodríguez in Spanish with the assistance of interpreter Beatriz Nuñez at the conclusion of today's session. Lucía voiced understanding of the results and recommendations and expressed interest in beginning services as soon as possible. A written summary in Spanish will be mailed to the family's home address on file within ten business days. Questions may be directed to Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners, PLLC at (919) 555-0188 or to this clinician directly.

Report prepared and electronically signed by Jennifer Hayes, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual service provider, on September 11, 2026.

Employer: Carolina Pines Pediatric Therapy, PLLC
Clinic Address: 4821 Weddington Road, Suite 110, Concord, NC 28027

ICD-10 Code(s): F80.2; F80.0
CPT Code(s) Billed: 92523; 92522
Home Language(s): Spanish (primary), English (secondary)
Interpreter Needed: No — evaluating clinician is bilingual (Spanish/English)

REASON FOR REFERRAL AND BACKGROUND

Teo is a 4;2-year-old boy referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by Patricia Alvarez, his Service Coordinator through the Cabarrus County CDSA. Teo lives with his parents, Diana Vásquez and Jorge Vásquez, his older sister Camila Vásquez (age 8), and his maternal grandmother, Rosa Fuentes, at 118 Ivy Creek Lane, Concord, NC 28025. The family also keeps a dog named Rocky, of whom Teo is very fond and whom he frequently mentions during play-based sampling.

Diana Vásquez reported that she and Jorge Vásquez first noticed Teo's language lagging behind that of his cousins, Isabella Cruz and Diego Cruz (children of Diana Vásquez's sister, Marisol Cruz), around Teo's second birthday. Before relocating to Concord, NC in the fall of 2023, the family lived in Honduras, where Teo received limited monitoring through a community early intervention program, the Programa Comunitario de Intervención Temprana y Apoyo Familiar para Niños con Discapacidades (PCITAFND). Diana Vásquez stated that the family's PCITAFND caseworker had recommended ongoing speech-language monitoring, but services lapsed during the move. After settling in Cabarrus County, the family was connected to the Cabarrus County CDSA at the suggestion of Teo's pediatrician, Dr. Henry Nguyen, who flagged expressive language delay at Teo's 3-year well-child visit.

Current concerns per report from Diana Vásquez and Jorge Vásquez include limited expressive vocabulary in both languages, difficulty being understood by unfamiliar listeners, frequent omission of final consonants, and increasing frustration when he cannot make himself understood. Teo attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy five mornings a week, where his lead teacher, Ms. Patterson, and assistant teacher, Keisha Owens, report that he is well liked by classmates Aiden Walsh and Sofia Martín but often resorts to pointing, pulling peers by the hand, or tantrumming rather than using words to request items during center time. Ms. Patterson noted that Teo recently bit Aiden Walsh during a dispute over a toy truck, which she attributed to communicative frustration rather than aggression.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Teo was born at 38 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery at Atrium Health Carolinas Medical Center on March 3, 2022. Birth weight was 6 lbs 14 oz. Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. Diana Vásquez reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with no maternal illness, substance use, or medication exposure. Teo remained in the well-baby nursery and was discharged home with his mother on March 5, 2022.

Medical history is significant for recurrent acute otitis media beginning around 10 months of age, with documented episodes at 10, 14, and 19 months. Teo underwent bilateral myringotomy with tube placement on November 8, 2023, performed by Dr. Samuel Ortiz, ENT, with resolution of chronic effusion per follow-up audiometric testing. A hearing screening completed at today's evaluation, consisting of otoacoustic emissions bilaterally, yielded results consistent with normal peripheral hearing sensitivity ("pass," bilaterally). No history of seizures, head injury, or hospitalization beyond the tube placement procedure was reported. Teo is not currently prescribed any medications. Vision was reported as unremarkable by Dr. Henry Nguyen at his most recent well-child visit.

Developmental milestones were reported as follows: sat independently at 6 months, walked independently at 13 months, first words emerged around 18 months ("mamá," "no," "agua"), and two-word combinations were not consistently observed until approximately 30 months. Diana Vásquez described this trajectory as notably slower than that of Camila Vásquez, who reportedly combined words by 16 months.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

The home is bilingual, with Spanish used as the predominant language of daily interaction, particularly between Teo and his grandmother, Rosa Fuentes, who resides with the family and provides primary daytime care. Rosa Fuentes speaks Spanish exclusively. Diana Vásquez and Jorge Vásquez are both fluent in Spanish and conversationally proficient in English, and they report code-switching frequently depending on context and listener. Camila Vásquez, who is enrolled in the bilingual immersion strand at her elementary school, is reported to be balanced in both languages and often serves as a language model and informal interpreter for Teo with English-speaking adults.

Diana Vásquez works nights at the Food Lion Distribution Center in Concord as an overnight inventory stocker, typically working from 10:00 PM to 6:00 AM four nights a week. Because of this schedule, Rosa Fuentes manages the bulk of Teo's daytime care and transportation to Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy, while Jorge Vásquez, who works days as a framer for Crescent Builders, handles evening routines. On Tuesday and Thursday evenings, when Jorge Vásquez occasionally works late, a neighbor and family friend, Shay Thompson, babysits Teo and Camila Vásquez from approximately 5:30 PM until 8:00 PM. Shay Thompson speaks only English with the children, and Diana Vásquez noted that Teo tends to use shorter, more telegraphic utterances during this time compared to when he is with Spanish-speaking family members.

Teo sees his cousins, Isabella Cruz and Diego Cruz, most weekends, and family gatherings are reported to occur predominantly in Spanish. Diana Vásquez denied any family history of speech, language, or learning disability beyond an uncle with a reported history of stuttering that resolved in childhood.

EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

Teo has attended Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy since August 2024, currently in the Pre-K 3 classroom under Ms. Patterson and Keisha Owens. The classroom follows an English-dominant curriculum with incidental Spanish support from bilingual staff and peers. Ms. Patterson reports that Teo participates willingly in group routines such as circle time and gross motor play but is frequently unable to answer simple "wh-" questions or follow two-step directions without visual or gestural support. He is described as socially motivated, affectionate with adults, and eager to play alongside Aiden Walsh and Sofia Martín, though interactions are often limited to parallel play rather than reciprocal verbal exchange.

Teo is currently receiving early intervention services under an Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) through the Cabarrus County CDSA, with Outcome 2 addressing expressive communication and Outcome 3 addressing social play skills. The IFSP was most recently reviewed on February 14, 2026, with the next annual review scheduled for February 14, 2027. Speech-language intervention has occurred on a limited consultative basis to date, pending this comprehensive evaluation to determine eligibility for direct weekly services.

SESSION SCHEDULE

Proposed direct intervention sessions, pending authorization, are summarized below:

| Day | Start Time | Stop Time | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 9:00 AM | 9:45 AM | Carolina Pines Pediatric Therapy, PLLC, 4821 Weddington Road, Suite 110, Concord, NC 28027 |
| Wednesday | 3:30 PM | 4:15 PM | Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy, Concord, NC (push-in) |
| Friday | 10:00 AM | 10:45 AM | Home visit, 118 Ivy Creek Lane, Concord, NC 28025 |

Transportation to Monday sessions will be provided by Rosa Fuentes. Wednesday push-in sessions require coordination with Ms. Patterson's classroom schedule. Friday home visits will occur during Rosa Fuentes's supervision window, as Diana Vásquez is typically asleep following her overnight shift at the Food Lion Distribution Center.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

This evaluation was conducted in both English and Spanish across two sessions on May 12, 2026 and May 14, 2026, at the office of Carolina Pines Pediatric Therapy, PLLC. Teo was accompanied by Diana Vásquez on both dates and by Rosa Fuentes on May 14, 2026. All test administration and scoring were completed by Jennifer Boyd, M.S., CCC-SLP, who is bilingual and administered both English and Spanish test forms directly without an interpreter. Procedures included standardized assessment, a hearing screening, oral-motor examination, parent interview, classroom observation, and spontaneous language sampling in both languages during structured play.

Teo separated easily from Diana Vásquez and engaged readily with toys and testing materials. Rapport was established quickly using preferred toys, including a toy dog that Teo spontaneously named after his own pet, Rocky. Attention and engagement were adequate for valid testing across both sessions, with brief breaks offered between subtests. Results below are considered a valid representation of Teo's current communication skills.

TEST RESULTS

| Test / Subtest | Language | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% CI | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) – Auditory Comprehension | English | 71 | 3rd | 65-77 | 2;6-2;9 |
| PLS-5 – Expressive Communication | English | 68 | 2nd | 62-74 | 2;3-2;6 |
| PLS-5 – Total Language Score | English | 67 | 1st | 61-73 | — |
| PLS-5 Spanish – Auditory Comprehension | Spanish | 79 | 8th | 72-86 | 3;0-3;3 |
| PLS-5 Spanish – Expressive Communication | Spanish | 75 | 5th | 68-82 | 2;9-3;0 |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) – Sounds-in-Words | English | 72 | 3rd | 66-78 | — |
| Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) – Morphosyntax | English | — | 6th | — | — |
| BESA – Morphosyntax | Spanish | — | 15th | — | — |
| BESA – Semantics | Spanish | — | 22nd | — | — |

On the GFTA-3, errors in English were predominantly final consonant deletion and stopping of fricatives, consistent with a phonological process disorder rather than isolated articulation errors. Composite intelligibility in connected speech was rated at approximately 60% for familiar listeners and 30-40% for unfamiliar listeners, consistent with parent and teacher report.

SPEECH SOUND AND LANGUAGE SAMPLE OBSERVATIONS

During the English language sample, Teo produced primarily one- and two-word utterances, with mean length of utterance calculated at 1.8 morphemes, below the expected range for his age. Representative productions included omission of final consonants, as in "ca" for "cat" and "do" for "dog," as well as cluster reduction, as in "poon" for "spoon." When shown a picture of a running dog resembling his own pet, Teo exclaimed "Rocky run," omitting the final /n/ in a stimulable but inconsistent production; with moderate cues (modeling plus tactile cue), he approximated "Rocky run[n]" with partial improvement.

In the Spanish sample, utterances were somewhat longer and more grammatically complete, with frequent omission of articles and occasional substitution of /p/ for /f/, as in "pacha" for "flacha" (a toy word used during play). Teo produced the target phrase "más agua" clearly and consistently to request a drink, and he used the possessive construction "mi perro" appropriately when referring to Rocky. He demonstrated use of present-tense verb forms in Spanish more consistently than in English, where verb morphology (third-person -s, past tense -ed) was largely absent.

Oral-motor examination revealed structures within normal limits for strength, symmetry, and range of motion, with no evidence of dysarthria or apraxia-consistent inconsistency across repeated trials of the same target. Diadochokinetic rates were age-appropriate on informal observation. Stimulability was good across most error sounds, with improvement to mild cues for /k/ in final position and min cues for /s/ clusters in initial position.

Pragmatic skills were judged adequate for structured interaction but limited in spontaneous peer-directed communication, consistent with teacher report regarding interactions with Aiden Walsh and Sofia Martín. Teo used eye contact, turn-taking, and joint attention appropriately with the examiner and showed emerging use of gesture plus single words to repair communication breakdowns when a listener indicated non-comprehension.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Results of this bilingual evaluation indicate that Teo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both English and Spanish, with relatively stronger skills in Spanish, his primary home language, consistent with typical patterns of bilingual language dominance rather than a language-specific deficit. Scores on the PLS-5 and PLS-5 Spanish fell in the low range in both languages, with Spanish scores falling closer to, though still below, average limits. Performance on the BESA further supports deficits across both languages in morphosyntax, with somewhat stronger semantic skills in Spanish. These cross-linguistic patterns are consistent with a true language disorder rather than second-language acquisition alone, as a disorder affecting only one language, or stronger performance in the child's less-dominant language, would instead suggest typical bilingual development.

Teo also presents with a speech sound disorder characterized by phonological process errors (final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, stopping) that are present, though to differing degrees, across both languages, further supporting a disorder affecting underlying phonological systems rather than dialectal or second-language transfer alone. Given his history of recurrent otitis media with effusion and tube placement, a component of his speech-language delay may be attributable in part to a history of fluctuating conductive hearing loss during a critical developmental window, though current hearing is within normal limits.

Teo's strong social motivation, good stimulability, and relatively intact pragmatic foundation are favorable prognostic indicators. His family's engagement, bilingual home environment, and existing relationship with the Cabarrus County CDSA provide a strong foundation for intervention. Continued support for both languages is recommended, as bilingualism is not contributing to, and should not be discontinued as a strategy for addressing, his language disorder.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Teo qualifies for direct speech-language intervention services under his IFSP based on standardized testing falling more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean in both languages assessed.

2. Direct speech-language therapy is recommended twice weekly for 45-minute sessions, targeting expressive and receptive language goals (IFSP Outcome 2) and speech sound production in both English and Spanish, per the schedule outlined above, delivered by Jennifer Boyd, M.S., CCC-SLP, or another qualified bilingual clinician at Carolina Pines Pediatric Therapy, PLLC.

3. A phonological approach such as the Cycles approach is recommended to target final consonant deletion and cluster reduction across both languages, given the cross-linguistic nature of Teo's phonological errors.

4. Parent coaching using Hanen-based strategies (for example, "OWL" — observe, wait, listen) is recommended for Diana Vásquez, Jorge Vásquez, and Rosa Fuentes to support language modeling across both languages during daily routines, given Rosa Fuentes's central caregiving role.

5. Continued exposure to and use of Spanish at home should be maintained and supported, not reduced, as Spanish is Teo's stronger and more developmentally advanced language at this time.

6. Classroom-based support at Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy is recommended, including visual schedules, modeling of two-word combinations, and pre-teaching of vocabulary, in coordination with Ms. Patterson and Keisha Owens.

7. Referral for occupational therapy evaluation is recommended to rule out contributing fine motor or sensory regulation factors related to behavioral frustration; Megan Shields, OTR/L, has been consulted and can accommodate evaluation within the next four weeks.

8. Repeat audiological monitoring is recommended given Teo's history of recurrent otitis media, to be coordinated through Dr. Henry Nguyen's office.

9. Re-evaluation of standardized scores is recommended in approximately six months, or at the next IFSP annual review on February 14, 2027, to monitor progress in both languages and determine continued eligibility.

10. The family should continue coordination with Patricia Alvarez at the Cabarrus County CDSA regarding service authorization and any applicable records transfer from the family's prior involvement with PCITAFND in Honduras, if such records can be obtained.

This report and its recommendations were discussed with Diana Vásquez in Spanish at the conclusion of the May 14, 2026 session, and she verbalized agreement with the proposed plan of care.

Respectfully submitted,

PIEDMONT SPEECH AND LANGUAGE SERVICES, PLLC
4420 Falls of Neuse Road, Suite 210, Raleigh, NC 27609
Telefono: 919-555-0147 Fax: 919-555-0148

INFORME DE EVALUACION DE HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Fecha de evaluacion: 15 de agosto de 2026
Nino: Mateo Alejandro Castillo Ramirez (tambien llamado Teo por la familia)
Fecha de nacimiento: 20 de octubre de 2023
Edad cronologica al momento de la evaluacion: 2;10
Numero de expediente: LD-20264471
Numero de Medicaid: 887234561B
Madre: Lucia Castillo Ramirez
Padre: Jorge Castillo Mendez
Direccion de la familia: 118 Pinewood Circle, Zebulon, NC 27597
Telefono de contacto: 919-555-0193
Evaluadora: Maria Elena Vasquez, M.S., CCC-SLP, de Piedmont Speech and Language Services, PLLC
Interprete: no se necesito; la evaluadora es bilingue en ingles y espanol
Fuente de referencia: Dra. J. Ortiz, pediatra, y la coordinadora de servicios M.R. de la Agencia de Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Wake

RAZON DE LA REFERENCIA

Mateo fue referido para una evaluacion de habla y lenguaje por preocupacion sobre su desarrollo de lenguaje expresivo y su claridad al hablar. Sus padres, Lucia y Jorge, reportan que Mateo usa pocas palabras comparado con otros ninos de su edad y que muchas veces es dificil entender lo que dice, incluso para la familia. La pediatra, Dra. J. Ortiz, noto el retraso durante la cita de los 2 anos y envio la referencia a la Agencia de Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Wake para servicios de intervencion temprana. La familia tambien asiste al grupo de juego bilingue del Centro Comunitario Nueva Esperanza, donde la maestra del grupo, Sra. Karen Lopez, tambien expreso preocupacion sobre el lenguaje de Mateo.

HISTORIA DE NACIMIENTO Y MEDICA

Mateo nacio a las 37 semanas de gestacion, por via vaginal, en el Hospital Regional Piedmont el 20 de octubre de 2023. El peso al nacer fue de 2.9 kg (6 lb 6 oz) y los puntajes de Apgar fueron 8 y 9. La madre reporta un embarazo sin complicaciones mayores, aunque tuvo presion alta leve en el tercer trimestre que fue monitoreada por su obstetra. Mateo paso dos dias en la unidad de cuidado especial por dificultad leve para alimentarse, pero fue dado de alta con su madre sin necesidad de oxigeno suplementario.

La historia medica es generalmente sin eventos significativos. Mateo tuvo tres infecciones de oido entre los 12 y 24 meses, tratadas con antibioticos; la ultima prueba de audicion, realizada en la oficina de la Dra. J. Ortiz el 3 de junio de 2026, mostro audicion dentro de limites normales en ambos oidos. No hay historia de convulsiones, hospitalizaciones mayores, ni cirugias. La familia niega antecedentes de autismo o sindromes geneticos conocidos. El desarrollo motor grueso y fino se reporta como tipico: camino solo a los 13 meses y usa una cuchara sin ayuda desde los 20 meses.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

Mateo vive con sus padres, Lucia y Jorge, su hermana mayor Sol Castillo Ramirez, de 7 anos, y su hermano Diego Castillo Ramirez, de 5 anos. La abuela materna, Carmen Ramirez, vive con la familia y cuida a los ninos mientras los padres trabajan. Jorge trabaja en Castillo Brothers Construction Company, donde hace trabajo de enmarcado y techado; en una nota anterior de servicios tambien aparece descrito como empleado de la compania de construccion Castillo Brothers. Lucia trabaja en Carolina Clean Cleaning Service limpiando oficinas por las noches, y los registros de la agencia tambien la mencionan como empleada del servicio de limpieza Carolina Clean. Antes de ese trabajo, Lucia trabajo brevemente en Restaurante El Compadre como cocinera.

En el hogar se habla principalmente espanol, aunque Sol y Diego ya hablan ingles en la escuela y a veces lo mezclan en casa. Lucia reporta que ella habla con Mateo mayormente en espanol, mientras que Jorge alterna entre los dos idiomas. La familia asiste regularmente a la Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida, donde Mateo participa en la clase de ninos los domingos. La familia tambien usa el programa de alfabetizacion bilingue de la Biblioteca Publica del Condado de Wake, al cual asisten los sabados por la manana.

Sol, la hermana mayor, tiene un desarrollo de lenguaje tipico segun el reporte de la maestra de kinder, Sra. Monica Fields, de Zebulon Elementary School. Mateo asiste tres dias por semana a Little Sprouts Early Learning Daycare, donde su maestra principal, Sra. Ashley Byrd, reporta que el usa gestos y sonidos para comunicarse pero muy pocas palabras claras. En el daycare, Mateo juega frecuentemente con otro nino llamado Kevin, y las maestras notan que Mateo se frustra cuando Kevin no entiende lo que quiere decir.

OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES

Durante la sesion de evaluacion, realizada el 15 de agosto de 2026 de 10:00 a.m. a 11:15 a.m. en la oficina de Piedmont Speech and Language Services, PLLC, Mateo se mostro inicialmente timido pero se calento rapido al ambiente. Se involucro en juego funcional con juguetes y mostro buena atencion compartida con la evaluadora. Uso gestos como senalar y mostrar objetos de manera consistente. Su inteligibilidad para oyentes desconocidos se estimo en aproximadamente 30%, mejorando a cerca de 60% cuando el contexto era conocido por el oyente.

Mateo produjo principalmente palabras de una silaba y algunas combinaciones de dos palabras, como "mas agua" y "no quiero". Mostro varios patrones fonologicos tipicos de su edad, incluyendo reduccion de grupos consonanticos y omision de consonantes finales. Al intentar producir la palabra blanco "sol", Mateo dijo "ol", omitiendo el fonema inicial /s/. Tambien produjo "tasa" para la palabra blanco "taza", sustituyendo /s/ por /θ/... en realidad sustituyo /θ/ con [s]. Con claves mod cues visuales y tactiles, logro aproximar el sonido /k/ en la palabra "casa" tres de cinco veces (3 de 5).

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS

Se administraron las siguientes pruebas estandarizadas, con participacion activa de los padres cuando fue apropiado:

1. Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale
2. Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
3. Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-III), subprueba de Comunicacion
4. Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition (PPVT-5)
5. Muestra de lenguaje espontaneo en espanol e ingles (observacion informal, no estandarizada)

Tabla de resultados:

Prueba / Subprueba | Puntaje estandar | Percentil | Edad equivalente
Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale - Interaccion y Apego | No aplica (descriptivo) | -- | dentro de limites esperados para la edad
Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale - Pragmatica | No aplica (descriptivo) | -- | 18-24 meses
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 - Sonidos en Palabras | 73 | 4to percentil | 1;8-2;0
Bayley-III - Comunicacion Expresiva | 70 | 2do percentil | 16-18 meses
Bayley-III - Comunicacion Receptiva | 82 | 12vo percentil | 22-24 meses
Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5 | 79 | 8vo percentil | 2;2-2;4

Los puntajes estandar tienen una media de 100 y una desviacion estandar de 15. Los puntajes de Mateo en articulacion y lenguaje expresivo cayeron consistentemente por debajo del rango esperado (85-115), mientras que su comprension receptiva, aunque tambien baja, se acerco mas al rango bajo-promedio.

En la muestra de lenguaje espontaneo, Mateo produjo un promedio de 1.4 palabras por enunciado, con un inventario fonetico limitado a aproximadamente 12 consonantes diferentes. Se observaron los siguientes procesos fonologicos de manera consistente: reduccion de grupos consonanticos (8/10 oportunidades), omision de consonante final (7/10), y frontalizacion velar en palabras como "gato" producida como "dato". Durante la tarea de imitacion directa, logro producir el fonema /p/ correctamente en posicion inicial en 9 de 10 intentos, pero el fonema /g/ solo en 2 de 10 intentos, incluso con claves max cues.

IMPRESIONES CLINICAS

Basado en los resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas, la observacion clinica y el reporte de los padres y maestras, Mateo presenta un retraso significativo en el desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo y un trastorno fonologico/articulatorio, con comprension receptiva relativamente mas fuerte pero tambien por debajo de lo esperado para su edad. Sus patrones fonologicos, incluyendo reduccion de grupos consonanticos y frontalizacion velar, son consistentes con un retraso fonologico mas que con una apraxia de habla infantil, aunque se recomienda monitoreo continuo dado lo limitado del inventario fonetico.

Es importante notar que el bilinguismo de Mateo (espanol predominante en casa, exposicion creciente al ingles en el daycare) no explica por si solo el patron observado, ya que sus dificultades se presentan de manera similar en ambos idiomas y son mas marcadas que lo tipico para ninos bilingues de su edad. El perfil es consistente con un trastorno de lenguaje expresivo combinado con un retraso fonologico, segun los criterios descritos en el DSM-5 y codificado bajo ICD-10 F80.1 (trastorno del lenguaje expresivo) y ICD-10 F80.0 (trastorno fonologico).

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda terapia de habla y lenguaje individual, dos veces por semana, con enfoque en vocabulario expresivo, estructura de oraciones y claridad articulatoria, usando un modelo de tratamiento bilingue.
2. Se recomienda el uso del enfoque Hanen con los padres para fomentar oportunidades de comunicacion en el hogar durante actividades diarias.
3. Se recomienda incorporar elementos del enfoque PROMPT para apoyar la produccion motora de los sonidos del habla, dado el patron de errores observado.
4. Si el progreso en articulacion es lento, se recomienda considerar el enfoque de Cycles para el tratamiento fonologico.
5. Se recomienda continuar la evaluacion de audicion de manera periodica dada la historia de infecciones de oido.
6. Se recomienda que la familia continue usando espanol en casa; el bilinguismo no debe ser desalentado y no es la causa del retraso observado.
7. Se recomienda coordinar servicios con la Agencia de Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Wake para asegurar que la terapia se incluya en el proximo IFSP, Resultado 2, relacionado con comunicacion funcional.
8. Se recomienda compartir este informe con Little Sprouts Early Learning Daycare y con la pediatra, Dra. J. Ortiz, para apoyar la continuidad de cuidado.
9. Se recomienda una reevaluacion en 6 meses para medir progreso y ajustar el plan de tratamiento segun sea necesario.

Agradezco a la familia Castillo Ramirez por su participacion activa y disposicion durante esta evaluacion. Quedo disponible para cualquier pregunta adicional.

Atentamente,

Maria Elena Vasquez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Patologa del Habla y Lenguaje Bilingue
Piedmont Speech and Language Services, PLLC
