Carolina Pediatric Health System – Departamento de Patología del Habla y Lenguaje, Campus Durham
4520 Avenida Erwin, Durham, 27705
Teléfono: (919) 555-2847 | Correo electrónico: habla.durham@carolinapediatrichealth.org | Sitio web: www.carolinapediatrichealth.org/habla

12 de agosto de 2026

Nombre del niño: Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez ("Teo")
Fecha de nacimiento: 3 de febrero de 2022 (edad cronológica actual: 4;6)
Número de expediente: CPH-204471
Número de Medicaid: 987654321A
Padres: Lucía Rodríguez Paredes y Jesús Flores Delgado ("Chuy")
Clínica evaluadora: Marisol Vega, M.S., CCC-SLP
Fechas de la evaluación: 5 de agosto de 2026 y 7 de agosto de 2026
Referido por: Dr. Hernán Soto, WakeMed Pediatrics – Campus Cary

Estimada señora Rodríguez Paredes y señor Flores Delgado:

Gracias por traer a Teo a su evaluación de habla y lenguaje. Fue un placer conocer a su hijo y conversar con ustedes sobre su desarrollo. En esta carta les explico, en palabras sencillas, lo que observamos durante las dos citas, lo que significan los resultados de las pruebas y qué recomendamos para ayudar a Teo a seguir avanzando.

ANTECEDENTES Y MOTIVO DE LA REFERENCIA

Mateo, a quien toda la familia llama "Teo", fue referido para esta evaluación por el Dr. Hernán Soto, pediatra en WakeMed Pediatrics – Campus Cary, después de notar en su revisión de los 4 años que Teo todavía no decía oraciones completas y que muchas de sus palabras eran difíciles de entender para personas fuera de la familia. La maestra de Teo en el centro infantil Little Learners Daycare, la señora Carmen Castañeda, también había comentado a la familia que Teo se frustraba cuando sus compañeros no le entendían, y que a veces dejaba de intentar comunicarse y se alejaba del grupo de juego.

La señora Rodríguez Paredes reportó que en casa Teo habla sobre todo en español, pero que en el centro infantil escucha principalmente inglés. Agregó que Teo entiende bien instrucciones simples en ambos idiomas, pero que su habla expresiva es limitada en los dos. El señor Flores Delgado mencionó que su propia niñez incluyó retrasos de habla, y que un hermano de él recibió terapia de lenguaje cuando era pequeño.

Antes de esta cita, la familia fue conectada con el Little Learners Program de intervención temprana del condado de Durham, a través de la coordinadora de servicios Diana Castillo. La señora Castillo completó una visita inicial en el hogar de la familia el 14 de junio de 2026 y recomendó una evaluación formal de habla y lenguaje antes de escribir el Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP).

HISTORIA DE NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA

Según el reporte de la señora Rodríguez Paredes, el embarazo de Teo fue complicado por presión arterial alta en el tercer trimestre. Teo nació en WakeMed Health & Hospitals, Unidad de Neonatología – Campus Raleigh a las 34 semanas de gestación, con un peso al nacer de 4 libras, 2 onzas y puntuaciones de Apgar de 7 al minuto y 9 a los cinco minutos. Pasó 11 días en la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales por dificultad respiratoria leve y para ganar peso antes de ser dado de alta.

La familia reportó que Teo tuvo tres episodios de infección del oído medio entre los 8 meses y los 2 años de edad, tratados con antibióticos por su pediatra. Fue evaluado por audiología en WakeMed Ear, Nose and Throat & Audiology – Campus Cary el 9 de enero de 2025, donde se le colocaron tubos de ventilación bilaterales (timpanostomía) después de documentarse líquido persistente en ambos oídos. Desde ese procedimiento, la familia no ha notado más infecciones ni problemas de audición evidentes. Una audiometría de seguimiento realizada en la misma práctica el 3 de marzo de 2025 mostró audición dentro de límites normales en ambos oídos.

No hay otra historia médica significativa. Teo no toma medicamentos de manera regular, no tiene alergias conocidas, y su desarrollo motor (sentarse, caminar) ocurrió dentro de rangos esperados, aunque un poco tarde según el recuerdo de la familia: caminó de manera independiente alrededor de los 16 meses.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR, SOCIAL Y DE LENGUAJE

Teo vive con sus padres, Lucía Rodríguez Paredes y Jesús Flores Delgado ("Chuy"), y sus dos hermanos: José Flores Rodríguez ("Pepe"), de 7 años, y Valentina Flores Rodríguez, de 2 años. La familia reside en 118 Calle Roble, Durham, 27703. La abuela paterna, Guadalupe Delgado Núñez ("Lupita"), vive a pocas cuadras y cuida a los niños varias tardes por semana mientras los padres trabajan.

El señor Flores Delgado trabaja en construcción para Carolina Concrete & Masonry, y la señora Rodríguez Paredes trabaja medio tiempo como auxiliar de cuidado en el hogar para Triangle Home Health Services. Ambos describieron el ambiente del hogar como principalmente hispanohablante: se habla español con los padres y con Lupita, mientras que Pepe alterna entre español e inglés, sobre todo cuando habla de la escuela.

La familia reportó que Teo dijo sus primeras palabras alrededor de los 18 meses, más tarde que sus hermanos. Comenzó a combinar dos palabras cerca de los 3 años, también más tarde de lo esperado. Actualmente, según la señora Rodríguez Paredes, Teo usa principalmente frases de dos y tres palabras ("quiero agua", "no mío", "Pepe jugar"), y rara vez produce oraciones completas. Su vocabulario incluye palabras familiares para comida, juguetes y personas de su entorno, pero la familia nota que Teo a veces usa gestos o jala la ropa de un adulto en lugar de hablar cuando se frustra.

En el centro infantil Little Learners Daycare, Teo asiste al salón de preescolar cinco días a la semana. Su maestra principal es la señora Carmen Castañeda, asistida por la señora Brenda Ocampo. La señora Castañeda reportó, en una nota compartida con la familia, que Teo juega sobre todo con un amigo, Juan Martínez ("Juanito"), y que ambos niños disfrutan construir torres de bloques juntos, aunque Teo habla muy poco durante el juego comparado con Juanito. En casa, Teo también disfruta jugar con el perro de la familia, Rocky, y suele imitar sonidos de animales con más facilidad que palabras completas.

COMPORTAMIENTO DURANTE LA EVALUACIÓN

Teo asistió a ambas citas acompañado por su madre, la señora Rodríguez Paredes. Se mostró tímido al inicio de la primera sesión, el 5 de agosto de 2026, pero se relajó después de los primeros 10 minutos de juego libre con bloques y figuras de animales. Participó de manera cooperativa en la mayoría de las tareas, aunque mostró mayor dificultad para mantener la atención durante actividades de lenguaje expresivo estructurado, requiriendo descansos breves y claves mod cues (claves moderadas) para completar varios ítems.

Durante la segunda sesión, el 7 de agosto de 2026, se realizó la evaluación de los sonidos del habla. Teo cooperó bien con tareas de imitación y nombramiento, aunque en ocasiones repitió la pregunta en lugar de responder directamente, una estrategia común en niños con lenguaje expresivo limitado.

Ninguna de las dos sesiones requirió interpretación formal, ya que la evaluadora, la señora Vega, es bilingüe certificada en español e inglés. Sin embargo, una colega, la intérprete Rosa Jiménez, estuvo disponible por teléfono durante parte de la primera cita para aclarar algunas preguntas de la entrevista familiar sobre terminología médica específica.

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS

Se administraron las siguientes pruebas estandarizadas, con instrucciones y estímulos presentados en español, el idioma principal del hogar:

| Prueba | Área evaluada | Puntuación estándar | Percentil | Rango de confianza |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), versión en español – Comprensión Auditiva | Lenguaje receptivo | 78 | 7mo | 73-83 |
| PLS-5 – Comunicación Expresiva | Lenguaje expresivo | 69 | 2do | 64-74 |
| PLS-5 – Puntuación Total de Lenguaje | Lenguaje general | 72 | 3ro | 67-77 |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) | Articulación | 65 | 1ro | 58-72 |
| Receptive-Expressive Emergent Language Test-4 (REEL-4), reporte de los padres | Lenguaje emergente | Edad equivalente: 2;6–3;0 | — | — |

En la escala PLS-5, Teo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 78 en Comprensión Auditiva, lo cual lo ubica en el rango bajo-promedio, cerca del límite de retraso significativo. Esto significa que Teo entiende la mayoría de instrucciones de un paso y muchas instrucciones de dos pasos, pero tiene dificultad con conceptos más abstractos (tiempo, cantidad, causa y efecto) esperados para su edad.

En Comunicación Expresiva, obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 69, en el percentil 2do, lo cual representa un retraso significativo. Durante la prueba, Teo nombró correctamente 8 de 10 (80%) objetos comunes mostrados en láminas, pero tuvo mucha mayor dificultad para formular oraciones completas, describir acciones en secuencia, o usar marcadores gramaticales como plurales y tiempos verbales de manera consistente.

En el GFTA-3, Teo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 65, percentil 1ro, lo cual indica un retraso significativo en el desarrollo de los sonidos del habla para su edad. Produjo correctamente sonidos tempranos como /m/, /p/, /n/ y /b/ en todas las posiciones de palabra, pero mostró patrones consistentes de simplificación en sonidos más tardíos.

RESULTADOS DE LA EVALUACIÓN DE ARTICULACIÓN Y FONOLOGÍA

Se observaron los siguientes patrones durante la evaluación de habla:

Sustitución de /k/ por [t]: Teo dijo "tasa" por "casa" y "teso" por "queso", sustituyendo consistentemente el sonido /k/ por [t] en posición inicial de palabra.

Omisión de /s/ final: en palabras como "más" y "dos", Teo omitió el sonido /s/ final, produciendo "má" y "do".

Sustitución de /ɾ/ por [l]: Teo produjo "pelo" por "pero" y "calo" por "carro", sustituyendo el sonido vibrante /ɾ/ por [l].

Simplificación de grupos consonánticos: en palabras con grupos como "pl" o "fl", por ejemplo "plato", Teo omitió la segunda consonante, produciendo "pato".

Estos patrones son consistentes con procesos fonológicos que, a esta edad, se esperaría que Teo estuviera resolviendo. Su inteligibilidad general se estimó en aproximadamente 50% para oyentes desconocidos y 70% para oyentes familiares, usando muestras de habla espontánea durante el juego.

En cuanto a comprensión auditiva en inglés, se administró una breve muestra informal (no estandarizada) de vocabulario en inglés usado en el centro infantil. Teo identificó correctamente 6 de 10 palabras comunes en inglés ("ball", "dog", "more", "up"), sugiriendo exposición limitada pero presente al idioma, consistente con un desarrollo bilingüe emergente típico para su situación de exposición al lenguaje.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Basado en la historia reportada por la familia, las observaciones clínicas directas, y los resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas administradas en español (el idioma dominante del hogar), Teo presenta un retraso significativo en el desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo, un retraso leve a moderado en el lenguaje receptivo, y un retraso significativo en el desarrollo de los sonidos del habla (articulación/fonología).

Es importante notar que estos resultados reflejan el desempeño de Teo en su idioma más fuerte, el español, y por lo tanto representan verdaderas áreas de necesidad y no simplemente una diferencia esperada asociada al bilingüismo. Los patrones de habla observados (sustituciones y omisiones consistentes de sonidos) y la limitación en la longitud y complejidad de las oraciones aparecen tanto en español como, de manera informal, en inglés, lo cual apoya la conclusión de un trastorno del lenguaje y del habla más que una diferencia típica de desarrollo bilingüe.

Estos hallazgos son consistentes con un diagnóstico de Trastorno del Desarrollo del Habla, con Fonología Predominante (F80.2), según los criterios de la Clasificación Internacional de Enfermedades, 10ma edición. Este código se usará para fines de documentación clínica y de facturación de los servicios recomendados a continuación.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Recomendamos que Teo reciba terapia de habla y lenguaje individual, idealmente dos veces por semana, con sesiones de aproximadamente 30 minutos cada una, usando los códigos de procedimiento 92507 (tratamiento individual de habla, lenguaje, voz) con posible uso adicional del código 92523 (evaluación de habla y lenguaje) en futuras re-evaluaciones. Los servicios deben enfocarse en:
   - Aumentar la longitud y complejidad de las oraciones en español, el idioma del hogar, usando estrategias como modelado, expansión y preguntas abiertas.
   - Abordar los patrones fonológicos identificados (sustitución de /k/, omisión de /s/ final, sustitución de /ɾ/, simplificación de grupos consonánticos) usando un enfoque de Ciclos (Cycles) adaptado al inventario fonológico del español.
   - Apoyar el desarrollo bilingüe de manera intencional, reforzando ambos idiomas en lugar de eliminar uno, ya que la investigación muestra que el bilingüismo no causa ni empeora los trastornos del lenguaje.

2. Recomendamos continuar la conexión con el Little Learners Program de intervención temprana para completar el proceso de IFSP, incluyendo metas específicas de comunicación. La coordinadora de servicios, Diana Castillo, puede ayudar a coordinar la terapia de habla con otros servicios que la familia esté considerando.

3. Sugerimos que la familia continúe comunicándose con la señora Castañeda en Little Learners Daycare para compartir estrategias simples que apoyen la comunicación de Teo durante el juego con compañeros como Juanito, por ejemplo, dar tiempo extra para que Teo responda antes de completar la oración por él.

4. Recomendamos que la familia continúe hablando español en casa con Teo, incluyendo con Lupita cuando ella lo cuida, ya que un hogar lingüísticamente rico en el idioma dominante apoya tanto el español como, eventualmente, el aprendizaje más fuerte del inglés.

5. Sugerimos una re-evaluación de audiología de rutina en aproximadamente 12 meses, dado el historial de infecciones de oído y tubos de ventilación, para confirmar que la audición se mantiene dentro de límites normales. Esta cita puede programarse directamente con WakeMed Ear, Nose and Throat & Audiology – Campus Cary.

6. Recomendamos compartir esta evaluación con el Dr. Soto en la próxima cita de rutina de Teo, para que el equipo médico tenga un registro completo de los servicios recomendados.

Con el apoyo adecuado, esperamos que Teo continúe progresando en su comunicación, tanto en español como en inglés, y que gane más confianza para jugar e interactuar con sus hermanos Pepe y Valentina, con su amigo Juanito, y con el resto de su familia.

Estamos disponibles para responder cualquier pregunta sobre esta evaluación o sobre los próximos pasos. Pueden comunicarse con nuestra oficina al (919) 555-2847 o por correo electrónico a habla.durham@carolinapediatrichealth.org. También pueden encontrar información general sobre nuestros servicios de habla y lenguaje en www.carolinapediatrichealth.org/habla.

Gracias por permitirnos ser parte del cuidado de Teo. Fue un gusto conocer a un niño tan curioso y cariñoso, y esperamos poder apoyar su crecimiento en los próximos meses.

Con cariño y respeto,

Marisol Vega, M.S., CCC-SLP
Patóloga del Habla y Lenguaje
Carolina Pediatric Health System – Departamento de Patología del Habla y Lenguaje, Campus Durham

Jennifer Harmon, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual clinician with Bright Path Speech & Language Services, conducted a 45-minute direct therapy session at 3:30 PM on October 9, 2026. Mateo attends Little Learners Daycare in Ms. Lopez's room on weekday mornings, then transitions to Little Learners Program in the afternoon for extended-day care. **Background and Referral**

Sofía is a 4;7-year-old girl who was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by her pediatrician, Dr. Anil Patel, following a well-child visit on August 3, 2026 at which her mother, Carla Beltrán-Soto, expressed concern about Sofía's limited vocabulary and difficulty being understood by unfamiliar listeners in both English and Spanish. Sofía was also referred internally through Piedmont CDSA after a routine developmental screening flagged delays in expressive language and articulation. The family's service coordinator, Patricia Nguyen, coordinated the referral and has remained the point of contact for IFSP-related scheduling.

Sofía currently attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center four days a week, where her teacher, Ms. Lopez, reports that Sofía is social but often gestures or points rather than using words to communicate her needs, and that other children in Ms. Lopez's room sometimes finish her sentences for her. Sofía has a close friend at daycare, Emma, with whom she plays during free choice time, though Ms. Lopez notes that Sofía tends to follow Emma's lead rather than initiate play verbally.

**Birth and Medical History**

Sofía was born at 38 weeks gestation at Piedmont Triad Regional Hospital via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. Carla Beltrán-Soto reported no complications during pregnancy, though she noted mild gestational hypertension managed without medication. Sofía was discharged home on day two of life and has met gross motor milestones within expected limits (sat independently at 6 months, walked at 13 months).

Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media, with four documented episodes between 18 and 30 months of age, two of which were treated with amoxicillin and two with azithromycin following allergic reaction concerns. Sofía underwent bilateral myringotomy with tube placement on June 4, 2024 at Piedmont Triad Regional Hospital, performed by Dr. Marcus Whitfield, ENT. Tubes extruded naturally by age three with no further infections reported. Hearing was last screened on July 22, 2026 and results were within normal limits bilaterally. Vision screening was also unremarkable. There is no reported history of seizure, head injury, or significant illness requiring hospitalization beyond the tube placement. Current ICD-10 diagnosis under consideration is F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder); today's visit was billed under CPT 92523.

**Family and Language History**

Sofía lives with her mother, Carla Beltrán-Soto; her father, Luis del Río; and her older sister, Camila del Río, age 7, who is reportedly a strong talker in both languages and sometimes speaks for Sofía at home. Carla Beltrán-Soto works days in the cut-and-sew department at Carolina Furniture Works and works three overnight shifts per week as a CNA, a second job she took on last year to help cover household expenses. Luis del Río works in residential construction and is often away from early morning until evening. Given both parents' demanding schedules, Sofía's paternal grandmother, Rosa Beltrán, provides afternoon and evening childcare several days a week and reports that Sofía primarily uses Spanish with her, though she understands simple English directions.

The household is bilingual, with Spanish spoken predominantly by Luis del Río and Rosa Beltrán, and a mix of English and Spanish spoken by Carla Beltrán-Soto, who was raised in Winston-Salem in a bilingual home herself. Carla Beltrán-Soto reported that Sofía's first words emerged around 22 months, later than her sister's first words at roughly 12 months. Early intervention services through Early Head Start began at age two following a referral from the family's WIC nutritionist, who noted feeding and language concerns during a routine visit. The family has also received support connecting to resources through Guilford County Smart Start and has an open case with Guilford County DSS related to a prior housing assistance application; Carla Beltrán-Soto noted this has sometimes created scheduling conflicts with therapy appointments.

The family's apartment complex manager, Mr. Dale Thompson, was mentioned by Carla Beltrán-Soto as having commented that Sofía seems "quieter than other kids her age" in the shared courtyard, which the mother found validating of her own concerns. The family's dog, Luna, is a frequent subject of Sofía's gestures and vocalizations at home; Carla Beltrán-Soto reported that Sofía will point at the back door and say "Luna fuera" when she wants the dog let outside, one of her more consistent two-word combinations.

**Assessment Procedures**

Testing was conducted across two sessions in the home setting, with portions administered in English and portions in Spanish per standardized bilingual protocols, using parallel forms where available. Sofía separated easily from her mother during both sessions and engaged readily with toys and picture materials. Rapport was established quickly, and behavior during testing was judged to be representative of her typical functioning, per parent report.

**Standardized Test Results**

| Test/Subtest | Date | Score Type | Score | Percentile | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | 09/15/2026 | Standard Score | 79 | 8th | 73-85 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication | 09/15/2026 | Standard Score | 76 | 5th | 70-82 |
| PLS-5 Total Language Score | 09/15/2026 | Standard Score | 76 | 5th | 71-81 |
| CELF-5 Preschool-2 Sentence Structure | 09/22/2026 | Scaled Score | 7 | 16th | 5-9 |
| CELF-5 Preschool-2 Word Structure | 09/22/2026 | Scaled Score | 6 | 9th | 4-8 |
| Goldman-Fristoe 3 Sounds-in-Words | 09/22/2026 | Standard Score | 70 | 2nd | 64-76 |

Age equivalents derived from the PLS-5 fell between 2;6–3;0 for both receptive and expressive domains, reflecting a gap of approximately 18-24 months relative to chronological age.

**Auditory Comprehension / Receptive Language**

On the PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension subtest, Sofía followed 2-step directions inconsistently (3 of 5 trials) and demonstrated understanding of basic spatial concepts (in, on, under) but struggled with more complex concepts such as "behind" and "between." She identified 8/10 common objects by function in Spanish but only 6/10 in English, suggesting somewhat stronger receptive skills in her home language. She demonstrated emerging understanding of early wh-questions ("what" and "where") but inconsistent responses to "why" and "how" questions across both languages.

**Expressive Language**

Expressively, Sofía's utterances were primarily 1-2 word combinations, with occasional 3-word utterances noted during play-based sampling (e.g., "mamá no aquí"). Mean length of utterance was calculated at 1.8 morphemes in Spanish and 1.4 morphemes in English, both well below expectations for her age. She used a limited range of grammatical morphemes, omitting plural markers and verb tense markers in both languages. During a structured naming task, Sofía labeled 9/20 pictured items correctly across both languages combined, frequently substituting gestures or approximations (e.g., pointing and saying "eso" for unfamiliar items).

**Speech Sound Production**

Articulation testing via the Goldman-Fristoe 3 revealed multiple sound errors affecting intelligibility, including final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and fronting of velars. Sofía produced "tat" for the target word "cat" and "poon" for "spoon," consistent with cluster reduction and stopping patterns typical of younger children. She demonstrated stimulability for /k/ in isolation with mod cues but was unable to produce it consistently in words. The phoneme /ɾ/, present in Spanish words such as "pero," was inconsistently produced, sometimes realized as [d]. Overall intelligibility in connected speech was estimated at approximately 40% to unfamiliar listeners and 65% to familiar listeners, per both clinician judgment and parent report.

**Oral Mechanism and Social Communication**

Oral mechanism examination was within normal limits for structure and function, with adequate range of motion for speech production. No signs of dysarthria or apraxia were observed, though a mild oral-motor coordination weakness was noted and will continue to be monitored. Socially, Sofía demonstrated appropriate eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking during play, and she used gestures and vocalizations purposefully to communicate wants and needs, suggesting pragmatic skills are a relative strength.

**Impressions**

Results of this evaluation indicate a moderate mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both English and Spanish, consistent with a primary language impairment rather than a language difference attributable solely to bilingual exposure, given that delays are present across both languages relative to same-age bilingual peers. Sofía also presents with a moderate speech sound disorder characterized by multiple phonological process errors that significantly reduce intelligibility, particularly to unfamiliar listeners such as classroom staff at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center. Her history of recurrent otitis media is a likely contributing factor to early language delay, though current hearing status is within normal limits and should not be considered an active barrier to progress.

Sofía's relative strengths in social communication, joint attention, and nonverbal communication are encouraging prognostic indicators. Her family's strong engagement, bilingual home environment, and existing connections with Piedmont CDSA, Early Head Start, and Guilford County Smart Start provide a solid foundation for continued intervention.

**Recommendations**

1. Sofía qualifies for ongoing speech-language intervention under her IFSP, Outcome 2 and Outcome 3, targeting expressive vocabulary growth and speech sound intelligibility.
2. Individual therapy twice weekly, 30 minutes per session, delivered bilingually, focusing on core vocabulary expansion, early morphosyntax (plurals, present progressive -ing), and phonological awareness activities.
3. Incorporate a Hanen-based coaching model for Carla Beltrán-Soto and Luis del Río to support language facilitation strategies during daily routines, given their limited availability for in-person sessions due to work schedules.
4. Target phonological processes using a Cycles approach, prioritizing final consonant deletion and cluster reduction, with ongoing stimulability work for /k/ and /ɾ/.
5. Collaborate with Ms. Lopez at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center to implement visual supports and simplified language models within the classroom setting, including strategies for supporting Sofía's interactions with peers such as Emma.
6. Coordinate with service coordinator Patricia Nguyen regarding continued eligibility and transition planning as Sofía approaches her third birthday transition timeline from Piedmont CDSA services.
7. Re-screen hearing in 6 months given history of recurrent otitis media, and refer back to Dr. Marcus Whitfield if any signs of middle ear dysfunction recur.
8. Re-evaluate standardized language and articulation scores in approximately 12 months to monitor progress and adjust the treatment plan accordingly.
9. Encourage continued bilingual input at home; research consistently supports dual-language exposure for children with language disorders, and there is no indication that reducing Spanish input would benefit Sofía's English development.

This evaluation and these recommendations were discussed with Carla Beltrán-Soto at the conclusion of testing on September 22, 2026. A written copy of this report will be provided to the family and, with consent, shared with Piedmont CDSA, Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, and Dr. Anil Patel's office.

Respectfully submitted,

Elena Vásquez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language, PLLC

NORTH CAROLINA INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM
INDIVIDUALIZED FAMILY SERVICE PLAN — SIX-MONTH REVIEW / REVISIÓN DE SEIS MESES

Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC

FAMILY INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN FAMILIAR

Mother/Madre: Guadalupe Flores Ramírez, conocida como "Lupita"
Home: (336) 555-0176 | Cell: 336-555-0190
Father/Padre: José Luis Martínez Cruz
Cell: (336) 555-0203, works second shift at Pinewood Furniture Manufacturing
Sibling/Hermano: Juan Martínez Flores Jr., age 5, called "Juanito" at home, attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center
Maternal grandmother/Abuela materna: Rosa Elena Cruz Villalobos, lives in Comitán de Domínguez, Chiapas, México, reachable at +52 963 123 4567; cares for Chuy on weekday mornings by video call "para que no se le olvide el español"
Primary language in the home: Spanish; father has intermediate English; Lupita prefers Spanish for all meetings.

Address: 214 Maple Hollow Drive, Burlington, NC 27215, Alamance County
Primary care physician: Dr. Hannah Kim, Burlington Pediatrics, (336) 555-0117

REASON FOR REVIEW

This six-month IFSP review was completed in the home on October 6, 2026 with Lupita present and José Luis Martínez Cruz joining by phone for the last fifteen minutes. Carla Jiménez (service coordinator) and Daniela Ortiz (bilingual SLP) conducted the visit. The purpose was to update present levels, review progress on outcomes, and confirm continued eligibility for Chuy.

FAMILY CONCERNS, PRIORITIES, AND RESOURCES / PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES

En sus propias palabras, Lupita dijo: "A veces Chuy se frustra porque quiere decir algo y no le salen las palabras, y entonces grita o me jala la mano." She also said, mixing languages as she often does, "I just want him to be able to tell me 'quiero agua' or 'más, por favor' instead of crying — eso es lo que más me importa ahorita."

José Luis Martínez Cruz added by phone: "Yo trabajo mucho, pero cuando llego los fines de semana quiero jugar con él, y a veces no sé qué quiere. Necesito que me digan cómo ayudarle en casa, nothing too complicated, just something I can do después del trabajo."

Priorities identified by the family:
1. Chuy will use more words and gestures to ask for things instead of crying.
2. Chuy will play better with his brother "Juanito" without hitting when frustrated.
3. The family wants help understanding what is "normal" bilingual development versus a delay, because Rosa Elena Cruz Villalobos insists by phone "es que aquí todos los niños hablan tarde, no te preocupes."

Family resources: a stable two-parent home, strong extended family support by phone and visits, Lupita's flexible schedule, and the father's steady income despite his shift hours.

OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED / OTRAS AGENCIAS

- Alamance County Department of Social Services (DSS): Chuy's family receives Food and Nutrition Services benefits through caseworker Teresa Ocampo, (336) 555-0128.
- Alamance County WIC Program: Chuy and Juanito are both enrolled; nutritionist Beth Allred coordinates with this team on feeding concerns, 336-555-0135.
- Partnership for Children of Alamance County (Smart Start): provided a car seat and referred the family to this program after a well-child visit flagged language concerns.
- Alamance-Caswell Early Head Start: Juanito was previously enrolled; the family is on the waiting list to enroll Chuy once he turns three.
- Burlington Pediatrics: Dr. Hannah Kim made the original referral to CDSA of the Piedmont on March 18, 2026.

DAILY ROUTINES / RUTINAS DIARIAS

Morning: Chuy wakes around 6:45 a.m. and watches his grandmother on video call while Lupita makes breakfast; he often points at the phone and says "Abu" for Rosa Elena Cruz Villalobos. Breakfast is usually eggs, beans, and tortilla, eaten at the kitchen table with Juanito.

Midday: Lupita takes both boys to the park near Maple Hollow Drive most days around 11:00 a.m.; Chuy enjoys the swings and will say "más" or "up" to request another turn, and reaches for other children's toys without asking, which sometimes leads to conflict with peers such as a neighbor child, "Teo," who also plays there.

Afternoon/nap: nap from about 1:30 p.m. to 3:00 p.m.. Juanito returns from Little Sprouts Early Learning Center around 4:00 p.m. and the boys play with blocks; Chuy will grab toys from Juanito and hit when told "no."

Evening/bedtime: dinner together around 6:30 p.m.; bath and books before bed around 8:00 p.m.. José Luis Martínez Cruz is home on weekends for this routine and reports it is his favorite time with Chuy.

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT

Communication: Chuy was most recently assessed using the Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5, Spanish-English bilingual edition) on September 29, 2026.

Score Summary:

| Subtest | Standard Score | 95% CI | Percentile | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auditory Comprehension | 76 | 73-83 | 5th | 2;0–2;3 |
| Expressive Communication | 71 | 68–79 | 3rd | 1;9-2;0 |
| Total Language Score | 73 | 70-80 | 4th | 2;0–2;3 |

These scores reflect a significant delay in expressive language, consistent with the family's reported concerns and the earlier Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale results from intake, which showed Chuy functioning at approximately 16-18 months expressively against a chronological age of 24 months at that time.

Current expressive vocabulary (parent report plus direct observation) includes approximately 25 words across English and Spanish combined, including "mamá," "papá," "agua," "más," "up," "no," and "bye-bye." He combines a word and a gesture (for example, pointing and saying "más") but produces almost no two-word combinations. Target word "perro" was attempted during play with a toy dog and produced as "eo," omitting the initial /p/ and the medial /ɾ/.

Receptively, Chuy follows one-step directions in both languages with mod cues (gestural plus verbal) and identifies 8 of 10 common objects by pointing when named in Spanish, and 6 of 10 in English.

Oral-motor and feeding: within normal limits per Dr. Hannah Kim's most recent well-child note dated August 14, 2026; Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at birth and no history of feeding difficulty.

Social-emotional and behavior: Chuy shows frustration-related aggression (hitting, grabbing) when he cannot communicate a want, consistent with family report. He engages readily in parallel play but limited reciprocal play; joint attention is emerging but inconsistent.

Gross/fine motor: age-appropriate per CDSA developmental specialist screening on April 2, 2026; no concerns at this time.

ELIGIBILITY

Chuy continues to demonstrate a significant developmental delay in the communication domain (greater than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean on the PLS-5 Expressive Communication subtest) and remains eligible for the NC Infant-Toddler Program under 10A NCAC 24A.

IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES / RESULTADOS Y ESTRATEGIAS

Outcome 1: Chuy will use two-word combinations to request desired items and actions during daily routines, increasing from his current single-word level to at least 10 different two-word combinations within six months.
Strategies: Model expansion in both languages ("más agua," "up please") during meals and play; Lupita will pause and wait after modeling to give Chuy a turn; use visual supports (first/then picture cards) to pair words with gestures; family to practice during the midday park routine and bedtime books.

Outcome 2: Chuy will replace hitting/grabbing with an acceptable communicative alternative (word, sign, or gesture for "mine" or "my turn") in at least 8 of 10 observed opportunities with peers and his brother.
Strategies: Teach a simple sign for "mine" alongside the word "mío"; José Luis Martínez Cruz and Guadalupe Flores Ramírez will narrate turn-taking during block play with Juan Martínez Flores Jr.; provider to model this approach using principles drawn from Hanen's "It Takes Two to Talk" during the next two home visits.

Outcome 3: The family will understand typical bilingual language milestones and distinguish them from Chuy's identified delay, so they can advocate for continued services even when extended family (such as Rosa Elena Cruz Villalobos) suggests waiting.
Strategies: Service coordinator Carla Jiménez will share bilingual developmental milestone handouts in Spanish; SLP Daniela Ortiz will review total-vocabulary versus single-language-vocabulary counting with the family, since Chuy's combined vocabulary of 25 words is more informative than either language alone; discuss at next review how to respond to well-meaning family pressure to "esperar."

Outcome 4: Chuy will increase his repertoire of consonant sounds in word-initial position, specifically /p/, /m/, /b/, and /t/, achieving 80% accuracy in structured play across 3 consecutive sessions.
Strategies: Use PROMPT-informed tactile cueing for bilabial sounds; practice target words "papá," "más," "bebé," and "toto" (a family word for shoes) during structured play; direct SLP sessions twice weekly, 30 minutes each, co-treated bilingually.

SERVICES

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Speech-Language Therapy | Daniela Ortiz, Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC | 2x/week, 30 min | Home | April 9, 2026 |
| Service Coordination | Carla Jiménez, CDSA of the Piedmont | Monthly | Home/phone | April 2, 2026 |
| Developmental Screening Follow-up | CDSA Developmental Specialist | As needed | Home | April 2, 2026 |

The next IFSP review is scheduled for April 6, 2027 or sooner if concerns arise. Lupita can reach the team directly at the phone numbers listed above; the family also keeps a card with the CDSA after-hours line, 1-800-555-0199, posted on the refrigerator.

TRANSITION PLANNING NOTE

Because Chuy will turn three on April 9, 2027, the team briefly discussed transition options, including continued evaluation for preschool special education through the local school system and the Alamance-Caswell Early Head Start waitlist. Formal transition planning will begin at least 90 days prior to the third birthday per state timelines; Carla Jiménez will initiate the transition conference and invite José Luis Martínez Cruz and Guadalupe Flores Ramírez in writing.

FAMILY SIGNATURE AND CONSENT

Guadalupe Flores Ramírez reviewed this IFSP review in Spanish with interpretation support confirmed as not needed, since Daniela Ortiz conducted the visit bilingually. Guadalupe Flores Ramírez stated she agrees with the outcomes as written and signed consent to continue services on October 6, 2026. José Luis Martínez Cruz gave verbal consent by phone, confirmed by Carla Jiménez, and will countersign at the next in-person visit.

Client / Cliente: María José Fernández Castillo (goes by "MJ")

Referral Source: Dr. Samuel Osei, pediatrician, and Keisha Brown, service coordinator, Piedmont CDSA
Examiner: Ana Lima, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (español/inglés)

S: (Subjective)

Reason for referral: MJ is a 4;6-year-old niña referred by Dr. Samuel Osei after a well-check flagged intelligibility and expressive-language concerns in both Spanish and English. Lucía Castillo Ramos and Javier Fernández Soto c/o MJ "no se le entiende bien" (not well understood) by family and unfamiliar listeners, and that she mixes idiomas constantly. Keisha Brown at Piedmont CDSA coordinated this bilingual eval d/t concern re: eligibility for Part C services prior to MJ's 5th birthday transition.

Birth and medical hx: MJ born at Duke Regional Hospital, 39 weeks gestation, NSVD (normal spontaneous vaginal delivery), Apgar 8/9, birth weight 3.2 kg (7 lb 1 oz). No NICU admit, no feeding tube, no reported hypoxia. Hx 3 episodes otitis media between 8 months and 18 months of age, tx'd with antibiotics; no PE tubes placed; no current ear complaints. Hearing screening 09/12/2024 WNL bilaterally per audiology, pass on OAE both ears. No hx seizure, no hx head injury. Vision screened WFL at well-check. Lucía Castillo Ramos denies maternal substance use or complications during pregnancy; reports mild gestational hypertension, managed, no hospitalization beyond delivery.

Developmental hx: gross/fine motor milestones per parent report WNL — sat 6 months, walked 13 months. First words (Spanish) ~14 months ("mamá," "agua"); 2-word combos ~28 months. Parents deny regression. Lucía Castillo Ramos states, "Antes decía más palabras que ahora siento que se quedó atrás comparada con su hermana Sol a esa edad."

Family composition and language hx: MJ lives with both parents, older sister Sol Fernández Castillo (edad 5;8), and younger brother Mateo Fernández Castillo (edad 2;3), at 142 Birchwood Lane, Durham, NC 27705. Home language is Spanish; Lucía Castillo Ramos and Javier Fernández Soto both report Spanish as L1, raised in Honduras and Michoacán respectively, now residing in Durham County. Maternal grandmother, Rosa Castillo Ramos ("abuela"), provides childcare 2 days/week and speaks only Spanish with MJ; she resides at 88 Cedar Grove Court, Durham, NC 27703. Lucía Castillo Ramos works as a nurse at Duke University Health System; Javier Fernández Soto works construction for Blue Ridge Construction Co. The family is enrolled with WIC. A family friend, Carmen Ruiz, recommended this practice to Lucía Castillo Ramos after her own son was seen here.

Lucía Castillo Ramos reports: "En casa habla puro español, pero en la guardería casi no habla. Allá dice que está 'muy callada.' Y cuando habla, mezcla todo: dice 'quiero water' en vez de 'quiero agua,' o 'el dog corre' en vez de 'el perro corre.'" She adds that intelligibility is worse in English: "en inglés casi no le entiendo nada, mod cues no ayudan si no sabe la palabra."

MJ attends Little Sprouts Daycare M–F, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM. Lead teacher Ms. Patterson and assistant Miss Ortiz report MJ follows 2-step directions in English with mod cues, prefers parallel over interactive play, and sits with classmates Emma and Diego during circle time but rarely initiates. Ms. Patterson wrote in a classroom note, "MJ watches Emma and copies her actions but doesn't use words to join in." No prior speech/language or OT/PT services. Family dog Rocky (labrador) is frequently mentioned by MJ at home and was used as a reinforcer during testing ("Rocky quiere jugar").

Prior supports: an interpreter, Rosa Elena Vásquez, supported a brief OT screening on 01/14/2025 (no services recommended at that time; fine motor WFL). This is MJ's first comprehensive speech-language eval.

O: (Objective)

Behavioral observations: MJ separated easily from Lucía Castillo Ramos in the waiting area, cooperative across both sessions, intermittently shy with unfamiliar adults, warmed with play-based rapport-building. Attention WFL for structured tasks ~15 min blocks; required mod cues (visual + verbal) to re-engage after breaks. Articulation testing conducted bilingually by examiner, a bilingual SLP.

Standardized and criterion-referenced measures administered across two visits at Carolina Pediatric Therapy Associates:

| Date | Measure | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 de marzo de 2025 | PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | 73 | 4th | 68-78 |
| 3 de marzo de 2025 | PLS-5 Expressive Communication | 70 | 2nd | 65-75 |
| 3 de marzo de 2025 | PLS-5 Total Language Score | 70 | 2nd | 66-74 |
| 03/14/2025 | CELF Preschool-3 Core Language Score | 72 | 3rd | 67-77 |
| 3 de marzo de 2025 | Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) Standard Score | 65 | 1st | 60-70 |
| el martes 4 de junio de 2025 | PLS-5 Total Language Score (re-admin) | 76 | 5th | 72-80 |

Informal Spanish Articulation Measures (SAM, informal) and phonological process analysis supplemented standardized English norms due to limited norming for bilingual Spanish speakers in this age range; results interpreted alongside GFTA-3 for cross-linguistic pattern comparison.

Phonology: Conversational and single-word sampling in both languages revealed consistent patterns of final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and stopping of fricatives across Spanish and English, suggesting a true phonological disorder rather than typical bilingual transfer. Percentage Consonants Correct (PCC): 62% English, 68% Spanish.

During a /l/ final-position probe using single-word targets ("sol", "mal", "col"), MJ was shown a picture of the sun and asked to label it. She paused, looked up at the examiner, and said, "como mi hermana," referencing her sister Sol, then produced [so] without the final /l/, consistent with final consonant deletion (observed 7 of 10 trials, 70%). With max cues (tactile + visual), she improved to [sol] on 3 of 10 trials. Examiner noted the overlap between the target word and the sibling's name produced visible hesitation each trial, requiring redirection ("sol, como el sol en el cielo") before MJ would attempt production again.

Additional single-word probes: /k/ initial — "casa" → [tasa] (fronting); /s/ clusters — "estrella" → [etreja] (cluster reduction); English /θ/ — "three" → [fri] (stopping, age-appropriate at 4;6). Stimulability: improved to min cues on /k/ and /s/-cluster targets; /l/ final remained resistant to mod cues, required max cues.

Oral mechanism exam: structure and function WFL, no overt dysarthria/apraxia signs, diadochokinetic rates age-appropriate. Hearing: screened WNL bilaterally 03/03/2025 (tympanometry type A bilaterally).

Language sample (MLU analysis, 50-utterance sample, SALT-coded): MLU in Spanish 3.1 morphemes, MLU in English 2.4 morphemes, both below expected range for 4;6. Omission of grammatical morphemes noted in both languages, e.g., [EW] coded for word-finding pauses occurring 9 times across sample. Pragmatics: joint attention intact, turn-taking WFL, initiates requests primarily via gesture + single words rather than phrases.

Session schedule proposed for ongoing bilingual intervention (see Plan below for rationale):

| Day | Start | Stop | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mondays | 9:00 AM | 9:45 AM | Little Sprouts Daycare (Room 2) |
| Wednesdays | 2:30 PM | 3:15 PM | Carolina Pediatric Therapy Associates, Durham office |
| Fridays | 10:15 AM | 11:00 AM | home visit, 142 Birchwood Lane, Durham, NC 27705 |

A: (Assessment)

MJ presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder (ICD-10 F80.2) evident across both Spanish and English, with a concomitant phonological disorder marked by final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and stopping. Standard scores cluster in the below-average to significantly-below-average range across measures (65–76), and the consistency of deficit across both languages and both testing dates (3 de marzo de 2025, el martes 4 de junio de 2025) supports a true language/phonological impairment rather than typical second-language acquisition or test unfamiliarity. The modest gain on re-administered PLS-5 Total Language Score (70 → 76) is within expected test-retest variability (overlapping 95% CI) and does not indicate resolution.

Relative strengths: social pragmatics WFL, joint attention intact, play skills age-appropriate, good stimulability on several error sounds with cueing. Rapport-building with the family dog Rocky as reinforcer, and the brief disruption during the "sol" probe tied to her sister Sol's name, both suggest MJ is emotionally engaged and relationally aware, a positive prognostic sign for therapy motivation.

MJ meets eligibility for Piedmont CDSA Part C services under NC Infant-Toddler Program criteria based on standard scores ≥1.5 SD below mean in two or more domains. Recommend IFSP Outcome #2 (communication) be updated to reflect bilingual service delivery.

P: (Plan)

Dear Mrs. Hernández,

I hope this note finds you well! I wanted to give you a quick update on Sofía's session today, October 9, 2026, at 3:30 PM. We worked together until 4:15 PM at the Little Learners Program therapy room, right after she finished her day at Little Learners Daycare.

Sofía came in happy and ready to work. Her babysitter, Marisol Reyes, dropped her off and mentioned that Sofía's cousin Diego had been visiting this week, which Sofía was excited to tell me about!

**Subjective:** Mrs. Hernández reports that Sofía has been using more two-word phrases at home, including with her dog, Bella. She said "Bella go" during play yesterday, which is a great milestone.

**Objective:** We targeted the /k/ and /g/ sounds using PROMPT cueing. Sofía produced "cat" with min cues 8/10 trials, up from 3 of 5 last week. We also reviewed her classroom vocabulary — she named her friends Emma and Liam from her class, and talked about her teacher, Ms. Patterson, who she adores.

Her articulation goal (IFSP Outcome 2) continues to progress. On the GFTA-3, her most recent standard score was 82 (12th percentile), compared to 76 at her March 3, 2026 evaluation. Age equivalent is now 3;2, within the 2;9–3;5 range for her chronological age of 3;6.

We also practiced the Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies you've been using at home — great carryover, by the way!

**Assessment:** Sofía is making steady gains. Her babbling with [w] substitutions for /r/ is decreasing, and she's starting to attempt [ɾ] in simple words like "car."

**Plan:** Continue weekly sessions on Tuesdays at 3:30 PM. I'd also like to coordinate with her service coordinator, Mr. Thomas Ellis at the Wake County CDSA, about scheduling her six-month review.

A few logistics notes:

- Next session is October 16, 2026 at 3:30 PM, same location.
- Please remember Sofía's AAC device charger — her older sister, Valentina, borrowed it last time by accident!

On a fun note, Sofía mentioned she's excited for the toddler story time at the Fuquay-Varina Public Library this Saturday morning at 10:00 AM, and she's still talking about the puppet show at Grace Community Church's fall festival last weekend!

If you have questions, please don't hesitate to reach out. You can call the clinic at (919) 555-0148 or email me directly at m.delacruz@littlelearnerstherapy.com. Our billing uses CPT code 92507 for individual therapy, modifier GN.

Also — I spoke briefly with her pediatrician's office, Fuquay-Varina Pediatrics, and they confirmed her recent hearing screening was within normal limits, which is wonderful news.

Thank you for being such an involved and supportive parent. Sofía is lucky to have you cheering her on! I'll see you both next week.

Warm regards,

Child Name: Mateo Hernández Cruz
Date of Birth: March 14, 2024
Age at IFSP Review: 2;2 (26 months)
Primary Language(s) in Home: Spanish, English
County of Residence: Chatham County
Family Address: 118 Willow Oak Lane, Siler City, NC 27344
CDSA Office: Piedmont Triad CDSA
Service Coordinator: Denise Alvarez
Medicaid ID: 987654321B
Record/Case ID: IFSP-2026-04471
Referral Date: November 3, 2025
Initial Evaluation Date: November 19, 2025
Initial IFSP Date: December 2, 2025
This Review Date: October 6, 2026
Next Review Due: April 6, 2027
Primary Diagnosis/ICD-10: F80.2, Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder
Treating Clinician: Marisol Vega, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Services Provider
Employer: Triangle Pediatric Therapy Partners, PLLC (referred to below as Triangle Pediatric Therapy, TPTP)
Office Address: 4420 Progress Court, Suite C, Durham, NC 27703
Office Phone: (919) 555-0148
Clinician Email: mvega@trianglepediatrictherapy.com
Agency Website: www.trianglepediatrictherapy.com

**Información Familiar / Family Information**

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez, his older sister, Hope (age 6), and his maternal grandmother, doña Lupe, who moved in with the family in February 2026 to help with child care. Mateo's father, Esteban Cruz, lives in Siler City and sees Mateo on weekends; he was not present for this review but was consulted by phone on October 1, 2026.

Lucía works two jobs to support the family. During the day she is a prep cook at a restaurant, and overnight three nights a week she works a stocking shift at QRS, a regional warehouse company whose full name she says she has never seen written out — "solo le decimos QRS." Because of this schedule, doña Lupe and sometimes Hope help get Mateo ready for daycare in the mornings. Lucía reports feeling "cansada todo el tiempo, pero no me puedo quejar, hay que seguir."

Mateo attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center four days a week from 7:45 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.. His classroom teacher, Miss Ana, reports that Mateo is social with peers but "gets frustrated fast when nobody understands him." At daycare, Mateo's closest friend is Diego, and the two are often found in the block corner together.

**Preocupaciones y Prioridades Familiares / Family Concerns and Priorities**

In the intake interview, conducted in Spanish at the family's request, Lucía shared the following concerns, recorded here in her own words:

"Mi mayor preocupación es que Mateo no habla como los demás niños de su edad. En la casa yo le entiendo casi todo, pero cuando estamos en la tienda o con gente que no lo conoce, nadie le entiende nada."

"A veces se enoja mucho porque quiere decir algo y no puede. Grita o jala la ropa, y yo no sé si es porque no entiende o porque no me puedo comunicar bien con él."

"Quiero que aprenda bien los dos idiomas, español e inglés, porque en la casa hablamos español pero en la escuela todo es en inglés. No quiero que se le olvide el español."

Lucía also said, "doña Lupe me ayuda mucho, pero ella tampoco habla inglés, entonces cuando Mateo empiece el prekínder, me preocupa que nadie en la escuela le entienda."

Based on these statements, the family and team identified the following priorities for the coming IFSP period:

1. Mateo will increase functional communication in both English and Spanish so that unfamiliar listeners, including Miss Ana and extended family, can understand his wants and needs.
2. The family will receive strategies, in Spanish, to support language development at home during daily routines.
3. Mateo's frustration-related behaviors will decrease as his expressive communication increases.

**Rutinas Diarias / Daily Routines**

Mornings: doña Lupe wakes Mateo around 6:30 a.m.; he eats breakfast (usually avena or cereal) and is often resistant to getting dressed. doña Lupe reports that singing helps, "le gusta cuando le canto 'Los Pollitos' mientras se viste."

Daycare: Mateo is dropped off around 7:45 a.m. by doña Lupe or Hope before her own school bus arrives. Miss Ana reports he participates in circle time but rarely initiates verbally, relying on pointing and pulling adults by the hand.

Evenings: Lucía or doña Lupe picks him up around 4:30 p.m.. Dinner, bath, and bedtime routine happen between 6:00 p.m. and 8:00 p.m.. Lucía notes that bath time is when Mateo "habla más," naming body parts and toys, though mostly in single words.

Weekends: Mateo sometimes visits Esteban in Siler City, where he also sees his paternal cousin, Will. Esteban reports similar frustration behaviors at his house.

**Otras Agencias / Other Agencies Involved**

The family currently receives support from WIC for nutrition services and has an open case with Chatham County DSS for Medicaid renewal. Lucía reported interest in enrolling Mateo in a Smart Start-funded playgroup once a spot opens. The family was also referred to El Centro Hispano for Spanish-language parenting resources, though Lucía has not yet attended a session due to her work schedule.

**Present Levels of Development / Niveles Actuales de Desarrollo**

Communication: On the Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), administered in both English and Spanish by Marisol Vega with interpretation support from Denise Alvarez, Mateo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 73 (95% CI 68-78, 4th percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 65 (95% CI 60-70, 2nd percentile), yielding an age equivalent of approximately 14 months. On the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, parent report and direct observation placed expressive language skills in the 11-13 month range.

Mateo's expressive vocabulary in structured sampling included approximately 25 consistent words across both languages, including "agua," "más," "mamá," "no," "pelota," and "arriba." He combined words inconsistently, producing two-word combinations in 2 of 10 opportunities (for example, "más agua"). Phonemic inventory is reduced; he was observed to substitute [w] for /r/ and to omit final consonants, as in his production of "pelota" as "peo." Stimulability testing showed he could imitate the target sound /p/ with moderate verbal and tactile cues in 3 of 5 trials.

Receptively, Mateo followed simple one-step directions in Spanish 8/10 trials and in English 5/10 trials, suggesting stronger receptive skills in the home language, consistent with a typical bilingual profile and not indicative of a disorder limited to one language.

Birth and medical history: Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestation, birth weight 6 lbs 11 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. No significant medical history is reported. Hearing was screened and passed at birth and again at the November 19, 2025 evaluation.

Motor, social-emotional, and adaptive skills are within age expectations per parent and teacher report, with mild concerns noted regarding frustration tolerance related to communication breakdowns.

**Resultados y Estrategias / Outcomes and Strategies**

**Outcome 1:** Mateo will use two- to three-word combinations to request, comment, and protest across settings (home, daycare) in both Spanish and English, as measured by caregiver log and direct observation, by April 6, 2027.

Strategies: Marisol Vega will model expansion techniques drawn from Hanen's "It Takes Two to Talk" during biweekly home visits, coaching Lucía and doña Lupe to expand Mateo's single-word utterances in Spanish during daily routines (bath time, meals). Miss Ana will use parallel talk and modeling in English during daycare activities. Home program materials will be provided in Spanish.

**Outcome 2:** Mateo will produce final consonants in single words with no more than minimal cues, increasing intelligibility to familiar and unfamiliar listeners, as measured quarterly by probe data, by April 6, 2027.

Strategies: Marisol Vega will implement a modified Cycles approach targeting final consonant deletion, incorporating PROMPT-informed tactile cueing given Mateo's stimulability for /p/ and /t/. Target words will be selected in both languages (e.g., "pelota"/"ball," "gato"/"cat") to support cross-linguistic transfer.

**Outcome 3:** The family will report at least two new strategies used successfully at home each month to support Mateo's communication and reduce frustration-related behaviors, as measured by caregiver interview, by April 6, 2027.

Strategies: Marisol Vega and Denise Alvarez will coordinate a joint home visit with El Centro Hispano staff to connect Lucía with a Spanish-language caregiver support group. Visual supports (first/then boards) will be introduced in both languages for use at daycare and home, with Miss Ana trained on their use during a consultation visit.

**Prestación de Servicios / Service Delivery**

Speech-language therapy will continue at a frequency of two 30-minute sessions per week, delivered in home and community settings, billed under CPT 92507 and CPT 92523 as appropriate. Sessions will be conducted primarily in Spanish with English integration per family preference, consistent with the family's stated priority of dual-language development.

Service coordination will continue monthly through Piedmont Triad CDSA, coordinated by Denise Alvarez. The team will reconvene for a six-month progress check on January 12, 2027, with full annual review scheduled for April 6, 2027.

This IFSP was reviewed and signed by Lucía Rodríguez (mother), with Marisol Vega (treating clinician, TPTP) and Denise Alvarez (service coordinator, Piedmont Triad CDSA) present. Esteban Cruz participated by phone and verbally concurred with the outcomes as written. doña Lupe was present and asked clarifying questions in Spanish, which were addressed directly by Marisol Vega without need for a separate interpreter, given her bilingual credentialing.

For questions regarding this plan, the family may contact Marisol Vega directly at mvega@trianglepediatrictherapy.com or through the Triangle Pediatric Therapy office at (919) 555-0148. Additional resources and intake forms in Spanish are available at www.trianglepediatrictherapy.com.

North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program — Individualized Family Service Plan Review

CHILD AND FAMILY INFORMATION

Child's Legal Name: María José Fernández del Río  Preferred Name: Majo  Date of Birth: April 2, 2024  Current Age: 2;6
Record No: NC-ITP-88213  Medicaid ID: 774120983K  Primary Home Language: Spanish  Secondary Language: English

Address: 418 Caraleigh Mills Rd, Raleigh, Wake County, NC 27603

Referring Agency: Asociación Comunitaria para el Desarrollo Infantil y Familiar (ACODIF)

Occupational Therapist: Brian Okafor  Physical Therapist: Hannah Kim  Spanish Interpreter (as needed): Marisol Ibarra
Evaluation Date: August 11, 2026  Initial IFSP Date: August 25, 2026  This Review Date: October 9, 2026  Next Review Due: April 9, 2027

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES (in the family's own words, recorded through interpretation)

Lucía del Río Vásquez reported, "Majo todavía no me dice 'mamá' ni 'más', y eso me preocupa mucho porque su hermano a esta edad ya hablaba bastante." She stated her top priority is for María José to request food and toys using words instead of pulling her hand. Javier Fernández-Castillo added, "I just want her to be understood by her brother and by other kids at daycare, not just by us." The family also noted that Majo gets frustrated at mealtimes and sometimes throws her cup, which they would like addressed alongside communication.

A secondary concern from the family is coordinating services between English-speaking providers and the home, since la abuela Rosa Vásquez, who cares for María José three afternoons a week, speaks only Spanish. The family asked that written home strategies be provided bilingually.

DAILY ROUTINES

Morning: María José wakes around 7:00 a.m., eats breakfast with Mateo Fernández del Río, and is dropped at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare by 8:15 a.m. Mother reports Majo points to the cereal box but does not yet say "más" or "leche" to request more.
Midday: Naps from 12:30 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. at daycare; staff report she follows simple one-step directions with gestures from Ms. Patterson.
Afternoon: Rosa Vásquez picks her up around 3:30 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays and supervises outdoor play with Luna and Mateo Fernández del Río.
Mealtime: Family eats dinner together around 6:00 p.m.; Majo prefers purees and becomes upset with mixed textures, sometimes throwing her cup when denied a second helping.
Bedtime: Bath at 7:30 p.m., books with father, asleep by 8:30 p.m.; father reports she babbles "bababa" and "dadada" during this routine but rarely imitates single words.

OTHER AGENCIES AND SUPPORTS

The family currently receives WIC nutrition support through the Wake County Human Services office and has an open case with Smart Start of Wake County for a future preschool voucher. The family was also referred to ACODIF for Spanish-language parent support groups meeting monthly at their community center on Method Rd. Lucía del Río Vásquez attended one ACODIF session in September 2026 and found it helpful.

EVALUATION SUMMARY

Communication was assessed using the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, which placed receptive language in the moderate delay range (age equivalent 14-16 months) and expressive language in the severe delay range (age equivalent 10-12 months). The Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 was administered informally given her limited word inventory; stimulability was noted for /m/, /b/, and /p/ in isolation. Gross and fine motor skills were screened using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition, with motor composite score of 91 (28th percentile), within normal limits. The Peabody Developmental Motor Scales-2 fine motor subtest yielded a scaled score of 9 (37th percentile).

María José produced five consistent words across settings: "mamá," "papá," "agua," "no," and an approximation "ba" for "ball." When shown a picture of a dog, she pointed and said what sounded like "Luna," spontaneously naming the family pet rather than labeling the picture, suggesting strong but narrow vocabulary use. Oral-motor exam was within normal limits. Hearing screening on July 30, 2026 passed bilaterally.

ELIGIBILITY AND DIAGNOSTIC CODES

Diagnosis: Expressive Language Delay, ICD-10 F80.1; Receptive-Expressive Language Delay ruled out as primary, secondary code F80.2 noted for monitoring. CPT codes billed for evaluation: 92523 (speech/language evaluation) and 96110 (developmental screening, standardized).

IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: María José will use 15 different spoken words consistently across home and daycare within 6 months, as measured by parent and teacher log and direct observation by Rebecca Townsend-Ellis.
Strategy: Model target words at min to mod cueing levels during meals and play; pause-and-wait strategy taught to Lucía del Río Vásquez, Javier Fernández-Castillo, and Rosa Vásquez using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" principles, delivered bilingually.

Outcome 2: María José will combine a gesture and a word (e.g., pointing plus "más") to make a request in 8/10 opportunities across three consecutive sessions.
Strategy: PROMPT-informed tactile cueing for bilabial sounds; home practice sheet provided in Spanish and English; daycare staff coached by Rebecca Townsend-Ellis on cueing during snack time.

Outcome 3: María José will tolerate two new food textures per week without a tantrum, as reported by parent log, supporting feeding and communication during mealtimes.
Strategy: Occupational therapy co-treatment with Brian Okafor using graded texture exposure; family to track responses nightly.

Outcome 4: María José will walk independently across uneven surfaces (grass, mulch) without falling for 10 consecutive steps, supporting participation in outdoor play with Mateo Fernández del Río and peers at daycare.
Strategy: Weekly physical therapy with Hannah Kim; home program reviewed with father given his evening routine with Majo.

Team also discussed classroom participation: Ms. Patterson reported Majo is beginning to imitate a peer, Noah, during circle time songs, which the team will monitor as an informal social outcome.

SESSION SCHEDULE

Transportation for the monthly service coordination visit is provided by ACODIF when the family's car is unavailable; this arrangement was confirmed with Denise Alvarado by phone on October 2, 2026.

NATURAL ENVIRONMENTS JUSTIFICATION

All direct therapy occurs in the home or at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare, consistent with natural environments requirements. Co-treatment sessions between Brian Okafor and Rebecca Townsend-Ellis are scheduled quarterly to align feeding and communication strategies.

TRANSITION PLANNING

Because María José will turn 3 on April 2, 2027, the team reviewed transition timelines. Denise Alvarado will initiate a referral to the local education agency by January 2, 2027, 90 days prior to the third birthday, per NC ITP policy. The family was given written transition information in Spanish and asked whether they wished to pursue Part B eligibility evaluation through Wake County Public School System; they agreed to proceed.

Mateo nacio a las 36 semanas de gestacion por cesarea de emergencia en Piedmont Regional Medical Center - Cary Campus, con un peso al nacer de 2,450 gramos (5 libras 6 onzas). Los puntajes de Apgar fueron 7 al minuto y 9 a los cinco minutos. Debido a dificultad respiratoria leve, Mateo paso 9 dias en Piedmont Regional NICU - Cary Campus antes de ser dado de alta el 28 de febrero de 2022. Durante su estancia en la unidad neonatal fue atendido por el neonatologo, el Dr. Samuel Ortiz, y por una terapeuta ocupacional del hospital, Miss Jenny, quien trabajo brevemente con la succion y alimentacion de Mateo.

No se reportan otras hospitalizaciones significativas. Mateo tuvo tres episodios de otitis media entre los 14 y los 22 meses de edad, tratados con antibioticos; no requirio tubos de ventilacion. Fue referido a audiologia en el 4 de marzo de 2024 por preocupacion de los padres sobre su audicion, y fue evaluado en Piedmont Regional Ear, Nose, Throat and Audiology - Morrisville Campus por el audiologo, a quien la familia conoce solo como "Mr. Tom". Los resultados de esa evaluacion mostraron audicion dentro de limites normales bilateralmente, con timpanogramas tipo A en ambos oidos. No hay antecedentes de convulsiones, lesion cerebral, ni cirugias. La vision fue evaluada como normal en su ultima visita pediatrica.

El desarrollo motor grueso y fino se reporta dentro de limites normales: camino de forma independiente a los 13 meses y uso tijeras para cortar lineas rectas a los 4 anios. Lucia no reporta preocupaciones de alimentacion actuales, aunque describe a Mateo como "selectivo" con texturas mixtas desde bebe.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

Mateo vive con su mama, la senora Lucia Ramirez Gomez, su hermano mayor Diego Flores Ramirez (8 anios) y su hermana menor Sofia Flores Ramirez (18 meses), en una casa alquilada en 118 Cedar Hollow Lane, Millbrook Creek, NC 27591. El papa, el senor Carlos Flores Diaz, vive y trabaja fuera del estado la mayor parte del ano y tiene contacto con la familia principalmente por telefono y video llamadas; regresa a casa aproximadamente cada seis a ocho semanas.

Lucia trabaja dos empleos para mantener a la familia. De dia trabaja como cocinera en el restaurante El Fogon Criollo, con turnos que normalmente van de 7:00 a.m. a 3:00 p.m.. Tres noches a la semana trabaja limpiando oficinas para una empresa que la familia conoce solo por sus siglas, TMS, en turnos de 11:00 p.m. a 6:00 a.m.. Debido a este horario, la cuidadora principal de los ninos durante buena parte de la semana es una vecina de confianza a quien la familia llama "doña Lupe", quien cuida a Mateo y a Sofia mientras Diego esta en la escuela. Una tia materna, tia Rosa, tambien ayuda ocasionalmente los fines de semana. Un vecino, Mike, a veces lleva a Lucia al trabajo nocturno cuando su carro no arranca.

Mateo asiste de dia a Little Stars Daycare mientras Lucia trabaja su turno matutino, de 8:00 a.m. a 2:30 p.m., de lunes a viernes. Su maestra principal es la maestra Carmen, y la asistente del salon es Miss Sara. Segun ambas, Mateo es carinoso y sigue instrucciones simples en ingles, pero su produccion verbal es dificil de entender incluso para companeros familiarizados con el, como su amigo Josue, con quien juega casi todos los dias durante el recreo.

En casa se habla principalmente espanol con Lucia y con doña Lupe, e ingles mezclado con espanol con Diego, quien esta en tercer grado y es dominante en ingles. Lucia estima que Mateo escucha espanol aproximadamente el 70% del tiempo en el hogar y ingles el 30% restante, principalmente a traves de television y de su hermano. Mateo tiene un perro pequeno llamado Rocky, y durante la sesion de evaluacion dijo espontaneamente "Rocky no" cuando el perro aparecio en una foto del libro de estimulacion, para indicar que el perro de la foto no era igual al suyo.

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS

Se administraron las siguientes pruebas estandarizadas, con apoyo de materiales en espanol cuando estuvieron disponibles, y con observacion clinica estructurada para complementar areas sin normas en espanol:

| Prueba / Subprueba | Puntaje estandar | Percentil | Intervalo de confianza |
|---|---|---|---|
| Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5) Spanish - Auditory Comprehension | 82 | 12 | 76-88 |
| PLS-5 Spanish - Expressive Communication | 71 | 3 | 65-77 |
| PLS-5 Spanish - Total Language Score | 75 | 5 | 70-80 |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) - Sounds-in-Words | 68 | 2 | 61-75 |
| Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals-5 (CELF-5) - Screening Test (administrado en ingles) | puntaje de corte no alcanzado | -- | -- |

Edad equivalente en comprension auditiva (PLS-5): 3;2-3;6
Edad equivalente en comunicacion expresiva (PLS-5): 2;9-3;0

Durante la administracion de las pruebas, Mateo se mostro cooperador la mayor parte del tiempo, aunque requirio descansos breves y reforzadores visuales (bloques, pegatinas) para mantener la atencion durante tareas mas largas. Siguio instrucciones de dos pasos en espanol en 8 de 10 ensayos y en ingles en 6 de 10 ensayos.

MUESTRA DE HABLA Y ANALISIS FONOLOGICO

Se obtuvo una muestra de habla espontanea de aproximadamente 100 enunciados durante juego libre y conversacion estructurada. Mateo combino palabras sueltas y frases cortas de dos a tres palabras, con inteligibilidad estimada en el 40% para oyentes desconocidos y en el 75% para su madre.

Se observaron los siguientes patrones de error consistentes con un trastorno fonologico, presentes tanto en espanol como en ingles:

- Sustitucion de /s/ por [t] en posicion inicial: dijo "tapo" por "sapo".
- Omision de consonantes finales: dijo "pa" por "pan".
- Simplificacion de grupos consonanticos: dijo "poto" por "plato".
- Sustitucion de /ɾ/ por [d]: dijo "cada" por "cara".
- En ingles, sustitucion de [w] por /r/: dijo "wabbit" por "rabbit".

Con claves articulatorias (mod cues), Mateo logro producir /s/ inicial correctamente en 5 de 10 intentos imitados, y con claves minimas (min cues) logro 2 de 10. Esto sugiere estimulabilidad moderada para este sonido, un indicador positivo para el pronostico de terapia.

El vocabulario expresivo de Mateo incluye sustantivos familiares, verbos de accion comunes y algunos adjetivos descriptivos basicos, pero carece de marcadores gramaticales consistentes (articulos, concordancia de genero, tiempos verbales) tanto en espanol como en ingles. Usa principalmente enunciados de una y dos palabras, con longitud media de enunciado estimada en 1.8 morfemas.

OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES Y SOCIALES

Durante la sesion, Mateo mostro buen contacto visual y disfruto de los juegos de causa y efecto. Se frustro en dos ocasiones cuando no pudo comunicar lo que queria, recurriendo a senalar y a jalar la mano de la evaluadora. En el salon de clase, segun la maestra Carmen y Miss Sara, Mateo participa en juego paralelo mas que en juego interactivo, y rara vez inicia conversacion con companeros aparte de Josue. Lucia y doña Lupe ambas reportan que entienden la mayoria de lo que dice Mateo en casa, pero que personas fuera del circulo familiar cercano, incluyendo a tia Rosa en ocasiones, piden que se les repita o traduzca.

IMPRESIONES DIAGNOSTICAS

Con base en los resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas, el analisis de la muestra de habla, y la informacion proporcionada por la familia y el personal de la guarderia, Mateo presenta un trastorno fonologico de moderado a severo (F80.0) junto con un trastorno del lenguaje expresivo de moderado a severo (F80.1), con comprension relativamente mas fuerte pero tambien por debajo del rango esperado para su edad. Los hallazgos son consistentes en ambos idiomas, lo cual apoya que las dificultades no se explican unicamente por exposicion a dos lenguas, sino que representan un trastorno primario del desarrollo del lenguaje.

No se identifican preocupaciones de voz ni de fluidez en este momento. La audicion fue documentada como normal en la evaluacion mas reciente de Mr. Tom en Piedmont Regional Ear, Nose, Throat and Audiology - Morrisville Campus.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda que Mateo continue recibiendo terapia de habla y lenguaje de manera individual, con una frecuencia de dos sesiones de 30 minutos por semana, prestadas en espanol con apoyo de ingles segun sea necesario, consistente con el Resultado 2 del IFSP actual.

2. Se recomienda el uso de un enfoque de Cycles para la intervencion fonologica, dirigido a los procesos de omision de consonante final, simplificacion de grupos consonanticos, y sustitucion de /s/ y /ɾ/.

3. Para apoyar el desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo y la interaccion social, se recomienda incorporar estrategias del modelo Hanen (por ejemplo, seguir la iniciativa del nino, ampliar sus enunciados) tanto en terapia como en el hogar y en la guarderia.

4. Se sugiere capacitar a Lucia y a doña Lupe en estrategias simples de estimulacion del lenguaje que puedan usar durante las rutinas diarias, dado el horario de trabajo de la madre y el papel central de doña Lupe como cuidadora.

5. Se recomienda coordinar con la maestra Carmen y Miss Sara en Little Stars Daycare para reforzar objetivos de comunicacion durante las actividades grupales, incluyendo oportunidades estructuradas de juego con companeros como Josue.

6. Se recomienda una reevaluacion formal en aproximadamente 6 meses para medir el progreso y determinar la necesidad de servicios continuos antes de la transicion fuera del programa de intervencion temprana.

7. Dado que no se identificaron preocupaciones de alimentacion que requieran intervencion especializada en este momento, no se recomienda referencia a terapia de alimentacion, pero se sugiere monitorear la seleccion de texturas por parte de la familia.

Esta evaluacion se facturo bajo el codigo 92523 (evaluacion de habla y produccion de sonidos del habla con evaluacion de lenguaje), y los servicios de terapia continuada se facturaran bajo el codigo 92507, segun autorizacion vigente.

Agradezco a la familia de Mateo, y en especial a Lucia, por su tiempo y disponibilidad durante esta evaluacion, a pesar de su horario de trabajo tan exigente. Quedo disponible para contestar cualquier pregunta sobre este informe.

Atentamente,

Veronica Castillo Mora, M.S., CCC-SLP
