Client Name: Mateo Alejandro Vásquez Ibarra    Preferred Name: Teo    Date of Birth: March 14, 2021
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;7    Gender: Male    Primary Language(s): Spanish and English
Evaluation Dates: September 22, 2025, September 29, 2025    Report Date: October 6, 2025
Referral Source: Dr. Priya Nandakumar, Cornerstone Pediatrics    Record/Case #: CC-4471920
Medicaid ID: 987654321A    CDSA Case #: FR-20394
Address: 412 Birchfield Lane, Lenoir, NC  28645
Home Phone: (828) 555-0147    Cell Phone (Mother): 828-555-9923    Cell Phone (Father): (828) 555-7781
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Fernanda Ibarra Reyes (mother), Diego Vásquez Morales (father)
Examiner: Isabel Marín Dobson, M.S., CCC-SLP    Employer: Foothills Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Interpreter: Yolanda Cepeda, certified medical interpreter    Service Coordinator: Marcus Teague, Children's Developmental Services Agency – Foothills Regional Office

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo is a 4;7-year-old bilingual (Spanish/English) boy referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Priya Nandakumar of Cornerstone Pediatrics following parental and preschool teacher concern regarding unintelligible speech, limited expressive vocabulary in both languages, and difficulty following multi-step directions in the classroom. His mother, Lucía Fernanda Ibarra Reyes, reports that Teo is frequently frustrated when unfamiliar listeners cannot understand him and has begun pointing or gesturing instead of attempting verbal communication. Mateo's preschool teacher, Ms. Hannah Whitfield, at the Head Start program's Juniper Street site, corroborates these concerns and notes that Teo relies heavily on peer Bryson to interpret his requests during center time. This evaluation was conducted to determine Teo's current speech sound production, receptive and expressive language skills across both of his languages, and eligibility for speech-language intervention services.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Fernanda Ibarra Reyes; his father, Diego Vásquez Morales; his older sister, Camila Vásquez Ibarra (age 7); and his infant brother, Santiago Vásquez Ibarra (age 11 months), at the family home on 412 Birchfield Lane in Lenoir. His maternal grandmother, Rosa Elena Reyes Campos, lives in the same household and provides daytime childcare for Teo and his younger brother while both parents work. The family also has a dog, Max, a mixed-breed terrier that Teo frequently talks about during sessions.

Lucía reports that the home language is primarily Spanish; she and Rosa Elena Reyes Campos speak almost exclusively Spanish with Teo, while his father, Diego, and older sister, Camila, mix Spanish and English depending on the activity. Teo began attending the Head Start program at age three and has received increasing exposure to English through classroom instruction, though his mother estimates his daily language exposure remains approximately 70% Spanish and 30% English. Lucía was born in the village of El Rosario, Sololá, Guatemala, and immigrated to the United States at age nineteen; her extended family, including Teo's maternal grandfather, still resides there and can be reached by phone at +502 5512-3348. Diego was born in Jalisco, Mexico, and moved to North Carolina as a teenager with his parents. His mother, Marisol Vásquez Delgado, who Teo refers to as his "abuela Mari," still travels frequently between Lenoir and her hometown of Tepatitlán de Morelos, and can be reached at 011-52-378-555-6124 when abroad.

Lucía works second shift as a seamstress at a textile plant (planta textil Carolina Fiber Mills) near Hickory, and Diego is employed as a laborer with Vega & Sons Construction Company (compañía de construcción Vega & Sons). Diego previously worked at a produce farm (finca Hillside Produce Farm) during the summer growing season and occasionally returns there for seasonal work. Rosa Elena Reyes Campos previously worked part-time for a cleaning service (servicio de limpieza Sparkle Clean Commercial Cleaning) before taking on full-time childcare responsibilities for the family. Teo's aunt, Marisol Ibarra Reyes, works as a cashier at a grocery store (tienda de comestibles Food Lion) in Lenoir and occasionally helps with pickup from the Head Start program. The family also frequently mentions a restaurant (restaurante El Jalisco) owned by Diego's cousin, where the family gathers on weekends and where Teo has been observed attempting to order food in both languages.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 35 weeks gestational age at Piedmont Crossing Health System – Mill Creek Campus on March 14, 2021, following a pregnancy complicated by preeclampsia and premature rupture of membranes. Delivery was via emergency cesarean section. Birth weight was 4 lbs 11 oz and Apgar scores were 6 at one minute and 8 at five minutes. Teo required admission to the Piedmont Crossing Health System – Mill Creek Campus Neonatal Intensive Care Unit for 18 days due to respiratory distress and feeding difficulties, including documented difficulty with suck-swallow-breathe coordination. He was managed in the NICU by neonatologist Dr. Samuel Okonkwo-Reyes and required a nasogastric feeding tube for the final week of his hospitalization before successfully transitioning to oral feeds. Lucía reports that Teo was monitored for aspiration risk during this period and underwent a modified barium swallow study, which was reportedly normal prior to discharge.

Following discharge, Teo was followed by pediatrician Dr. Priya Nandakumar at Cornerstone Pediatrics for routine well-child care and prematurity-related follow-up. At approximately 14 months of age, he experienced recurrent bilateral otitis media, ultimately requiring bilateral myringotomy with tube placement performed by Dr. Teresa Galvão at Blue Ridge ENT & Audiology Associates. Lucía reports at least five documented ear infections between ages one and three. A subsequent audiological evaluation at 26 months of age, conducted by audiologist Dr. Whitley Combs, showed normal hearing sensitivity bilaterally with type A tympanograms following tube placement; hearing has not been formally reassessed since that time, though Lucía denies any current concerns regarding Teo's hearing. Teo has no reported history of seizures, head injury, or other significant medical conditions. His only current medication is a daily multivitamin. Developmental milestones were reportedly delayed, with independent walking achieved at 19 months and first words (in Spanish) emerging around 22 months, with slower than typical vocabulary growth noted thereafter by both parents.

EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

Teo was first referred to Children's Developmental Services Agency – Foothills Regional Office at age two following parental concern about delayed language, and he received home-based early intervention speech therapy from approximately June 2023 through his third birthday. Records from that period, reviewed with parental consent, indicate slow but steady progress in single-word vocabulary in both languages. Teo transitioned to center-based services and currently attends the Head Start program at the Juniper Street site five days per week, where his classroom teacher is Ms. Hannah Whitfield and the classroom assistant is Mr. Caleb Boone. Prior to Head Start, Teo briefly attended Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy for approximately four months before the family withdrew him due to concerns that staff were not comfortable supporting a Spanish-dominant child.

Ms. Whitfield reports that Teo is social and enjoys parallel play with classmates Owen and Bryson but becomes withdrawn during large-group instruction and struggles to answer "wh-" questions or retell simple events from his day. She notes that unfamiliar adults, including substitute teachers, frequently misunderstand Teo's speech, and that he has begun to rely on Bryson to relay messages to adults on his behalf. The family receives support from Smart Start of Caldwell County and has previously accessed services through WIC for nutritional supplementation during Teo's infancy.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Teo presented as a friendly, cooperative child who separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with the examiner, Isabel Marín Dobson, across both evaluation sessions. Rapport was established quickly using toys and books in both English and Spanish. Teo demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks of approximately 15-20 minutes with brief movement breaks and was motivated by social praise and a sticker reward system. His play skills were age-appropriate, including representational and sequenced pretend play (for example, feeding a stuffed animal and putting it to bed). No concerning behaviors were noted. Interpreter Yolanda Cepeda was present for portions of the parent interview to ensure Lucía's full participation and understanding of assessment procedures, though Lucía is conversationally proficient in English.

Speech intelligibility was judged to be approximately 40% in context with an unfamiliar listener (the examiner) and approximately 65% as reported by familiar family members. Given Teo's documented history of early language exposure to Spanish as the primary language, with increasing but still developing exposure to English, this evaluation included formal and informal measures in both languages consistent with best practices for bilingual language assessment, in order to differentiate a speech-language disorder from the expected process of second-language acquisition.

ASSESSMENT TOOLS ADMINISTERED

The following standardized and informal measures were administered: Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) – Morphosyntax, Semantics, and Phonology subtests; Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3); Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish Edition – Auditory Comprehension and Expressive Communication subtests; an English-language spontaneous speech-language sample; a Spanish-language spontaneous speech-language sample obtained with parental and interpreter support; an oral mechanism examination; and a hearing screening (pure-tone, bilateral, pass/refer).

TEST RESULTS

Oral Mechanism Examination: Structures and function of the lips, tongue, hard and soft palate, and jaw were within normal limits for speech production. No signs of structural abnormality, overt or submucous cleft, or dysarthria were observed. Diadochokinetic rates were judged to be mildly reduced for age but adequate to support intelligible connected speech.

Hearing Screening: Teo passed a bilateral pure-tone hearing screening at 20 dB HL across 500, 1000, 2000, and 4000 Hz, conducted at the start of the first evaluation session, consistent with Lucía's report of no current hearing concerns.

Articulation and Phonology: On the GFTA-3, Teo obtained a raw score corresponding to a Standard Score of 71 (95% CI: 65-77), placing him at the 3rd percentile for his age. Error patterns observed included gliding of liquids (for example, "wion" for "lion"), final consonant deletion, and cluster reduction, consistent across both English and Spanish productions, indicating a phonological disorder rather than a dialectal or bilingual-related difference, since these patterns occurred in both of his languages and are not accounted for by typical Spanish-influenced English or typical second-language acquisition patterns. Specific phoneme errors included inconsistent production of /s/ clusters, substitution of [w] for /ɾ/ in Spanish words (for example, "pewo" for "perro"), and omission of final /s/ in both languages. Teo was stimulable for /k/ and /g/ in isolation and in syllables with moderate cues, but not in connected speech.

Receptive and Expressive Language – Spanish (PLS-5 Spanish Edition):

Auditory Comprehension: Standard Score 76 (95% CI: 70-82), 5th percentile, Age Equivalent 2;6-2;9
Expressive Communication: Standard Score 72 (95% CI: 66-78), 3rd percentile, Age Equivalent 2;3-2;6
Total Language Score: 72, 3rd percentile

Receptive and Expressive Language – English (BESA Semantics and Morphosyntax, administered in English):

Semantics subtest: Standard Score 68, 2nd percentile
Morphosyntax subtest: Standard Score 65, 1st percentile
Bilingual Index Score: 64, indicating language skills that fall below expectations even when accounting for his bilingual language development and relative amount of exposure to each language

Spontaneous language samples in both English and Spanish supported the standardized findings. In a 15-minute Spanish sample, Teo's Mean Length of Utterance was 2.8 morphemes, below expectations for his age. He demonstrated omission of grammatical morphemes, including articles and verb conjugation markers, and relied heavily on two-word combinations (for example, "más agua," "no quiero"). In the English sample, Teo produced primarily single words and occasional two-word combinations (for example, "more juice," "go home"), with minimal use of grammatical morphemes such as plural -s, present progressive -ing, and third-person singular -s, which is lower than would be expected even for a child in the early stages of English acquisition relative to his length of exposure.

Narrative and Pragmatic Skills: Teo demonstrated emerging but limited narrative skills in both languages, typically labeling pictures rather than producing connected narratives. When asked to retell a simple three-event story in Spanish with picture support, he produced one to two relevant utterances with moderate cues and prompting, falling short of the expected 3 of 5 story grammar elements for his age. Pragmatic skills, including eye contact, turn-taking, and joint attention, were judged to be age-appropriate in both structured and unstructured contexts.

IMPRESSIONS

Based on the results of this comprehensive bilingual evaluation, Teo presents with a speech sound disorder (phonological disorder) and a language disorder affecting both his receptive and expressive language skills, evident across both of his languages, Spanish and English. His difficulties cannot be attributed solely to second-language acquisition, limited English exposure, or dialectal variation, given that error patterns, below-average standard scores, and reduced morpheme production were documented consistently in both Spanish, his dominant and first-exposed language, and English. This cross-linguistic pattern, combined with his history of prematurity, recurrent otitis media, and early expressive language delay, is consistent with a primary speech-language impairment.

Teo's reduced speech intelligibility, estimated at approximately 40% with unfamiliar listeners, is significantly impacting his ability to participate in classroom instruction and peer interaction, as reflected in reports from Ms. Whitfield regarding his reliance on peer interpretation. His scores across formal measures in both languages fall within the clinically significant range (below the 10th percentile), supporting eligibility for speech-language intervention services under North Carolina's Developmental Disabilities criteria and corresponding educational eligibility categories.

Diagnostic Impressions:
1. Speech Sound Disorder (Phonological), consistent with ICD-10 code F80.0
2. Developmental Language Disorder, Mixed Receptive-Expressive, consistent with ICD-10 code F80.2

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Teo qualifies for and would benefit from individual speech-language therapy services, recommended at a frequency of two sessions per week, 30 minutes per session, delivered bilingually or with interpreter support to maximize carryover across both home and school settings.
2. Therapy should target phonological patterns identified above (gliding, final consonant deletion, cluster reduction) using an evidence-based approach such as the Cycles Phonological Remediation Approach, applied consistently across both Spanish and English targets.
3. Expressive and receptive language goals should address grammatical morpheme use, sentence expansion, and narrative skill development in both languages, incorporating strategies consistent with the Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" program to support parent-mediated language facilitation at home.
4. The family is encouraged to continue supporting Teo's Spanish language development at home, as strong first-language skills support, rather than hinder, second-language acquisition.
5. A referral is recommended to the Children's Developmental Services Agency – Foothills Regional Office for continued service coordination through Marcus Teague, and for consideration of an updated audiological evaluation given Teo's history of recurrent otitis media and tube placement, despite currently passing a hearing screening.
6. Collaboration between this clinician, Ms. Whitfield, and Mr. Boone in the Head Start classroom is recommended to support consistent strategy use, including visual supports and reduced reliance on peer interpretation by classmates such as Bryson.
7. Re-evaluation is recommended in approximately 12 months, or sooner if parent or teacher concerns increase, to monitor progress and reassess eligibility.

This evaluation and report were completed by the undersigned. Please contact this office with any questions regarding these findings or recommendations.

Isabel Marín Dobson, M.S., CCC-SLP
Foothills Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Office Phone: 828-555-3042    Fax: 828-555-3043
Email: imarindobson@foothillspeechnc.com

October 9, 2026 – 2:15 PM–3:00 PM, home-based visit, 412 Willow Creek Lane, Hickory, NC 28601.

I, Priya Nair, MS, CCC-SLP, provided bilingual speech-language intervention for Mateo Alvarez Cruz (4;2) through Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC, also known as Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language or "CPSLT." Session occurred with su mamá Lucía Rodríguez present; Carlos Alvarez called in briefly from work.

Mateo was born at 32-week gestational age, birth weight 1,580 grams, at Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital – Hemby Campus on June 14, 2022, with a 5-minute Apgar of 7. He spent 21 days in the Atrium Health Levine Children's NICU under Dr. Samuel Okafor, neonatology, and is followed for recurrent otitis media by Dr. Emily Grant at Atrium Health Levine Children's ENT & Audiology – Hemby Campus.

Today Mateo worked on CV and CVC word shapes targeting /k/ and /g/ in initial position using PROMPT cueing. He produced "caca" and "gato" with mod cues at 7/10 trials, and spontaneously labeled his dog, saying "Canela come," at 3 of 5 opportunities. Receptive tasks mirrored PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension goals; he pointed correctly to 8/10 items.

Lucía reported that Mateo's abuela in Mexico, Rosa Cruz, calls daily to practice songs; her number is +52 55 5512 3456. Lucía can be reached at (704) 555-0192 or 704.555.0133. The family's CDSA of the Foothills service coordinator, Marisol Tan, can be reached at 919-555-0147 regarding IFSP Outcome 2 review, scheduled for November 3, 2026.

Sofía (7) joined briefly and modeled "más gato" for Mateo, supporting peer-style modeling. Recommend continued twice-weekly sessions; discussed referral to WIC for nutrition follow-up given slow weight gain since 26 months.

child is Mateo Alejandro Cruz Rodríguez date of birth January 20, 2024 nc itp child id 4482910 medicaid id 921047583B secondary insurance member id BCBS 7729301-02 cdsa record number 55821 authorization number AUTH-2026-00847 mother is Lucía Rodríguez Díaz cell 828-555-0198 father is Esteban Cruz Morales both parents were present for this visit along with mateo's older brother Diego Cruz Rodríguez who is five and the maternal grandmother Rosa Díaz who helps care for mateo most afternoons while his parents work service coordinator for this case is Jennifer Alvarez from foothills cdsa who was not able to attend this visit due to a scheduling conflict but reviewed the outcomes by phone beforehand

mateo was born at 37 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 5 pounds 8 ounces and apgar scores of 8 and 9 he was referred to foothills cdsa on March 3, 2025 by his pediatrician Dr. Patricia Nguyen at Caldwell Pediatric Associates due to limited babbling and no first words by eighteen months initial eligibility evaluation was completed March 18, 2025 using the PLS-5 and initial ifsp was written April 2, 2025 the most recent prior review was October 2, 2025 and todays visit is the annual review next review is due April 1, 2027

preocupaciones de la familia la mamá lucía dijo "mateo entiende todo lo que le decimos pero no nos puede decir lo que quiere y eso lo frustra mucho" she said he will point and grunt and sometimes hit his brother diego when he cant get his message across el papá esteban agregó "yo quiero que el pueda ir a la escuela hablando como los demás niños no quiero que se burlen de el" he also mentioned worry about mateo starting pre k in a year and not being ready la abuela rosa said "yo le hablo en español todo el día pero a veces siento que no me entiende bien" family priorities for this period are one that mateo uses more words to ask for things at home two that he stops hitting when hes frustrated and three that the family gets more strategies to use in spanish since most of the home language is spanish and english is used more at daycare

daily routines mateo wakes around 7:00 am and eats breakfast with diego at the kitchen table mom reports breakfast is a good time for requesting because he loves "leche" and will reach but does not yet say the word clearly he attends Little Explorers Child Development Center monday through friday from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm where his teacher is Ms. Brenda Hall ms. hall reports mateo plays near a peer named Ellie during free play but mostly plays alongside her rather than with her at home after daycare rosa picks him up and they do snack time together then free play with his toy trucks and the family dog Max who mateo loves to chase around the living room bath time is around 6:30 pm and bedtime routine starts at 7:30 pm with a book that mom reads mostly in spanish

otras agencias involucradas the family receives wic benefits through Caldwell County WIC and food assistance has been coordinated through Caldwell County DSS in the past year diego previously attended Caldwell County Early Head Start before starting kindergarten and the family has been connected with Smart Start of Caldwell County for a childcare subsidy that helps pay for mateo's spot at little explorers father esteban works full time at Carolina Furniture Works in Lenoir and mother lucía works part time at Ingles Market so childcare coverage during the day depends on little explorers and after four thirty on rosa

present levels this slp administered the PLS-5 on September 20, 2026 in a combination of english and spanish following best practice for bilingual assessment auditory comprehension standard score fell in the 73-83 range with a percentile rank of 4th and age equivalent of 2;0–2;3 expressive communication standard score was 68 with a percentile of 2nd and age equivalent of 1;9–2;0 total language score fell at 70 confidence interval 65-75 which places mateo well below average for his chronological age of 2;8 informal spanish language sample collected in the home showed similar patterns of understanding exceeding expression receptively mateo follows two step directions in both languages such as "dame el carro y cierra la puerta" and points accurately to body parts and familiar objects when named in either language expressively he has approximately 10 words total across both languages including "mamá" "papá" "agua" produced as "aba" and "más" he does not yet combine words he communicates primarily through pointing pulling adults by the hand and occasional grunts

speech sound patterns noted include final consonant deletion as in "pa" for "pan" and substitution of /t/ for /k/ as in "tasa" for "casa" which is developmentally appropriate for his age so no concerns there this is primarily an expressive and receptive language delay rather than a pure speech sound disorder occupational therapist Kayla Simmons also evaluated fine motor skills and found mild delays in bilateral coordination that may be contributing to frustration behaviors billing for this evaluation visit was coded cpt 92523 with icd-10 F80.9 developmental disorder of speech and language unspecified

resultados del ifsp y estrategias

Outcome 1 mateo will use at least ten different single words consistently across home and daycare to request preferred items and activities within six months criteria is three to five independent productions daily without a model strategies include using a hand over hand or gestural model first then fading to verbal model only using Hanen "it takes two to talk" strategies of following his lead expanding his communication attempts and commenting rather than always asking questions parents and rosa will narrate daily routines in spanish since that is the dominant home language and this slp will model the same strategies in english during daycare consultation visits so both languages are supported this slp provided min to mod cues during todays session and mateo successfully requested "más" 4 of 5 trials using a picture card system similar to PECS that was introduced at this visit

Outcome 2 mateo will combine two words together such as action plus object or person plus object within six months to communicate wants needs and comments criteria is five spontaneous two word combinations across three consecutive sessions strategies include expansion where an adult takes his one word utterance and adds one more word modeling short phrases during play and using the picture card system to build two picture requests parents reported at todays visit that mateo has started pointing to two pictures in sequence at home which is an early sign of this skill emerging

Outcome 3 mateo will use an acceptable replacement behavior such as pointing to a picture or pulling an adult to a desired item instead of hitting when frustrated in at least 8 of 10 observed frustrating situations within four months strategies include teaching the family and daycare staff to recognize the early signs of frustration and offer the picture system before frustration escalates ms hall agreed to use the same picture cards at little explorers so the strategy is consistent across settings rosa expressed some hesitation saying "a mi me da pena usar las tarjetas en publico" and this slp reassured her that consistency matters more than setting and offered to make a smaller travel size set of cards for her to carry

discussion of progress since the last review mateo has made slow but steady progress his vocabulary has grown from approximately four words at the last review to ten words now and he is beginning to combine gestures with vocalizations more consistently the family has been very consistent with carryover of strategies at home which this slp commends father esteban noted "yo sé que esto toma tiempo pero quiero ver que el progrese más rápido" this slp explained that language development especially in a bilingual home follows its own pace and that exposure to both languages is a strength not a cause of the delay and should continue

transition planning was briefly discussed since mateo will turn three in January 2027 and the family was given information about the preschool exceptional children process through the local school system a transition conference will be scheduled closer to his third birthday and jennifer alvarez will coordinate that meeting with the family and this slp

service delivery mateo currently receives speech language therapy one time per week for 45 minutes in the home and consultation at little explorers once monthly for 30 minutes occupational therapy with kayla simmons occurs biweekly for 30 minutes in the home next speech session is scheduled for October 8, 2026 at 2:00 pm and the monthly daycare consultation is scheduled for October 15, 2026 at 1:00 pm family was given written copies of all three outcomes in both english and spanish and signed consent for continued services today parents signature obtained from both lucía rodríguez díaz and esteban cruz morales this slp signature sofía martínez m.s. ccc-slp date October 1, 2026

recommendations for next steps continue weekly direct speech language therapy in the home with monthly consultation visits at daycare continue biweekly ot services reassess with a formal language measure in approximately six months to monitor progress toward outcome one and two provide family with additional bilingual vocabulary cards for use at home and daycare coordinate with jennifer alvarez regarding upcoming transition planning as mateo approaches his third birthday follow up by phone with caldwell county wic regarding continued nutrition support since the family mentioned at todays visit that their wic certification is due for renewal next month end of note

Buscando: Nota de sesión diaria – Mateo Hernández Cruz

De: María Fernanda Castillo, patóloga del habla y lenguaje <mcastillo@carolinaspeechpartners.com>
Para: Lucía Hernández <luciah82@gmail.com>
CC: Carla Jiménez, intérprete <cjimenez@interpretnc.org>
Fecha: 6 de octubre de 2026, 4:10 p.m.
Asunto: Nota de sesión diaria – Mateo Hernández Cruz

Buenas tardes, Sra. Hernández:

Le escribo con la nota de la sesión de hoy, 6 de octubre de 2026, a las 3:30 p.m. en el centro preescolar Semillitas del Alba, en calle Elm 245, Greensboro, condado de Guilford.

S: La maestra, Srta. Daniela Ponce, reportó que Mateo tuvo una mañana tranquila y jugó con su compañero Josué en el área de bloques. Su abuela, Rosa, lo recogerá hoy porque usted trabaja doble turno: por la mañana en Sabores del Sur y por la noche en ABC, la agencia de cuidado a domicilio.

text:
Child Name: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Mendoza ("Teo")
Date of Birth: April 8, 2024
Chronological Age at Review: 26 months
Medicaid ID: 804552913B
CDSA Record Number: CR-20248815
Program: NC Infant-Toddler Program
CDSA Office: Caldervale CDSA, Pinebrook, Caldervale County
Service Coordinator: Brenda Walsh, M.Ed.
IFSP Review Date: September 22, 2026
Next Review Due: March 22, 2027
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Mendoza Rivas (madre); Héctor Cruz Lima (padre)
Home Address: 412 Willow Bend Lane, Pinebrook, 27529
Home Phone: (910) 555-0148
Parent Email: lucia.mendozarivas82@example.com
Primary Home Language(s): Spanish and English
Report Author: Elena Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP
Contract Agency/Employer: Tarheel Pediatric Therapy, PLLC
Evaluation Dates: September 10, 2026 and September 15, 2026
Primary Eligibility: Established Condition — F80.1 expressive language disorder, F80.0 phonological disorder

INFORMACIÓN DE LA FAMILIA / FAMILY INFORMATION

Teo is a 26-month-old boy who lives with both parents, Lucía and Héctor, his older sister Sofía ("Sofi", age 5), and his maternal grandmother, Rosa Mendoza Rivas, who moved in with the family in June 2026 to help with childcare while Héctor works at Pinebrook Auto Body and Lucía works part-time at the front desk of Caldervale Family Dental. The family also has a dog, Rocky, who Teo follows around the house and tries to call by name.

Mateo was born at Caldervale Regional Medical Center at 37 weeks gestation, birth weight 5 lbs 9 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9. Lucía reports an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery. Medical history is otherwise unremarkable; pediatrician Dr. Anjali Patel has followed Teo since birth and has no concerns about hearing, which was confirmed with a passed newborn screen and a repeat audiological screening on August 3, 2026.

Abuela Rosa speaks only Spanish with Teo; Héctor speaks mostly Spanish at home with some English; Lucía code-switches throughout the day depending on the activity. Sofi is fully bilingual and often translates for Teo when he gets frustrated, which Lucía notes both helps and, at times, lets him avoid trying to talk himself.

COORDINACIÓN DE SERVICIOS / SERVICE COORDINATION

Brenda Walsh has served as Teo's service coordinator through Caldervale CDSA since the initial referral in July 2026. Brenda coordinated the eligibility evaluation, connected the family with Caldervale County DSS for Medicaid redetermination, and attends IFSP meetings along with Elena Ortiz, the speech-language pathologist, and occupational therapist Keisha Brown. Brenda confirmed with the family that all currently assigned providers will continue as listed through the next review.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA / FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES

When asked about her main concerns, Lucía said, "Lo que más me preocupa es que Teo no habla como Sofi hablaba a esta edad. Ella ya decía frases completas, y él solo dice unas pocas palabras sueltas." She added, in English, "He gets so frustrated — he'll point and grunt, and if we don't guess right away, he just melts down."

Héctor shared a related priority during the home visit on September 15, 2026: "Yo quiero que pueda decirme lo que necesita sin que Sofi tenga que hablar por él. A veces siento que ella es la voz de él." Abuela Rosa agreed, noting that Teo "entiende todo lo que le decimos, en español y en inglés, pero le cuesta mucho sacar las palabras."

The family's priorities, as stated at the meeting, are:
1. Que Teo pueda pedir lo que quiere con palabras, not just gestures — family wants functional requesting in both languages.
2. Clearer speech sound production so that people outside the family, like Early Head Start staff, can understand him.
3. Strategies Abuela Rosa can use during the day while the parents are at work, since she is the primary daytime caregiver.
4. Continued help navigating paperwork for Caldervale County WIC Program and childcare subsidy renewal through Caldervale County Partnership for Children.

RUTINAS DIARIAS / DAILY ROUTINES

Teo's typical day begins around 6:45 a.m., when Abuela Rosa gets him up and dressed while Lucía prepares breakfast. Héctor leaves for Pinebrook Auto Body by 7:00 a.m.. Teo attends Pinebrook Early Head Start on weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., where his classroom teacher, Marisol Alvarez, reports he plays alongside a classmate named Jaxon but rarely initiates verbally with peers.

After pickup around 4:00 p.m., Teo has a snack, plays in the backyard with Rocky, and watches a short video in Spanish before dinner, which the family eats together around 6:30 p.m.. Bath time is around 7:15 p.m., and bedtime routine with Lucía or Abuela Rosa reading a bilingual picture book begins at 7:45 p.m., with lights out by 8:15 p.m..

Teo eats most table foods but is a picky eater; Lucía has worked with a nutritionist, Patricia Gómez, through Caldervale County WIC Program on expanding his diet beyond rice, beans, and quesadillas.

OTRAS AGENCIAS / OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

The family currently works with several agencies in addition to Caldervale CDSA:
- Caldervale County DSS: Medicaid and SNAP benefits, with redetermination due November 2026.
- Caldervale County WIC Program: nutrition supplementation and feeding guidance, coordinated by Patricia Gómez.
- Caldervale County Partnership for Children: childcare subsidy supporting Teo's enrollment at Pinebrook Early Head Start.
- Pinebrook Early Head Start: center-based early education, classroom teacher Marisol Alvarez.

Brenda Walsh noted that the DSS redetermination paperwork was mailed to the family's address on Willow Bend Lane and that she will follow up with the family by October 15, 2026 to confirm it was submitted.

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT

Receptive and expressive language were assessed using the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), administered in both English and Spanish with items alternated by dominance per item content, supplemented by the Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA) for cross-linguistic comparison. On the PLS-5, Teo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 88 (21st percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 73 (4th percentile, confidence interval 68–78), with an age equivalent of 16 months. These scores reflect a significant gap between what Teo understands and what he can say, consistent across both languages.

Articulation and phonology were assessed with the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3), yielding a standard score of 70 (2nd percentile). Teo demonstrated final consonant deletion, stopping of fricatives, and velar fronting, with phonemes /k/ and /g/ produced as [t] and [d] respectively across both languages.

During a structured imitation task, Teo was shown a photo of the family dog, Rocky, and asked to label it. His production, "Wocky," demonstrated gliding of /ɾ/ and was consistent across three trials (3 of 3). When shown a photo of his sister, Sofi, and asked "¿quién es?", he produced "Fofi," substituting /f/ for the initial fricative and demonstrating consistent medial consonant production. Both productions were elicited with moderate cues and a modeled target.

Functional communication observed across the two evaluation sessions included single-word requests ("más," "agua," "arriba"), used in 8 of 10 opportunities with gestural support, and no observed two-word combinations. Play skills, assessed informally, were age-appropriate; Teo engaged in pretend feeding of a stuffed animal and sequenced a three-step block task independently.

IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Teo will use two-word combinations to request preferred items and activities in both English and Spanish, in 8 of 10 opportunities across three consecutive sessions, as measured by provider observation and parent report.

Strategies: Elena Ortiz will use bilingual language stimulation and expansion techniques during weekly sessions, modeling two-word combinations immediately after Teo's single-word attempts (e.g., "más" → "más agua"). Abuela Rosa and Lucía will be coached using strategies adapted from Hanen's "It Takes Two to Talk" principles, translated and modeled bilingually, focusing on following Teo's lead and pausing to allow initiation before providing a model. Héctor will practice the same strategies during evening routines on weekends.

Outcome 2: Teo will produce word-initial /k/ and /g/ correctly in single words with minimal verbal cues in 4 of 5 trials across two consecutive sessions.

Strategies: Elena Ortiz will target velar fronting using a Cycles approach, cycling through core vocabulary words in both languages that contain word-initial /k/ and /g/ (including "casa," "gato," "cookie," "go"). Home practice cards with these words, including an image of Rocky paired with the target word "perro"/"dog" rather than his name, will be sent home weekly to avoid reinforcing the name itself as the practice target.

Outcome 3: Abuela Rosa and Lucía will report using at least two specific communication strategies during daily routines (mealtime, bath time, play) within 60 days of this review, as measured by caregiver report at the next session.

Strategies: Elena Ortiz will provide direct coaching during home visits scheduled around Abuela Rosa's availability, since she is present during the majority of Teo's waking hours. Coaching will include modeling expansion and "wait time" strategies during snack and bath routines, with written and verbal instructions provided in Spanish. Brenda Walsh will check in by phone at the one-month mark to troubleshoot any barriers to carryover.

PLAN DE SERVICIOS / SERVICE DELIVERY

Speech-language therapy: individual sessions, 92507 (modifier GN), once weekly for 45 minutes, Tuesdays from 9:15 a.m. to 10:00 a.m., in the home on Willow Bend Lane, provided by Elena Ortiz through Tarheel Pediatric Therapy, PLLC, beginning October 1, 2026 and continuing through the next review on March 22, 2027.

Occupational therapy consultation: Keisha Brown will provide a one-time consultation visit on October 20, 2026 from 1:00 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. to screen fine motor skills related to feeding and self-feeding independence, at the family's request after Lucía raised concerns about utensil use.

Service coordination: Brenda Walsh will conduct a home visit on November 5, 2026 at 10:30 a.m. to review progress on all three outcomes and confirm the status of the DSS and WIC paperwork discussed above.

All services will be delivered in the family's preferred language for each activity, with Elena Ortiz providing services bilingually without need for a separate interpreter, given her fluency in both English and Spanish.

CONSENTIMIENTO Y FIRMAS / CONSENT AND SIGNATURES

Lucía Mendoza Rivas and Héctor Cruz Lima reviewed this IFSP in both English and Spanish during the meeting on September 22, 2026 and provided verbal and written consent for all outcomes and services listed above. Abuela Rosa was present for the portions of the meeting addressing daily caregiving strategies and indicated she understood and agreed with the plan.

Prepared by: Elena Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP
Reviewed by: Brenda Walsh, Service Coordinator, Caldervale CDSA
Date Signed: September 22, 2026

text:
CONFIDENTIAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

**Child's Name:** Mateo Alejandro Hernández Cruz (called "Teo" at home and at Little Learners Daycare)
**Date of Birth:** March 14, 2022
**Chronological Age at Evaluation:** 4;2
**Date of Evaluation:** May 19, 2026, 9:15 AM–11:40 AM
**Language(s) of Evaluation:** English and Spanish
**Medicaid ID:** 784215639K
**Case Record Number:** CT-40217
**Evaluating Clinician:** Camila Ortiz Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (English/Spanish), Little Learners Program
**Referral Source:** Dr. Anjali Patel, pediatrician, Catawba Valley Pediatrics
**Service Coordinator:** Brittany Shuford, Catawba County CDSA

**Parents/Guardians:** Lucía Cruz Ramírez (mother) and Jesús Hernández Flores (father, known as "Chuy")
**Home Address:** 418 Magnolia Lane, Hickory, Catawba County, NC 28601
**Contact Phone:** (828) 555-0147
**Clinic Contact:** cortiz@littlelearnersprogram.com | www.littlelearnersprogram.com

---

**BACKGROUND INFORMATION**

Teo is a 4;2-year-old boy referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by Dr. Anjali Patel due to parent and teacher concern regarding limited intelligibility, reduced expressive vocabulary in both English and Spanish, and difficulty following multi-step directions. Teo currently attends Little Learners Daycare five days a week, where his classroom teacher is Ms. Ana López and the classroom assistant is Ms. Brenda Settle. He has been enrolled at Little Learners Daycare since he was 18 months old. Teo also receives weekly developmental therapy through Catawba County CDSA under an active Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP), Outcome 2, and this evaluation was requested to update present levels of performance ahead of the annual review.

This evaluation was conducted in a mixed-language format reflecting the home language environment. Background information was obtained through parent interview with Lucía Cruz Ramírez, review of records from Catawba Valley Pediatrics and Catawba County CDSA, a classroom observation at Little Learners Daycare on May 12, 2026, direct standardized and informal assessment, and clinical observation across two settings.

**BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY**

Teo was born on March 14, 2022 at Carolina Pines Hospital in Hickory at 38 weeks gestation following an uncomplicated pregnancy. Birth weight was 6 lbs 11 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. Lucía Cruz Ramírez reported no complications during delivery and a brief hospital stay of two days.

Medical history is notable for recurrent otitis media between 8 months and 22 months of age, treated with multiple courses of antibiotics; bilateral myringotomy tubes were placed on November 3, 2023. Hearing was reassessed by audiology on January 9, 2026 and documented as within normal limits bilaterally. There is no reported history of seizure, significant head injury, or hospitalization beyond ear-related procedures. Teo passed his newborn hearing screening and has met gross motor and fine motor milestones within expected ranges per Dr. Anjali Patel's records. A developmental-behavioral screening completed at Catawba County CDSA on February 2, 2026 flagged communication as the primary area of concern, with motor and social-emotional domains within age expectations.

Family medical history is significant for a paternal cousin, José Hernández Luna ("Pepe"), who received speech therapy services between ages three and five. Jesús Hernández Flores reported that he himself was a "late talker" as a child but did not receive formal services.

**FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY**

Teo lives with his parents, Lucía Cruz Ramírez and Jesús Hernández Flores, and his older sister, Guadalupe Hernández Cruz ("Lupita"), age 7, at the family home on Magnolia Lane in Hickory. Lupita attends second grade and is described by her parents as verbally advanced for her age in both languages. The family also keeps a dog, Rocky, who Teo frequently talks about and imitates; Lucía Cruz Ramírez noted that one of Teo's clearest spontaneous phrases is when he says "Teo pet Rocky" while patting the dog.

The home language environment is primarily Spanish, spoken by both parents approximately 70% of the time, with English used increasingly by Lupita and during daycare pickup conversations. Lucía Cruz Ramírez works part time at Catawba Valley Manufacturing, and Jesús Hernández Flores works full time at Hickory Furniture Mart. Because of their work schedules, Teo is cared for several afternoons a week by a family babysitter, Rosa María Delgado, who speaks only Spanish with him, and occasionally by his maternal grandmother, Elena Ramírez, who lives nearby in Conover.

Parents report that Teo said his first words around 16 months, later than his sister, and that his vocabulary growth has been slow in both languages since then. He is described as a social child who enjoys playing with his cousin José Hernández Luna during family gatherings and with classmates at daycare, including Juan Martínez ("Juanito"), Emma Sue Carpenter, and Diego Alvarez. Ms. Ana López reported that Teo often gestures or pulls peers toward objects rather than using words to request, and that unfamiliar listeners frequently ask her to "translate" what he says.

A family friend, Marta Gonzalez, originally recommended Little Learners Daycare to the family when Teo was an infant, and she has remained in occasional contact with Lucía Cruz Ramírez since.

**CURRENT SERVICES**

Teo currently receives weekly developmental therapy and monthly occupational therapy consultation through Catawba County CDSA. His occupational therapist is Hannah Kim. The family was connected to Catawba County CDSA through a referral from Smart Start of Catawba County when concerns were first raised at his 2-year well-child visit. This evaluation will inform a recommendation for direct speech-language services through Little Learners Program, to run alongside his existing IFSP services.

Proposed session schedule, pending authorization, is as follows:

| Day | Start | Stop | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 9:00 AM | 9:45 AM | Little Learners Program, office |
| Wednesday | 3:30 PM | 4:15 PM | Little Learners Daycare, classroom |
| Friday | 10:00 AM | 10:45 AM | Little Learners Program, office |

Classroom-based sessions at Little Learners Daycare will be coordinated with Ms. Ana López and will target carryover of goals with same-age peers present.

**ASSESSMENT TOOLS AND PROCEDURES**

The following standardized and informal measures were administered across two languages, with order and language counterbalanced to reduce fatigue effects:

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English and Spanish editions
- Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax and Semantics subtests
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Oral mechanism examination
- Language sample analysis (conversational and narrative, English and Spanish), transcribed using SALT conventions
- Parent and teacher interview and checklist (unstandardized)
- Clinical observation during structured and unstructured play

**TEST RESULTS**

*Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) – Spanish Edition*

| Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% CI | Age Equivalent | Range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auditory Comprehension | 76 | 5th | 70–82 | 2;9–3;1 | Below Average |
| Expressive Communication | 71 | 3rd | 65–77 | 2;4–2;8 | Below Average |
| Total Language Score | 72 | 3rd | 67–77 | 2;6–2;10 | Below Average |

*Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) – English Edition*

| Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% CI | Age Equivalent | Range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auditory Comprehension | 79 | 8th | 73–85 | 2;11–3;3 | Below Average |
| Expressive Communication | 74 | 4th | 68–80 | 2;7–2;11 | Below Average |
| Total Language Score | 75 | 5th | 70–80 | 2;8–3;0 | Below Average |

Conceptual scoring, which credits a correct response in either language, yielded a Total Language Score of 83 (13th percentile, 95% CI 77–89), suggesting that single-language scores likely underestimate Teo's combined linguistic knowledge but that a true delay is also present.

*Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA)*

| Subtest | Scaled Score | Percentile | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| Morphosyntax, Spanish | 5 | 5th | Below Average |
| Morphosyntax, English | 6 | 9th | Below Average |
| Semantics, Spanish | 6 | 9th | Below Average |
| Semantics, English | 7 | 16th | Low Average |

*Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)*

Standard Score: 78 (7th percentile, 95% CI 72–84)

Sounds-in-Words errors included fronting of /k/ and /g/ (e.g., "tat" for target "cat"), gliding of /r/ (e.g., "wabbit" for "rabbit"), and inconsistent production of the Spanish tap /ɾ/ in medial position, observed as "pego" for target "perro". Stimulability testing showed that Teo could approximate /k/ in isolation with moderate cues but not yet in words.

**LANGUAGE SAMPLE AND INFORMAL OBSERVATIONS**

A 50-utterance conversational language sample was collected in each language during play with toy animals and a farm set. Teo's mean length of utterance in Spanish was 2.3 morphemes and in English was 2.1 morphemes, both below expectations for his age. Utterances were coded with SALT conventions; omissions of grammatical morphemes were marked with bound-morpheme codes such as [EW] for early word forms. Teo relied heavily on nouns and a limited set of early verbs ("want," "go," "no"), with frequent omission of articles, copulas, and subject-verb agreement markers in both languages. He combined two to three words at most (e.g., "Teo quiere agua," "more juice please").

During a structured narrative retell task using a wordless picture book, Teo produced primarily single-word labels and required maximal cues to sequence events, correctly ordering only 2 of 5 story elements. In contrast, during unstructured play he initiated requests and protests consistently, and he used gestures and eye contact effectively to repair communication breakdowns, suggesting relatively intact pragmatic skills despite limited structural language.

Intelligibility was judged to be approximately 50% to an unfamiliar listener in connected speech and approximately 75% to a familiar listener, consistent with parent and teacher report.

**ORAL MECHANISM AND HEARING**

Oral peripheral examination revealed structures and function within normal limits for speech; no evidence of significant oral-motor weakness, dysarthria, or structural abnormality was observed. Hearing sensitivity is documented as within normal limits per the January 9, 2026 audiological evaluation, and tympanic membranes were reported as clear on most recent pediatric exam.

**CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS**

Based on standardized and informal assessment, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Teo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language delay affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with a true bilingual language disorder rather than typical second-language acquisition. Scores fall consistently below average across both standardized languages and both receptive and expressive domains, and conceptual scoring, while higher, remains within the delayed range. Teo also presents with a moderate speech sound disorder affecting both languages, characterized by fronting, gliding, and inconsistent production of the Spanish tap /ɾ/, consistent with a phonological pattern rather than an isolated articulation error.

Teo's strengths include relatively intact pragmatic and social communication skills, strong nonverbal problem-solving during play, and a supportive, language-rich bilingual home and daycare environment. His history of recurrent otitis media during a developmentally sensitive period for speech-sound learning is a likely contributing factor, though current hearing is within normal limits.

These findings are consistent with the concerns raised by Lucía Cruz Ramírez and Jesús Hernández Flores, by Ms. Ana López at Little Learners Daycare, and by Dr. Anjali Patel, and support continued eligibility for IFSP services as well as the addition of direct speech-language therapy.

**RECOMMENDATIONS**

1. Teo qualifies for and would benefit from direct speech-language therapy targeting expressive and receptive language in both Spanish and English, delivered bilingually, at a frequency of two to three 30–45 minute sessions per week, as outlined in the proposed schedule above through Little Learners Program.

2. Therapy should address phonological patterns affecting intelligibility in both languages, using a cycles-based phonological approach and targeting the Spanish tap /ɾ/, velar sounds /k/ and /g/, and liquid /r/.

3. Continue collaboration with Catawba County CDSA and occupational therapist Hannah Kim to ensure coordinated goals across Teo's IFSP, with the current review scheduled for August 4, 2026.

4. Continue classroom-based support at Little Learners Daycare, including modeling expanded utterances and pairing new vocabulary with gestures, coordinated with Ms. Ana López and Ms. Brenda Settle.

5. Encourage continued exposure to and use of both Spanish and English at home; discourage any reduction of Spanish input, as bilingualism is not a cause of Teo's delay and supports his long-term language development.

6. Monitor for future transition planning; the family should begin exploring dual-language preschool options, including the Title I preschool program at Oakwood Elementary, ahead of Teo's transition out of IFSP services near his third birthday review.

7. Re-evaluate audiological status if any recurrence of middle ear infection occurs, given the history of chronic otitis media.

8. Reassess speech and language skills in approximately 6 months to monitor progress and adjust the treatment plan as needed.

Thank you for the opportunity to evaluate Teo. Please contact me at cortiz@littlelearnersprogram.com or visit www.littlelearnersprogram.com with any questions regarding these results or recommendations.

Respectfully submitted,

Camila Ortiz Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Little Learners Program
Hickory, NC

Nombre del niño: Mateo Hernández Ramírez
Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de febrero de 2023
Edad actual: 2;8
Número de expediente: CDSA-00482913
Número de Medicaid: N847293015A
Madre: Lucía Rodríguez
Padre: Carlos Hernández
Dirección: 214 Calle Pine, Burlington, Condado de Alamance
Teléfono: (336) 555-0147
Coordinadora de servicios: María Torres
Oficina CDSA: Piedmont CDSA, oficina del Condado de Alamance
Terapeuta del habla y lenguaje bilingüe: Jennifer Smith, M.S., CCC-SLP
Agencia de terapia: Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services
Fecha de la reunión del IFSP inicial: 3 de marzo de 2026
Fecha de esta revisión: 2 de octubre de 2026

RESUMEN DE LA HISTORIA

Mateo nació a las 37 semanas de gestación, con un peso de 2,680 gramos y un puntaje de Apgar de 8/9. Su mamá, Lucía Rodríguez, reporta que el embarazo fue sin complicaciones mayores. Mateo vive con sus padres y su hermana mayor, Rosa Hernández Ramírez, de 5 años, en una casa alquilada en Burlington. Rosa asiste a la escuela primaria del área y, según la familia, le encanta jugar con Mateo y "traducirle" lo que él quiere decir.

La familia es bilingüe: en casa se habla principalmente español, aunque Carlos Hernández también usa frases en inglés cuando está presente la abuela paterna, Elena Hernández, quien vive con ellos dos veces por semana para ayudar con el cuidado de los niños.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA

Durante la entrevista de revisión, Lucía Rodríguez expresó, en sus propias palabras: "Mateo todavía no dice casi nada, solo señala lo que quiere. Cuando está frustrado grita o jala mi mano hacia el refrigerador." Carlos Hernández agregó: "En la guardería dicen que él los entiende, pero no habla con los otros niños."

Las prioridades que la familia identificó para esta revisión son:
1. Que Mateo use más palabras para pedir comida y juguetes en casa.
2. Que pueda comunicarse con su hermana Rosa sin frustrarse.
3. Que la maestra en la guardería entienda mejor sus intentos de comunicación.

RUTINAS DIARIAS

Lucía Rodríguez trabaja en el restaurante El Rancho Mexicano, en el turno de la tarde, mientras que Carlos Hernández trabaja para Pinnacle Construction Company como ayudante de construcción. Debido a estos horarios, Mateo pasa las mañanas con su abuela Elena Hernández y asiste al Centro de Desarrollo Infantil Little Steps las tardes de lunes a viernes, en el salón de las Mariposas, a cargo de la maestra Ms. López. La maestra López reporta que Mateo sigue instrucciones simples en inglés y en español, pero rara vez inicia comunicación verbal con sus compañeros, entre ellos Daniela y Josué.

La familia también mencionó que la tía materna, Sol Martínez, cuida a Mateo los fines de semana y ha notado que él se comunica mejor con gestos cuando está cansado. Sol Martínez trabaja en Sparkle Clean Services, una compañía de limpieza, en turnos nocturnos, por lo que su disponibilidad varía.

La rutina típica incluye desayuno a las 7:00 a.m., llegada a la guardería a las 8:30 a.m., y cena familiar alrededor de las 6:30 p.m., momento que la familia identificó como una buena oportunidad para practicar vocabulario de comida.

OTRAS AGENCIAS Y PROGRAMAS INVOLUCRADOS

La familia recibe apoyo del Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Alamance (DSS del Condado de Alamance) para asistencia con vivienda, y está inscrita en el programa WIC de la Oficina WIC del Condado de Alamance. Lucía Rodríguez también mencionó que está en lista de espera para el programa Early Head Start de Alamance, con la esperanza de que Mateo pueda recibir más horas de intervención temprana estructurada. La coordinadora, María Torres, confirmó que la Partnership for Children del Condado de Alamance también ofrece un programa de visitas domiciliarias que la familia está considerando.

EVALUACIÓN Y DIAGNÓSTICO

Se administró el PLS-5 (Preschool Language Scale-5) en español, con los siguientes resultados: Comprensión Auditiva, puntaje estándar de 73 (percentil 4), rango de confianza 68-78; Expresión Verbal, puntaje estándar de 65 (percentil 1), rango de confianza 60-70. La edad equivalente para expresión verbal fue de 14 meses, comparada con su edad cronológica de 2;8. También se observó el uso espontáneo de vocabulario: Mateo produjo de forma consistente las palabras "agua", "mamá" y "más", pero omitió consonantes finales, por ejemplo produciendo "aba" en vez de "agua".

El diagnóstico actual es trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo, código F80.2. Los servicios se facturaron bajo los códigos 92523 (evaluación de habla y lenguaje) y 92507 (tratamiento individual de habla, lenguaje o audición), con el modificador GN correspondiente a servicios de terapia del habla-lenguaje.

RESULTADOS (OUTCOMES) Y ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1: Mateo usará al menos 10 palabras nuevas de forma espontánea en el hogar y en la guardería para pedir objetos preferidos, con 80% de precisión a lo largo de dos sesiones consecutivas.
Estrategias: Modelado de lenguaje aumentado durante rutinas de comida y juego; uso de la técnica Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" para guiar a los padres en la expansión de los enunciados de Mateo; la maestra López implementará modelado paralelo durante actividades de merienda en el salón de las Mariposas.

Resultado 2: Mateo combinará dos palabras (por ejemplo, "más agua") en al menos 8 de 10 oportunidades observadas durante la sesión de terapia.
Estrategias: Uso del enfoque PROMPT para apoyar la producción de secuencias de dos palabras; práctica de rutinas de juego con Rosa como modelo de lenguaje entre hermanos, bajo supervisión de los padres.

Resultado 3: La familia reportará mayor confianza al interpretar las señales comunicativas de Mateo en al menos 3 de 5 rutinas diarias identificadas (comida, baño, juego).
Estrategias: Entrenamiento a los padres sobre espera estructurada (tiempo de espera de 5 segundos) y uso de claves visuales simples; coordinación con Sol Martínez para mantener consistencia los fines de semana.

Durante la sesión de revisión, Mateo logró producir el fonema /m/ de forma correcta en posición inicial en 9 de 10 intentos, pero continuó omitiendo el fonema /k/ en posición final, sustituyéndolo por una oclusiva glótica [ʔ]. Se usaron niveles de apoyo mod cues y, en algunos casos, max cues para elicitar producciones de dos palabras.

FECHAS DE SERVICIO

Las sesiones de terapia del habla y lenguaje se proveen dos veces por semana, generalmente los lunes y jueves, en el hogar de la familia. Las últimas sesiones documentadas fueron el 21 de septiembre de 2026, el 24 de septiembre de 2026 y el 28 de septiembre de 2026. La próxima revisión semestral del IFSP está programada para el 15 de marzo de 2027.

COORDINACIÓN Y SEGUIMIENTO

La coordinadora de servicios, María Torres, continuará comunicándose con la familia mensualmente para verificar el progreso hacia los resultados establecidos y para coordinar la solicitud al programa Early Head Start de Alamance. Se recomendó además una evaluación auditiva de seguimiento, ya que no se ha documentado una prueba auditiva formal desde el nacimiento. La familia fue referida al Hospital Alamance Regional Medical Center para dicha evaluación, con cita pendiente de confirmación por parte de la clínica de audiología.

Lucía Rodríguez firmó el consentimiento para continuar los servicios actuales y para compartir información con la guardería Little Steps y con la maestra López, a fin de alinear las estrategias entre el hogar, la terapia y el salón de clases.

Notas adicionales: la familia solicitó que los materiales educativos se entreguen en español, y expresó interés en recibir orientación bilingüe adicional por parte de Jennifer Smith sobre el desarrollo típico del lenguaje en niños bilingües, ya que les preocupa que exponer a Mateo a dos idiomas esté "retrasando" su habla. Se explicó a la familia, con el apoyo de materiales en español proporcionados por Piedmont CDSA, que el bilingüismo no causa ni empeora los retrasos de lenguaje, y que las estrategias actuales apoyan el desarrollo en ambos idiomas.

Firma de la terapeuta: Jennifer Smith, M.S., CCC-SLP
