MEMBER PROFILE: Carolina Piedmont Children's Developmental Services Agency (CDSA)  Referral Source:  Dra. Patricia Núñez, Pediatra  Report Date:  September 18, 2026

Child's Name:  María José Fuentes Alvarado  Preferred Name:  Majo  Date of Birth:  April 2, 2022  Age at Evaluation:  4;5  Sex:  Female  Medicaid ID:  WX48217639K  Case/Record ID:  CPCDSA-2026-01184

Parent/Guardian:  Lucía Fuentes Beltrán  Relationship:  Madre biológica  Address:  214 Willowbrook Lane, Siler City, NC 27344  Phone (home):  (919) 555-0167  Phone (cell):  (919) 555-8842  Email:  lucia.fuentes84@example.com

Father:  Héctor Fuentes Beltrán  Occupation:  Supervisor at Piedmont Poultry Processing  Primary Language(s):  Español, some English

Evaluating Clinician:  Marisol Castellanos-Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual SLP  Employer (full legal name):  Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC  Employer (short form):  Carolina Bilingual Therapy  Employer (abbreviation):  CBTP  Interpreter Present:  No (clinician bilingual, Spanish-dominant evaluation conducted directly)  Evaluation Location:  CPCDSA satellite office, Pittsboro, NC  Evaluation Date(s):  September 10, 2026 and September 12, 2026  Evaluation Time:  9:30 AM to 11:15 AM

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Majo was referred by her pediatrician, Dra. Patricia Núñez, after her mother Lucía reported, en la cita de los 4 años, que "mi hija casi no habla, y cuando habla nadie le entiende, ni yo." Lucía noted that Majo's cousin Yamileth, who is the same age, "ya habla oraciones completas" and that the family has started to worry about the gap. Héctor Fuentes Beltrán added during intake that at home Majo "se frustra mucho, llora y nos jala la ropa" when she cannot make herself understood. The family requested evaluation in both languages because Majo is cared for primarily in Spanish at home but hears English from her older half-sister Daniela Beltrán and at the nonprofit after-school program she attends.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Historia de nacimiento y desarrollo (Birth and Developmental History): Lucía Fuentes Beltrán reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with routine prenatal care at Chatham Regional Medical Center. Majo was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, birth weight 6 lbs 14 oz, Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. No NICU stay was required. Lucía reported that Majo met early gross motor milestones within expected limits (sat sin apoyo around 6 months, walked independently around 13 months) but that first words were delayed; mother recalls first recognizable word ("mamá") around 22 months, with no combination of two words noted until closer to 3;6.

Historia médica (Medical History): Majo had recurrent otitis media between ages 18 and 30 months, with pressure equalization (PE) tubes placed by Dr. Randall Okafor, ENT, at UNC Children's Specialty Clinic on March 3, 2025. Tubes extruded naturally and no further infections have been reported since early 2026, per mother's report and confirmed in a letter from Dr. Okafor dated June 11, 2026. Vision screening at the pediatrician's office was within normal limits on August 5, 2026. No seizure history, no significant illnesses, and family denies any genetic syndrome diagnosis. Majo is up to date on immunizations per Lucía's report.

Historia familiar y lingüística (Family and Language History): The household includes Lucía, Héctor, Majo, her half-sister Daniela Beltrán (age 11), and periodically the paternal grandmother Rosalba Beltrán Soto, who helps with childcare "cuando yo trabajo turno de noche," per Lucía. The family identifies Spanish as the primary home language; Héctor reports limited English proficiency, while Lucía described herself as "medio medio" — able to manage basic conversational English from working part-time at a local daycare laundry service. Daniela is reportedly fluent in both languages and often translates for her mother at medical appointments. The family regularly attends services at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Esperanza in Siler City, where Majo participates in a toddler Sunday school class led by Hermana Flor Patiño. The family also uses the Chatham County Smart Start home-visiting program, and a home visitor, Araceli Domínguez, M.Ed., has been coming monthly since January 2026 to support early literacy. Majo additionally attends a twice-weekly bilingual playgroup at the Siler City Public Library run through a community literacy grant, where staff member B. Hinton has noted that Majo "mostly plays alone or points instead of talking to the other kids."

Historia educativa (Educational History): Majo does not currently attend a formal daycare or preschool program. The family had considered enrolling her at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare in Pittsboro but deferred enrollment pending this evaluation. She has had informal playdates with a neighbor's child, Esmeralda Chávez, age 4, whose mother reports that the two girls "communicate fine with gestures but Majo doesn't really talk even in Spanish with her."

Pets: The family has a small dog named Canela, and Lucía reported that Majo often says "nene" when pointing at the dog, which the family believes may be an attempt at "Canela" or possibly a generalized word for animals; this was explored further during testing (see Articulation/Phonology section below).

PROCEDURES ADMINISTERED

Testing was conducted across two sessions at the CPCDSA satellite office in Pittsboro. Session one focused on receptive and expressive language testing in Spanish; session two focused on English screening, articulation/phonology, and oral-motor examination. Lucía was present for both sessions and provided informal translation checks when requested, though the clinician, Marisol Castellanos-Reyes, is fully bilingual and administered all Spanish-language measures directly without need for an interpreter.

The following measures were administered:

Preescolar Language Scale, Fifth Edition — Spanish Edition (PLS-5 Spanish)
Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals, Fifth Edition (CELF-5) — select English subtests for cross-linguistic comparison
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) — administered in Spanish with phonemic transcription
Oral-motor and feeding screening (informal, clinician-developed checklist)
Parent interview and language sample analysis (Spanish, 50-utterance sample)
Hearing screening referral (deferred; recent audiological results reviewed from July 22, 2026 visit at UNC Children's Specialty Clinic, within normal limits bilaterally)

TEST RESULTS

Preescolar Language Scale-5 Spanish Edition (PLS-5 Spanish)

Subtest                           Raw Score    Standard Score    Percentile Rank
Auditory Comprehension            18          71               3rd
Expressive Communication          14          65               1st
Total Language Score              --           66               1st

Majo's performance on the PLS-5 Spanish fell within the severely delayed range for both receptive and expressive language, with a Total Language Score of 66 (1st percentile), consistent with a confidence interval of 61-71. During testing, Majo was able to identify 6 of 10 common objects by name receptively but used primarily single words and some gestures expressively. She produced phrases such as "mas agua" (quiero más agua) and "no quero" (no quiero) spontaneously, but struggled to combine more than two words consistently. Age equivalent for Expressive Communication was calculated at 24 months, a gap of approximately 29 months from her chronological age of 4;5.

Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals-5 (CELF-5) — English Screening

Given that Majo has limited English exposure, only the Sentence Structure and Word Structure subtests were administered as a screening measure, with results interpreted cautiously given exposure history.

Subtest                  Standard Score    Percentile
Sentence Structure       68               2nd
Word Structure            70               2nd

These English scores are considered an underestimate of true ability given minimal English language exposure, and are included here only to document current functioning at the time of referral, not as evidence of a second, independent impairment.

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), administered in Spanish

Raw Score: 34  Standard Score: 72  Percentile: 3rd

Phonemic inventory analysis revealed inconsistent production of /r/ and /ɾ/ sounds, with frequent substitution of [d] for /ɾ/ (e.g., "do" for "dos"... note: distinct from the error on "carro," below). Majo also demonstrated final consonant deletion in multisyllabic words, e.g., producing "pa" for "pan" and "sol" correctly but "flo" for "flor." Cluster reduction was noted on words with /tr/ and /pl/ clusters, e.g., "tes" for "tres." She produced "cao" for "carro," reflecting liquid simplification of medial /r/. Stimulability testing showed that with moderate cues (mod cues), Majo could approximate /ɾ/ in isolation but not consistently within words. Intelligibility was judged to be approximately 40% to unfamiliar listeners and 65% to familiar listeners (per parent report), consistent with mother's comment that "solo yo le entiendo, y a veces ni yo."

Oral-Motor and Feeding Screening

Informal oral-motor examination revealed adequate lip closure, mildly reduced tongue lateralization, and age-appropriate dentition. No significant feeding concerns were reported by Lucía, though she noted that Majo "es bien quisquillosa" (picky) with textured foods, preferring purees and soft foods over items requiring more chewing, such as raw vegetables. This pattern will be monitored but does not currently meet criteria for a separate feeding diagnosis.

Language Sample Analysis

A 50-utterance spontaneous language sample was collected during play-based interaction using toy animals and a dollhouse. Mean length of utterance (MLU) in morphemes was calculated at 1.8, which falls well below the expected range of 3.0-3.5 for her chronological age. Majo used primarily single-word and two-word combinations (e.g., "mamá agua," "no quero," "mas leche"), with occasional use of possessive constructions ("mío"). She demonstrated use of the SALT code [EW] (word-finding/exact word) at several points where she appeared to search for a label before abandoning the attempt and pointing instead. Pragmatically, Majo initiated interaction by pointing and vocalizing but rarely used verbal bids spontaneously; most verbal output was elicited by direct questions from the clinician or mother.

IMPRESSIONS

Majo presents with a severe mixed receptive-expressive language disorder in her primary language (Spanish), as evidenced by standard scores on the PLS-5 Spanish falling more than 2 standard deviations below the mean across both receptive and expressive domains (Total Language Score 66, 1st percentile, CI 61-71). Given that English exposure is minimal and that the family's stated goal is for Majo to communicate effectively first in Spanish at home, her English screening scores are not interpreted as evidence of a distinct, separate disorder but rather reflect limited current exposure overlaid on an underlying primary language impairment. Co-occurring speech sound disorder is present, with articulation/phonology standard score of 72 (3rd percentile) on the GFTA-3 (Spanish administration), characterized by cluster reduction, final consonant deletion, and liquid simplification patterns consistent with a phonological process disorder rather than a purely articulatory/motor-based disorder. These findings are consistent with the diagnostic impression of a Language Disorder with accompanying Speech Sound Disorder (ICD-10: F80.2, Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder; ICD-10: F80.0, Phonological Disorder), warranting continued intervention per IFSP.

History of recurrent otitis media and PE tube placement is a relevant contributing factor to the speech sound disorder, though the persistence of errors well past the resolution of middle ear issues (confirmed otitis-free since early 2026) suggests the disorder is not solely attributable to fluctuating hearing history and warrants treatment independent of medical status. Family's bilingual environment should be supported and not viewed as causative or contributory to the disorder; rather, intervention should proceed bilingually, consistent with best practice for dual-language learners, honoring the home language of Spanish while supporting emerging English exposure through Daniela, the library playgroup, and eventual preschool enrollment.

Majo's pragmatic communication style — primarily gesture- and pointing-based with limited spontaneous verbal initiation — combined with parent-reported frustration behaviors (crying, pulling at clothing) suggests communication breakdown is contributing to behavioral frustration at home, which should improve as expressive language skills develop through intervention.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Majo qualifies for ongoing early intervention services through Carolina Piedmont Children's Developmental Services Agency (CDSA) under an active IFSP, with speech-language therapy services continuing at a frequency of twice weekly, 45-minute sessions, delivered in the home language (Spanish), consistent with IFSP Outcome #2 (functional communication) and IFSP Outcome #3 (speech sound intelligibility).

2. Therapy approach should incorporate Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies to support parent-implemented language facilitation, given Lucía's stated interest in learning strategies she can use "todo el día, no solo en terapia." The clinician will also incorporate elements of the Cycles approach to target phonological patterns (final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, liquid simplification) in a developmentally sequenced manner.

3. Continue to monitor otitis media history; family should follow up with Dr. Okafor or primary pediatrician Dra. Patricia Núñez if any recurrence of ear infection symptoms occurs, given the historical contribution to early language delay.

4. Family is encouraged to continue attending the bilingual playgroup at the Siler City Public Library and the toddler class at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Esperanza, as both provide valuable peer language models and community support; staff member B. Hinton at the library program may be a helpful source of informal progress observations given her familiarity with Majo in a naturalistic peer setting.

5. Consider formal preschool enrollment, ideally at a bilingual program such as Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare, to provide structured peer interaction and additional language modeling in both Spanish and English; this recommendation should be revisited closer to Majo's third birthday transition planning timeline given her upcoming transition out of CPCDSA services.

6. Recommend continued collaboration with the Chatham County Smart Start home visiting program; home visitor Araceli Domínguez, M.Ed. should be included in care coordination communications going forward with family consent, given her ongoing monthly contact with the family and potential to reinforce therapy strategies between sessions.

7. Re-evaluate in approximately 6 months (target: March 2027) to assess progress and determine continued eligibility and service intensity under the IFSP, or sooner if significant concerns arise.

8. Family should be connected, if not already, with Chatham County WIC office for nutritional guidance given reported feeding selectivity, and this clinician will coordinate with the IFSP service coordinator, Noelia Campos, to ensure this referral is documented in the care plan.

9. This clinician recommends that all providers working with the family copy initials-only identifiers where appropriate in shared records per agency practice; for instance, this report references the home visitor by full credential but future shared summaries may refer to her as A.D. per family preference discussed at the close of this evaluation. Similarly, the family requested that correspondence sent to the home use initials for the older sibling, who is sometimes referred to in agency paperwork as D.B. to minimize confusion with another client in the CDSA caseload with a similar name.

This evaluation was completed by Marisol Castellanos-Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist, of Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC (CBTP), under contract with Carolina Piedmont Children's Developmental Services Agency. Questions regarding this report may be directed to the undersigned at Carolina Bilingual Therapy offices, phone (919) 555-7310, or by email at mcastellanos@carolinabilingualtherapy.example.com. CAROLINA BILINGUAL SPEECH & LANGUAGE SERVICES, PLLC
Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Confidential Speech-Language Evaluation Report / Informe Confidencial de Evaluación del Habla y Lenguaje

Child/Niño: Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez (called "Teo" by the family)
Date of Birth: April 9, 2023
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 3;2
Gender: Male
Primary Language(s): Spanish (dominant), English (emerging)
Medicaid ID: 987654321A
Insurance Member ID: BCBS-NC-44218907
NC ITP Child ID: ITP-2023-0456
Record/Authorization Number: AUTH-55102-RC
Evaluation Dates: September 15, 2026 and September 22, 2026
Report Date: October 3, 2026
Evaluator: Daniela Vega, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Service Coordinator: Patricia Nuñez, Central Piedmont CDSA office
Interpreter Present: Marisol Castillo (Spanish/English, parent interview portions)

Referral Source: Central Piedmont CDSA office, following referral from Randolph County DSS and WIC

Address: 214 Maple Hollow Lane, Asheboro, Randolph County, NC 27203
Phone: (336) 555-0147
Email: lucia.rodriguez0409@gmail.com

---

REASON FOR REFERRAL / MOTIVO DE LA REMISIÓN

Teo was referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by his service coordinator, Patricia Nuñez, after concerns were raised by his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Paredes, and by staff at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center regarding limited expressive vocabulary and reduced intelligibility in both English and Spanish. Mrs. Rodríguez Paredes reported, "Teo no dice casi nada, solo señala lo que quiere" ("Teo barely says anything, he just points at what he wants"). She further explained that she had hoped his speech would "catch up" once he started daycare, but instead she has noticed him becoming more frustrated and withdrawn around unfamiliar children. The family was connected to early intervention services through Smart Start of Randolph County and the Central Piedmont CDSA office earlier this year, and this evaluation was requested to update his current IFSP and determine whether additional or modified services are warranted.

---

BACKGROUND INFORMATION / ANTECEDENTES

This evaluation was conducted across two sessions at the family's home on Maple Hollow Lane in Asheboro, with the mother, Lucía Rodríguez Paredes, present for both. The father, Carlos Flores Méndez, joined by phone for the second session due to his work schedule at Piedmont Poultry Processing, Inc., where he works the evening shift. The paternal grandmother, Rosa Paredes de León, who lives with the family and provides daytime care three days a week, was also present for both sessions and contributed extensive observations in Spanish regarding Teo's communication at home. Teo's older brother, Diego Flores Rodríguez, age 7, was at school during both testing sessions but was described by the family as a model for Teo's English exposure and as his most frequent playmate at home.

The family's dog, Rocky, was present during part of the home visit. Teo was observed saying "wa wa" while pointing at Rocky's water bowl, which the mother interpreted as an attempt at "agua." Teo also pulled this evaluator by the hand toward Rocky's bed and said "Wocky" when asked where the dog sleeps, a production the family confirmed is his consistent attempt at "Rocky's" name.

Prior to this evaluation, Teo had not received formal speech-language intervention, although a developmental screening completed through WIC in January 2026 flagged possible delays and prompted referral to the Central Piedmont CDSA office.

---

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA MÉDICA Y DE NACIMIENTO

Teo was born on April 9, 2023 at Carolina Piedmont Regional Medical Center at 34 weeks gestational age following premature labor. Birth weight was 4 lbs 11 oz (2,126 grams). Apgar scores were 6 at one minute and 8 at five minutes. He was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit for 11 days for respiratory support and feeding difficulties, under the care of neonatologist Dr. Anita Krishnan. Mrs. Rodríguez Paredes recalled, "fue muy difícil verlo tan pequeñito con todos esos cables, pensé que algo iba a salir mal" ("it was very hard to see him so small with all those wires, I thought something was going to go wrong").

Following discharge, Teo was followed by pediatrician Dr. Samuel Whitfield at his office in Asheboro for routine well-child care. Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media, with 6 documented episodes between 8 and 24 months of age, and placement of bilateral pressure-equalization tubes at 18 months by an ENT physician. No tubes have required replacement. Hearing was most recently screened within normal limits bilaterally on August 28, 2026. There is no history of seizure, head injury, or significant illness beyond the above. Vision has not been formally assessed, although no concerns were reported by the family or by staff at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center.

Developmental milestones were reported as mildly delayed: sitting independently at 9 months, walking independently at 19 months. First words in Spanish ("mamá," "agua") emerged around 16 months, but vocabulary growth has been slow since, with the mother estimating fewer than 20 consistent words across both languages combined at the time of this evaluation.

---

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y LINGÜÍSTICA

Teo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez Paredes; his father, Carlos Flores Méndez; his brother, Diego Flores Rodríguez; and his paternal grandmother, Rosa Paredes de León. The family's primary home language is Spanish, and extended family, including a maternal aunt who visits most weekends, speak to Teo almost exclusively in Spanish. Carlos Flores Méndez works full time at Piedmont Poultry Processing, Inc., and Lucía Rodríguez Paredes stays home with Teo except for part-time hours assisting a neighbor with housekeeping. A babysitter, Yesenia Cortés, watches Teo on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons so that Lucía Rodríguez Paredes can attend adult English classes offered through Smart Start of Randolph County.

Per parent report using a language exposure questionnaire, Teo's input is approximately 80% Spanish and 20% English, with English exposure primarily occurring through his brother Diego Flores Rodríguez and through his enrollment five mornings a week at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center, where instruction is delivered primarily in English by lead teacher Brianna Holt and assistant teacher Dulce Infante. Ms. Holt reported that Teo "rarely initiates with peers and mostly watches the other children," and noted a classmate, Easton Briggs, who has become a favorite play partner despite the language barrier between them. A second classmate, Nadia Thompson, was also mentioned as someone Teo follows around the classroom during free play.

The grandmother, Rosa Paredes de León, stated, "en casa le hablamos puro español, pero él casi no repite nada, y cuando quiere algo solo llora o jala la ropa" ("at home we speak to him only in Spanish, but he barely repeats anything, and when he wants something he just cries or pulls on our clothes"). No concerns were raised regarding hearing, oral-motor structure, or feeding at this time, aside from the resolved otitis history noted above. The family denied any history of regression in skills previously acquired.

---

REVIEW OF RECORDS / REVISIÓN DE EXPEDIENTES

Records reviewed included prior developmental screenings from WIC, a March 2026 well-child note from Dr. Samuel Whitfield's office, and the family's existing IFSP documentation maintained by the Central Piedmont CDSA office. The family's enrollment and nutrition records are also held by WIC, and the family receives ongoing case management support through Randolph County DSS, including assistance with housing stability earlier in 2026.

The family was additionally connected, through their service coordinator, to the Coalición Hispana de Apoyo Familiar y Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Randolph (CHAFDI), a community-based organization providing bilingual family navigation, transportation assistance, and parent support groups for Spanish-speaking families with young children. CHAFDI has assisted the family with transportation to evaluation appointments and has translated written materials related to the IFSP process. Lucía Rodríguez Paredes reported that CHAFDI staff "me explican todo en español, porque a veces en las citas no entiendo todos los términos" ("they explain everything to me in Spanish, because sometimes at appointments I don't understand all the terms").

---

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES / PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

Assessment occurred across two sessions and included formal standardized testing, parent interview, language sample analysis, and informal observation of play-based interaction in both structured and naturalistic contexts. Marisol Castillo provided interpretation during portions of the parent interview conducted in Spanish and assisted with translation of test prompts administered in Spanish during standardized testing.

Standardized measures administered included:

- Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-Bilingual Edition
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), select subtests administered in English
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Receptive-Expressive Emergent Language Test, Third Edition (REEL-3), parent-report form completed with Lucía Rodríguez Paredes

Informal procedures included a 15-minute language sample collected during unstructured play, an oral-motor examination, and a parent-report checklist of vocabulary in both languages.

---

TEST RESULTS / RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS

On the PLS-5 Spanish-Bilingual Edition, Teo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 76 (5th percentile; 68-84 confidence interval) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 71 (3rd percentile; 63-79 confidence interval), yielding a Total Language score of 72 (3rd percentile; 65-79 confidence interval). Age equivalents were 2;3 for Auditory Comprehension and 2;0 for Expressive Communication, reflecting a gap of approximately 14 months below his chronological age in expressive language, even when assessed in his dominant language.

On the CELF Preschool-3, administered in English given his classroom exposure, Teo achieved a scaled score of 4 on Sentence Structure and a scaled score of 3 on Word Structure, both falling well below the average range of 7-13.

Score Summary Table:

Measure	Domain	Standard/Scaled Score	Percentile	Age Equivalent
PLS-5	Auditory Comprehension	76	5th	2;3
PLS-5	Expressive Communication	71	3rd	2;0
CELF Preschool-3	Sentence Structure	4	2nd	--
CELF Preschool-3	Word Structure	3	1st	--
GFTA-3	Sounds-in-Words	65	1st	<2;0
REEL-3	Expressive Language Ability	70	2nd	1;10

On the GFTA-3, Teo demonstrated a standard score of 65 (1st percentile), with a phonemic inventory limited primarily to /m/, /p/, /b/, /n/, and inconsistent production of /t/ and /d/. Error patterns included final consonant deletion (e.g., "pa" for "pan"), velar fronting (e.g., "tato" for "gato"), and liquid gliding, with /ɾ/ consistently produced as [w] (e.g., "cawo" for "carro"). Intelligibility in context was estimated at 30% to unfamiliar listeners and 60% to familiar listeners, consistent with family report that strangers "casi nunca le entienden" ("almost never understand him").

---

LANGUAGE SAMPLE AND OBSERVATION / MUESTRA DE LENGUAJE Y OBSERVACIÓN

During a 15-minute play-based sample, Teo produced 9 intelligible single words and 2 two-word combinations ("mas agua," "no quiero"), reflecting a mean length of utterance in words (MLU-w) of 1.2. He used pointing and gesture as his primary communication strategy across both sessions, consistent with parent and grandmother report. He demonstrated joint attention and appropriate turn-taking during a shared book task with minimal cueing, and responded to his name and simple one-step directions in Spanish on 8/10 trials and in English on 4/10 trials, suggesting stronger receptive skills in his dominant language.

When shown a picture of a dog similar to Rocky, Teo spontaneously said "guau guau" and, with mod cues, attempted "perro," approximating it as "peo." He required max cues to imitate English target words such as "ball" (produced as "ba") and "more" (produced as "mo"). During a bubble-blowing routine, he produced "mas" with min cues to request continuation, his most consistent two-syllable-level request across both sessions.

An oral-motor examination revealed structures and function within normal limits for speech production, with no evidence of oral-motor weakness, tongue-tie, or dysphagia. Teo demonstrated age-appropriate feeding skills per parent report, with no choking, coughing, or texture aversions noted.

---

IMPRESSIONS / IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Teo presents with a Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with a true language impairment rather than second-language acquisition alone, given his significant delay relative to typical bilingual development milestones and the degree of delay documented even in his dominant language, Spanish. He additionally presents with a Speech Sound Disorder characterized by a restricted phonemic inventory and reduced intelligibility across both languages, with error patterns that are not fully attributable to typical phonological interference between Spanish and English.

Relevant diagnostic codes include F80.9 (Developmental disorder of speech and language, unspecified) and R62.0 (Delayed milestone in childhood). Billing for this evaluation was submitted under CPT codes 92523 and 92522.

Given his history of prematurity, NICU admission, and recurrent otitis media, medical and audiological factors likely contributed to his early communication delays. However, given that his otitis media has been resolved for over a year and his most recent hearing screening was within normal limits, his current language and speech sound profile reflects an ongoing, clinically significant communication disorder that warrants continued, intensive intervention rather than a wait-and-see approach.

---

CURRENT IFSP STATUS AND SERVICES / ESTADO ACTUAL DEL IFSP Y SERVICIOS

Teo has been enrolled in Part C early intervention since February 10, 2026, with his most recent IFSP review conducted on August 18, 2026 through the Central Piedmont CDSA office, service coordinator Patricia Nuñez. His current outcomes and documented progress are summarized below.

IFSP Outcome Review Table:

Outcome 1: Teo will use 20 functional words across settings	Bilingual modeling, parent coaching in Hanen strategies, visual supports	Emerging; 9 words observed	08/18/2026
Outcome 2: Teo will follow one-step directions in both languages	PROMPT-based cueing, naturalistic routines at home and daycare	Partial; stronger in Spanish	08/18/2026
Outcome 3: Teo will increase intelligible consonant productions	Cycles approach targeting final consonants, home practice sheets	Minimal progress; continued deletion patterns	08/18/2026
Outcome 4: Family will access bilingual community supports	Referral to CHAFDI and Smart Start of Randolph County playgroups	Met; family attending monthly	08/18/2026

Current Session Schedule / Horario de Sesiones:

Patient Name: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Fernández ("Teo")
Date of Birth: August 14, 2021
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Evaluation Dates: October 2, 2025 and October 6, 2025
Report Date: October 9, 2025
Primary Home Languages: Spanish and English
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Fernández Ruiz (mother), Alejandro Cruz Mendoza (father)
Referral Source: Dr. Hamid Khan, pediatrician
Service Coordinator: Maria Santos, Piedmont Regional CDSA
Evaluating Clinician: Jennifer Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP/L, Bilingual Spanish-English
Employer: Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC (also referred to as "Triangle Bilingual Speech" or "TBSLT")
Medicaid ID: 748203915T
Record/Case ID: LD-2025-00482
Address: 482 Hollyridge Lane, Garner, NC 27529
County of Residence: Wake County
Phone: (919) 555-0148
Email: jortiz@trianglebilingualspeech.com

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo, known to his family as "Teo," is a 4;2-year-old bilingual (Spanish/English) boy referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Hamid Khan due to parent and teacher concern regarding delayed expressive language, limited intelligibility, and difficulty following multi-step directions in both languages. Lucía Fernández Ruiz reports that Teo has fewer words than his sister Valentina Cruz Fernández ("Vale") did at the same age, and that unfamiliar listeners often cannot understand him. Ms. Angela Lopez, his lead teacher at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare, echoed these concerns and noted that Teo relies heavily on gesture and often repeats classmates' words rather than generating his own phrases.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Teo was born at Carolina Pines Regional Hospital in Garner, NC, at 36 weeks gestational age following a pregnancy complicated by preeclampsia. Birth weight was 5 lb 8 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. He spent 9 days in the NICU for respiratory support and feeding difficulty but required no surgical intervention. Lucía reports no prenatal substance exposure and an otherwise unremarkable delivery aside from the early gestational age.

Medical history is significant for recurrent otitis media, with 6 documented ear infections between 8 months and 24 months of age. Bilateral myringotomy tubes were placed on 03/11/2023 by Dr. Priya Nair, ENT, and extruded spontaneously around 30 months of age; they were not replaced. An audiology evaluation on 01/14/2025 was within normal limits bilaterally, and Teo passed his newborn hearing screening at birth. His CDSA intake form, completed in a day/month/year format common on the family's paperwork, lists his birth date as 14/08/2021.

Teo achieved early motor milestones within normal limits: he sat independently at 6 months and walked at 13 months. Fine motor skills are age-appropriate per parent report. There is no history of seizure, head injury, or loss of consciousness. Family history is notable for a paternal cousin with a diagnosed speech sound disorder, and Alejandro Cruz Mendoza reports his own history of late talking as a child.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Teo lives with his parents, Lucía Fernández Ruiz and Alejandro Cruz Mendoza; his older sister Valentina Cruz Fernández ("Vale," age 7); and the family dog, Rocky, at their home on Hollyridge Lane in Garner. Several nights a week, Teo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Ruiz Delgado, stays in the home and provides childcare; she speaks primarily Spanish with the children.

Lucía reports that the home language environment is approximately 70% Spanish and 30% English. Mom works nights at Southern Star Poultry Processing, where she is employed on the sanitation line, and Rosa or Alejandro cares for the children in the evenings while she is at work. Alejandro works days as a foreman for Carolina Grading & Paving and speaks both Spanish and English with Teo, though he reports feeling "más cómodo" using Spanish.

An initial bilingual intake interview was conducted primarily in Spanish by phone on 3 de marzo de 2025. A brief follow-up call occurred el martes 4 de marzo, at which point Lucía confirmed that Teo had recently moved into the daycare's language-enriched classroom. During these calls, Lucía reported that Teo said his first words around 18 months ("agua," "mamá") and began combining two words by 30 months. She described his expressive vocabulary as noticeably behind that of Vale at the same age. Lucía also noted that Teo frequently mixes languages within the same utterance, which she attributes to normal bilingual development rather than confusion, a view that is consistent with current research on typical code-switching in bilingual children.

The family receives early intervention service coordination through Maria Santos at Piedmont Regional CDSA. Lucía reports the family also receives nutritional support through WIC and has previously attended Smart Start parenting classes. The family is not currently involved with DSS.

Teo attends Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare five days per week, from 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., where his lead teacher is Ms. Angela Lopez and his assistant teacher is Mr. Daniel Reyes. According to Ms. Lopez, Teo plays well with classmates Josué and Camila but becomes frustrated when peers do not understand his requests, sometimes resorting to pushing.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

Teo was assessed over two sessions, October 2, 2025 and October 6, 2025, at the Triangle Bilingual Speech clinic located at 118 Fieldstone Court, Suite 2, Raleigh, NC 27610. Assessment was conducted in both Spanish and English by Jennifer Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP/L, who is fully bilingual; no interpreter was required.

Procedures included standardized testing, a parent interview, a teacher questionnaire completed by Ms. Lopez, language sample analysis, an oral mechanism examination, and an informal articulation and phonology screening. Teo was cooperative throughout both sessions, though he required frequent redirection and mod cues to maintain attention to table-top tasks during the second session.

STANDARDIZED TEST RESULTS

Date | Measure/Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% CI
10/02/2025 | PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | 76 | 5th | 70-82
10/02/2025 | PLS-5 Expressive Communication | 71 | 3rd | 65-77
10/02/2025 | PLS-5 Total Language Score | 72 | 3rd | 67-77
10/06/2025 | GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words | 68 | 2nd | 61-75
10/06/2025 | CELF Preschool-2 Receptive Language Index | 79 | 8th | 74-84
10/06/2025 | CELF Preschool-2 Expressive Language Index | 73 | 4th | 68-78
10/06/2025 | Receptive Language Age Equivalent | — | — | 2;6–3;0

All standardized scores above represent performance combining responses from both of Teo's languages, per each test's bilingual administration guidelines, with credit given for a correct response in either Spanish or English.

CLINICAL OBSERVATIONS / INFORMAL MEASURES

During the language sample, Teo produced an average utterance length of 2.8 morphemes (MLU), consistent with an expressive language level more than 1.5 SD below age expectations. His spontaneous productions included consistent sound substitutions, such as /k/ → [t] and /r/ → /w/. When asked to describe a picture of his pet, Teo said "Rocky tomiendo," intending "comiendo" (eating), illustrating the /k/-for-[t] substitution in context. In another sample, he labeled a picture of a rabbit as "wabbit," reflecting the gliding of /r/.

Standardized articulation testing (GFTA-3, Sounds-in-Words, standard score 68, 2nd percentile) identified the following phonological processes: final consonant deletion (e.g., "ca" for "cat"), cluster reduction (e.g., "top" for "stop"), and gliding of liquids (/r/ → /w/, /l/ → /w/). Intelligibility was judged to be approximately 40% in context for unfamiliar listeners and 65% for familiar listeners such as Lucía and Rosa.

Oral mechanism examination revealed structures and function within normal limits for speech production, with no significant asymmetries and age-appropriate diadochokinetic rates. Teo passed an objective hearing screening performed the same day via otoscopy and tympanometry, within normal limits bilaterally.

IMPRESSIONS

Based on parent interview, teacher report, standardized testing administered in both of Teo's languages, and direct clinical observation, Teo presents with a Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder, ICD-10 code F80.2, and a Speech Sound Disorder, ICD-10 code F80.0. Deficits are evident across both Spanish and English and are not attributable solely to typical bilingual language acquisition, second-language learning, or dialectal variation. CPT code 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression) was used to bill this evaluation.

Teo's receptive and expressive language scores both fall more than 1.5 SD below the mean, and his speech intelligibility is significantly reduced for unfamiliar listeners. These findings, combined with history of recurrent otitis media, support ongoing speech-language intervention.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Teo qualifies for ongoing bilingual speech-language intervention based on standardized scores more than 1.5 SD below the mean in receptive and expressive language domains, as well as impaired speech intelligibility.
2. Individual bilingual speech-language therapy twice weekly, 30 minutes per session, targeting expressive vocabulary, grammatical morphology, and phonological processes. A combined Cycles approach is recommended for phonology, with Hanen-based strategies ("It Takes Two to Talk") incorporated for caregiver coaching.
3. Continued coordination with Maria Santos at Piedmont Regional CDSA regarding IFSP Outcome #2 (communication) and IFSP Outcome #3 (social-emotional), to be reviewed at the next IFSP review meeting on January 15, 2026.
4. Classroom collaboration with Ms. Lopez and Mr. Reyes at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare to reinforce target vocabulary and support peer communication, particularly with classmates Josué and Camila.
5. Follow-up hearing screening in 6 months given Teo's history of recurrent otitis media.
6. A structured home program for Lucía Fernández Ruiz, Alejandro Cruz Mendoza, and caregiver Rosa Ruiz Delgado, emphasizing bilingual language modeling, vocabulary expansion, and consistent use of both home languages rather than restriction to one.
7. Re-evaluation in approximately 12 months to monitor progress in both languages, or sooner if clinically indicated.

This report was completed and signed by Jennifer Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP/L (J. Ortiz), on behalf of Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC ("TBSLT").

NORTH CAROLINA INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM
Individualized Family Service Plan — Annual Review / Revisión Anual del IFSP

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Hernández (called "Teo" at home)
Date of Birth: April 3, 2024
Medicaid ID: 7482913665A
CDSA Case Number: DE-22948
CDSA Office: Neuse River CDSA, Duplin County Office
Service Coordinator: Diana Martínez
Previous IFSP Date: March 10, 2026
This Review Date: September 22, 2026

Family Information / Información de la Familia
Mother: Lucía Hernández Flores
Father: Jesús Cruz Ramírez ("Chuy")
Sister: Guadalupe Cruz Hernández ("Lupita")
Grandmother/caregiver: Rosa Hernández Flores ("abuela Rosa")
Home address: 142 Possum Hollow Road, Wallace, NC 28466, Duplin County
Home phone: (910) 555-2847
Mother's cell: (910) 555-7731
Family email: lucia.hernandez84@gmail.com

Evaluator / Evaluadora: Teresa Álvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP (bilingüe, inglés-español)
Pamlico Pediatric Speech & Language Services
talvarez@pamlicopeds-slp.com | www.pamlicopeds-slp.com

I. Historia del Nacimiento y Antecedentes Médicos / Birth and Medical History

Teo was born at 37 weeks' gestation at Sampson Regional Medical Center in Clinton, NC on April 3, 2024, weighing 5 lbs 14 oz. Apgar scores were 6 and 8 at 1 and 5 minutes. He spent 12 days in the Sampson Regional Medical Center NICU for respiratory distress and was followed there by neonatologist Dr. Minh Tran. His pediatrician, Dr. Patricia Owens of Wallace Pediatric Associates, referred the family to CDSA after noting delayed babbling at the well-child visit.

Mamá Lucía shared during the home visit: "Cuando Teo estaba en la incubadora, los médicos me decían que todo iba a estar bien, pero yo sentía mucho miedo. Él no llevó leche por la boca por casi dos semanas — le pusieron una sonda." She reported no further hospitalizations after discharge, though Teo had recurrent ear infections treated with two courses of amoxicillin between 8 and 14 months and was referred to ENT, who placed bilateral ear tubes under CPT 69436. Diagnosis on referral was coded R62.0 (delayed developmental milestone); today's working diagnosis is F80.2, mixed receptive-expressive language disorder.

Padre Jesús added, half in English and half in Spanish: "Yo trabajo mucho, pero I try to be there for bath time porque that's when Teo talks the most — bueno, lo que puede decir."

II. Preocupaciones y Prioridades de la Familia / Family Concerns and Priorities

Lucía stated, "Lo que más me preocupa es que Teo no me dice lo que quiere. Señala mucho, pero las palabras no salen. Su hermana Lupita a esta edad ya hablaba oraciones completas, y por eso sé que algo es diferente." She added that extended family sometimes dismiss her worry, saying "ya va a hablar," which frustrates her.

Jesús prioritized functional communication at daycare: "I want the teachers at Little Sprouts Daycare to understand him. Right now if he no les dice nada, se frustra y les pega a los otros niños."

Family priorities documented for this review:
1. Increase Teo's use of two- and three-word combinations in both English and Spanish.
2. Reduce frustration-related aggression at daycare and at home with Lupita.
3. Help abuela Rosa, who provides care three days a week while Lucía works, use consistent bilingual strategies.
4. Coordinate with Duplin County WIC Program regarding continued nutrition supports now that Teo eats more table food.

III. Daily Routines / Rutinas Diarias

Teo wakes around 6:30 a.m. and eats breakfast with Lupita before Lucía leaves for her shift at Golden Valley Poultry Plant — la planta de pollos Golden Valley, in Rose Hill, NC, where she works the processing line starting at 7:00 a.m.. Jesús drops both children at abuela Rosa's house before driving to job sites for Cardenas Construction Company — la empresa de construcción Cardenas — where he has worked framing houses for six years. Abuela Rosa takes Teo to Little Sprouts Daycare in Wallace, NC three mornings a week; his teacher there is Ms. Denise Carter, and his classroom aide is Señora Gómez. On non-daycare days, Teo stays home with abuela Rosa, who reports he "se entretiene solo con sus carritos" for long stretches but gets upset when his routine changes.

Evening routine includes dinner around 6:00 p.m., bath at 7:30 p.m. (the family's best language opportunity, per Jesús), and bedtime by 8:30 p.m.. The family's dog, "Canela," sleeps in Teo's room, and he often says the dog's name clearly even though most other words are reduced.

IV. Other Agencies Involved / Otras Agencias

The family currently receives or has applied for services through:
- Duplin County Department of Social Services (food and childcare subsidy)
- Duplin County WIC Program (nutrition supports since infancy)
- Partnership for Children of Duplin County (Smart Start-funded playgroup referral)
- ENC Early Head Start of Duplin County (waitlisted for fall enrollment)

Service coordinator Diana Martínez is coordinating the Early Head Start waitlist status and will follow up with the family by October 15, 2026.

V. Developmental Assessment Results / Resultados de la Evaluación

Teo was administered the Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition, Spanish-English Bilingual Edition (PLS-5) and the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale. Testing occurred across two sessions, in both English and Spanish, with input from Lucía and abuela Rosa on home language use.

Subtest | Standard Score | 95% Confidence Interval | Percentile Rank | Age Equivalent
Auditory Comprehension | 76 | 70–85 | 5th | 18–21 months
Expressive Communication | 68 | 62–77 | 2nd | 14–17 months
Total Language Score | 70 | 64–79 | 2nd | 16–19 months

At chronological age 2;5, Teo's scores reflect a moderate-to-severe delay in expressive language relative to receptive skills, consistent with the referring concern. On the Rossetti, social-emotional and interaction scales fell within age expectations at 2;3–2;6, while gesture and vocabulary scales fell below 2;0.

Articulation screening showed emerging substitution patterns typical of bilingual phonological development: Teo produced /t/ for /k/ in word-initial position (target "casa," produced ""tasa"") and final consonant deletion, saying ""aga"" for target "agua." He imitated target words with moderate cues about 6 of 10 trials and spontaneously used approximately 20 words across both languages per parent report, including "más," "no," "agua" (approximated), and "Canela" (the dog's name, produced clearly).

Mean length of utterance was calculated at 1.2 morphemes (SALT code [EW] used for unintelligible attempts, occurring in roughly 30% of utterances sampled).

VI. Outcomes / Resultados del IFSP

Outcome 1: Teo will use two-word combinations (e.g., "más agua," "no quiero") to request and reject in both English and Spanish, increasing from a baseline of 1 of 10 opportunities to 7 of 10 opportunities across two consecutive sessions.
Strategies: Use Hanen-based "OWL" (Observe, Wait, Listen) strategies during daily routines; bilingual expansion by both parents and abuela Rosa modeled in whichever language the adult uses naturally; visual supports introduced at Little Sprouts Daycare in coordination with Ms. Denise Carter.

Outcome 2: Teo will reduce frustration-related aggression (hitting, pushing) during transitions, decreasing from an average of 5 incidents per daycare day to 1 or fewer, as he gains functional communication alternatives.
Strategies: Teach a picture-based requesting system drawing on PECS principles for high-frustration contexts; consistent bilingual labeling of emotions ("enojado," "mad") by all caregivers; coordination between SLP and daycare staff on a shared visual schedule.

Outcome 3: Teo will imitate and later spontaneously produce early-developing consonants (/m/, /p/, /b/, /n/) in word-initial position with no more than minimal cues, improving intelligibility for familiar listeners from an estimated 30% to 60%.
Strategies: PROMPT-informed tactile-kinesthetic cueing during individual sessions; bath-time sound play suggested to Jesús given his report that this is their highest-engagement routine; home practice sheet provided in both English and Spanish.

VII. Service Delivery

Speech-language therapy: two 45-minute sessions per week, home-based, provided by Teresa Álvarez under CPT 92526, billed through Neuse River CDSA, Duplin County Office against Medicaid ID 7482913665A.
Service coordination: monthly contact by Diana Martínez, next visit scheduled November 5, 2026.
Service begin date: March 17, 2026. Next annual review due by September 10, 2027, with a six-month check-in scheduled for March 18, 2027.

VIII. Signatures

Service Coordinator: Diana Martínez ___________________ Date: September 22, 2026

Nota de la clínica: "Gracias a la familia Cruz Hernández por su paciencia y por compartir tanto sobre su Teo, su Chuy cuando está jugando, y por dejarnos entrar a su rutina de baño todas las semanas." text:
EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Nombre del niño: Mateo Andrés Fernández Ríos  Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de marzo de 2021  Edad actual: 4;7
Fecha de la evaluación: 2 de octubre de 2025  Fecha del informe: 9 de octubre de 2025
Número de expediente: MCR-20458  Número de Medicaid: 987654321A
Dirección: 214 Calle Olmo, Cary, Carolina del Norte 27511  Condado: condado de Wake
Teléfono de contacto: (919) 555-2847  Correo electrónico: lrios.familia@gmail.com
Clínica: Triángulo Terapias del Habla, PLLC  Sitio web: www.trianguloterapiashabla.com
Dirección de la clínica: 4820 Avenida Pinares, Raleigh, Carolina del Norte 27609
Patóloga del habla y lenguaje: Laura Jiménez, M.S., CCC-SLP  Intérprete: Rosa Delgado
Pediatra: Dr. Esteban Carrillo  Terapeuta ocupacional: Nicole Harmon, OTR/L
Fisioterapeuta: Brian Osei, PT  Coordinadora de servicios: Yesenia Campos
Agencia remitente: CDSA del Triángulo  Guardería/preescolar: Rinconcito de las Mariposas
Maestra principal: Srta. Brenda Castellanos  Maestra asistente: Srta. Diana Walcott

RAZÓN DE LA REMISIÓN

Mateo es un niño de 4;7 años que fue remitido para una evaluación integral de habla y lenguaje por su pediatra, el Dr. Esteban Carrillo, y por el programa de intervención temprana del CDSA del Triángulo, debido a preocupaciones persistentes sobre su inteligibilidad y el desarrollo de su vocabulario en los dos idiomas del hogar. Su madre, Lucía Ríos Domínguez, y su padre, Andrés Fernández Paredes, reportan que Mateo usa oraciones cortas y que frecuentemente omite sonidos finales, lo cual dificulta que personas fuera del círculo familiar inmediato lo entiendan. La coordinadora de servicios, Yesenia Campos, solicitó esta evaluación como parte de la revisión anual del Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia, específicamente para actualizar el resultado número 3 relacionado con la comunicación funcional.

La evaluación se realizó en el hogar de la familia, ubicado en 214 Calle Olmo, Cary, Carolina del Norte 27511, y en las instalaciones del Rinconcito de las Mariposas, ubicado en 905 Calle Roble, Cary, Carolina del Norte 27513. Debido a que ambos padres se sienten más cómodos comunicándose en español, la entrevista con la familia se llevó a cabo completamente en ese idioma, mientras que las observaciones en el preescolar se realizaron con el apoyo de la intérprete Rosa Delgado, quien tradujo del inglés al español las instrucciones de las maestras cuando fue necesario. El código de procedimiento utilizado para la evaluación fue CPT 92523 (evaluación del habla y del lenguaje con interpretación).

HISTORIA DE NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA

Según el informe materno, el embarazo de Mateo llegó a las 38 semanas de gestación, sin complicaciones significativas reportadas. El parto fue vaginal, y Mateo nació con un peso de 3,100 gramos y una puntuación de Apgar de 8 al minuto y 9 a los cinco minutos. No hubo necesidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales. La madre indica que Mateo fue dado de alta del Hospital Materno WakeMed Cary a las 48 horas de vida, sin complicaciones adicionales.

El historial médico de Mateo incluye otitis media recurrente, con un total de seis episodios documentados entre los 8 meses y los 3 años de edad. Se le colocaron tubos de ventilación bilaterales a la edad de 22 meses, procedimiento realizado por un otorrinolaringólogo en Raleigh. Desde entonces, la frecuencia de infecciones de oído ha disminuido considerablemente, aunque la madre reporta un episodio leve hace aproximadamente seis meses que se resolvió con antibióticos recetados por el Dr. Esteban Carrillo.

Mateo también tiene un diagnóstico de hipotonía leve, identificado por su fisioterapeuta, Brian Osei, durante una evaluación a los 18 meses de edad. Esta hipotonía afecta principalmente el tono muscular del tronco y, según los informes de terapia ocupacional de Nicole Harmon, también puede influir en el control oral-motor necesario para la articulación precisa. La terapeuta ocupacional ha observado dificultades masticatorias con alimentos de textura dura, por lo cual la familia ha modificado algunas comidas en el hogar.

No hay antecedentes de convulsiones, hospitalizaciones mayores después del período neonatal, ni cirugías adicionales fuera de la miringotomía. La visión y la audición fueron evaluadas más recientemente el 15 de agosto de 2025, con resultados dentro de límites normales bilateralmente, según el audiólogo del programa de detección auditiva infantil del condado. Los diagnósticos actuales relevantes para esta evaluación incluyen F80.2 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo, provisional) y F80.0 (trastorno fonológico del habla).

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE IDIOMA

Mateo vive con su madre, Lucía Ríos Domínguez; su padre, Andrés Fernández Paredes; su hermana mayor, Sol Fernández Ríos, de siete años; y su abuela materna, Carmen Domínguez Vega, quien vive con la familia y ayuda con el cuidado de los niños durante el día. La familia también cuenta con el apoyo ocasional de una vecina y amiga cercana, Yolanda Pérez, quien recoge a los niños de la guardería cuando los padres trabajan hasta tarde. La familia tiene además un perro llamado Rocky, que Mateo menciona con frecuencia durante el juego.

El idioma predominante en el hogar es el español. La madre, Lucía Ríos Domínguez, trabaja como asistente administrativa en Construcciones del Roble LLC, y el padre, Andrés Fernández Paredes, trabaja como técnico de mantenimiento en Sistemas Industriales Carolina. Ambos padres hablan español como primera lengua y tienen un dominio intermedio del inglés. La abuela, Carmen Domínguez Vega, habla únicamente español y es quien pasa más tiempo con Mateo durante las mañanas antes de que lo lleven a la guardería.

Mateo fue expuesto principalmente al español durante sus primeros tres años de vida. A partir de los 3 años, comenzó a asistir al Rinconcito de las Mariposas, un preescolar bilingüe donde las actividades se conducen mayormente en inglés con apoyo limitado en español. Según la maestra principal, Srta. Brenda Castellanos, y la maestra asistente, Srta. Diana Walcott, Mateo entiende instrucciones simples en ambos idiomas, pero su producción expresiva es más limitada en inglés. En el salón, Mateo interactúa principalmente con dos compañeros, Liam y Ava, con quienes comparte juegos de bloques y actividades de arte.

La hermana de Mateo, Sol, es bilingüe funcional y a menudo traduce para su hermano menor cuando juega con compañeros de habla inglesa. Es relevante notar, para fines de la terapia fonológica, que una de las palabras meta seleccionadas en sesiones previas fue la palabra "sol", la cual Mateo produce consistentemente como [so], omitiendo el sonido final /l/ en posición final de sílaba. Esta coincidencia entre la palabra meta y el nombre de su hermana ha generado cierta confusión durante actividades de juego dirigido, ya que Mateo en ocasiones asocia la palabra con ella en lugar del astro. Durante una actividad de imitación directa en esta evaluación, se le pidió a Mateo que dijera "hola, Sol", frase que produjo como [ola so], manteniendo la omisión de /l/ también en el nombre propio.

OBSERVACIÓN CONDUCTUAL DURANTE LA EVALUACIÓN

Mateo se presentó a la evaluación acompañado de su madre, Lucía Ríos Domínguez, y de su abuela, Carmen Domínguez Vega. Mostró inicialmente timidez con la evaluadora, Laura Jiménez, pero se mostró más cómodo después de aproximadamente 10 minutos de juego libre con bloques y figuras de animales. Mantuvo contacto visual apropiado, respondió a su nombre de manera consistente y demostró intención comunicativa clara a través de gestos, señalamiento y aproximaciones verbales.

Durante la sesión en la guardería, realizada por la tarde alrededor de las 1:30 p.m., se observó que Mateo participaba activamente en el círculo de canciones dirigido por la Srta. Brenda Castellanos, aunque con producciones verbales limitadas en comparación con sus compañeros de la misma edad. Durante el recreo de la tarde, alrededor de las 2:15 p.m., se observó una interacción espontánea entre Mateo y su compañero Liam, en la cual Mateo produjo la frase "Rocky corre rápido" como [oki ko ápido], ilustrando omisiones consistentes de consonantes iniciales y finales.

Mateo demostró niveles de atención apropiados para su edad durante tareas estructuradas de aproximadamente 15 minutos de duración, aunque requirió redirección ocasional durante tareas menos preferidas, como la nominación de láminas. La intérprete, Rosa Delgado, asistió en la administración de instrucciones durante las porciones en inglés de la evaluación, confirmando que Mateo comprendía las consignas básicas pero mostraba inconsistencia en sus respuestas expresivas en ese idioma.

PRUEBAS ADMINISTRADAS Y RESULTADOS

Se administraron las siguientes pruebas estandarizadas, con apoyo de interpretación según fue necesario:

1. Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA) – Morfosintaxis, español
2. Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA) – Fonología, español
3. Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5), versión en español – Comprensión Auditiva y Comunicación Expresiva
4. Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), adaptado informalmente al español
5. Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, 100 enunciados, transcrita y analizada mediante codificación tipo SALT

Resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas:

Prueba / Subprueba                              Puntaje estándar      Percentil        Intervalo de confianza (95%)
BESA – Morfosintaxis (español)                   76               5to percentil      71-81
BESA – Fonología (español)                       81               10mo percentil     76-86
PLS-5 – Comprensión Auditiva                      79               8vo percentil      73-85
PLS-5 – Comunicación Expresiva                    72               3er percentil      67-77
PLS-5 – Puntaje de Lenguaje Total                 74               4to percentil      69-79
GFTA-3 (adaptado, español)                        70               2do percentil      65-75

La equivalencia de edad derivada de la subprueba de Comunicación Expresiva del PLS-5 fue de 2;6-3;0, lo cual representa un retraso significativo en relación con su edad cronológica de 4;7. En la subprueba de Fonología de BESA, Mateo mostró procesos fonológicos consistentes con omisión de consonantes finales y reducción de grupos consonánticos, descritos en mayor detalle a continuación.

ANÁLISIS FONOLÓGICO Y DE LENGUAJE ESPONTÁNEO

El análisis de la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo de 100 enunciados reveló una longitud media de enunciado de 3.1 morfemas, consistente con un nivel de desarrollo gramatical por debajo de lo esperado para su edad. Se identificaron procesos fonológicos persistentes, incluyendo omisión de consonante final (por ejemplo, "pan" producido como [pa]), reducción de grupos consonánticos (por ejemplo, "flor" producido como [for]), y sustitución de /ɾ/ por [w] en posición inicial (por ejemplo, "ratón" producido como [watón]).

En una tarea de repetición de palabras, Mateo logró producir correctamente 8/10 palabras monosilábicas sin grupos consonánticos, pero solo 3 de 10 palabras con grupos consonánticos complejos. Su inteligibilidad general fue estimada por la evaluadora, con apoyo de la intérprete, en aproximadamente 60% para oyentes familiares y 35% para oyentes no familiares, en contexto conversacional espontáneo.

Un segmento representativo de la transcripción, codificado con convenciones tipo SALT, se presenta a continuación:

"Yo quiero [ese] uno" [EW]
"Rocky no [tá] aquí"
"Sol [uwa] conmigo" (intentando decir "juega conmigo")

Durante una de las actividades con claves de apoyo, Mateo respondió favorablemente a claves moderadas, logrando producir la palabra "flor" correctamente con claves táctiles y modelo auditivo repetido, aunque no logró generalizar la producción sin apoyo. Con claves mínimas, su tasa de éxito en palabras con grupos consonánticos fue considerablemente menor.

HORARIO DE SESIONES DE TERAPIA PROPUESTO

Día          Hora de inicio      Hora de fin         Lugar
Lunes        9:00 a.m.       9:45 a.m.       214 Calle Olmo, Cary, Carolina del Norte 27511
Miércoles    1:00 p.m.       1:45 p.m.       Rinconcito de las Mariposas
Viernes      10:30 a.m.      11:15 a.m.      Triángulo Terapias del Habla, PLLC

Las sesiones de los lunes se realizarán en el hogar de la familia por la mañana, antes de que Mateo sea llevado a la guardería alrededor de las 11:00 a.m.. Las sesiones de los miércoles se coordinarán directamente con la Srta. Brenda Castellanos en el Rinconcito de las Mariposas, durante el bloque de actividades dirigidas por la tarde. Las sesiones de los viernes se llevarán a cabo en la clínica, con transporte proporcionado por la abuela, Carmen Domínguez Vega, quien generalmente recoge a Mateo de la guardería alrededor de las 10:00 a.m. los viernes.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Con base en los resultados obtenidos en las pruebas estandarizadas, la observación conductual, y el análisis de la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, Mateo presenta un trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo de moderado a severo, con un componente fonológico significativo que afecta notablemente su inteligibilidad en ambos idiomas. Sus puntajes en todas las medidas estandarizadas administradas se ubicaron por debajo de 1.5 desviaciones estándar de la media, consistente con los criterios diagnósticos de F80.2 y F80.0.

Es importante notar que, debido a la exposición dual al español y al inglés en el entorno de la guardería, el perfil de Mateo no puede atribuirse únicamente a factores de aprendizaje bilingüe típico. Sus dificultades están presentes en ambos idiomas, lo cual respalda la presencia de un trastorno subyacente del lenguaje y del habla, más allá de las diferencias esperadas asociadas al desarrollo bilingüe. Los procesos fonológicos observados, incluyendo la omisión consistente de consonantes finales, también contribuyen significativamente a su baja inteligibilidad, particularmente con oyentes no familiares, incluyendo compañeros como Liam y Ava en el entorno escolar.

La historia de otitis media recurrente y la hipotonía leve documentada por el fisioterapeuta, Brian Osei, y la terapeuta ocupacional, Nicole Harmon, representan factores contribuyentes relevantes que deben considerarse en la planificación del tratamiento, particularmente en lo relacionado con el control motor-oral necesario para la articulación precisa de grupos consonánticos.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda que Mateo continúe recibiendo terapia de habla y lenguaje individual, con una frecuencia de tres sesiones de 45 minutos por semana, según el horario propuesto anteriormente, durante un período inicial de seis meses, con reevaluación del progreso en ese momento.

2. Se recomienda el uso del enfoque PROMPT para abordar los componentes motor-orales de la producción del habla, dado el componente de hipotonía identificado por el equipo de terapia ocupacional y fisioterapia.

3. Se recomienda la incorporación del enfoque Cycles para el tratamiento de los procesos fonológicos identificados, particularmente la omisión de consonante final y la reducción de grupos consonánticos, con metas específicas organizadas en ciclos de aproximadamente 60 días cada uno.

4. Se recomienda que la familia participe en un programa de capacitación tipo Hanen, específicamente diseñado para padres de niños bilingües con retrasos de lenguaje, para apoyar las estrategias de estimulación del lenguaje en el hogar en ambos idiomas.

5. Se recomienda coordinación continua con la Srta. Brenda Castellanos y la Srta. Diana Walcott en el Rinconcito de las Mariposas, para asegurar la generalización de las metas de terapia al entorno escolar, incluyendo durante las interacciones con compañeros como Liam y Ava.

6. Se recomienda mantener comunicación regular con el pediatra, Dr. Esteban Carrillo, respecto a la recurrencia de infecciones de oído, dado su posible impacto continuo en el desarrollo del lenguaje receptivo.

7. Se recomienda que la coordinadora de servicios, Yesenia Campos, actualice el IFSP para incluir metas específicas relacionadas con la inteligibilidad funcional en entornos bilingües, y que se considere una referencia adicional al Programa de Nutrición Infantil del Condado de Wake para apoyo nutricional relacionado con las dificultades masticatorias observadas.

8. Se recomienda continuar el monitoreo del progreso mediante muestras de lenguaje espontáneo trimestrales y re-administración parcial del PLS-5 en aproximadamente seis meses, con el fin de documentar el avance hacia las metas establecidas.

9. Se recomienda que la familia continúe utilizando estrategias de modelado en español durante las actividades diarias con la abuela, Carmen Domínguez Vega, y que la hermana, Sol Fernández Ríos, participe en actividades de juego estructurado diseñadas para fomentar, en lugar de sustituir, las producciones independientes de Mateo.

Este informe fue preparado por Laura Jiménez, M.S., CCC-SLP, con el apoyo de la intérprete Rosa Delgado, y será compartido con la familia, el pediatra Dr. Esteban Carrillo, y el equipo del CDSA del Triángulo para su revisión e incorporación al plan de servicios de Mateo.
