PLAN INDIVIDUALIZADO DE SERVICIOS FAMILIARES (IFSP) — REVISIÓN DE SEIS MESES
Programa de Infantes y Niños Pequeños de Carolina del Norte (NC Infant-Toddler Program)

Oficina de CDSA: CDSA Piedmont Triad, oficina de Greensboro
Fecha de la reunión de revisión: 12 de octubre de 2026
Fecha del IFSP inicial: 18 de marzo de 2026
Fecha de la próxima revisión programada: 12 de abril de 2027

Niño: Mateo Alejandro Castillo Reyes (en casa le dicen Teo)
Fecha de nacimiento: 4 de enero de 2025 (edad actual: 21 meses)
Número de caso de CDSA: CDSA-2025-04471
Número de Medicaid: 987654321B
Dirección: 4821 Spring Garden Street, Greensboro, NC 27403
Condado: Guilford
Teléfono de contacto familiar: (336) 555-0148
Correo electrónico de contacto: lucia.rodriguez85@gmail.com

Coordinadora de Servicios: Ana Beltrán, CDSA Piedmont Triad, teléfono (336) 555-0199, correo ana.beltran@cdsapiedmont.org
Terapeuta del habla y lenguaje bilingüe que redacta este informe: Marisol Fernández, M.S., CCC-SLP, contratada a través de Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC
Interprete que apoyó partes de la reunión: Yesenia Gómez

I. INFORMACIÓN FAMILIAR

Mateo vive con su mamá, Lucía Rodríguez Peña (28 años), su papá, Jorge Castillo Hernández (31 años), y su hermana mayor, Valentina (4 años), en una casa alquilada en Greensboro. El español es el idioma principal del hogar. Jorge trabaja como técnico de mantenimiento en Honda Aircraft Company, turno de 6:00 a.m. a 2:30 p.m.. Lucía trabaja medio tiempo, de 9:00 a.m. a 1:00 p.m., en la oficina corporativa de Biscuitville. Mientras los padres trabajan, la abuela materna, a quien la familia llama doña Lupe, cuida a Mateo y a Valentina tres días a la semana; los otros dos días Mateo va a la guardería Little Sprouts Early Learning Center. La familia también tiene un perro pequeño llamado Firulais, al que Mateo señala y nombra como "pepo" para "perro".

Historia del nacimiento: Mateo nació a las 34 semanas de gestación en Cone Health Women's Hospital, campus de Greensboro, con un peso al nacer de 1,980 gramos y un Apgar de 6 al minuto y 8 a los cinco minutos. Pasó 18 días en la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales (NICU) del mismo hospital por dificultad respiratoria e hipoglucemia. Al salir de la NICU, el pediatra de seguimiento, Dr. Samuel Owens, de Cone Health Pediatrics en el campus de Wendover, refirió a la familia al CDSA por preocupación de retraso global.

En agosto de 2026, por preocupación de posible pérdida auditiva después de episodios repetidos de otitis media, la familia fue referida a Novant Health Ear, Nose & Throat & Audiology, campus de Kernersville, donde el audiólogo Dr. Felix Whitaker confirmó audición dentro de límites normales bilateralmente mediante timpanometría y ABR condicionado. El otorrinolaringólogo, Dra. Renata Suh, recomendó monitoreo continuo pero no cirugía en este momento.

II. PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA (en sus propias palabras)

Lucía compartió: "Mateo entiende casi todo lo que le decimos, pero cuando quiere algo solo señala o hace sonidos. Nos preocupa que cuando empiece la escuela no lo van a entender." Jorge agregó: "Yo quiero que aprenda a decir palabras completas, no solo 'ma' o 'pa'. Y que juegue más con su hermana en vez de frustrarse y pegarle."

doña Lupe mencionó durante la reunión: "Cuando está conmigo en la casa, señala la nevera y dice 'aba' para agua, pero si no le entiendo rápido se tira al piso llorando."

Prioridades identificadas por la familia:
1. Que Mateo use más palabras habladas para pedir comida, agua y juguetes, en vez de solo gestos.
2. Que disminuyan las rabietas relacionadas con la frustración de comunicación.
3. Que la familia reciba estrategias en español para practicar en casa durante las rutinas diarias.
4. Que la coordinadora de servicios ayude a la familia a mantener la elegibilidad de Medicaid y a solicitar beneficios de WIC renovados.

III. RUTINAS DIARIAS

La mañana comienza alrededor de las 6:30 a.m., cuando Jorge se prepara para el trabajo y Lucía viste a los niños. El desayuno es entre 7:00 a.m. y 7:30 a.m.; Mateo participa señalando el cereal y diciendo "ea" para "leche". Los días de guardería, Lucía lo deja en Little Sprouts Early Learning Center a las 8:15 a.m., donde su maestra principal es Miss Ana. Los días en casa con doña Lupe, la rutina incluye juego libre en la sala de 9:00 a.m. a 10:30 a.m. y una siesta de 1:00 p.m. a 3:00 p.m..

La cena familiar es alrededor de las 6:30 p.m., seguida de tiempo de juego con Valentina hasta el baño a las 7:45 p.m. y la hora de dormir a las 8:30 p.m.. Los fines de semana, la familia asiste a un grupo de juego organizado por Early Head Start de Greensboro, donde la visitadora del hogar es la maestra Carmen.

IV. OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS

Agencia	Persona de contacto	Teléfono	Función
CDSA Piedmont Triad	Ana Beltrán	(336) 555-0199	Coordinación de servicios
Guilford County DSS	Teresa Nkemelu	(336) 555-0212	Beneficios y Medicaid
Guilford County WIC	Brenda Castellanos	(336) 555-0177	Nutrición infantil
Guilford County Partnership for Children / Smart Start	Katrina Fells	(336) 555-0233	Subsidio de guardería
Early Head Start de Greensboro	la maestra Carmen	(336) 555-0260	Visitas al hogar y grupo de juego
Little Sprouts Early Learning Center	Miss Ana	(336) 555-0144	Cuidado diario

La familia renovó su caso de WIC el 3 de septiembre de 2026 con la Sra. Castellanos, y el subsidio de cuidado infantil de Smart Start fue aprobado el 15 de septiembre de 2026 a través de la Sra. Fells. La familia sigue en proceso de recertificación de Medicaid con el DSS; Lucía indicó que el papeleo vence el 30 de noviembre de 2026.

V. RESULTADOS DE EVALUACIÓN

La evaluación inicial se realizó el 10 de marzo de 2026 y la evaluación de seguimiento para esta revisión se realizó el 28 de septiembre de 2026, ambas por Marisol Fernández, M.S., CCC-SLP en el hogar familiar, con apoyo de interpretación de Yesenia Gómez cuando fue necesario. Se administraron instrumentos estandarizados en español e inglés según corresponda, con observación clínica y muestra de lenguaje.

Fecha	Prueba / Subprueba	Puntaje estándar	Percentil	Intervalo de confianza (95%)
10/03/2026	PLS-5 Spanish — Comprensión Auditiva	76	5	70-82
10/03/2026	PLS-5 Spanish — Comunicación Expresiva	68	2	61-75
10/03/2026	Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale — Pragmática	Edad equivalente 11 meses	—	9-13 meses
28/09/2026	PLS-5 Spanish — Comprensión Auditiva	81	10	74-88
28/09/2026	PLS-5 Spanish — Comunicación Expresiva	73	4	66-80
28/09/2026	CELF Preschool-2 Spanish — Conceptos y Direcciones	7	16	5-9

Observación clínica: Durante el juego, Mateo combinó dos gestos con una vocalización para pedir ayuda. Produjo de manera espontánea las aproximaciones "aba" para "agua" y "ea" para "leche"; con claves mod logró imitar "pan" con apoyo visual y táctil, acercándose a /pan/ con omisión de la consonante final en 3 de 5 intentos. En inventario fonético, produjo los sonidos /p/, /m/, /a/ y /e/ de forma consistente, con sustitución de [t] por /k/ en posición inicial. Al pedírsele que repitiera "gato", produjo "dato", codificado en la muestra de lenguaje como [EW] por sustitución de velar.

En la rejilla de vocabulario expresivo, la familia reportó un vocabulario funcional de aproximadamente 15 palabras y 20 gestos consistentes, comparado con 8 palabras reportadas en la evaluación inicial, lo cual representa un aumento de casi el 90%.

Diagnóstico de trabajo: Trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo (F80.2), con retraso fonológico leve a moderado asociado. Código de procedimiento facturado para la evaluación: CPT 92523. Código de procedimiento facturado para las sesiones de intervención continua: CPT 92507.

VI. RESULTADOS DEL IFSP Y ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1 (continuado del IFSP inicial): Mateo usará palabras habladas de una o dos sílabas para pedir objetos y acciones preferidas en al menos 5 de 10 oportunidades durante las rutinas de comida y juego, observado por la familia y confirmado por la terapeuta.
Estado: progreso parcial. En la sesión del 25 de septiembre de 2026, Mateo alcanzó 6 de 10 oportunidades con claves mínimas durante el refrigerio de la tarde.
Estrategias: uso del enfoque Hanen para seguir el interés del niño ("sígueme la corriente"), espera estructurada antes de ofrecer un objeto deseado, y modelado de palabras objetivo con énfasis prosódico en español.

Resultado 2 (nuevo, agregado en esta revisión): Mateo combinará un gesto y una palabra, o dos palabras, para formar una comunicación de dos elementos en al menos 4 de 8 oportunidades observadas en el hogar y en la guardería.
Estrategias: estrategias de PROMPT para apoyo táctil-kinestésico de la colocación articulatoria durante la producción de palabras objetivo; uso de rutinas repetidas en casa (hora del baño, hora de la comida) para crear oportunidades predecibles de comunicación.

Resultado 3 (continuado): La familia recibirá entrenamiento continuo en estrategias de lenguaje en español para usar durante las rutinas diarias, con revisión mensual del progreso por parte de la terapeuta y la coordinadora de servicios.
Estrategias: hojas de práctica en español enviadas a Lucía y Jorge después de cada sesión; demostración en vivo de técnicas con doña Lupe durante al menos una sesión mensual, dado su papel central en el cuidado diario.

Resultado 4 (nuevo): Se reducirán los episodios de frustración conductual (llanto, tirarse al piso, golpear) relacionados con fallas de comunicación a menos de 3 episodios por semana, según reporte familiar en el registro de rutinas.
Estrategias: enseñanza de un gesto funcional de "más" y una tarjeta visual simple como puente hacia el lenguaje hablado; posible introducción de estrategias tipo PECS si el progreso verbal se estanca en la próxima revisión.

Nota sobre fonología: dado el patrón de sustitución velar observado, se considerará un enfoque de ciclos fonológicos (Cycles approach) si persiste después de la próxima revisión, enfocándose en los sonidos /k/ y /g/ en posición inicial.

VII. CALENDARIO DE SERVICIOS

Servicio	Proveedor	Frecuencia	Duración	Ubicación
Terapia de habla y lenguaje, bilingüe	Marisol Fernández, M.S., CCC-SLP	2 veces por semana	9:30 a.m. a 10:15 a.m.	Hogar familiar, Greensboro
Coordinación de servicios	Ana Beltrán	Mensual	30 minutos	Telefónico o en el hogar
Visita del hogar de Early Head Start	la maestra Carmen	Semanal, martes	10:30 a.m. a 11:15 a.m.	Hogar familiar
Seguimiento audiológico	Dr. Felix Whitaker	Cada 6 meses	45 minutos	Novant Health Ear, Nose & Throat & Audiology, campus Kernersville
Seguimiento pediátrico	Dr. Samuel Owens	Cada 3 meses	20 minutos	Cone Health Pediatrics, campus Wendover

Las sesiones de terapia de habla y lenguaje continuarán en el hogar familiar los martes y jueves, de 9:30 a.m. a 10:15 a.m., con Lucía o doña Lupe presentes según la disponibilidad. Las sesiones de guardería con Miss Ana continuarán de forma paralela, de lunes a miércoles, de 8:15 a.m. a 3:00 p.m., sin facturación de Medicaid por parte de la guardería.

VIII. PLAN DE TRANSICIÓN Y PRÓXIMOS PASOS

Dado que Mateo cumplirá 3 años en enero de 2028, la coordinadora de servicios, Ana Beltrán, explicó que la planificación formal de transición hacia servicios preescolares del distrito escolar comenzará aproximadamente 9 meses antes de esa fecha. Mientras tanto, la familia continuará con el apoyo combinado de CDSA Piedmont Triad, Early Head Start de Greensboro y los servicios de terapia en el hogar.

La próxima reunión de revisión del IFSP está programada para el 12 de abril de 2027 a las 2:00 p.m. en el hogar familiar, con la participación esperada de Lucía, Jorge, Ana Beltrán y Marisol Fernández.

IX. CONSENTIMIENTO Y FIRMAS

Los padres confirmaron haber recibido una copia de este IFSP revisado y estar de acuerdo con los resultados y servicios descritos arriba. La reunión se realizó en español, con Yesenia Gómez disponible para aclarar términos técnicos en inglés cuando fue necesario.

SECTION 2: FAMILY'S CONCERNS, PRIORITIES, AND RESOURCES (in the family's own words)

Ana Torres shared the following during today's review, with interpretation support provided by Lucia Fernandez, certified bilingual interpreter:

"Our biggest concern right now is that Camila still mixes up her sounds. She says things like 'tai' for 'sal' and we can't always tell what she wants. Her big sister, Sol, talks for her a lot, and we worry Camila depends on that too much at home."

"At home we are proud that she imitates more words now. She says 'mamá' and 'papá' clearly, and she tries to copy her sister when they play with blocks or watch cartoons together."

"Our priority for this year is that Camila can tell her teacher at daycare what she needs without pointing. We also want her to be understood by her cousins when the whole family is together, and by her grandmother when she visits on weekends."

Diego Torres added: "I want to make sure we are doing the right things at home in both languages. Sometimes people tell us to only speak English, but we don't want her to lose Spanish."

Family Resources Identified: extended family support (cousins Mateo Flores and Valentina Flores visit most weekends, along with their mother, Camila's aunt), a grandmother, Carmen Reyes, who comes on Saturdays, reliable childcare through Rosa Fernández (babysitter, Tuesdays and Thursdays), stable housing, and both parents employed with flexible scheduling that allows them to attend therapy sessions.

CAROLINA BILINGUAL SPEECH & LANGUAGE SERVICES, PLLC
4821 Forestville Road, Suite 220, Raleigh, NC 27616
Tel: (919) 555-0148 | Fax: (919) 555-0149
Email: intake@carolinabilingualslp.com

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT
Informe de Evaluación del Habla y Lenguaje

Client / Niño: Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez ("Mateo," "Teo")
Date of Birth: December 5, 2021
Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Dates of Evaluation: February 10, 2026 and February 12, 2026
Report Date: February 19, 2026

Evaluating SLP: Jennifer Walsh, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (Spanish/English) clinician
Interpreter present: Sandra Ibarra, certified medical interpreter, Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Referral Source: Dr. Anil Patel, pediatrician, WakeMed Physician Practices

NC Medicaid ID: 920481736B
Insurance Member ID (Blue Cross NC, secondary): ZLH294817502
NC ITP Child ID: ITP-2026-04471
Authorization/Record Number (CDSA): CDSA-2026-11287

Parent/Guardian: Lucía Rodríguez (mother), Héctor Flores (father)
Home Address: 118 Juniper Lane, Garner, Wake County, 27529
Home Phone: (919) 555-0273 | Mother's Cell: (919) 555-0391

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Anil Patel following concerns raised at his 4-year well-child visit regarding limited intelligibility and reduced expressive vocabulary in both English and Spanish. Mateo is currently enrolled through Wake County CDSA (Children's Developmental Services Agency), under NC ITP Child ID ITP-2026-04471, and receives case coordination through Wake County Partnership for Children. His mother, Lucía Rodríguez, reported during the intake interview, "No le entiendo casi nada cuando habla rápido, y en la escuela dicen que se frustra porque no lo entienden." His father, Héctor Flores, added, "At home we mix, pero en la daycare solo es inglés, and he gets quiet."

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at WakeMed Children's Hospital on December 5, 2021 at 39 weeks gestational age via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Birth weight was 7 lbs 2 oz; Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. Lucía Rodríguez reported no complications during pregnancy, though she noted mild gestational hypertension managed with diet in the third trimester. Mateo met early gross motor milestones within normal limits (sat independently at 6 months, walked at 13 months), but his parents report that early vocalization and babbling were delayed relative to his older sister.

Mateo had recurrent otitis media between 12 and 24 months of age, with four documented ear infections treated with antibiotics (ICD-10 H66.90). Tympanostomy tubes (CPT 69436) were placed at 22 months by Dr. Megan Reyes, pediatric ENT, with resolution of recurrent infections. A hearing screening following tube placement showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally. No history of seizures, significant head injury, or hospitalization beyond the tube placement procedure. Family history is significant for a maternal uncle with a reported history of late talking that resolved by early elementary school, per parent report.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez; his father, Héctor Flores; and his older sister, Valentina Flores, age 7. Lucía Rodríguez works as a shift lead at the Harris Teeter distribution center in Garner, and Héctor Flores works second shift at the Perdue Farms processing plant in Wake County. Because of their schedules, Mateo and Valentina Flores are frequently cared for by their babysitter, Rosa Pérez, who has watched the children three afternoons a week for the past two years; Lucía Rodríguez referred to her warmly as "nuestra R.P., es como familia." Mateo's maternal grandmother, M.R., also helps with pickup from daycare on Fridays and speaks exclusively Spanish with him.

The home language is predominantly Spanish, estimated by parent report at roughly 70% Spanish and 30% English. Lucía Rodríguez reported, "Yo le hablo en español todo el tiempo, pero su papá a veces le dice cosas en inglés porque quiere que esté listo para la escuela." Valentina Flores, who is in second grade and fully bilingual, often code-switches with Mateo at home, saying things like "Teo, ven aquí, come here, vamos a jugar." Extended family frequently visits, including Mateo's cousins, Diego Rodríguez and Camila Rodríguez, who live nearby in Clayton and speak primarily Spanish with occasional English mixed in during play.

The family's dog, Rocky, and their cat, Luna, are both frequently mentioned by Mateo during play-based observation; he was observed saying "Rocky corre" while pointing to the dog in a picture book, and later attempted "Luna duerme" when shown a photo on his mother's phone. Lucía Rodríguez noted that Mateo often narrates to the pets in simplified Spanish when no one else is listening, which she finds encouraging.

The family receives support through several community resources. Lucía Rodríguez reported ongoing enrollment with the Wake County WIC Program and noted that a caseworker at the Wake County Department of Social Services (DSS) helped the family apply for Medicaid when Mateo was an infant. The family was also connected to Wake County Smart Start for early literacy materials distributed in both English and Spanish, which Lucía Rodríguez said have been helpful for bedtime reading routines.

EDUCATIONAL / DAYCARE HISTORY

Mateo attends Sunshine Bilingual Daycare and Preschool five days a week from 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.. His lead teacher, Ms. Amanda Lopez, and classroom aide, Mr. Carlos Mendez, report that despite the "bilingual" name of the program, instruction in Mateo's classroom is conducted primarily in English, with limited Spanish support available only from Mr. Carlos Mendez during transitions. Ms. Amanda Lopez shared in a phone consultation, "He's a sweet kid, but he gets left out of conversations because the other kids can't understand him, and he sometimes just watches instead of joining in."

Classmates Liam Chen and Sofia Martínez are frequently mentioned as Mateo's preferred playmates during free choice time, though Ms. Amanda Lopez noted that Mateo tends to follow their lead in play rather than initiate verbally. During a classroom observation on February 11, 2026, this examiner observed Mateo attempt to join a block-building activity with Liam Chen by pointing and gesturing rather than using verbal requests, despite having relevant vocabulary available in both languages per parent report.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Across both evaluation sessions, Mateo presented as a friendly, curious child who separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with the examiner and interpreter once rapport was established. He demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks of 10-15 minutes with brief breaks. Mateo showed clear frustration when his attempts at communication were misunderstood, at times abandoning verbal attempts in favor of gesture or simply walking away from the task, consistent with parent and teacher report.

Mateo demonstrated active code-switching during both sessions, frequently beginning a sentence in Spanish and finishing in English or vice versa (e.g., "quiero el... the red one"). This pattern is developmentally appropriate for a bilingual child of his age and language exposure and was not counted against him in error analysis; rather, productions were credited if the target was produced correctly in either language.

ASSESSMENT TOOLS AND PROCEDURES

The following standardized and informal measures were administered in both English and Spanish, with Sandra Ibarra providing interpretation and the examiner administering Spanish-language items directly where proficient:

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English and Spanish forms
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3)
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)
- Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax and Phonology subtests
- Spontaneous language sample (English and Spanish, 50 utterances each) analyzed using SALT conventions
- Oral mechanism examination and hearing screening
- Parent and teacher interview, classroom observation

TEST RESULTS

Score Summary Table

Measure	Subtest	Standard Score	Percentile Rank	Age Equivalent
PLS-5 (English)	Auditory Comprehension	78	7th	2;9
PLS-5 (English)	Expressive Communication	72	3rd	2;6
PLS-5 (Spanish)	Auditory Comprehension	88	21st	3;6
PLS-5 (Spanish)	Expressive Communication	85	16th	3;4
CELF Preschool-3	Core Language Score	76	5th	--
GFTA-3	Sounds-in-Words	70	2nd	--
BESA	Morphosyntax	81	10th	--
BESA	Phonology	79	8th	--

Confidence intervals (95%) ranged from 68-78 on the GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words standard score to 81-91 on the PLS-5 Spanish Auditory Comprehension standard score, indicating consistent patterns across measures.

Composite scores suggest that Mateo's overall communicative competence, when both languages are considered together rather than English alone, falls closer to the low average range, consistent with cross-linguistic research on simultaneous bilingual development. However, deficits were noted in both languages relative to typically developing bilingual peers, suggesting a true language disorder rather than typical bilingual language difference alone.

Articulation and Phonology

Mateo demonstrated the following sound errors on the GFTA-3 and during spontaneous speech sampling: fronting of velars (/k/ and /g/ produced as /t/ and /d/, e.g., "tat" for target "cat"), final consonant deletion (e.g., "ba" for target "ball"), and liquid gliding, with /l/ and /ɾ/ produced as [w] (e.g., "wuego" for target "luego"). His speech intelligibility was judged to be approximately 40% intelligible to unfamiliar listeners in connected speech, improving to roughly 60% with context and gesture support. With moderate cues, Mateo was able to produce the target sounds in isolation with 8/10 accuracy for /k/ and 7/10 for /g/, suggesting stimulability and good prognosis with intervention.

Language Sample Analysis

Mean length of utterance in morphemes (MLU-m) was 2.8 in English and 3.4 in Spanish, both below expected ranges for chronological age (expected MLU-m 4.0-5.0). Grammatical forms omitted included third-person singular -s, past tense -ed, and in Spanish, correct gender agreement on articles (e.g., "la perro" for "el perro"). SALT coding identified frequent [EW] (error word) codes associated with omitted grammatical morphemes in both languages. During the sample, Mateo produced the target phrase "más jugo, please" when requesting a drink, and later attempted "the dog is runs" when narrating a picture, both coded as grammatical errors consistent with his profile.

IMPRESSIONS

Based on comprehensive assessment across both of Mateo's languages, results are consistent with a diagnosis of Developmental Language Disorder (ICD-10 F80.9) affecting both receptive and expressive language, with co-occurring Speech Sound Disorder (ICD-10 F80.0). Deficits are present across both English and Spanish, which rules out typical bilingual second-language acquisition patterns or language difference as the sole explanation for his profile; a true disorder affecting the underlying language system is indicated.

Mateo's strengths include good stimulability for speech sound targets with minimal to moderate cueing, strong nonverbal problem-solving skills noted informally during testing, a supportive home environment with rich language exposure in Spanish, and motivation to communicate despite frustration. Areas of concern include significantly reduced intelligibility across both languages, limited grammatical morphology, and reduced opportunities for Spanish language modeling in his current daycare placement, which may be compounding rather than causing his underlying disorder.

SESSION SCHEDULE

The following schedule reflects Mateo's current and recommended therapy sessions:

Day	Start Time	Stop Time	Location
Monday	9:00 a.m.	9:45 a.m.	Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC, 4821 Forestville Road, Suite 220, Raleigh
Wednesday	3:30 p.m.	4:15 p.m.	Sunshine Bilingual Daycare and Preschool, Garner
Friday	10:00 a.m.	10:45 a.m.	Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC, 4821 Forestville Road, Suite 220, Raleigh

Group language sessions, which include peer Jayden Ortiz and two other children, are held on Wednesdays from 4:30 p.m. to 5:15 p.m. at the same clinic location.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo qualifies for ongoing early intervention services through Wake County CDSA under his existing IFSP (NC ITP Child ID ITP-2026-04471). It is recommended that service frequency increase from one to two sessions weekly given the severity of findings across both languages.

2. Direct speech-language therapy should target: (a) phonological processes including velar fronting and final consonant deletion using a Cycles approach; (b) expressive grammar in both English and Spanish using naturalistic, play-based strategies consistent with Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" principles; and (c) functional communication strategies to reduce frustration-related behaviors.

3. Given the mismatch between the daycare's advertised bilingual model and the English-only classroom environment, this examiner recommends the family discuss language supports with Ms. Amanda Lopez and daycare administration, and consider requesting that Mr. Carlos Mendez provide more consistent Spanish language modeling during structured activities.

4. Continued use of PROMPT techniques is recommended during articulation drills given Mateo's positive response to tactile-kinesthetic cueing observed during the evaluation session on February 12, 2026.

5. Parents are encouraged to continue rich Spanish language exposure at home, including narrating daily routines, reading bilingual books provided through Wake County Smart Start, and incorporating Mateo's interest in Rocky and Luna into language-building play (e.g., narrating pet care routines in both languages).

6. Re-evaluation of hearing status is recommended annually given history of recurrent otitis media, coordinated through Dr. Megan Reyes or primary care with Dr. Anil Patel.

7. Continued coordination with Wake County Partnership for Children is recommended to ensure consistent case management as Mateo approaches transition planning at age three... note: transition to preschool services should be planned well before his third birthday given current ITP enrollment, with transition conference to be scheduled through CDSA by September 2026.

IFSP OUTCOME REVIEW

The table below summarizes progress on Mateo's current IFSP outcomes as of this evaluation.

Outcome	Strategies	Progress	Date
Mateo will increase intelligibility of connected speech to 60% with familiar listeners	Cycles approach targeting velar fronting and final consonant deletion; home practice with visual cue cards in English and Spanish	Partial progress; intelligibility improved from 25% to 40% with unfamiliar listeners	January 15, 2026
Mateo will use 3-4 word utterances to request and comment during play	Hanen-based naturalistic language strategies; parent coaching during home visits	Good progress; MLU increased from 2.1 to 2.8 (English) and 2.6 to 3.4 (Spanish)	January 15, 2026
Mateo will reduce frustration behaviors when not understood by using a replacement communication strategy	PROMPT cueing paired with gesture and point-to-picture backup strategy introduced by occupational therapist	Emerging; uses pointing consistently but verbal replacement attempts remain inconsistent	January 15, 2026
Mateo will demonstrate correct gender agreement on common Spanish articles in spontaneous speech	Direct modeling and recast strategies during Spanish-language play sessions	Minimal progress; errors persist at similar rate since initiation of service	January 15, 2026

SUMMARY

Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez, a bilingual Spanish/English-speaking 4;2-year-old, presents with a Developmental Language Disorder and co-occurring Speech Sound Disorder affecting both of his languages, confirmed through comprehensive bilingual assessment including the PLS-5, CELF Preschool-3, GFTA-3, and BESA. His difficulties are not attributable to typical bilingual development or language difference, as deficits were documented across both English and Spanish. He continues to qualify for early intervention services through Wake County CDSA and is recommended for increased service frequency, continued use of Cycles, Hanen, and PROMPT approaches, and closer collaboration between home, daycare, and service providers to ensure consistent Spanish language modeling. His family remains highly engaged and motivated, and his home environment, including his sister Valentina Flores, babysitter Rosa Pérez, grandmother M.R., and extended family, provides a strong foundation for continued progress.

This report was prepared following direct assessment, parent and teacher interview, and record review. Please contact this examiner at (919) 555-0148 or jwalsh@carolinabilingualslp.com with any questions.

Respectfully submitted,

Jennifer Walsh, M.S., CCC-SLP
Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC

**Reason for Review**

This periodic IFSP review was completed for María José Hernández Ortiz, known to her family as "Majo," to update present levels of development, review progress on current outcomes, and revise strategies ahead of her upcoming transition-planning conversation. This is Majo's fifth periodic review since enrollment and her third within the current eligibility period. She remains enrolled in North Carolina's Infant-Toddler Program through Piedmont CDSA – Lexington Office with a primary eligible diagnosis of F80.1 (expressive language disorder) and a secondary history of prematurity (R62.0). Speech-language services are billed under 92523 (evaluation) and 92507 (individual treatment).

**Family Information and Household Composition**

Majo lives at home with her mother, Daniela Ortiz Martínez; her father, Carlos Hernández Reyes; and her older brother, Mateo Hernández Ortiz, age 5. The family's maternal grandmother, Rosa Martínez, lives two streets away and provides childcare most afternoons while both parents work. Daniela works as a home health aide for ComForCare Home Care, typically from 7:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.. Carlos works two jobs to support the household: an overnight shift at Royal Food Processing and a weekend custodial shift at the VFW post on the edge of town. Because of this schedule, Carlos is usually asleep during daytime appointments, and Daniela remains the primary contact for scheduling.

The family speaks Spanish at home and English with providers and at Majo's daycare. Mateo attends kindergarten nearby and is described by his parents as Majo's "best teacher," since he narrates play and models words for her constantly. Extended family, including cousins and Rosa Martínez, gather at the home most Sundays, which the family identifies as an important but currently difficult context for Majo, who tends to withdraw in larger groups.

**Family Concerns, Priorities, and Resources**

During the home visit on September 18, 2026, Daniela shared the family's concerns in her own words, translated with her permission: "Lo que más nos preocupa es que Majo se frustra mucho cuando no la entendemos. Grita o nos jala la mano en vez de decirnos lo que quiere." She also said, "Queremos que hable más con su hermano y con sus primos, porque en las reuniones familiares ella se queda callada." Carlos joined partway through the visit on a break between jobs and added, in Spanish, "Yo quiero que ella pueda decirle a su abuela lo que necesita sin tener que adivinar." He also mentioned a longstanding worry that Majo's hearing might be affected, since she sometimes does not turn when he calls her name from another room, even though her recent hearing test came back normal.

The family's priorities for this review period are: (1) reducing Majo's frustration-related behaviors (hitting, pulling) by giving her more functional ways to request and protest; (2) increasing her intelligibility so that extended family, including Rosa Martínez and visiting cousins, can understand her; and (3) preparing for her transition out of the Infant-Toddler Program before her third birthday.

The family's resources include a stable two-income household despite the demanding schedule, a supportive grandmother willing to practice home strategies, and strong motivation from Mateo, who enjoys "teaching" his sister new words. Daniela noted that finding time to attend appointments is difficult given her schedule at ComForCare Home Care, and the family asked whether some visits could be scheduled on her days off, which the team will try to accommodate going forward.

**Daily Routines**

Majo wakes around 6:30 a.m. and eats breakfast with Mateo before he leaves for school. She attends Little Sprouts Early Head Start three days a week from 8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., where her lead teacher, Keisha Brown, reports that Majo plays near peers but rarely initiates with them; one classmate, Josiah, frequently brings her toys and she accepts them without words. On non-daycare days, Rosa Martínez cares for her at home, where routines include a midday meal, outdoor play in the backyard, and a nap from about 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m.. Evenings involve dinner as a family, bath time, and a bedtime routine with books that Daniela reads in Spanish. On weekends, the family often visits a nearby park or attends the Sunday gathering with extended relatives, where Majo is reported to stay close to Daniela rather than joining cousin play. Majo goes to bed around 8:00 p.m., and the family reports minimal screen time during the week, with slightly more on weekend mornings.

**Developmental and Medical History**

Majo was born at 32 weeks gestation, weighing 3 pounds, 6 ounces, with Apgar scores of 6 and 8. She spent 19 days in the neonatal intensive care unit at Trinity Health Carolinas – Lexington Campus following delivery, where she required supplemental oxygen and had early feeding difficulty requiring a nasogastric tube for the first 9 days. She was discharged home on full oral feeds and followed by early intervention physical therapy for mild hypotonia during her first year, which has since resolved.

Majo's pediatrician, Dr. James Whitfield, referred the family to the Infant-Toddler Program at her 4-month well visit due to feeding and tone concerns. She was seen for an audiology evaluation on June 11, 2026 at Trinity Health Carolinas ENT & Audiology – High Point Campus; audiologist M.R. documented normal hearing bilaterally across all tested frequencies and recommended no further audiologic follow-up at this time, which the family found reassuring given their ongoing concern about her name-response behavior. Majo was also seen by ENT physician Dr. Patricia Nguyen at Trinity Health Carolinas Pediatric Specialty Clinic – Winston-Salem Campus on August 4, 2026 for evaluation of frequent upper respiratory infections and recurring ear infections reported at a rate of roughly 4 episodes per year; no chronic ear disease was found on exam, and myringotomy tubes were not recommended at this time, though the family was advised to monitor closely over the winter season.

**Other Agencies and Services**

The family receives nutrition support through WIC and has an open case with Davidson County DSS for a one-time energy assistance benefit applied for earlier this year. Majo was referred to Davidson County Smart Start for a developmental playgroup, though the family has not yet been able to attend due to scheduling conflicts with Daniela's work. Service coordination through Piedmont CDSA – Lexington Office continues to be managed by Brenda Collins, who also coordinates with Majo's pediatric medical home and shares updates with Dr. James Whitfield's office before each review.

**Assessment Results**

Current assessment was completed on September 15, 2026 by Jessica Park, bilingual SLP, using parent report, play-based observation, and direct testing in both Spanish and English. Language input at home is estimated by parent report at approximately 70% Spanish and 30% English.

The Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale was administered using parent report and direct elicitation. Majo demonstrated skills in the interaction-attachment and pragmatics domains consistent with her chronological age, but scored approximately 9 months below age expectations in expressive language, with an age equivalent of 18 months. Her receptive language age equivalent was 22 months, within the low average range.

The Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4 (cognitive and language subtests) was administered jointly with Majo's early intervention team. She obtained a Receptive Communication scaled score of 7 (16th percentile) and an Expressive Communication scaled score of 4 (2nd percentile), yielding a composite Language standard score of 78 (7th percentile, 73-83 confidence interval). Cognitive scores fell within the average range, with a standard score of 97.

Gross and fine motor skills were screened using the Peabody Developmental Motor Scales-3, which yielded a Total Motor Quotient of 91 (27th percentile), within normal limits, consistent with her history of mild hypotonia that has largely resolved.

A bilingual vocabulary checklist completed by Daniela estimated a total productive vocabulary of approximately 35 words across both languages, with roughly 22 Spanish words and 13 English words, and minimal true translation equivalents, which is expected at this stage of bilingual development.

Articulation was informally sampled given Majo's young age; a formal Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 is planned once she reliably imitates single words in isolation. During the sample, she produced /p/, /m/, /b/, and /n/ consistently in word-initial position, but substituted [t] for /k/ and omitted final consonants, producing "pa" for "pan." She combined two words occasionally, such as "mas aba" for "más agua" (more water), typically with moderate cues.

**Present Levels of Development**

*Communication:* Majo communicates primarily through gestures, vocalizations, and a growing set of single words in both Spanish and English. She understands significantly more than she produces, following two-step directions in Spanish (3 of 4 trials) with minimal cues. She frequently code-switches within short utterances, for example pairing an English word with a Spanish carrier phrase. When frustrated, she is reported to hit, pull hands, or scream rather than request verbally or gesturally, consistent with the family's top concern.

*Social-Emotional:* Majo is affectionate with family and seeks out Daniela and Mateo for comfort. At Little Sprouts Early Head Start, Keisha Brown reports she plays alongside peers but needs adult support to join group activities, and she tends to watch rather than approach unfamiliar children at larger gatherings.

*Motor and Self-Care:* Age-appropriate gross motor skills; feeds herself with a spoon with moderate spilling; working on using an open cup independently; occasional food refusal with mixed or unfamiliar textures, though no formal feeding evaluation has been requested by the family at this time.

**Outcomes and Strategies**

Outcome 1: Majo will use 3-5 word combinations to request and protest instead of physical behaviors, in at least 4 of 5 observed opportunities across home and daycare settings, by the next review.
Strategies: Jessica Park will coach Daniela, Carlos, and Rosa Martínez using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies, including expectant waiting and modeling short requesting phrases in Spanish ("quiero más," "ayuda, por favor"). Keisha Brown will model the same phrases during daycare transitions. Sessions will occur biweekly in the home and will include Mateo as a communication partner when available, since he is highly motivated to prompt his sister.

Outcome 2: Majo will increase intelligibility of single words so that unfamiliar listeners, including extended family, can understand her familiar words in 7 of 10 attempts.
Strategies: Direct therapy will target final consonant inclusion and the /k/-for-[t] substitution using PROMPT tactile cueing during structured play. Home practice will focus on five core target words selected by the family, modeled slowly with maximum cues fading to minimal cues over the review period, with Rosa Martínez practicing the same target words during afternoon care.

Outcome 3: The family will identify and begin attending at least one community-based playgroup or peer interaction opportunity before transition planning.
Strategies: Brenda Collins will assist the family in rescheduling the Davidson County Smart Start playgroup referral around Daniela's work calendar at ComForCare Home Care, and will explore whether a weekend option exists given Carlos's schedule at Royal Food Processing and the VFW.

**Service Delivery**

Speech-language therapy: 60 minutes weekly, individual, in the home, delivered by Jessica Park through Carolina Pediatric Therapy Associates, PLLC, billed under 92507. Service coordination: monthly contact by Brenda Collins, Piedmont CDSA – Lexington Office. This review reflects services delivered between April 9, 2026 and October 2, 2026. The next periodic review is scheduled for April 2, 2027, with transition planning to begin no later than July 2027.

Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC
(conocida como "Piedmont Pediatric Speech"; siglas "PPSLS")
4820 Kildaire Farm Road, Suite 210, Cary, 27518
Tel: (919) 555-0172 • Fax: (919) 555-0173
Correo electrónico: intake@piedmontpeds-slp.com

INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y EL LENGUAJE

Nombre de la niña: María José Reyes del Río (familiarmente "MJ")
Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de abril de 2021
Edad cronológica en la evaluación: 4;6
Fecha de la evaluación: 2 de octubre de 2026
Número de expediente: CDSA-2026-01452
Número de Medicaid: 900234567A
Agencia remitente: CDSA de la Región del Piedmont
Coordinadora de servicios: Brenda Soto-Vega
Evaluadora: Yolanda Fuentes-Campos, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingüe (inglés/español)
Intérprete: no se requirió; la evaluadora es bilingüe

Madre: Lucía del Río Hernández
Padre: Diego Reyes Sánchez
Dirección: 142 Birchwood Lane, Fuquay-Varina, Condado de Wake, 27526
Teléfono: (919) 555-0148

RAZÓN DE LA REMISIÓN

María José Reyes del Río fue remitida a Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC ("PPSLS") para una evaluación del habla y el lenguaje tras una revisión de rutina del IFSP el 15 de septiembre de 2026, en la cual su coordinadora de servicios, Brenda Soto-Vega, de CDSA de la Región del Piedmont, notó un progreso limitado en los resultados relacionados con el lenguaje expresivo. El pediatra de la niña, Dr. Esteban Villalobos, también expresó preocupación por la inteligibilidad del habla en una nota de referencia fechada el 8 de septiembre de 2026. La maestra de la niña en Centro Pequeños Pasos, la Sra. Carmen Olvera, reportó que MJ con frecuencia señala objetos en vez de nombrarlos y que sus compañeros de clase, entre ellos Santiago Lemus y Valentina Cho, a menudo no entienden lo que ella intenta comunicar durante el juego.

La evaluadora, Yolanda Fuentes-Campos, realizó la evaluación en el hogar de la familia el 2 de octubre de 2026 entre las 9:30 a.m. y las 11:15 a.m., con la participación de la madre, Lucía del Río Hernández.

HISTORIA PRENATAL Y DE NACIMIENTO

Según reporta la madre, Lucía del Río Hernández, el embarazo de María José Reyes del Río fue a término, sin complicaciones significativas, con control prenatal regular. La niña nació a las 38 semanas de gestación en el WakeMed Cary Hospital el 14 de abril de 2021, con un peso al nacer de 3,200 gramos y una puntuación de Apgar de 8 al minuto y 9 a los cinco minutos. No se reportaron complicaciones neonatales ni estadía en la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales.

HISTORIA MÉDICA

María José Reyes del Río ha tenido un historial de otitis media recurrente, con tres episodios documentados entre los 18 meses y los 30 meses de edad, tratados con tubos de ventilación colocados por el Dr. Marcus Abernathy, otorrinolaringólogo, el 3 de marzo de 2023. Una audiometría de seguimiento realizada el 20 de agosto de 2026 resultó dentro de límites normales bilateralmente. No hay historial de convulsiones, hospitalizaciones adicionales, ni cirugías mayores. La madre reporta que la niña toma actualmente un multivitamínico diario; no se reportan otros medicamentos.

El diagnóstico codificado para esta evaluación corresponde a F80.9 (trastorno del desarrollo del habla y el lenguaje, no especificado), facturado bajo el código 92523 (evaluación de producción del habla y comprensión del lenguaje).

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE IDIOMA

El hogar de María José Reyes del Río es predominantemente hispanohablante. La madre, Lucía del Río Hernández, y el padre, Diego Reyes Sánchez, hablan español como primer idioma; el inglés se usa de manera limitada en el hogar, principalmente por el hermano mayor de MJ, Joaquín Reyes del Río, de 9 años, quien asiste a la escuela primaria local y traduce ocasionalmente para sus padres.

La familia vive con la abuela materna, Rosario Hernández Fuentes, quien cuida de MJ tres días a la semana mientras los padres trabajan. El padre, Diego Reyes Sánchez, trabaja en la construcción para Carolina Builders Construction Company (también referida por la familia como "la Compañía de Construcción Carolina Builders"), con turnos que a menudo se extienden hasta después de las 6:00 p.m.. La madre, Lucía del Río Hernández, trabaja medio tiempo en el restaurante La Cocina de Doña Rosa y anteriormente trabajó en la tienda Tienda Fuentes ("Fuentes Store") del centro de Fuquay-Varina. Antes del nacimiento de MJ, la madre trabajó en turnos nocturnos en la planta procesadora Carolina Poultry Processing Plant (conocida también como "la Planta Procesadora de Pollo Carolina"), un empleo que, según reporta, limitó el tiempo de interacción verbal con Joaquín Reyes del Río durante su primera infancia.

Un tío materno, hermano de Lucía del Río Hernández, trabaja en la granja familiar Hernández Family Farm ("Granja Hernández") en el condado vecino, y visita los fines de semana. La abuela, Rosario Hernández Fuentes, también recibe apoyo de un servicio de limpieza, Estrella Cleaning Service ("Servicio de Limpieza Estrella"), donde trabaja una prima de la familia, Yesenia del Río Campos, los sábados.

La familia reporta ingreso familiar que califica para asistencia de WIC y ha recibido previamente apoyo de Smart Start del Condado de Wake para servicios de cuidado infantil subvencionado.

HISTORIA DEL DESARROLLO DEL LENGUAJE

Según reporta la madre, María José Reyes del Río dijo sus primeras palabras alrededor de los 22 meses, considerablemente más tarde que su hermano Joaquín Reyes del Río, quien habló sus primeras palabras alrededor de los 12 meses. Actualmente, MJ combina dos palabras de manera inconsistente (por ejemplo, "quiere agua", "no más") pero rara vez produce oraciones de tres o más palabras. La madre reporta que la familia de la mascota, el perro Rocky, con frecuencia acompaña a MJ durante el juego, y que durante una muestra espontánea de lenguaje la niña dijo "quiero jugar con Rocky" de manera relativamente clara, aunque con omisión de la consonante final.

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

Se administraron las siguientes pruebas estandarizadas y procedimientos informales:

1. Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale
2. Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3)
3. Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-4), subpruebas de comunicación
4. Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Fifth Edition (PPVT-5), adaptada informalmente al español
5. Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo (20 minutos), transcrita y analizada con códigos SALT
6. Observación clínica y entrevista a los padres

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS

Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale: Comprensión del lenguaje: edad equivalente 2;6–3;0; Expresión del lenguaje: edad equivalente 2;0–2;6. Estos resultados ubican a MJ significativamente por debajo de su edad cronológica de 4;6.

Bayley-4, Subprueba de Comunicación Expresiva: puntuación escalar de 4, percentil 2. Subprueba de Comunicación Receptiva: puntuación escalar de 6, percentil 9.

PPVT-5 (administración informal en español): puntuación estándar de 71, intervalo de confianza del 95%: 65-77, percentil 3.

GFTA-3: puntuación estándar de 73, intervalo de confianza del 95%: 68-78, percentil 4.

Tabla resumen de puntuaciones:

Prueba | Puntuación estándar/escalar | Percentil | Edad equivalente
Rossetti — Comprensión | N/A | N/A | 2;6–3;0
Rossetti — Expresión | N/A | N/A | 2;0–2;6
Bayley-4 — Comunicación Expresiva | 4 | 2 | N/A
Bayley-4 — Comunicación Receptiva | 6 | 9 | N/A
PPVT-5 | 71 | 3 | N/A
GFTA-3 | 73 | 4 | N/A

ANÁLISIS FONOLÓGICO

Durante la administración del GFTA-3 y la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, se observaron los siguientes patrones de error:

Ante el estímulo "pelota", MJ produjo "peota" (omisión de la líquida /l/ en posición intervocálica). Ante el estímulo "carro", produjo "calo" (sustitución de la vibrante múltiple /r/ por la lateral /l/). Ante el estímulo "perro", produjo "pego" (sustitución de /r/ por /g/, con omisión de la vocal final). Ante el estímulo "taza", produjo "tasa" (proceso fonológico de frontalización). Ante el estímulo "globo", produjo "gobo" (simplificación de grupo consonántico, omisión de /l/).

Se identificaron los siguientes procesos fonológicos persistentes más allá de la edad esperada: reducción de grupos consonánticos (afecta /pl/, /gl/, /bl/), gliding de líquidas (/r/ → [l], /ɾ/ → [j]), y omisión de consonante final. La inteligibilidad general del habla de MJ se estimó en 40% para oyentes familiares y menos del 20% para oyentes no familiares, según lo observado durante la sesión y reportado por la madre.

MJ respondió favorablemente a claves articulatorias con claves verbales moderadas ("mod cues"), logrando producir el fonema /k/ de manera aislada en 8 de 10 intentos con apoyo, pero solo en 3 de 10 intentos sin apoyo ("claves mínimas"). Con máximas claves táctiles, logró aproximar el fonema /g/ en posición inicial en 6 de 10 ensayos.

OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES

MJ se mostró colaborativa durante la mayor parte de la sesión, aunque mostró frustración observable cuando sus intentos de comunicación no fueron comprendidos de inmediato por la evaluadora. Recurrió frecuentemente a gestos, señalamiento y vocalizaciones no específicas para comunicar sus necesidades. Mostró buen contacto visual, atención conjunta apropiada para su edad, y juego simbólico consistente con las expectativas del desarrollo, incluyendo secuencias de juego con una muñeca y un set de cocina de juguete.

La madre, Lucía del Río Hernández, reportó que en el Centro Pequeños Pasos, MJ interactúa principalmente con dos compañeras, Isabela Ferreira y Génesis Padilla, pero que con frecuencia se retira del juego grupal cuando no logra hacerse entender.

REVISIÓN DE RESULTADOS DEL IFSP

A continuación se presenta la tabla de revisión del IFSP, con el progreso hacia cada resultado desde la última revisión:

Resultado	Estrategias	Progreso	Fecha
Resultado 1: MJ usará oraciones de 2-3 palabras para pedir objetos deseados	Modelado de lenguaje expandido, tiempo de espera, rutinas de juego estructurado	Progreso mínimo; continúa principalmente en etapa de una palabra	15 de septiembre de 2026
Resultado 2: MJ seguirá instrucciones de dos pasos en el hogar	Instrucciones visuales, repetición, práctica en rutinas diarias	Progreso emergente; sigue instrucciones familiares con apoyo contextual	15 de septiembre de 2026
Resultado 3: MJ aumentará la inteligibilidad de su habla para oyentes familiares	Estimulación fonológica, modelado articulatorio, retroalimentación auditiva	Progreso limitado; inteligibilidad permanece baja	15 de septiembre de 2026
Resultado 4: La familia implementará estrategias de lenguaje en rutinas del hogar	Entrenamiento a la madre, materiales bilingües, visitas de coordinación	Progreso adecuado; la madre reporta uso consistente de estrategias	15 de septiembre de 2026

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Con base en los resultados obtenidos, María José Reyes del Río presenta un retraso significativo tanto en el lenguaje receptivo como expresivo, junto con un trastorno fonológico de moderado a severo que afecta de manera considerable su inteligibilidad del habla. Sus habilidades de comunicación se ubican consistentemente por debajo del percentil 10 en todas las medidas estandarizadas administradas, lo cual es congruente con los informes de la maestra, Sra. Carmen Olvera, y de los padres respecto a dificultades de comunicación funcional en el hogar, en el centro de cuidado infantil, y en interacciones con pares.

La historia de otitis media recurrente, documentada por el Dr. Marcus Abernathy, pudo haber contribuido a las dificultades actuales, aunque la audiometría reciente del 20 de agosto de 2026 no indica una pérdida auditiva activa. El entorno bilingüe del hogar no se considera la causa principal de las dificultades observadas, ya que se identifican retrasos comparables en ambos idiomas y no hay evidencia de un patrón de adquisición típica en ninguno de los dos.

Estos hallazgos son consistentes con un diagnóstico de trastorno del desarrollo del lenguaje (TDL) con un componente fonológico significativo, codificado como F80.9.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda que María José Reyes del Río continúe recibiendo servicios de intervención temprana a través de CDSA de la Región del Piedmont, con un aumento en la frecuencia de terapia del habla y lenguaje a dos sesiones de 30 minutos por semana.

2. Se recomienda la incorporación del enfoque Hanen ("It Takes Two to Talk") para entrenar a la madre, Lucía del Río Hernández, y a otros cuidadores, incluyendo a la abuela, Rosario Hernández Fuentes, en estrategias de estimulación del lenguaje durante las rutinas diarias.

3. Se recomienda la implementación del enfoque PROMPT para abordar los patrones articulatorios y fonológicos observados, dada su eficacia documentada en el tratamiento de trastornos motores del habla y fonológicos severos.

4. Alternativamente, el enfoque de Cycles podría utilizarse para abordar de manera sistemática los procesos fonológicos identificados (reducción de grupos consonánticos, gliding de líquidas, omisión de consonante final).

5. Se recomienda una reevaluación audiológica de seguimiento en seis meses, dado el historial de otitis media recurrente, a cargo del Dr. Marcus Abernathy o un proveedor equivalente.

6. Se recomienda coordinar con el Centro Pequeños Pasos y la Sra. Carmen Olvera para implementar estrategias de apoyo al lenguaje durante las actividades grupales, incluyendo tiempo de espera estructurado y modelado de lenguaje expandido.

7. Se recomienda que la familia continúe con el apoyo de Smart Start del Condado de Wake para asegurar la continuidad del cuidado infantil subvencionado mientras los padres mantienen sus horarios laborales actuales.

8. Se recomienda una revisión del IFSP en un plazo no mayor a seis meses para actualizar los resultados y estrategias en función del progreso observado.

Este informe fue preparado por Yolanda Fuentes-Campos, M.S., CCC-SLP, en nombre de Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC ("PPSLS"), y refleja el desempeño de María José Reyes del Río durante la sesión de evaluación del 2 de octubre de 2026. Para preguntas adicionales, comuníquese con Piedmont Pediatric Speech al (919) 555-0172 o al correo intake@piedmontpeds-slp.com.

October 2, 2026

Re: Speech-Language Evaluation Report for María José Torres Hernández
Date of Birth: March 14, 2022
Medicaid ID: 482915637B
CDSA Case Number: CDSA-2026-01144

Dear Carlos and Lucía,

Thank you for trusting me with María José's speech-language evaluation. I am Daniela Reyes-Moreno, M.S., CCC-SLP, a bilingual speech-language pathologist with Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC. I saw María José for two sessions, on September 18, 2026 and September 25, 2026, at our clinic in Durham. I tested her in both English and Spanish, since your family uses both languages at home. This letter explains what I found and what I recommend next.

**Reason for the Evaluation**

María José's pediatrician, Dr. Patricia Nguyen, referred her for a speech and language evaluation after her 4-year well-check on August 11, 2026. You had also raised concerns with Monica Fields, the service coordinator at the Durham County Children's Developmental Services Agency, that María José's speech is harder to understand than other children her age. Her teacher at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, Ms. Amanda Collins, shared similar concerns and noted that María José often points or gestures instead of using words when she is frustrated.

**Birth and Medical History**

María José was born at Duke Regional Hospital at 37 weeks gestational age, weighing 5 lbs 14 oz at birth, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9. She spent three days in the newborn nursery for mild jaundice but had no NICU stay. Lucía reported a healthy pregnancy with regular prenatal care. María José met early motor milestones (sitting, walking) within typical ranges, but her parents noted she was later to combine words than her older brother, Diego, was at the same age. She has had five ear infections since age 18 months and had ear tubes placed in February 2025 by Dr. Samuel Oyelaran, an ENT. Her hearing was last screened on March 3, 2026 and was within normal limits bilaterally. She has no known seizure history and takes no daily medications. Her ICD-10 diagnosis code from this evaluation is F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder), and the billing code used today was CPT 92523.

**Family and Language History**

María José lives with her parents, Carlos Torres Medina and Lucía Hernández Ibarra, her older brother Diego (age 7), and her younger sister Camila (age 18 months). Her maternal grandmother, Rosa Ibarra Campos, lives with the family and cares for the children while Lucía works. Rosa speaks only Spanish with the children. Carlos works at Blue Ridge Furniture Manufacturing, and Lucía works part-time at Sunrise Poultry Processing. The family's home language is primarily Spanish, with English introduced through Little Sprouts Early Learning Center and television. Lucía estimates María José hears about 70% Spanish and 30% English at home.

The family receives support from several local programs. Lucía told me they are enrolled with the Durham County WIC Program for nutrition support, and the family has an open case with Durham County Department of Social Services. Camila attends Durham Early Head Start, and the family was connected to early intervention through a referral from the Triangle Partnership for Children (the local Smart Start partner agency for Durham County). I encouraged Carlos and Lucía to keep that connection active, since Smart Start affiliates often help families navigate preschool speech services.

At home, María José enjoys playing with the family dog, Max, and with her cousin Valentina when the family visits relatives. Lucía's mother, Rosa, mentioned that María José's great-aunt in Mexico, Beatriz, calls often; her number is +52 55 1234 5678 in case the family wants to coordinate a shared session by phone. At daycare, María José's favorite friend is a classmate named Ethan, and the two often play in the dramatic-play area together.

**Behavioral Observations**

María José separated easily from Lucía and engaged well with toys and books during both sessions. She was attentive for about 20 minutes at a time before needing a short movement break. She used a mix of English and Spanish words and showed strong nonverbal communication, including pointing, eye contact, and gesture. When she could not find a word, she sometimes said "no puedo" or shrugged. She was cooperative throughout testing and seemed to enjoy the picture-based tasks most.

**Standardized Test Results**

I used both English and Spanish versions of standardized tools, along with a bilingual language sample, to get a full picture of María José's skills in each language.

| Test / Subtest | Date Administered | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% Confidence Interval |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension (English) | September 18, 2026 | 82 | 12th | 76-88 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication (English) | September 18, 2026 | 75 | 5th | 69-81 |
| PLS-5 Total Language Score (English) | September 18, 2026 | 77 | 6th | 71-83 |
| BESA Morphosyntax (Spanish) | September 25, 2026 | 88 | 21st | 81-95 |
| BESA Semantics (Spanish) | September 25, 2026 | 91 | 27th | 84-98 |
| GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words | September 18, 2026 | 70 | 2nd | 65-75 |

On the GFTA-3, María José substituted /t/ for /k/ and /d/ for /g/ in most positions, and she deleted final consonants in about 60% of words tested. She produced the Spanish tap /ɾ/ inconsistently, correct in 3 of 5 trials. When asked to name a picture of a banana, she said "nana," and when asked to name "pescado" (fish), she said "pe-ca." She was stimulable for /k/ in isolation with moderate cues and produced it correctly with minimal cues in syllables by the end of the session.

Her expressive vocabulary diversity was below average for her age in both languages, though stronger in Spanish. In a 50-utterance language sample, she used two-word combinations about 8 of 10 times she attempted a sentence, such as "mas agua" and "dog run," but rarely used three-word combinations. Her mean length of utterance was estimated at 2.1 morphemes, which falls at roughly the 2;6 age-equivalent level, below her chronological age of 4;6.

**Impressions**

Based on today's testing, parent and teacher report, and classroom observation, María José presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both English and Spanish, along with a moderate speech sound disorder. Her difficulties are consistent across both languages, which tells me this is a true language and speech disorder and not simply a difference related to learning two languages. Her strengths include good social communication, strong nonverbal skills, and a cooperative, curious approach to new tasks.

**Recommendations**

1. Individual speech-language therapy, one to two times per week, addressing both speech sound production and expressive/receptive language, delivered bilingually when possible.
2. Continued use of Hanen strategies at home to support language growth during daily routines, which I can model for the family during a coaching visit.
3. A classroom consultation with Ms. Amanda Collins at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center to support carryover of new sounds and vocabulary during the school day.

Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
4718 Monroe Road, Suite 210, Charlotte, 28205
Tel: (704) 555-0133 | Fax: (704) 555-0134

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT / INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Hernández ("Teo")
Date of Birth: September 15, 2021
Chronological Age (CA): 4;10
Gender: Male
Parents/Guardians: Lucía Rodríguez Cruz (mother), Jorge Cruz Medina (father)
Home Address: 2214 Senna Drive, Charlotte, 28214, Mecklenburg County
Mother's Cell: 980-555-0147 | Father's Cell: 704.555.0198
Medicaid ID: 784512369B
Case/Record ID: CDSA-2026-01154
Date(s) of Evaluation: July 28, 2026 and July 30, 2026
Evaluator: Camila Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP
Referral Source: Rafael Alvarez, M.D. (pediatrician)
Primary Language(s) in the Home: Spanish and English
Interpreter: Not needed; evaluator is bilingual (Spanish/English)

Razón de la referencia y antecedentes del caso. Teo fue referido a este servicio por su pediatra, el Dr. Rafael Alvarez, en Novant Health Huntersville Medical Center, after his four-year well-child visit revealed persistent concerns about expressive language and intelligibility. Su mamá, Lucía Rodríguez Cruz, reports that "Teo entiende todo lo que le decimos, pero cuando él quiere explicar algo, se frustra porque no le salen las palabras." Father, Jorge Cruz Medina, added in the intake interview that at home Teo mixes both languages freely, "igual que su hermana cuando tenía su edad," referring to his older sister Valentina Cruz Rodríguez ("Vale"), now seven. Teo also has a younger brother, Diego Cruz Rodríguez, age sixteen months, who is not yet a concern to the family. Teo was previously followed by Mecklenburg County CDSA under Service Coordinator Marisol Ortiz, who opened an IFSP on November 3, 2025 and conducted a six-month review on May 4, 2026; this evaluation updates Teo's IFSP Outcome 2, which addresses functional communication across environments.

Historia de nacimiento y médica. Lucía reports an uncomplicated pregnancy until 32 weeks gestation, when she developed preeclampsia and was admitted to Novant Health Huntersville Medical Center. Teo was delivered by emergency cesarean section at 34 weeks gestational age, weighing 4 lbs, 2 oz with Apgar scores of 6 and 8 at one and five minutes, respectively. He spent 18 days in the NICU at Novant Health Huntersville Medical Center, where he required supplemental oxygen and had difficulty with suck-swallow-breathe coordination; a feeding specialist there, Hannah Brooks, OTR/L, worked with the family on oral feeding before discharge. Lucía recalls, "casi no lo pudimos cargar las primeras dos semanas, estaba muy delicadito." Medical history is otherwise significant for recurrent otitis media, with six documented episodes between 12 and 30 months of age. Teo received bilateral pressure-equalization tubes on February 14, 2023, placed by Priya Patel, M.D., at Atrium Health Levine Children's – Myers Park Campus. A subsequent audiological evaluation on June 3, 2024 by Susan Kim, Au.D., at the same campus documented hearing within normal limits bilaterally, with type A tympanograms at that visit. No seizures, no significant head trauma, and no hospitalizations since the NICU stay are reported. Immunizations are up to date per the pediatrician's records, and Teo takes no current medications. Vision was screened as normal at the same well-child visit that prompted this referral.

Historia familiar y de lenguaje. The household is Spanish-dominant, with Lucía and Jorge both reporting Spanish as their first and preferred language, though both are functionally bilingual for work and community purposes. Jorge works night shifts at Daimler Trucks North America's plant in Mount Holly, while Lucía is employed part-time at a Harris Teeter distribution center. Primary daytime childcare for Teo and his younger brother Diego is provided by their niñera, Esperanza Gutiérrez Díaz, who has cared for the family's children since Vale was an infant and speaks only Spanish with the boys. Teo attends Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare three mornings per week, where his lead teacher is Debra Lopez and the classroom assistant is Tyler Banks. Ms. Lopez reports that Teo is social but often defers to gestures and single words with peers such as Aiden Matthews, Emma Chen, and Sofía Nieves, and that he becomes notably quiet during English-only circle time compared to free play, when he code-switches comfortably. Extended family is close-knit: paternal cousins Juan Pablo Rodríguez ("Juanito") and José Luis Rodríguez ("Pepe") visit most weekends and are described by Jorge as Teo's closest playmates outside daycare. Teo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Elena Hernández Soto, lives in Puebla and speaks with the family by video call several times weekly; her number there is +52 222 555 0176. Lucía noted that her mother worries about Teo's speech too: "mi mamá me dice que ni ella le entiende cuando él le cuenta de la escuela." The family also has a dog, Canela, who Teo reportedly talks to constantly in a mix of both languages, sometimes more fluently than he speaks to adults, per parent report.

At home, family routines are bilingual and flexible rather than strictly separated by speaker. Older sister Vale often translates for Teo when he gets frustrated, which Lucía says has become a pattern of concern: "ella le adivina lo que quiere antes de que él termine de decirlo." Developmental milestones were reportedly delayed across domains: Teo sat independently around 9 months, walked at 17 months (adjusted for prematurity), and said his first words, "mamá" and "agua," around 22 months. Word combinations did not emerge until approximately 3;0. Jorge reports that extended family initially attributed the delay to "ser bilingüe," a belief the evaluator addressed directly during the interview, clarifying that bilingual exposure does not cause or compound a primary language disorder.

Observaciones conductuales y clínicas. Teo presented as a friendly, easily redirected child who separated from his mother without difficulty for the standardized testing portion of the session, though Lucía remained in the room per family preference. Attention to task was adequate with frequent breaks and preferred toys, including a small truck he called "troka" throughout the session. Play skills were age-appropriate, with functional and some symbolic play observed, such as feeding a stuffed dog and saying "Canela come." Oral-motor structures were within normal limits for strength, symmetry, and range of motion; no evidence of dysarthria, apraxia indicators, or structural abnormality was observed, and diadochokinetic rates for /pataka/ sequences were judged age-appropriate informally. Hearing was screened at this visit and passed bilaterally at 25 dB across frequencies of 500–4000 Hz, consistent with his most recent audiological evaluation.

Spontaneous speech samples in both English and Spanish were analyzed for phonology, morphosyntax, and pragmatics. In Spanish, Teo substituted /ɾ/ for /l/ in words like "cala" for "cara," and simplified consonant clusters, producing "pato" for "plato." In English, he exhibited final consonant deletion, producing "ka" for "cat" and "do" for "dog," the latter notably when referring to Canela. Cross-linguistic error patterns were consistent with a phonological disorder affecting both languages rather than typical second-language interference, which was an important differential given his bilingual status. Morphosyntactically, Teo relied heavily on two- and three-word utterances in both languages, frequently omitting grammatical morphemes such as Spanish gender/number agreement ("la perro" instead of "el perro") and English copula and auxiliary forms ("he happy" instead of "he is happy"). Pragmatically, Teo used gesture, pointing, and single words to repair communication breakdowns and often looked to Vale or Lucía for repair rather than attempting self-repair verbally.

Resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas. The following standardized and criterion-referenced measures were administered in both English and Spanish as appropriate, with results interpreted cautiously given Teo's bilingual language history and the limited availability of Spanish norms for some instruments.

Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English and Spanish editions:
Auditory Comprehension (English): standard score 76, 5th percentile
Expressive Communication (English): standard score 71, 3rd percentile
Total Language Score (English): standard score 72, 3rd percentile, confidence interval 68-78
Auditory Comprehension (Spanish): standard score 79, 8th percentile
Expressive Communication (Spanish): standard score 74, 4th percentile

Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), English edition:
Sentence Structure subtest: scaled score 5
Word Structure subtest: scaled score 6
Expressive Vocabulary subtest: scaled score 7
Core Language Score: standard score 73, age equivalent 2;6–3;0

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3):
Sounds-in-Words standard score: 68, 2nd percentile
Percentage of consonants correct: 62%

Informal Spanish phonology probe (criterion-referenced): 11 of 20 target words produced with at least one sound error; consistent errors on /ɾ/, /s/ final-position deletion, and consonant cluster reduction.

Expressive language sample, mean length of utterance: 2.1 morphemes in English, 2.4 morphemes in Spanish, both below expectations for CA.

Trial dynamic assessment: when provided with modeling and moderate (mod) cues, Teo successfully imitated two- and three-word combinations 7 of 10 trials, suggesting responsiveness to intervention and ruling against a purely performance-based explanation for his low scores.

Impresiones clínicas. Based on today's assessment, parent and teacher report, and medical and developmental history, Teo presents with a Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder, ICD-10 F80.2, co-occurring with a Phonological Disorder, ICD-10 F80.0, affecting both of his languages. CPT code 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression) applies to today's assessment. His difficulties are evident across Spanish and English, which, per current best practice in bilingual assessment, supports a true language disorder rather than a language difference attributable to dual-language exposure, limited English proficiency, or typical bilingual developmental variation; this distinction is important given extended family's prior assumption that the delay was simply because he is "bilingüe." His prematurity, prolonged NICU course, and history of recurrent otitis media with documented conductive hearing loss episodes are all plausible contributing factors, though his most recent audiological evaluation and today's screening confirm hearing within normal limits bilaterally at present. Teo's strong nonverbal play skills, social engagement, and responsiveness to cueing during dynamic assessment are favorable prognostic indicators.

Recomendaciones. 1. Teo qualifies for and should receive speech-language therapy services, recommended at a frequency of two 45-minute sessions per week, delivered bilingually in Spanish and English, through either continued Mecklenburg County CDSA early intervention services or a transition plan to preschool special education services as he approaches age five. 2. Given Teo's profile, a combined treatment approach is recommended. PROMPT (Prompts for Restructuring Oral Muscular Phonetic Targets) is recommended to address his phonological and oral-motor coordination difficulties across both languages. Cycles approach for phonological remediation is recommended to target his cluster reduction and final consonant deletion patterns in a structured, developmentally sequenced manner. 3. Given the family's reliance on Vale and Lucía to interpret Teo's communicative intents, parent coaching through the Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" program is strongly recommended to help Lucía and Jorge build in strategic pauses and expectant waiting so Teo has more opportunity for independent verbal attempts, rather than having his needs anticipated or met nonverbally. 4. Although Teo does not currently present with the profile of a child requiring augmentative or alternative communication, should his frustration and shutdown behaviors increase before expressive gains are evident, a trial of PECS (Picture Exchange Communication System) core vocabulary boards bilingually labeled in Spanish and English could be introduced as a bridge strategy at daycare and at home, in coordination with Debra Lopez at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare. 5. The Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol was considered given Teo's motor-based sound errors, and may be incorporated as a supplementary approach within sessions if progress with PROMPT and Cycles plateaus, particularly for shaping multisyllabic word approximations in both languages. 6. Continued audiological monitoring is recommended given his otitis media history; a follow-up evaluation with Susan Kim, Au.D., at Atrium Health Levine Children's – Myers Park Campus is suggested within the next 12 months or sooner if further ear infections occur. 7. Coordination with Mecklenburg County CDSA Service Coordinator Marisol Ortiz is recommended to update IFSP Outcome 2 to reflect today's findings and to ensure continuity of bilingual services; the family may also benefit from connecting with Smart Start of Mecklenburg County for additional bilingual playgroup resources. 8. Given Vale's role as an informal interpreter and the family's limited availability during Jorge's night-shift schedule at Daimler Trucks North America, flexible scheduling of therapy sessions, including evening or Saturday morning slots, is recommended; the family indicated Saturdays at 9:00 a.m. or weekday evenings after 5:30 p.m. work best. 9. Information was shared with the family regarding bilingual language development and dispelling the myth that exposure to two languages causes or worsens language delay, which the evaluator reviewed directly with Rosa Elena Hernández Soto by phone during a portion of the feedback session at the family's request, using the number +52 222 555 0176. 10. Re-evaluation is recommended in approximately six months, or sooner if requested by the family, Mecklenburg County CDSA, or Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare staff.

This evaluator is available to discuss these findings and recommendations further. Camila Reyes can be reached at (704) 555-0133 or by email at camila.reyes@carolinabilingualslp.com. The family's preferred contact is Lucía Rodríguez Cruz at 980-555-0147 or lucia.rodriguez82@gmail.com. A copy of this report has been sent to Rafael Alvarez, M.D., and to Service Coordinator Marisol Ortiz at Mecklenburg County CDSA.

Esta evaluadora agradece a la familia Rodríguez Cruz y a Esperanza Gutiérrez Díaz por su colaboración durante esta evaluación, y felicita a Teo por su esfuerzo y buena disposición durante las dos sesiones. "Él se portó muy bien," comentó Lucía al final de la cita, a lo que Teo respondió sonriendo, "yo bueno," levantando el pulgar hacia su mamá.
