REASON FOR REFERRAL

Pt referred by Piedmont CDSA for comprehensive speech-language eval following parent concern re: limited expressive vocab, unintelligible speech, and behavior frustration noted by Teo's daycare, Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy. Piedmont CDSA opened case August 5, 2026 after pediatrician referral. SC Priya Nair coordinated intake w/ family, confirmed Medicaid eligibility, and scheduled eval w/ CPSLT b/c CG requested a bilingual provider. Interpreter Marisol Vega assigned via ACSTC roster for both sessions.

BACKGROUND INFO

Teo is a 3;2-yo male, home language Spanish (primary), limited English exposure at Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy approx 4 of 5 days/wk since March 2026. CG report concerns began approx 6 months ago when teacher Angela Lopez noted Teo not following 2-step directions in Eng, frequent pointing/gesturing instead of verbalizing wants, and tantrums when not understood. Asst teacher Brian Walsh corroborated via daily note log. Family lives at 142 Sweetbriar Lane, Hickory, NC 28601, Catawba County.

Mother Lucía Rodríguez Flores (age 29) is pt's primary CG, home full-time. Father Diego Hernández Soto (age 32) works 2nd shift at Hickory Furniture Manufacturing Co., limited availability for appts. Older sister Camila Hernández Flores (age 7, 1st grade) attends Southside Elementary School; no speech/lang concerns reported for Camila. Pt's maternal grandmother Rosa Flores Díaz (abuela) lives 10 min away, helps w/ childcare 2x/wk, speaks only Spanish w/ pt. Paternal cousins Nico Hernández (age 5) and Valentina Soto (age 4) visit weekly; mother reports pt plays well w/ Nico but gets frustrated when Valentina doesn't understand his requests. Family also uses babysitter Dalia Cortez approx 1x/wk when both parents work. Family pet, a dog named Rocky, is reportedly pt's favorite "friend"; mother says pt will say "Rocky no" when dog barks but little else spontaneously.

Family receives support fr/ multiple agencies: enrolled in Catawba County WIC Program since infancy, previously attended parent groups through Smart Start of Catawba County, and Teo was referred by pediatrician to Catawba Valley Early Head Start for possible enrollment pending CDSA eval outcome. Family also has open case w/ Catawba County Department of Social Services (DSS) re: housing assistance, unrelated to current referral per mother report.

BIRTH & MEDICAL HISTORY

Per mother report and review of hospital d/c summary provided by CG: pt born August 14, 2023 at Catawba Valley Medical Center, gestational age 38 weeks, via vaginal delivery, no complications noted. Birth weight 6 lbs 11 oz. Apgar scores 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 min. NICU stay not required. Pediatrician of record: Dr. Samuel Osei, Catawba Pediatric Associates; most recent well-child visit July 22, 2026 noted normal growth, hearing screen passed bilaterally (OAE), no chronic ear infxns reported. Hx of 2 episodes otitis media (ages 14mo & 22mo), resolved w/ antibiotics, no tubes placed, no current concerns per Dr. Osei's note.

No sig. medical dx otherwise. Developmental milestones per CG: sat unsupported approx 7mo, walked approx 14mo, first words (Spanish) approx 15mo ("mamá," "agua"), word combos delayed - mother reports pt still mostly uses single words or gestures at 3;2. No hx of seizures, no genetic testing done, no prior SLP/OT/PT services prior to CDSA referral. Vision screening w/in normal limits per pediatrician.

Pt currently receiving OT eval concurrently through Piedmont CDSA w/ Rachel Kim, OTR/L, re: fine motor/self-feeding concerns noted by mother (picky eating, mod difficulty w/ utensils). PT screening completed September 15, 2026 by James Patterson, PT, DPT - gross motor WNL, no PT services recommended at this time.

FAMILY & LANGUAGE HISTORY

Home language environment: Spanish spoken approx 90% of time at home by both parents and Rosa Flores Díaz; English introduced primarily through Camila (who is becoming more Eng-dominant from school) and daycare exposure. Per CG report (via interpreter Marisol Vega), pt's language development has been slower in BOTH languages compared to Camila at the same age, which mother states is distinct fr/ expected bilingual acquisition variability and has caused concern across multiple settings/informants (daycare, pediatrician, extended family).

Mother denies fam hx of speech/lang disorder, learning disability, or autism on either side; however pt's paternal uncle reportedly "talked late" per family report w/ no further details available. No hx of hearing loss in family. Pt attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy M-F mornings; classroom teacher Angela Lopez reports pt plays alongside peers but rarely initiates verbal interaction. Classmates Ethan Combs and Sofia Nguyen are reported as pt's preferred playmates; Angela Lopez notes pt will often pull Ethan Combs's sleeve rather than request verbally.

CG reports exposure to Spanish-language media (children's shows) approx 1 hr/day, no concerns re: excessive screen time per guidelines discussed. Family attended several Smart Start of Catawba County playgroups Fall 2025 where staff first suggested CG discuss concerns w/ pediatrician.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

Eval conducted across 2 sessions (approx 90 min each) in clinic setting at CPSLT office, 2200 Tate Blvd SE, Hickory, NC. Interpreter Marisol Vega facilitated all parent interview and instructions were provided in Spanish w/ Eng probes interspersed per standardized protocol allowances. Both parents attended session 1; father Diego Hernández Soto unable to attend session 2 due to work schedule at Hickory Furniture Manufacturing Co. Standardized and informal measures administered in both Spanish and English where appropriate per test publisher guidelines for bilingual admin.

Tools administered:
- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish/English bilingual edition
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax and Phonology subtests
- Spontaneous language sample (Spanish, approx 50 utterances) analyzed w/ SALT conventions
- Oral mech exam
- Hearing screen (pass, bilateral, 20 dB at 1000, 2000, 4000 Hz)
- Parent interview/case hx (via interpreter)
- Clinical observation of play-based interaction

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Pt separated from mother w/ mild protest, warmed quickly to clinician and interpreter w/in approx 5 min. Attention to task fair, required frequent redirection and preferential use of novel toys to maintain engagement. Pt demonstrated functional play skills (stacking blocks, pretend feeding doll) but limited symbolic/narrative play. Pt used gestures (pointing, reaching, pulling CG's hand) as primary communication mode, supplemented by approx 15-20 intelligible single words across both languages observed during session. Articulation noted as significantly reduced in intelligibility - unfamiliar listener (clinician) understood approx 30% of pt's spontaneous utterances; familiar listener (mother) reported understanding approx 60-70%.

Pt required mod cues to imitate target words; e.g., when shown picture of dog, pt said "wawa" for target "perro" (/peɾo/), demonstrating final consonant deletion and liquid simplification. When asked to name family dog, pt spontaneously said "Rocky" clearly, suggesting familiar/practiced words show better production accuracy than novel targets. No significant behavioral dysregulation observed during testing; one brief frustration episode occurred when pt could not retrieve desired toy from closed bin and resorted to crying rather than requesting "open" or "ayuda" - resolved w/ mod cues and modeling.

TEST RESULTS

Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) - Spanish/English Bilingual Edition

Domain | Standard Score | Percentile | Age Equivalent
Auditory Comprehension | 71 | 3rd | 1;9
Expressive Communication | 68 | 2nd | 1;6
Total Language Score | 66 | 1st | 1;7
95% CI for Total Language Score: 61-71

Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA)

Subtest | Scaled Score | Percentile
Morphosyntax - Spanish | 4 | 2nd
Morphosyntax - English | 3 | 1st
Phonology - Spanish | 5 | 5th

Combined morphosyntax performance falls w/in the "at risk" range per BESA bilingual norms, consistent across both languages (not an artifact of language dominance alone), supporting suspicion of primary language impairment rather than typical bilingual variability.

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) - administered in Spanish w/ Eng supplementation

Standard Score: 62  Percentile: 1st  Age Equivalent: <2;0

Sound Errors Noted (Spanish phoneme inventory):
- Final consonant deletion: target /peɾo/ ("perro") → produced [peo]
- Liquid simplification: /ɾ/ → [w] or omitted in all positions tested
- Cluster reduction: /pl/, /kl/ clusters reduced to singleton consonant in 8 of 10 opportunities
- Velar fronting occasionally noted: /k/ → [t] in word-initial position, approx 40% of opportunities
- Stimulability: pt stimulable for /ɾ/ in isolation w/ max cues; not yet stimulable in CV context

Spontaneous Language Sample (Spanish, 50 utterances coded)

MLU (morphemes): 1.4
Utterance types: 88% single-word, 12% two-word combos
Most frequent 2-word combos: "más agua," "no quiero," "Rocky no" (re: dog)
SALT code example: [EW] marked for 4 unintelligible utterances during sample

Oral Mechanism Exam: WNL for structure and function. No evidence of dysarthria or significant oral-motor planning deficit beyond expected for age/dx under consideration.

Hearing Screening: Pass bilaterally at 20 dB, 1000, 2000, 4000 Hz. No further audiological referral indicated at this time based on screening alone; recommend repeat screen at next well visit per standard protocol given hx of 2 prior OM episodes.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Teo presents w/ a Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder affecting BOTH Spanish and English, consistent across multiple standardized measures (PLS-5, BESA) and confirmed via clinical observation and parent report across settings (Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy, home, extended family). Performance is depressed relative to bilingual peer norms in both the heritage language (Spanish, primary home lang) and the emerging second language (English), which per BESA bilingual guidelines and clinical judgment rules out typical bilingual language variability/second-language acquisition lag as sole explanation.

Co-occurring moderate-severe Speech Sound Disorder noted, characterized by multiple phonological process patterns (final consonant deletion, liquid simplification, cluster reduction, occasional velar fronting) resulting in significantly reduced intelligibility (approx 30% to unfamiliar listeners). Given pt's age (3;2) and severity/pattern of errors, concern for underlying phonological disorder rather than solely developmental delay is warranted; several patterns (liquid simplification, cluster reduction persisting at this age) exceed what would be expected developmentally for a monolingual or bilingual 3;2-yo per normative data reviewed.

Pt's use of gesture as primary communicative mode, limited symbolic play, and reported frustration/behavioral escalation when not understood are consistent w/ functional impact of combined expressive language and speech sound deficits on daily communication and social participation (at home, daycare, and with peers Ethan Combs and Sofia Nguyen).

No red flags for autism spectrum disorder identified during this eval (e.g., pt demonstrated joint attention, functional play, social referencing to CG and clinician); however, given overall profile, continued monitoring across domains via the multidisciplinary CDSA team (OT eval w/ Rachel Kim, PT screening already completed by James Patterson) is recommended, and any emerging social-communication concerns should be flagged promptly to SC Priya Nair and pediatrician Dr. Samuel Osei.

DIAGNOSTIC IMPRESSION / ICD-10

- F80.2 Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder
- F80.0 Phonological Disorder (Speech Sound Disorder)

CPT codes for billing: 92523 (eval of speech sound production and language) with modifier GN for therapy services under outpatient speech-lang program; 92506 not separately billed per payer policy, combined under 92523 per current CDSA authorization AUTH-556213-NC.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Pt qualifies for and is recommended for ongoing speech-language therapy services through Piedmont CDSA IFSP process, Outcome #2 (communication) and Outcome #3 (reducing frustration/behavior via functional communication), to be finalized at upcoming IFSP mtg scheduled October 20, 2026.

2. Recommend bilingual (Spanish/English) individual speech-lang therapy, 2x/week, 30-45 min sessions, provided by bilingual SLP or SLP + qualified interpreter, through CPSLT or comparable CDSA-approved provider, focusing on:
   a. Expanding expressive vocab and word combinations in Spanish (home-dominant lang) as foundation lang, w/ cross-linguistic transfer strategies for Eng as pt enters more Eng-dominant settings
   b. Phonological intervention targeting final consonant deletion, liquid simplification, and cluster reduction using a Cycles approach, w/ min-mod cueing hierarchy
   c. Functional communication training to reduce reliance on gesture/frustration behaviors - incorporate PECS-style visual supports initially, fading as verbal output increases, informed by Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" parent-coaching principles
   d. PROMPT-informed tactile-kinesthetic cueing may be trialed given motor planning component of sound errors noted

3. Parent coaching sessions recommended 1x/month minimum, conducted in Spanish w/ interpreter Marisol Vega or equivalent cert. interpreter as needed, to train Lucía Rodríguga Flores and Diego Hernández Soto in home strategies (expansion, modeling, reducing direct question demands, following pt's lead per Hanen framework).

4. Continue coordination w/ Catawba Valley Early Head Start re: potential enrollment to increase structured Eng language exposure in supportive, small-group setting; SC Priya Nair to facilitate referral paperwork.

5. Classroom consultation recommended w/ Little Sprouts Early Learning Academy staff (Angela Lopez, Brian Walsh) to share simple in-classroom supports (visual schedule, allowing extra response time, pairing verbal models w/ gesture) to support pt's participation and reduce frustration episodes involving peers Ethan Combs and Sofia Nguyen.

6. Recommend repeat hearing screening at next pediatric well visit w/ Dr. Samuel Osei given hx of recurrent OM, even though current screen passed, b/c fluctuating conductive loss can affect phonological development.

7. Continue OT services as indicated per Rachel Kim's concurrent eval; no additional PT services needed per James Patterson's screening.

8. Family may benefit from continued connection w/ Smart Start of Catawba County playgroups for additional structured peer interaction opportunities, and continued WIC nutrition support given prior picky-eating concerns flagged in OT referral.

9. Recommend re-eval in 6 months (approx April 2027) to monitor progress across both languages and adjust IFSP outcomes/goals as needed; sooner re-eval warranted if autism-related or other new concerns emerge per multidisciplinary team input.

10. All documentation and authorization renewals to be coordinated through SC Priya Nair at Agencia de Coordinación de Servicios Tempranos del Condado de Catawba (ACSTC), (828) 555-0199, and copied to Piedmont CDSA case file per standard CDSA reporting requirements.

This eval and these recs reflect pt's performance across 2 sessions on September 29, 2026 and October 2, 2026. Results should be interpreted w/in context of standardized bilingual tools used and single clinical snapshot; ongoing monitoring across home, daycare, and therapy settings recommended to confirm trajectory.

Respectfully submitted,

Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist

CONFIDENTIAL BILINGUAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT
EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE — CONFIDENCIAL

Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
4420 Ramsey Street, Fayetteville, NC 28311
Tel: (910) 555-0147 | Fax: (910) 555-0148

Client/Cliente: Mateo Alejandro Fernández Ruiz ("Teo")
Date of Birth: August 13, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Date of Evaluation: October 15, 2026
Record/Case ID: LDI-48217
Medicaid ID: 902317456B
Referral Source: Denise Alvarado, Service Coordinator, Children's Developmental Services Agency – Cumberland County
Referral Date: June 10, 2026
Evaluator: Alexandra Cruz, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual SLP

S: (SUBJETIVO / SUBJECTIVE)

Teo is a 4;2-year-old bilingual (Spanish-English) male referred by Children's Developmental Services Agency – Cumberland County ("the CDSA") following a Part C eligibility screening that flagged significant expressive and phonological delays. His mother, Lucía Rodríguez Fernández, reports: "no le entiendo casi nada de lo que dice, solo yo y su papá le entendemos un poco." Father, Carlos Fernández Díaz, present for the first 20 minutes of intake, adds that Teo "gets frustrated y empieza a gritar cuando nadie le entiende."

Family history gathered via parent interview, review of CDSA intake packet, and prior records from Cape Fear Valley Medical Center. Household composition: mother Lucía Rodríguez Fernández (works second shift at Food Lion Distribution Center), father Carlos Fernández Díaz (employed at a local tire plant), older sister Sol Fernández Rodríguez (age 7, typically developing, attends elementary school), and maternal grandmother Rosa Díaz ("Abuela Rosa"), who lives with the family and provides after-school care three days a week. Paternal cousins Ángel Fernández and Camila Fernández, ages 6 and 4, visit weekly and play with Teo in the backyard; mother notes Teo "se pone muy contento" when they come over but mostly plays alongside them rather than with them. A part-time babysitter, Yolanda Pérez, watches Teo two mornings a week before daycare drop-off. The family dog, Luna, a mixed-breed rescue, is frequently mentioned by mother as a comfort object: "cuando está triste abraza a Luna y se calma."

Birth and Medical History: Full-term pregnancy, spontaneous vaginal delivery at Cape Fear Valley Medical Center on August 13, 2022. Birth weight 7 lbs 8 oz, Apgar scores 8 at 1 minute and 9 at 5 minutes. No NICU stay. Mother denies maternal illness, substance use, or complications during pregnancy. Gross and fine motor milestones reportedly within normal limits; walked independently at 13 months. Hearing screened at birth, passed bilaterally. Pediatrician Dr. Ahmed Khan referred the family for audiological re-screening in March 2026 after mother raised concerns at a well-child visit; results were within normal limits bilaterally per report on file. No history of chronic ear infections, though mother recalls "dos o tres" episodes of otitis media between ages 1 and 2, treated with antibiotics, no tubes placed. Diagnostic code on referral paperwork lists F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, rule-out) and F80.0 (phonological disorder, rule-out).

Family and Language History: Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home; mother reports approximately 80% Spanish, 20% English input, with English increasing since Teo began attending Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare in January 2026. Mother's first language is Spanish (Mexican dialect, family originally from Michoacán); father is bilingual, raised partly in Fayetteville and partly in Guadalajara. No report of language delay in sister Sol or in either parent. Grandmother Rosa speaks only Spanish to Teo. At daycare, teacher Griselda Lopez reports Teo uses mostly gestures and single words with classmates Emma Thompson and Jayden Brooks, and that he "shuts down" during circle time when he cannot produce a requested word. Ms. Lopez notes he responds well to visual supports already in use at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare.

Family history of speech/language or learning disorders: mother reports a maternal uncle who "no hablaba bien hasta los 5 o 6 años" per family report, otherwise unremarkable. No history of autism, hearing loss, or genetic syndromes in first-degree relatives.

Services to date: Teo was enrolled briefly in Fayetteville Early Head Start at age 2 but was withdrawn when the family's transportation fell through; service coordinator Denise Alvarado notes the family re-enrolled in home-visiting services through CDSA in April 2026. Family currently receives support from Cumberland County WIC Program and was connected to Partnership for Children of Cumberland County (Smart Start) for a childcare subsidy in May 2026; that subsidy currently funds Teo's placement at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare. Family has had intermittent contact with Cumberland County Department of Social Services regarding SNAP benefits; no open child welfare case per parent report and CDSA file.

Parent priorities (elicited in Spanish, translated/summarized): mother wants Teo to "poder decir lo que quiere sin frustrarse" and to be understood by his sister Sol and cousins Ángel and Camila. Father prioritizes school readiness, noting Teo starts kindergarten screening within the next two years.

O: (OBJETIVO / OBJECTIVE)

Evaluation conducted over two sessions, October 15, 2026 and October 20, 2026, at Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC, with mother Lucía Rodríguez Fernández present both sessions and interpreter services not required, as evaluator Alexandra Cruz is bilingual Spanish-English. CPT code 92523 (speech sound and language evaluation) billed under authorization AUTH-77410-CF.

Behavioral observations: Teo separated easily from mother, engaged readily with toys and testing materials. Attention to task adequate with min-mod cues to redirect. Play skills age-appropriate; engaged in pretend play ("el perrito come," referencing Luna) and turn-taking games without difficulty. Eye contact and joint attention within normal limits. No concerns regarding social reciprocity noted.

Standardized Assessment:

Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-English Bilingual Edition, administered in both languages per protocol, best-performance scoring.

| Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile | Age Equivalent | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auditory Comprehension | 82 | 12th | 3;1 | Below Average |
| Expressive Communication | 68 | 2nd | 2;4 | Significantly Below Average |
| Total Language Score | 73 | 4th | n/a | Below Average |

95% Confidence Interval for Total Language Score: 68-78.

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3), English administration, supplemented with Spanish phonological probes (informal, Fonológico en Español protocol).

| Measure | Score | Percentile |
|---|---|---|
| Sounds-in-Words Standard Score | 65 | 1st |
| Percent Consonants Correct (PCC-English) | 58% | n/a |
| Percent Consonants Correct (PCC-Spanish, informal) | 61% | n/a |

Phonological processes noted across both languages: final consonant deletion (e.g., "pan" → [pa]), stopping of fricatives (e.g., "sapo" → [tapo]), cluster reduction (e.g., "flor" → [for]), and gliding of liquids (e.g., /ɾ/ produced as [w] in words like "carro"). Stimulability testing: Teo stimulable for /s/ in isolation and in CV syllables with mod cues, not yet stimulable for /ɾ/ or consonant clusters even with max cues.

Single-word probe list targeting /s/ in initial position included "sapo," "salsa," "silla," and, per clinical protocol, the clinician avoided using the child's sister's name as a target; however, when asked to label a picture of the sun during the Spanish probe set, Teo spontaneously produced "sol" instead of the target picture label, substituting his sister's name — a pattern mother confirmed happens at home when Sol's name is used frequently around mealtime routines. This was coded as a non-target substitution rather than a correct production and was not scored toward the articulation probe.

Oral-peripheral exam: structures and function within normal limits; no concerns for dysarthria or structural anomaly. Diadochokinetic rates age-appropriate for gross screening purposes.

Language sample: 50-utterance spontaneous sample collected in free play with mother and evaluator, coded per SALT conventions. Mean length of utterance (MLU) in morphemes: 2.1, below expected range for age (3.5-4.2). Predominant utterance types: single words and two-word combinations (e.g., "más agua," "no quiero"). Code-switching within utterances noted and considered typical for bilingual development (e.g., "quiero el car," "dame el juice"), not counted as error. One utterance coded [EW] for an elaborated word attempt that was unintelligible even in context. Overall intelligibility estimated at 3 of 10 words to unfamiliar listener, 6 of 10 to familiar listener (mother), consistent with parent report.

Receptive language informally probed via following directions in both languages: followed two-step related directions in Spanish ("agarra el carro y pónlo en la caja") with 8/10 accuracy; English two-step directions 5/10 accuracy, reflecting lower exposure rather than a receptive deficit per se.

Social communication/pragmatics: appropriate requesting, protesting, and commenting observed, though largely gestural or single-word. No red flags for autism spectrum disorder noted on informal observation; no concerns raised by Ms. Lopez or parents regarding restricted interests or repetitive behavior. Dr. Khan's most recent well-child note (reviewed with parent consent) likewise does not flag ASD concerns.

A: (ASSESSMENT / EVALUACIÓN)

Results indicate a moderate-to-severe expressive language disorder and a moderate phonological disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with a true bilingual language/speech sound disorder rather than typical second-language acquisition or dialectal variation. Error patterns are present and proportionally similar across both languages, which, combined with below-average receptive scores and family history, supports a disorder rather than a difference. Teo meets criteria consistent with ICD-10 codes F80.1 (expressive language disorder) and F80.0 (phonological disorder); mixed type given co-occurring deficits.

Diagnoses support continued Part C eligibility and an updated IFSP. Severity and bilingual profile warrant services delivered primarily in Spanish, the home language, with English language stimulation incorporated as Teo's exposure increases at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare. Frustration behaviors reported by mother and Ms. Lopez are consistent with communication frustration secondary to the disorder, not a primary behavioral or social-emotional diagnosis at this time; recommend monitoring.

Strengths: age-appropriate play skills, intact joint attention and social reciprocity, stimulable sound inventory suggesting good prognosis with intervention, supportive and engaged family, and existing bilingual exposure that should be leveraged rather than reduced.

P: (PLAN)

1. Recommend direct speech-language therapy, 2x/week, 30-minute sessions, delivered primarily in Spanish with English carryover, individual format initially transitioning to small group as intelligibility improves.

2. Recommend a Cycles phonological approach to target the identified error patterns (final consonant deletion, stopping, cluster reduction, gliding) across both languages, cycling through pattern targets every 5-6 weeks per standard protocol.

3. For expressive language, recommend a combined Hanen ("It Takes Two to Talk") coaching model for parents Lucía Rodríguez Fernández and Carlos Fernández Díaz, alongside direct PROMPT tactile-cueing techniques in session to support motor planning for speech production, particularly for liquids and clusters.

4. Given frustration and limited intelligibility, recommend introducing a visual supplement (picture exchange strategies informed by PECS principles) for use at home and at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare during high-demand routines (transitions, requesting), to reduce frustration while speech and language goals are addressed directly. Kaufman Speech to Language Protocol hierarchy considered as a secondary approach if motor-based approximation targets are needed for highly unintelligible multisyllabic words.

5. Coordinate with Children's Developmental Services Agency – Cumberland County and service coordinator Denise Alvarado to update the IFSP, adding Outcome 3 (expressive communication) and Outcome 4 (speech sound production), with review scheduled for January 12, 2027.

6. Recommend continued audiological monitoring given history of otitis media; re-screen if any further episodes occur, coordinate with Dr. Ahmed Khan.

7. Provide family with bilingual home-practice materials emphasizing shared book reading and naturalistic language modeling in Spanish, per Hanen framework; encourage continued Spanish input from grandmother Rosa Díaz and limit well-meaning but unhelpful correction attempts noted from extended family during gatherings with cousins Ángel Fernández and Camila Fernández.

8. Share results, with parental consent already obtained, with Griselda Lopez at Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare and with Partnership for Children of Cumberland County to support continued subsidy eligibility and classroom accommodations (visual schedule, extra processing time, bilingual peer modeling with classmates Emma Thompson and Jayden Brooks).

9. No referral to Cumberland County Department of Social Services indicated at this time regarding child welfare; existing WIC and childcare subsidy supports through Cumberland County WIC Program and Partnership for Children of Cumberland County appear sufficient and should continue.

10. Re-evaluate in approximately 6 months (April 2027) to monitor progress toward IFSP outcomes and determine need for continued Part C services versus transition planning toward preschool special education evaluation given Teo's age.

Prognosis: Good, given stimulable sound inventory, strong family engagement, intact play and social skills, and appropriate match between recommended bilingual service delivery model and the family's home language environment. Consistency of attendance, supported by continued transportation coordination through CDSA and babysitter Yolanda Pérez's flexibility with pickup/drop-off, will be an important factor in progress.

Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC

S (Subjetivo): Su mamá Lucía de la Cruz reporta que Mateo tuvo una semana difícil — "Mateo no durmió bien" desde el 1 de junio. Mom works two jobs, including evenings at QuikMart #42 and mornings as a CNA for Johnston County DSS home health contract; she said, "estoy agotada pero necesito las dos." Mateo's daycare, Little Sprouts Daycare in Smithfield, reported similar articulation patterns per teacher Ms. Alvarado.

A (Análisis): Steady progress toward IFSP Outcome #2 (functional communication). Family stressors (dual employment, housing near 27577) impact carryover; referred again to Early Head Start for respite support and Partnership for Children of Johnston County for childcare subsidy navigation.

P (Plan): Continue biweekly visits. Next review scheduled 3 de julio de 2026. Contact clinic at (919) 555-2047 or dosei@carolinapinespediatrictherapy.com with questions. Pediatrician Dr. Felipe Nguyen copied per care plan ICD-10 F80.0, CPT 92507.

Nota adicional: perrito familiar Canela estuvo presente, ayudó a motivar producciones espontáneas — Mateo dijo "Canela corre" espontáneamente.

Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners
884 Sycamore Court, Suite 2, Maple Ridge, NC 27301
(336) 555-0148 • smartinez@carolinabilingualtherapy.com

October 9, 2026

Dear Lucía and Carlos,

¡Hola! Thank you both for making time to meet with us on October 2, 2026 for Mateo's annual IFSP review. Gracias por su paciencia — I know it is hard to find a morning when Lucía is not sleeping after a night shift. This letter is a summary, in plain language, of everything we talked about, so you have it to keep and to share with anyone who helps care for Teo.

Quiénes estuvieron en la reunión / Who was at the meeting: you, Lucía Rodríguez; your service coordinator, Michelle Brown, from Piedmont CDSA; our interpreter, Ana Gutiérrez, who made sure everything was clear in both languages; occupational therapist Jennifer Kim; physical therapist David Thompson; and me, Sofía Martínez, your speech-language pathologist. Carlos joined us by phone during his lunch break.

Nuestra familia / Our family

Mateo Alejandro Hernández Cruz, whom everyone calls Teo, was born on March 14, 2024 and is now 2;7. He was born at 37 weeks gestation, weighing 6 lbs 2 oz, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9. He lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez; his father, Carlos Hernández; and his big sister, Camila, who is six, at 214 Hollyhock Lane, Maple Ridge, NC 27301. His grandmother, Rosa Cruz, whom the family calls Abuela, watches Teo and Camila several afternoons a week while Carlos is still at work. Lucía works nights at the Piedmont Foods Distribution Center, stocking shelves on the overnight shift, and Carlos works days as a mechanic at Hendrick Auto Repair. An aunt, Marisol Cruz, visits most Sundays and often helps with Teo's bath time.

Lo que ustedes nos dijeron / What you told us

Lucía said, "Queremos que Teo hable más para que pueda decirnos qué necesita, en vez de llorar o jalarnos la mano." She also told us, "En la casa hablamos español casi todo el tiempo, pero yo sé que en la guardería hablan inglés, y a veces no sé si eso lo confunde." Carlos added, in English, "We just want him to be able to tell us what he wants, and to play with other kids without getting frustrated." Camila chimed in, laughing, "I'm teaching him 'please' and 'por favor' so he says it both ways!" These priorities guided everything we planned together.

Rutinas diarias / Daily routines

Teo wakes around 6:30 a.m. and has breakfast with Camila before Carlos drops both children at Little Learners Daycare by 7:45 a.m.. He is in Ms. Lopez's room, where he plays at circle time next to his friend Diego and likes stacking blocks. The daycare director, Karen Phillips, told us Teo has started pointing to pictures in books during story time, which is wonderful progress. Rosa Cruz picks the children up around 4:00 p.m. on days Lucía is sleeping, and the family eats dinner together around 6:30 p.m. once Carlos is home. After dinner, Teo loves to chase their dog, Max, around the backyard before bath and bedtime around 8:00 p.m..

On Sunday mornings the family attends Iglesia Bautista Monte Sion, where Teo goes to the nursery room with other toddlers while Lucía and Carlos attend service. On Tuesday afternoons, when her shift allows, Lucía takes Teo and Camila to the bilingual storytime program at the county library, called Leamos Juntos, which Lucía says Teo really enjoys because of the songs and finger puppets.

Otros programas y agencias / Other programs and agencies

In addition to speech-language therapy through Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, Teo attends the Little Learners Program, a twice-weekly early intervention playgroup run by Piedmont CDSA, where he works on motor skills and social play with other toddlers. The family also receives nutrition support through WIC and was recently connected with Smart Start of Pinebrook County for a possible childcare subsidy so Lucía can cut back on overnight hours. Teo's pediatrician, Dr. Patel, at Maple Ridge Pediatrics, continues to monitor his growth and referred him for a hearing screening on August 11, 2026, which he passed in both ears. As Teo gets closer to turning three, we also began talking about transition planning with Pinebrook County Schools Exceptional Children's Preschool Program.

Evaluación y progreso / Evaluation and progress

On September 20, 2026, I completed an updated speech-language evaluation using the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5). Teo's Auditory Comprehension standard score was 78 (7th percentile), and his Expressive Communication standard score was 73, placing his overall language ability in the 73-83 range with 95% confidence. His expressive language age equivalent fell between 1;6 and 1;10. His diagnosis remains Expressive Language Disorder, ICD-10 F80.1. Jennifer Kim's fine motor screening placed him at an age equivalent of 2;0, and David Thompson's gross motor measures showed steady gains since his March 2026 evaluation.

In single words, Teo is using approximately 30 different words, mostly in Spanish, including "mamá," "agua," and "más." He imitated the word "pelota" during our session, producing it as "beyota", showing he can approximate the shape of the word with moderate cues. His sound system includes /m/, /p/, /a/, but he still substitutes /w/ for /l/ and /ɾ/, as in his production of "bola" as "bowa". He combined two words together one time during the session, saying "más agua" ("more water") with minimal cues, coded as [EW] in our session notes.

Nuestras metas / Our outcomes and strategies

Outcome 1: Teo will use two-word combinations in Spanish and/or English to request and comment during daily routines, increasing from his current one spontaneous combination to 3 of 5 opportunities across a session. We will use strategies from Hanen, including "OWL" (observe, wait, and listen), both at home and at Little Learners Daycare, so Teo hears the same approach in both languages. We encouraged Rosa Cruz to narrate daily tasks in Spanish, since she spends the most daytime hours with him.

Outcome 2: Teo will imitate and later spontaneously produce his target sounds /w/ and /l/ in single words with 80% accuracy, using motor-based cueing from PROMPT during play-based sessions.

Outcome 3: Teo will tolerate and request help during frustrating moments using a gesture or word instead of crying, in 8 out of 10 observed opportunities, supported by consistent routines at home, at Little Learners Daycare, and in his playgroup at Piedmont CDSA.

Jennifer Kim will continue working with Teo on fine motor skills for feeding and play, and David Thompson will focus on gross motor coordination so he can keep up with Camila and his friends at the park.

Fechas de servicio / Service dates

Teo's initial IFSP was written on June 2, 2025, following his referral through Piedmont CDSA. This annual review took place on October 2, 2026, and his next review is scheduled for April 2, 2027, with a full annual re-evaluation due by June 2, 2027. Speech-language sessions will continue twice weekly for 30 minutes, billed under CPT 92507 with modifier GN.

Para contactarnos / How to reach us

Teo's Medicaid number on file is 987654321B, and his IFSP case number is IFSP-2026-04471. If you have questions about any of this, please call Michelle Brown at Piedmont CDSA at (336) 555-0199, or call me directly at (336) 555-0148 or email smartinez@carolinabilingualtherapy.com. Ana Gutiérrez is also happy to help interpret any phone calls if that is easier for the family.

Gracias de nuevo por confiar en nosotros con el cuidado de Teo. It is a joy to watch him grow, and we are so glad to be part of your team.

Con cariño,

Sofía Martínez, MS, CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners

INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y DEL LENGUAJE

1. INFORMACIÓN DE IDENTIFICACIÓN

Nombre del niño: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Fernández, conocido en casa y en la escuela como "Teo"
Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de marzo de 2021
Edad cronológica en el momento de la evaluación: 4;6
Sexo: masculino
Idiomas del hogar: español e inglés
Fechas de evaluación: 15 de septiembre de 2026 y 22 de septiembre de 2026
Fecha del informe: 29 de septiembre de 2026
Número de expediente: WC-20264471
Número de identificación de Medicaid: 789456123B
Evaluadora: Patricia Nguyen-Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP, patóloga del habla y el lenguaje bilingüe
Empresa: Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Dirección de la clínica: 4521 Jones Franklin Road, Suite 210, Cary, NC 27518
Teléfono de la clínica: (919) 555-0148
Correo electrónico: pnguyenalvarez@trianglebilingualslp.com
Sitio web: www.trianglebilingualslp.com
Distrito escolar: Wake County Public School System
Escuela actual: Forest Pines Elementary School
Salón: clase de pre-kínder para necesidades especiales, a cargo de la maestra Carmen (Carmen Jiménez), con el apoyo del asistente Mr. Tom (Tom Sullivan)
Guardería anterior: Centro Preescolar Rayitos de Sol, a cargo de Miss Ana (Ana Whitfield)

2. MOTIVO DE LA REMISIÓN

Teo fue remitido para una evaluación integral del habla y el lenguaje por recomendación de su pediatra, el Dr. Michael Osei, y por preocupaciones expresadas por su madre, Lucía Fernández Morales, y su padre, Jorge Cruz Delgado, sobre su retraso en el desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo y receptivo, además de dificultades para producir ciertos sonidos del habla. La coordinadora de servicios del CDSA del Piedmont Oriental, Brenda Collins, solicitó esta evaluación como parte de la revisión trienal del plan individualizado de servicios familiares (IFSP) de Teo, cuyo número de resultado es el Resultado 2 del IFSP vigente. la maestra Carmen también notificó al equipo que Teo presenta dificultad para seguir instrucciones de dos pasos en el salón y que con frecuencia recurre a gestos en lugar de palabras para comunicarse con sus compañeros, entre ellos Liam y Sofía.

3. ANTECEDENTES DE NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICOS

Teo nació el 14 de marzo de 2021 en el WakeMed Cary Hospital, producto de un embarazo a término de 39 semanas de gestación. El parto fue vaginal, sin complicaciones significativas. Su peso al nacer fue de 3,200 gramos y su puntaje de Apgar fue de 8 al minuto uno y 9 a los cinco minutos. No requirió ingreso a la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales.

La madre reporta un historial de tres episodios de otitis media aguda entre los 8 meses y los 18 meses de edad, tratados con antibióticos orales por el pediatra, el Dr. Michael Osei, en su consultorio de Garner. No se colocaron tubos de ventilación (miringotomía). Una prueba de audición más reciente, realizada el 3 de agosto de 2026 por audiología pediátrica, arrojó resultados dentro de límites normales bilateralmente, con timpanogramas tipo A en ambos oídos.

El desarrollo motor grueso y fino de Teo se describe como típico para su edad: caminó de forma independiente a los 13 meses y actualmente puede subir escaleras alternando los pies, saltar con ambos pies y manipular crayones con un agarre de trípode emergente. No hay antecedentes de convulsiones, hospitalizaciones mayores, cirugías ni lesiones craneales. Teo no toma medicamentos de manera regular. Su visión fue evaluada como normal en su última revisión pediátrica el 12 de julio de 2026.

El diagnóstico médico de referencia que figura en su expediente, asignado por el Dr. Michael Osei, es F80.2 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo), conforme a la Clasificación Internacional de Enfermedades, Décima Revisión.

4. ANTECEDENTES FAMILIARES Y DE LENGUAJE

Teo vive con su madre, Lucía Fernández Morales, su padre, Jorge Cruz Delgado, y su hermana mayor, Valentina Cruz Fernández, de siete años, en una vivienda en 118 Sunflower Lane, Garner, Wake, NC 27529. La familia también convive de cerca con la abuela materna, a quien todos llaman doña Lupe (Guadalupe Torres), quien cuida a Teo y a Valentina Cruz Fernández tres tardes por semana mientras sus padres trabajan. Una niñera de confianza de la familia, Rosa Elena Vásquez, también ayuda ocasionalmente los fines de semana. La familia tiene una perrita llamada Luna, con quien Teo disfruta jugar en el patio.

La madre, Lucía Fernández Morales, trabaja como asistente administrativa en una clínica dental local. El padre, Jorge Cruz Delgado, es técnico de soporte en Lenovo, en su sede de Morrisville. Ambos padres reportan haber crecido hablando español como primera lengua en México y haber aprendido inglés como lengua adicional durante la adolescencia.

Según el reporte parental, el español es el idioma predominante en el hogar (aproximadamente 70% del tiempo de interacción), mientras que el inglés se usa el 30% restante, principalmente cuando Valentina Cruz Fernández practica tareas escolares en voz alta o cuando la familia ve programas infantiles en inglés. doña Lupe habla exclusivamente español con Teo, mientras que en la escuela Teo recibe instrucción casi en su totalidad en inglés por parte de la maestra Carmen y Mr. Tom.

Los padres describen a Teo como un niño cariñoso, curioso y sociable con adultos conocidos, pero que muestra timidez y frustración al intentar comunicarse con compañeros nuevos. Lucía Fernández Morales indica que sus primeras palabras en español aparecieron alrededor de los 20 meses, más tarde de lo esperado, y que su vocabulario combinado en ambos idiomas sigue siendo notablemente menor que el de su hermana a esa misma edad. No hay antecedentes familiares reportados de trastornos del habla, el lenguaje o el aprendizaje, aunque la madre menciona que un tío paterno fue "de pocas palabras" de niño.

5. PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

La evaluación se llevó a cabo en dos sesiones. La primera sesión tuvo lugar el 15 de septiembre de 2026 de 9:30 a.m. a 11:00 a.m. en las oficinas de Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC, y la segunda sesión se realizó el 22 de septiembre de 2026 de 10:15 a.m. a 11:15 a.m. en el mismo lugar. Ambas sesiones fueron conducidas en su totalidad por la evaluadora bilingüe, Patricia Nguyen-Alvarez, sin necesidad de un intérprete adicional. Los padres, Lucía Fernández Morales y Jorge Cruz Delgado, estuvieron presentes para la entrevista inicial y para proporcionar información sobre el desarrollo de su hijo mediante cuestionarios estandarizados.

Se administraron los siguientes instrumentos estandarizados, en español e inglés según correspondiera a las normas de cada prueba:

- Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish Edition
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool, Third Edition (CELF Preschool-3)
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Test de Vocabulario en Imágenes Peabody (TVIP)
- Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA), subpruebas de morfosintaxis

Además, se llevó a cabo una muestra de lenguaje espontáneo de 15 minutos en español y de 15 minutos en inglés durante juego estructurado, observación clínica directa durante ambas sesiones, revisión de registros escolares y médicos, y entrevista estructurada con los padres utilizando el cuestionario de desarrollo del lenguaje de la clínica. Se solicitaron además formularios de observación conductual a la maestra Carmen y a Miss Ana, quienes los completaron y los devolvieron antes de la segunda sesión.

Los servicios facturados durante esta evaluación corresponden a los códigos de Terminología de Procedimiento Actual (CPT) 92523 (evaluación de la producción del habla y la comprensión y expresión del lenguaje) y 92507 (tratamiento de trastornos del habla, el lenguaje, la voz y/o la comunicación y/o la deglución, sesión individual), este último correspondiente a una breve sesión de prueba terapéutica realizada al final de la segunda cita para observar la respuesta de Teo a niveles de apoyo (cueing).

6. RESULTADOS DE LA EVALUACIÓN

6.1 Lenguaje receptivo y expresivo

En el PLS-5, Spanish Edition, Teo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 76 (percentil 5) en Comunicación Auditiva y una puntuación estándar de 71 (percentil 3) en Comunicación Expresiva, con un Total de Lenguaje de 73 (intervalo de confianza del 95%: 68-78). Estos resultados ubican su desempeño dentro del rango descriptivo "muy por debajo del promedio" en ambas modalidades.

En inglés, administrado como medida complementaria mediante el CELF Preschool-3, Teo obtuvo un Índice de Lenguaje Central de 70 (percentil 2), con una puntuación escalar de 4 en la subprueba de Estructura de Oraciones y una puntuación escalar de 5 en Conceptos y Siguiendo Direcciones. Cabe notar que, dado que Teo recibe la mayor parte de su exposición al inglés en un entorno escolar relativamente reciente (aproximadamente 13 meses de exposición continua), estos resultados deben interpretarse con cautela y en el contexto de su desarrollo bilingüe típico.

En el TVIP, obtuvo una edad equivalente de vocabulario receptivo de 2;9, considerablemente por debajo de su edad cronológica de 4;6, con una puntuación estándar de 65.

En las subpruebas de morfosintaxis del BESA, Teo mostró dificultad consistente con la concordancia de género y número en español (por ejemplo, produjo "la perro" en lugar de "el perro") y con la marcación verbal de tiempo pasado tanto en español como en inglés (omitió consistentemente el morfema /-ó/ y el morfema /-ed/, produciendo "ayer yo come" y "yesterday I walk").

6.2 Articulación y fonología

En el GFTA-3, Teo obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 78 (percentil 7), con errores de sustitución y omisión consistentes con los siguientes procesos fonológicos: frontalización velar (produjo "tasa" por "casa"), simplificación de grupos consonánticos (produjo "pato" por "plato") y sonorización de obstruyentes finales. A nivel de sonidos individuales, Teo sustituyó consistentemente /k/ por [t] en posición inicial de palabra y mostró distorsión de /ɾ/ en posición intervocálica, produciendo algo cercano a [d].

Durante la muestra de habla espontánea, su inteligibilidad fue estimada por la evaluadora en aproximadamente 60% con oyentes familiares y notablemente más baja con oyentes desconocidos. Durante una tarea de repetición estructurada de 10 palabras monosílabas con grupos consonánticos iniciales, Teo produjo correctamente 3 de 10 (30%), consistente con un retraso fonológico significativo para su edad.

6.3 Respuesta a niveles de apoyo (prueba terapéutica breve)

Durante la breve sesión de prueba terapéutica facturada bajo el código 92507, se evaluó la capacidad de Teo para imitar la secuencia /k/ en sílabas aisladas con distintos niveles de apoyo. Con apoyo máximo (modelo visual y táctil simultáneo), Teo logró producir /k/ correctamente en 8/10 ensayos (80% de precisión). Con apoyo moderado (modelo auditivo únicamente), su precisión descendió a 4/10 ensayos (40%). Esto sugiere un buen potencial de respuesta a la intervención directa con apoyo estructurado, lo cual es un hallazgo pronóstico positivo.

6.4 Tabla resumen de puntuaciones estandarizadas

| Prueba / Subprueba | Puntuación estándar / escalar | Percentil | Intervalo de confianza |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Comunicación Auditiva | 76 | 5 | 68-84 |
| PLS-5 Comunicación Expresiva | 71 | 3 | 64-78 |
| PLS-5 Total de Lenguaje | 73 | 4 | 68-78 |
| CELF Preschool-3 Índice de Lenguaje Central | 70 | 2 | 64-76 |
| GFTA-3 Puntuación Estándar | 78 | 7 | 73-83 |
| TVIP Puntuación Estándar | 65 | 1 | 58-72 |

6.5 Observación conductual y pragmática

Durante ambas sesiones, Teo mantuvo contacto visual apropiado, respondió a su nombre de forma consistente y demostró intención comunicativa clara a través de gestos, señalamiento y vocalizaciones, incluso cuando las palabras no estaban disponibles. Participó con entusiasmo en actividades de juego simbólico, incluyendo un esquema de juego en el que alimentaba a un peluche y decía "bebé come" repetidamente, demostrando el uso de una estructura de dos palabras de manera espontánea. En otro momento, señaló la puerta y dijo "Luna fuera" para indicar que quería que la perrita de la familia saliera a jugar.

Teo mostró turnos conversacionales apropiados para su edad y respondió adecuadamente a preguntas simples de sí/no, aunque tuvo dificultad notable con preguntas de "por qué" y "cómo", respondiendo frecuentemente con repetición de parte de la pregunta (ecolalia) o con "no sé". No se observaron conductas sensoriales atípicas, estereotipias motoras ni dificultades significativas de reciprocidad social que sugirieran un trastorno del espectro autista; el perfil observado es consistente con un trastorno primario del lenguaje.

El formulario completado por la maestra Carmen indica que, en el salón, Teo sigue instrucciones de un paso de manera consistente (reportado en 9/10 oportunidades observadas) pero solo sigue instrucciones de dos pasos en 4/10 oportunidades sin repetición o gestos de apoyo. Miss Ana, desde su experiencia previa con Teo en Centro Preescolar Rayitos de Sol, reportó observaciones similares, agregando que Teo se comunicaba mejor en grupos pequeños que en actividades de grupo completo.

7. IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Con base en los resultados estandarizados, la observación clínica directa y los reportes de los padres y del personal escolar, Teo presenta un trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo de moderado a severo, que afecta tanto el español como el inglés, consistente con un trastorno primario del lenguaje (anteriormente denominado trastorno específico del lenguaje) más que con una diferencia esperada propia del desarrollo bilingüe típico. Esta determinación se basa en el hecho de que el rendimiento de Teo se encuentra significativamente por debajo del rango esperado en ambos idiomas, en múltiples dominios lingüísticos (vocabulario, morfosintaxis, comprensión auditiva), y es consistente con los reportes parentales de un inicio tardío del lenguaje y una trayectoria de desarrollo lenta en comparación con su hermana a la misma edad.

Adicionalmente, Teo presenta un trastorno fonológico de moderada severidad que afecta su inteligibilidad, particularmente con oyentes no familiares, y que involucra procesos fonológicos típicamente asociados con etapas de desarrollo más tempranas (frontalización velar, simplificación de grupos consonánticos). Su buena respuesta a niveles de apoyo estructurado durante la prueba terapéutica breve (8/10, 80% con apoyo máximo) sugiere un pronóstico favorable con intervención directa y consistente.

No se identificaron preocupaciones significativas en el dominio pragmático-social más allá de las esperadas como consecuencia secundaria de sus limitaciones lingüísticas y fonológicas. El perfil de Teo no sugiere un diagnóstico primario dentro del espectro autista, aunque se recomienda monitoreo continuo conforme progresa su lenguaje.

8. DIAGNÓSTICO

Con base en los hallazgos de esta evaluación, se asigna el siguiente código diagnóstico conforme a la Clasificación Internacional de Enfermedades, Décima Revisión (CIE-10 / ICD-10):

F80.2 — Trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo (trastorno primario del lenguaje, afectando español e inglés, con trastorno fonológico concomitante)

9. RECOMENDACIONES

9.1 Con base en los resultados de esta evaluación, se recomienda que Teo reciba terapia de habla y lenguaje individual continua, con una frecuencia sugerida de dos sesiones de 30 minutos por semana, conducida en español, con generalización planificada hacia el inglés conforme avance su dominio en su lengua primaria. Esta recomendación se alinea con la evidencia que indica que la intervención en la lengua materna fortalece el desarrollo en ambos idiomas en niños bilingües con trastornos del lenguaje.

9.2 Se recomienda que estos servicios continúen prestándose a través del CDSA del Piedmont Oriental bajo el IFSP vigente, con coordinación continua por parte de Brenda Collins, hasta la transición de Teo a servicios de educación especial preescolar a través del Wake County Public School System al cumplir los cinco años.

9.3 Se recomienda que el equipo del IFSP, en colaboración con la maestra Carmen y Mr. Tom en Forest Pines Elementary School, incorpore estrategias de apoyo visual y de modelado de lenguaje dentro del aula, incluyendo el uso de apoyos visuales para instrucciones de dos pasos y oportunidades estructuradas de práctica en grupos pequeños, dado que Teo responde mejor en ese formato según lo reportado por Miss Ana y la maestra Carmen.

9.4 Se recomienda implementar un enfoque terapéutico basado en el programa Hanen para el entrenamiento de los padres, Lucía Fernández Morales y Jorge Cruz Delgado, con el fin de aumentar las oportunidades de modelado de lenguaje durante las rutinas diarias del hogar, incluyendo las horas que Teo pasa con doña Lupe. Se recomienda además incorporar principios del enfoque PROMPT para abordar los patrones de error articulatorio identificados, dado que estos parecen tener una base motora-articulatoria además de fonológica.

9.5 Se recomienda que la familia reciba referencia a servicios de apoyo adicionales según sea necesario, incluyendo verificación de elegibilidad continua para WIC y para el programa estatal Smart Start de Wake County, que ofrece recursos de alfabetización temprana bilingüe para familias en la zona de Garner y Clayton.

9.6 Se recomienda una reevaluación formal del progreso de Teo en un plazo de seis meses, o antes si se observa un estancamiento en el progreso terapéutico, para determinar la necesidad continua de servicios y ajustar los objetivos del plan de tratamiento.

9.7 Se recomienda que todos los proveedores involucrados, incluyendo al pediatra, el Dr. Michael Osei, mantengan comunicación regular con esta clínica para asegurar la coordinación de cuidados. Cualquier pregunta sobre este informe puede dirigirse a la evaluadora, Patricia Nguyen-Alvarez, al correo electrónico pnguyenalvarez@trianglebilingualslp.com o al teléfono de la clínica (919) 555-0148. Información adicional sobre los servicios ofrecidos por Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC está disponible en www.trianglebilingualslp.com.

10. RESUMEN

Mateo Alejandro Cruz Fernández ("Teo"), un niño bilingüe de 4;6, presenta un trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo (CIE-10 F80.2) de moderado a severo que afecta tanto el español como el inglés, acompañado de un trastorno fonológico de moderada severidad. Su desarrollo médico, motor y social general es, por lo demás, consistente con su edad, y no se identificaron preocupaciones significativas dentro del espectro autista. Se recomienda terapia de habla y lenguaje continua conducida primariamente en español, con coordinación activa entre la familia, el CDSA del Piedmont Oriental, el equipo escolar en Forest Pines Elementary School y esta clínica.

Respetuosamente sometido,

Patricia Nguyen-Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Patóloga del Habla y el Lenguaje, Licencia de Carolina del Norte
Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC

BILINGUAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Carolina Piedmont Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
4410 Harwell Road, Suite B, Garner, NC 27529
Phone: (919) 555-0148  Fax: (919) 555-0149

Evaluator: Patricia Gómez, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual (English/Spanish)
Date of Evaluation: September 22, 2026
Report Date: September 29, 2026

CHILD: Mateo Alonso Fuentes ("Teo")
Date of Birth: July 15, 2022      Chronological Age at Testing: 4;2
Gestational Age at Birth: 36 weeks      Birth Weight: 5 lbs 9 oz
Medicaid ID: 803552147K
Insurance Member ID (BlueOptions): YLZ9284731
NC ITP Child ID: ITP-0047732
Authorization/Record #: AUTH-26-11290

Parent/Guardian 1: Lucía Fuentes Ramos (mother)
Parent/Guardian 2: Daniel Fuentes (father)
Home Address: 118 Maplewood Court, Clayton, NC 27520
Home Phone: (919) 555-0271      Mother's Cell: (919) 555-0290
Primary Home Language(s): [X] Spanish  [X] English  [ ] Other
Interpreter Used: [X] Yes (bilingual evaluator, no outside interpreter needed)  [ ] No

Setting Observed: [X] Home  [ ] Daycare  [ ] Clinic  [ ] Other
Referral Source: Tanner County CDSA, via Service Coordinator Mr. Tom

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a bilingual speech-language evaluation by his Early Intervention service coordinator, Mr. Tom, following concerns raised at his annual IFSP review on August 11, 2026. Lucía Fuentes Ramos reports that Teo is difficult to understand in both Spanish and English, uses short utterances, and has begun to show frustration when classmates and family members cannot understand him. Lucía Fuentes Ramos also reports concern after speaking with la maestra Carmen at pickup, who noted that Mateo often points or gestures instead of using words during circle time.

BACKGROUND

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Fuentes Ramos, his father, Daniel Fuentes, and his older sister, Valentina Fuentes (age 7), in a single-family home in Clayton. Lucía Fuentes Ramos works two jobs to support the family: she is employed during the day at Clayton Foods Distribution on the packing line, and overnight several nights a week with BCS, a commercial cleaning crew that services office buildings in Garner. Daniel Fuentes works full-time as a mechanic and is often the one who brings Mateo to and from his program.

On the nights Lucía Fuentes Ramos works for BCS, Mateo and his sister Valentina Fuentes stay with a neighbor, doña Lupe, who has watched the children since Teo was an infant and speaks only Spanish with him. A paid babysitter, Jasmine Cole, also helps on weekday afternoons when both parents are working, and she reports using mostly English with Mateo. The family's dog, Rocky, a terrier mix, is frequently mentioned by Mateo in play and is a strong motivator during structured activities.

[X] Home   [X] Daycare/Preschool   [ ] Clinic   [ ] Other settings reported by caregiver

Mateo attends Sunrise Head Start Center four days a week from 8:30 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.. His lead teacher is la maestra Carmen, and the assistant teacher is Miss Ana. Both report that Mateo is social and well liked but struggles to be understood by peers, including his close friends Emily and Josh. la maestra Carmen shared that during a recent snack time, Mateo said "I want tuh" and his classmate Josh did not understand what he meant and asked him to repeat it three times before another child helped interpret.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 36 weeks gestation at Riverside Women's Hospital in Raleigh on July 15, 2022, weighing 5 lbs 9 oz. Apgar scores were 7 and 9 at one and five minutes. Lucía Fuentes Ramos reports a NICU stay of 9 days for feeding support and mild jaundice, treated with phototherapy. No seizures, intubation, or surgeries were reported.

Developmental milestones were reportedly within normal limits for gross and fine motor skills; Mateo walked independently at 13 months. Expressive language milestones were delayed: first words were reported around 22 months, and two-word combinations did not emerge until approximately 34 months. Mateo passed his newborn hearing screening and has had no documented ear infections requiring tubes. A recent audiological screening on August 3, 2026 through Tanner County CDSA showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally.

Mateo's pediatrician, Dr. Hannah Lee at Cape Fear Pediatric Associates, diagnosed him with a phonological disorder (ICD-10: F80.0) and referred the family for ongoing speech-language services (CPT: 92523). Mateo currently receives occupational therapy for mild fine motor delays through Tanner County CDSA, one session per week, with occupational therapist Rachel Nguyen.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Lucía Fuentes Ramos grew up in Monterrey and moved to North Carolina as a young adult; Spanish is her first and most comfortable language. Daniel Fuentes was born in Durham and is bilingual, though he reports using more English at work and with extended family. At home, both languages are used: Lucía Fuentes Ramos and doña Lupe speak primarily Spanish with Mateo, while Daniel Fuentes, Valentina Fuentes, and babysitter Jasmine Cole use primarily English.

Extended family lives nearby and sees Mateo frequently, including his cousins Sofía Ramos and Diego Ramos, who are close in age and often play with him on weekends. Lucía Fuentes Ramos reports that Mateo is more verbal and animated in Spanish with his cousin Sofía Ramos than he is at daycare, suggesting language use may vary by comfort and context rather than reflecting a true language preference.

Valentina Fuentes is reported to be a typically developing reader and talker in both languages and often "translates" for Mateo when others cannot understand him, which Lucía Fuentes Ramos worries may be reducing Mateo's motivation to repair his own speech.

Family history is reportedly significant for a maternal uncle who had a "late talker" history and received speech therapy as a child, though no formal records were available for review.

PRIOR AND CURRENT SERVICES

[X] Early Intervention (Part C)   [ ] Preschool Special Education (Part B)   [ ] Private Clinic Only

Mateo has received home-based developmental therapy through Tanner County CDSA since February 2025, under IFSP Outcome 2 (communication) and IFSP Outcome 3 (fine motor). Family reports that his EI team has lightly introduced PECS picture cards at home for requesting preferred items, with mixed carryover reported by Lucía Fuentes Ramos. No formal articulation or language therapy program has yet been implemented.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

[X] Parent/Caregiver Interview   [X] Standardized Testing   [X] Language Sample   [X] Classroom/Home Observation   [ ] Dynamic Assessment

Testing was conducted in both English and Spanish across two sessions, on September 15, 2026 and September 22, 2026, in the family's home. Mateo was cooperative throughout, though attention was best supported with frequent breaks and use of his toy dog, which he called "Rocky," as reinforcement. Rapport was established quickly; Mateo was observed to be a socially engaged child who used eye contact, joint attention, and gesture effectively to compensate for limited intelligibility.

TEST RESULTS

Standardized Assessment Battery:

| Measure | Domain | Standard Score | Percentile | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) | Auditory Comprehension | 82 | 12th percentile | 3;1 |
| PLS-5 | Expressive Communication | 76 | 5th percentile | 2;9 |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition | Sound Production | 71 | 3rd percentile | — |
| Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA) | Phonology | 79 | 8th percentile | — |
| BESA | Morphosyntax, Spanish | 85 | 16th percentile | — |

Confidence interval for PLS-5 Expressive Communication: 70-84 (95%).

Speech Sound Production: In English, Mateo demonstrated reduction of consonant clusters ("poon" for "spoon"), final consonant deletion ("ca" for "cat"), and fronting of velars ("tat" for "cat"). In Spanish, similar patterns were noted, including simplification of the tap /ɾ/ to [l] ("pelo" for "perro") and cluster reduction in words such as "tes" for "tres." Overall intelligibility was judged to be approximately 40% to unfamiliar listeners and 65-70% to familiar listeners in context.

Language Sample: A 50-utterance conversational sample was collected in Spanish and a 50-utterance sample in English. Mean length of utterance in Spanish was 2.8 morphemes; in English, 2.3 morphemes. Mateo produced primarily subject-verb or verb-object combinations ("quiero agua," "Rocky run") with limited grammatical morphology (e.g., inconsistent use of plural -s and verb tense marking in both languages). Vocabulary diversity was judged to be mildly reduced for age in both languages, with cross-linguistic influence noted (code-switching within utterances, e.g., "I want mas").

Oral Mechanism Exam: Structure and function within normal limits; no evidence of dysarthria or apraxia of speech. Diadochokinetic rates were age-appropriate.

Social Communication and Play: Mateo demonstrated appropriate eye contact, joint attention, and symbolic play (feeding and walking a toy dog he named "Rocky" after the family pet). No concerns for social communication disorder were noted at this time.

Response to Cueing: Mateo was stimulable for several target sounds with moderate cues (tactile and visual), improving production of word-initial /k/ from omission to a distorted but present attempt with min cues on 3 of 5 trials.

CLASSROOM AND HOME OBSERVATION

[X] Observed at Daycare   [X] Observed at Home

During a 30-minute observation at Sunrise Head Start Center, Mateo engaged with Emily and Josh during free play but used primarily gesture and single words. Miss Ana redirected him gently when he became frustrated after Josh could not understand a request related to blocks. At home, Mateo was observed interacting comfortably with his cousins Sofía Ramos and Diego Ramos during a brief visit, using more Spanish and longer utterances than typically observed at daycare.

IMPRESSIONS

Mateo presents with a moderate expressive language delay and a moderate-to-severe phonological disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with a true bilingual speech-language impairment rather than second-language acquisition alone, given that error patterns are present and comparable across both languages. His receptive language is a relative strength, though also below age expectations. Reduced intelligibility appears to be contributing to frustration, reliance on gesture, and dependence on his sister, Valentina Fuentes, to communicate on his behalf.

Mateo presents with:
- Moderate expressive language delay (English and Spanish)
- Mild-moderate receptive language delay
- Moderate-severe phonological disorder (cross-linguistic patterns)
- Age-appropriate oral motor structure/function
- Appropriate social communication and play skills
- Positive stimulability to cueing, suggesting good candidacy for therapy

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo qualifies for ongoing speech-language intervention under his IFSP, recommended at 2 sessions per week, 30 minutes each, in his dominant home language context with bilingual support as available.
2. Therapy should address phonological patterns using a cycles-based approach (Cycles) targeting final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and velar fronting across both languages.
3. PROMPT techniques are recommended to support motor planning for speech sound production given Mateo's positive response to tactile cueing.
4. Continue and expand use of PECS as a visual support for requesting, while prioritizing verbal attempts first with moderate cues before presenting the picture symbol.
5. Family coaching is recommended using a Hanen framework, specifically strategies from It Takes Two to Talk, to support Lucía Fuentes Ramos and Daniel Fuentes in using expansion and modeling strategies at home, given their demanding work schedules and limited availability for clinic-based sessions.
6. If single-word vocabulary growth remains slow, consider supplementing with Kaufman praxis-based cards to target motor speech sequencing for core vocabulary.
7. Recommend continued coordination with occupational therapist Rachel Nguyen and service coordinator Mr. Tom to align IFSP goals.
8. Recommend sharing strategies with la maestra Carmen and Miss Ana at Sunrise Head Start Center so that classroom supports (modeling, wait time, visual choices) are consistent with home and therapy approaches.
9. Encourage caregivers, including doña Lupe and babysitter Jasmine Cole, to continue using their respective home languages consistently rather than switching, to support balanced bilingual development.
10. Re-evaluation recommended in 6 months or at next IFSP review, whichever comes first, to monitor progress and adjust service intensity.

This evaluation and these recommendations are based on standardized assessment, language sampling, caregiver report, and direct observation on the dates noted above. Please contact this office with any questions.

Respectfully submitted,

Patricia Gómez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Piedmont Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
